title: A Needs Analysis for the Development of Collaborative Inquiry-Based Academic Supervision to Improve the Implementation of Deep Learning in Vocational High Schools
abstract: The importance of developing collaborative inquiry-based academic supervision to improve the implementation of deep learning serves as the rationale for this study. This study aims to analyze the need for developing collaborative inquiry-based academic supervision to improve the implementation of deep learning. A survey method was used, employing a quantitative descriptive approach. The study was conducted at six vocational high schools (SMK) under the XII Regional Education Office of Central Java Province. title: Network pharmacology, single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning and experimental validation identifying CHEK2 and HPGD as key therapeutic targets of berberine in diabetic nephropathy
abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a severe microvascular complication of diabetes with limited therapeutic options. Berberine exhibits renoprotective potential, yet its precise molecular targets and mechanisms of action in DN remain unclear. Berberine targets were retrieved from TCMSP, SEA, and SwissTargetPrediction databases. Bulk transcriptomic microarray datasets (GSE96804, GSE30122) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset (GSE131882) were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). title: The digitalization of labor intermediation and its legal limits: employment agencies, temporary employment agencies and public services in the face of artificial intelligence
abstract: El presente trabajo analiza el impacto de la inteligencia artificial en las agencias de colocación, las empresas de trabajo temporal y los servicios públicos de empleo desde la perspectiva del Derecho del Trabajo. El estudio examina cómo la implantación de algoritmos y sistemas automatizados de decisión transforma los procesos de intermediación laboral, modificando las formas tradicionales de selección, clasificación y asignación de trabajadores. abstract: Estimating petrophysical properties in petroleum exploration and reservoir management is crucial as these physical properties help petroleum engineer(s) understand the most likely distribution and/or presence of oil/gas reservoirs, as well as decide whether that certain field might be exploitable or not. Accurate assessments of properties such as porosity, permeability, and water saturation are essential for predicting reservoir behaviour, optimizing well placement, and enhancing recovery strategies. abstract: This investigation evaluates the important parameters affecting the fresh and hardened properties of a quaternary blended ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS)-based geopolymer matrix optimized through the Taguchi approach. Four variables were investigated using an L16 orthogonal array: waste glass powder (WGP), metakaolin (MK), pond ash (PA) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) molarity, each at four levels. title: A Numerical Study on the High-Velocity Ballistic Performance of TPMS Sandwich Structures
abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) structures have significant potential for lightweight ballistic armor. Unlike previous quasi-static or low-velocity studies, this research explicitly addresses the terminal ballistic regime and perforation morphology. It evaluates three Ti6Al4V TPMS sandwich cores (Diamond, Gyroid, Primitive) subjected to 7.62 mm Armor-Piercing (AP) projectiles at 830 m/s using Abaqus/Explicit. title: Genus-Level Coral Community Assessment Using Underwater Photo Transect and Ecological Indices in an Industrial Coastal Area
abstract: This study presents a genus-level coral community assessment using underwater photo transect data and ecological indices in an industrial coastal area of East Java, Indonesia. Coral reef monitoring was conducted in August 2025 at four observation stations, namely Lighthouse, Water Intake, East Water Discharge, and West Water Discharge, using a 70-m underwater photo transect and a 1 × 1 m photoquadrat frame. title: Spondylodiscitis and epidural abscess after spinal surgery: case series highlighting diagnostic and therapeutic challenges
abstract: Objective: To describe the clinical, radiological, microbiological, treatment, and functional characteristics of three patients with postoperative spondylodiscitis (SD) and/or spinal epidural abscess.Methods: We retrospectively reviewed postoperative SD/EA cases managed at a regional hospital between 2019 and 2023. Patients with previous spinal surgery, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed SD with or without EA, and at least 3 months of follow-up were included. title: Machine learning-assisted evaluation of pH and scavenger effects on methylene blue photodegradation using green-synthesized Nb2O5 nanoparticles
abstract: The expansion of industrial activities has significantly increased water contamination by organic pollutants, especially persistent synthetic dyes (e.g., methylene blue - MB), which pose environmental and health risks. In this context, sustainable and efficient treatment technologies are required. Heterogeneous photocatalysis has emerged as a promising approach, particularly when combined with green-synthesized nanomaterials. title: AI-driven assessment of forest dynamics and ecosystem services in response to land use change: current progress and future perspectives
abstract: Forests cover approximately 31% of the global land surface and provide critical ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, hydrological regulation, and biodiversity support, yet ongoing deforestation and fragmentation are progressively eroding these services. title: Detection and Mapping of Seawater Intrusion Using Machine Learning Integration of Hydro-Chemical, Soil Salinity, and Remote Sensing Indices
abstract: The process of groundwater salinization and seawater intrusion affects coastal aquifers of arid and semiarid areas owing to excessive abstraction of groundwater, land use change, and climatic variability. In this study, hydrochemistry, Remote sensing, Geographic Information System, and machine learning techniques are combined to analyze the level of groundwater salinity and seawater intrusion in Ramanathapuram District, Tamil Nadu, India. title: Understanding Biogeographic Patterns in Sepiolidae (Cephalopoda)
abstract: ABSTRACT The biogeography of the bobtail squid family Sepiolidae is reviewed. Species of the Sepiolinae subfamily are only found in coastal waters of the ‘Old World’, with a high degree of diversification in the Mediterranean Sea and the Coral Triangle in the Indo‐Pacific region. The Rossiinae subfamily inhabits coasts of both the Old and New Worlds. Finally, the Heteroteuthinae subfamily exhibits widespread distribution patterns in the oceans of the whole world. title: Defesa e autonomia tecnológica na Amazônia Azul: PROSUB, PFCT e SISGAAZ
abstract: The Blue Amazon concentrates strategic resources, infrastructure, and economic flows whose protection depends on state, industrial, and technological defense capabilities. This article analyzes how Defense Economics and the Political Economy of the Sea interact in the interpretation of three Brazilian strategic maritime programs: the Submarine Development Program (PROSUB), the Tamandaré-Class Frigates Program (PFCT), and the Blue Amazon Management System (SISGAAZ). title: Integrating compaction energy into predictive models for pervious concrete permeability
abstract: Pervious concrete is an innovative material that effectively manages stormwater runoff. This study aims to develop predictive models for the permeability of pervious concrete, with a particular emphasis on the role of compaction energy. A comprehensive modelling approach was adopted, incorporating Linear Regression, Two-Factor Interaction model, Quadratic model, and Artificial Neural Network to examine the relationships between permeability and key mix design variables. abstract: This work examines bio-convective magnetized Ree-Eyring nanofluid flow on a convectively heated Riga surface. Thermal diffusion is controlled through use of Cattaneo-Christov thermal flux and Brownian motion effects along with thermal radiations. title: Satellite insights into diatom biomass dynamics and environmental drivers in the eastern China marginal seas
abstract: Diatoms are among the dominant phytoplankton groups in marginal seas and play a pivotal role in marine primary production and biogeochemical cycling. In this study, focusing on the eastern China marginal seas (ECMS), we developed a remote sensing model to retrieve diatom biomass ( C diat ) directly from remote sensing reflectance. Multiple linear regression and machine-learning methods were evaluated using in situ observations and satellite-in situ matchup datasets. title: Vertical accuracy of satellite-derived bathymetry developed using ICESat-2 ATL03 data for Brazilian coastal waters
abstract: Satellite-Derived Bathymetry (SDB) offers a cost-effective solution for mapping and monitoring coastal environments, especially where in situ data are limited or outdated. The ICESat-2 mission, through its ATL03 photon-counting lidar product, provides high-resolution geolocated photon data suitable for depth retrieval in optically shallow waters. title: Rational interfacial design and mechanisms of polymer-MOF hybrids for electrochemical heavy metal sensing in aqueous matrices
abstract: Heavy metal ions (HMIs), such as Pb 2+ , Cd 2+ , Cu 2+ , and Hg 2+ , are persistent, non-biodegradable water contaminants that demand analytical methods combining high sensitivity, selectivity, and field portability. Hybrid materials that integrate conductive polymers with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as a versatile electrochemical sensing platform, combining tunable, ion-selective binding sites with the electrical conductivity and processability required for practical electrodes. title: Machine-learning-guided hydrothermal engineering of Cobalt-modified ZnFe₂O₄ for visible-light-active porous photocatalytic coating for urban infrastructure
abstract: This study presents a machine-learning-guided hydrothermal strategy for optimizing Cobalt-modified ZnFe 2 O 4 (ZF–Co) photocatalysts. Moreover, a novel scalable porous inorganic coating platform compatible with retrofit implementation on existing urban infrastructures was developed for visible-light-driven atmospheric pollutant mitigation. title: Sea level modelling and forecasting combining analytical and deep learning methods, case study: Piraeus, Greece
abstract: Abstract This study contributes to sea level modelling and prediction through the development of a framework proposal consisting of both an analytical approach and Deep Learning methodologies. Analyses have focused on the strategically important harbour of Piraeus located near the metropolitan city of Athens, Greece. The research leverages a database comprising tide gauge recordings and meteorological variables, spanning the period from 1999 to 2019. Using these datasets an analytical model was designed. title: A remote sensing image processing method based on edge computing and deep learning
abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and edge computing has increased the demand for accurate and low-latency remote sensing image classification; however, conventional cloud-centric approaches face challenges related to processing latency, communication overhead, and efficient analysis of diverse land-cover scenes. This research proposes a remote sensing image processing method based on edge computing and deep learning (DL), integrating an Adaptive Chameleon Swarm-tuned Efficient Three-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (ACS-E3DCNN). A total of 1,997 documents published between 2000 and 2026 were retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using VOSviewer through keyword co-occurrence, overlay, and density visualizations, as well as co-authorship analysis at the author, institution, and country levels. abstract: Abstract We develop a random analog predictor (RAP) algorithm for the forecasting of Arctic sea ice extent (SIE) on seasonal timescales. This is a stochastic variant for scalar time series of the method of the analogues that only uses the historical SIE record to produce ensemble forecasts. When comparing the observations with the most representative forecast of the ensemble (as identified through the band–depth, a centrality measure for functional data) the algorithm shows negligible bias and RMSE no larger than $$0.6\cdot 10^6$$ km $$^2$$ . title: Aplicación de aprendizaje automático para el análisis de cobertura vacunal, efectos adversos y respuesta inmune postvacunación de COVID-19: revisión sistemática
abstract: Recent studies use machine learning (ML) models to analyze complex patterns in COVID-19 vaccination coverage, adverse effects, and antibody-mediated immune response. The aim of this review is to synthesize the evidence systematically on the application of ML in these three domains. This study included original studies published between 2020 and 2025 by searching MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library. title: Remediating submerged marine munitions in European seas: Stakeholder priorities, requirements, perceived risks and constraints
abstract: European coastal waters contain hundreds of thousands to millions of submerged munitions following World Wars I and II. This war legacy poses critical ecological, human health, economic, and security risks through accidental detonations and leakage of toxic substances from corroding munitions, underscoring the urgent need for remediation. We conducted a structured survey of knowledgeable stakeholders to identify their needs, constraints, and priorities for remediating submerged marine munitions. title: In the Age of AI—Are National Models and Data Sets Still Important for Stream Flow Prediction?
abstract: Abstract Accurate streamflow prediction is critical for effective water resource management, and recent advances in deep learning and multi‐basin data sets have significantly improved model skill. Global deep‐learning models, trained on thousands of catchments have demonstrated strong generalization across diverse climates and continents. However, these models rely solely on globally available meteorological inputs, potentially overlooking the value of nationally developed data sets with enhanced regional accuracy. abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of China’s promulgation of the Ecological and Environmental Code and the impending repeal of the Environmental Impact Assessment Law, the future direction of China’s EIA system requires renewed examination. Based on 2,061 EIA-related legal research articles indexed in Scopus and CNKI from 2005 to 2025, this study adopts a systematic comparative approach that integrates bibliometric analysis with normative analysis. title: Information geometry and early-warning signals for groundwater drought: diagnosis, not prediction, and implications for sustainable aquifer monitoring
abstract: Groundwater sustains water supply, baseflow and ecosystems through dry periods, so anticipating groundwater drought would strengthen sustainable aquifer management; whether such advance warning is attainable from monitoring records, however, remains unresolved. This study tests, against explicit null models, whether three families of indicators can predict major droughts from groundwater levels alone, using 106 boreholes across Great Britain and complete hydrological years from 1953 to 2025. title: Improving SST Prediction Accuracy of Ina-Flows Model in Karimun Jawa and Bira
abstract: Sea surface temperature (SST) is an important parameter in ocean-atmosphere interaction, but BMKG Ina-Flows model outputs may still contain systematic bias. This study evaluates the accuracy of Ina-Flows SST predictions and improves their performance through machine learning-based bias correction at MAWS Karimun Jawa and Bira. The dataset consists of Ina-Flows SST outputs and MAWS observations from 1 December 2023 to 7 December 2024. abstract: Marine wharves, consisting of concrete or steel decks supported by pile foundations, operate in harsh marine environments involving waves, vessel impacts, and corrosive seawater. Even minor cracks or early-stage corrosion in piles can lead to sudden structural failure. Early detection is therefore essential. title: Predicting petrol prices in Zambia using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence under a regulated cost-plus pricing framework
abstract: Abstract Fuel price volatility presents significant economic and policy challenges in import-dependent economies such as Zambia. This study implements and compares four machine learning models: Ridge Linear Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression and Long Short-Term Memory, using the MAE, RMSE, R² and DM statistic as the performance evaluation metrics. title: Towards plastic property extraction from shallow indentation data
abstract: While high-throughput synthesis techniques enable rapid exploration of materials, the typical micrometer-scales make mechanical property evaluation challenging. Nanoindentation is a viable tool at this scale, however, it only provides hardness and modulus. This work, the second in a three-part study, focuses on extracting plasticity parameters from shallow spherical indentation using machine learning. abstract: Cranioplasty implants must provide mechanical protection while remaining lightweight and promoting biological integration. This study investigates bio-inspired lattice-based cranial implants incorporating four topologies: body-centred cubic (BCC), cubic, honeycomb and re-entrant. Finite element analysis (FEA) evaluated the quasi-static compressive behaviour of patient-independent cranial implant models made from polyetheretherketone (PEEK) and titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V). title: Abundance, distribution, and origins of hawksbill sea turtles on the nearshore Atlantic reefs of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
abstract: Hawksbill sea turtles (Eretmochelys imbricata) representing multiple regional stocks are known to reside in SE Florida, and play an important functional role in the health of coral reef ecosystems. title: Smart Port Technologies: A Scoping Review
abstract: The maritime industry is undergoing a profound digital transformation, with smart ports emerging as critical nodes in global supply chains. This comprehensive literature review synthesizes current research on key enabling technologies for smart ports, including Digital Twins, Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), Computer Vision, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), automation systems, and cybersecurity frameworks. title: Integrating fatty acid signatures through machine learning for traceability and nutritional profiling of wild and farmed gilthead sea bream (Sparus aurata)
abstract: Fatty acid composition of seafood can provide insights into its nutritional value and tools for traceability analysis. In this study, the fillet fatty acid compositions of wild-caught gilthead sea bream and specimens produced under cage-reared and pond-reared aquaculture regimes in Northeast Atlantic waters were evaluated to (i) assess nutritional quality using lipid quality indices and (ii) test the traceability discrimination potential of fatty acids using machine-learning classification (Random Forest) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis. Ram.exe Has Entered the Chat: Synthetic Gods and the Rise of AI-Deity Agitprop in India
abstract: Abstract This article examines ‘theogonetic agitprop’: the use of divine avatars in India generated by artificial intelligence ( AI ) to fuse devotional affect with Hindutva political communication. Focusing on deepfake Ram and Ram Lalla videos, Krishna-style chatbots, violent goddess memes, and related social media reactions, it shows that generative tools make sacred figures programmable, iterable, and persuasive across WhatsApp, X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, and Telegram. title: A model for “AI”-relevant vulnerability
abstract: Abstract The recent growth in discussions of “artificial intelligence” has been accompanied by a proportional growth in the discussion of vulnerability of and to “artificial intelligence”. Meanwhile, the concept of vulnerability has not seen any deeper analysis adequate to capture all of the newly discussed phenomena. Popular conceptions of vulnerability either lack the necessary normative force to make it morally relevant, or they are limited to vulnerability to harms, which would exclude a range of entities that we would ordinarily consider to be vulnerable. abstract: Introduction: Modern artificial intelligence (AI) emerges from the convergence of computing, statistics, and data availability. This article examines the water consumption associated with its expansion and its ecological and ethical implications. Methods: A critical reflection on the water demands of data centers draws on illustrative Chilean cases. Results: The cases illustrate the pressures that AI infrastructure places on water resources in the territories where it operates. title: El derecho de autor en obras generadas con inteligencia artificial: análisis de la jurisprudencia china
abstract: The expansion of artificial intelligence has posed new challenges for copyright law, particularly regarding the protection of content produced through such systems. This article examines Chinese case law on works generated with artificial intelligence based on six cases concerning images and documents created using technological tools. title: Spatio-temporal prediction of significant wave heights in the South China Sea using a Wind-GeoDiff deep learning framework
abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (SWH) is important for improving the simulation of the ocean mixed layer, sea surface temperature, and the atmospheric boundary layer. It also has significant implications for marine engineering applications and navigation safety. In this study, we propose Wind-GeoDiff, a two-stage deep learning framework that combines an improved 3D-Geoformer and an Elucidated Diffusion Model (EDM)-based conditional diffusion module guided by forecast wind fields, for predicting the evolution of SWH in the South China Sea and adjacent waters up to 72 h ahead. abstract: This article examines the central claim of the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas (2026), namely that artificial intelligence is fundamentally different from human intelligence and that, therefore, the human person requires special protection. Drawing on epistemology, philosophy of mind, and Kantian thought, the author argues that contemporary AI systems are marked by two fundamental limitations: they lack understanding and experience. title: A Review of Reverse Electrodialysis Process Simulation Approaches Applied to Concentrated Brines
abstract: Reverse electrodialysis (RED) is an emerging process intensification technology for sustainable energy generation from the salinity gradient between concentrated brines and dilute streams. Concentrated brines, generated in large volumes by seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination, mining operations, and saltworks, represent an abundant and underutilised resource whose energetic valorisation via RED can simultaneously reduce brine disposal impacts and contribute to decarbonising the water-energy nexus. abstract: Fine-scale ocean dynamics strongly influence coastal mixing, sediment transport, and vertical exchange, yet remain difficult to observe at the spatial scales at which they occur. Here, we use total surface current vectors measured by the airborne Ocean Surface Current Airborne Radar (OSCAR) to investigate sub-kilometer divergence, vorticity, shear rate, and vertical velocities in the tidally dominated Iroise Sea around Ushant Island. abstract: Image-based visual assessment provides a practical approach for documenting coral health signs in coastal systems where laboratory diagnosis is not available. This study applied a quadrat-based Underwater Photo Transect (UPT) method combined with Regions of Interest (ROI)-based ImageJ annotation to identify visually observable coral health signs, rather than laboratory-confirmed coral diseases, in the thermal-discharge coastal waters surrounding the Paiton Power Plant (PLTU Paiton), East Java, Indonesia. title: Rabbit production research in Southeast Asia: a bibliometric and systematic mapping review
abstract: Rabbit production remains relatively small, but has significant potential as a sustainable livestock in Southeast Asia. Despite a growing body of literature on it, there has been a lack of comprehensive analysis to synthesize these studies within the regional context. This study, therefore, addressed that gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis and a systematic mapping of rabbit production research in Southeast Asia using a specific search string. abstract: Reliable energy access remains a significant concern in rural Southeast Asia, particularly in off-grid communities marked by insufficient infrastructure, challenging geographic conditions, and limited technical expertise. Although renewable-energy microgrids, such as solar, biomass, hybrid photovoltaic-battery systems, and small hydropower, are increasingly deployed to reduce electrification gaps, inadequate maintenance strategies threaten the long-term reliability and sustainability of these systems. abstract: Background: Drought is one of the most complex and damaging hydroclimatic hazards, particularly in West Africa where water resources are highly sensitive to climate variability and change. This study analyzes the future evolution of meteorological, climatic, and hydrological droughts in the Gambia River basin controlled at the Kédougou gauging station in southeastern Senegal. abstract: Abstract Despite recent progress in quantifying anthropogenic carbon (C anth ) in global oceans, coastal regions remain understudied due to methodological and observational challenges. Here, we develop and generalize a Regional rEgression–based Coastal Anthropogenic carbon estimation algorithm (RECA) designed specifically for coastal environments. title: From ice hazards to system failures: analysis and prevention of catastrophic icebreaker escort accidents on the Northern Sea Route
abstract: The study examines catastrophic safety incidents in icebreaker escort operations on the Northern Sea Route (NSR). It develops strategies to prevent future accidents by analysing the Baikal–Vladivostok accident in the Yenisey Gulf of the Kara Sea in 2024 as a case study using the Swiss Cheese Model (SCM). The SCM-based analysis organised the documented factors associated with the Baikal–Vladivostok accident into multiple safety layers, including escort planning, safe-distance management, communication, operational coordination, and environmental conditions. title: Magnífica Humanitas: una lectura desde el humanismo y la ética ambiental
abstract: This article offers a reading of Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical Magnifica Humanitas (2026) from the standpoint of environmental ethics and Latin American humanism. Through a hermeneutic documentary analysis, it examines the tensions between the technocratic paradigm and integral human development, the material and social costs of artificial intelligence (energy, water, rare-earth mining, microwork) and their relation to Costa Rica’s energy vulnerability amid El Niño. title: Detection of Marine Litter on Arctic Beaches Based on Aerial Photography Using the YOLOv8s CNN
abstract: Marine litter beach accumulation is a pressing issue not only for urban coastal areas but also for remote and uninhabited regions such as the Arctic. Existing manual litter collection and identification methods remain labor-intensive. An assessment of the volume and composition of marine litter was conducted for the Russian Arctic coastlines using high-resolution airphotos. title: Vibrio alginolyticus: an emerging marine pathogen at the intersection of aquaculture, public health, and antimicrobial resistance
abstract: Vibrio alginolyticus is a halophilic, Gram-negative marine bacterium that has emerged as a significant opportunistic pathogen affecting both marine animals and humans. As one of the most abundant vibrios in coastal and estuarine environments worldwide, V. alginolyticus causes substantial economic losses in aquaculture through vibriosis in fish, shrimp, and shellfish, while also being responsible for wound infections, otitis externa, and occasionally gastroenteritis in humans following seawater exposure or seafood consumption. title: FishMonitorAI: An Efficient and Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Underwater Fish Detection in Resource-Constrained Environments
abstract: Accurate and efficient fish detection in underwater environments is fundamental to the advancement of automated aquaculture monitoring and selective fishing systems. However, the deployment of existing object detection models in such environments remains challenging due to wavelength-dependent light absorption, suspended-particle scattering, low contrast, and biological occlusion caused by schooling behavior, all of which are further compounded by the substantial computational overhead of conventional architectures. To address these limitations, this paper proposes FishMonitorAI, a lightweight

title: Interpretable machine learning for predicting cumulative plastic strain of marine soils under multi-factor coupling effects
abstract: Accurate prediction of cumulative plastic strain (CPS) is essential for assessing the deformation stability of marine strata subjected to artificial ground freezing (AGF). This study aims to clarify how variations in clay content and pore-water salinity regulate cyclic responses after freeze–thaw (FT) disturbance. Cyclic triaxial tests were conducted to investigate CPS under coupled effects of clay content, salinity, FT disturbance, and cyclic stress ratio (CSR). title: Ocean acoustic field prediction method based on dual-branch physics-informed neural network under insufficient environmental parameters
abstract: Accurate computation of the ocean acoustic pressure field is crucial for underwater acoustic applications. Traditional numerical models depend on comprehensive environmental priors, such as full-depth sound speed profiles (SSPs) and bottom geoacoustic parameters. To address challenges posed by uncertain bottom geoacoustic parameters and depth-truncated SSPs, this study presents a Dual-Branch Physics-Informed Neural Network (DB-PINN) to predict the acoustic pressure field while simultaneously reconstructing the full-depth SSP. title: Active acoustic tomography methods for underwater situational awareness and fish resource monitoring
abstract: BACKGROUND: The ocean is opaque to electromagnetic radiation, so underwater situational awareness over large areas remains a predominantly acoustic problem. Conventional underwater situational awareness means—active sonar, passive listening systems, and optical systems—offer either high resolution at short range or long range at low resolution. title: Data scarcity to strategic insight: monitoring global SDG progress using big earth data and AI
abstract: Evidence-informed sustainable development goals (SDGs) remain constrained by incomplete, geographically uneven and temporally sparse reporting. This study implements a systematic approach using 20 peer-reviewed Big Earth Data and artificial intelligence (AI)-derived datasets to address monitoring gaps across seven SDGs. By integrating multi-source geospatial datasets, AI-based methods, and established validation procedures, we assess regional imbalance and temporal patterns of SDG progress at the global scale. abstract: Nutrients play a fundamental role in plant growth, soil fertility, and overall agricultural productivity. However, inefficient fertilizer application in conventional farming systems often leads to nutrient imbalance, reduced soil quality, and increased environmental degradation. The emergence of precision agriculture and artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced new opportunities for improving nutrient management through data-driven decision-making. title: Estimation of the Pitzer Parameters for 1-1, 2-1, 1-2, 3-1, and 1-3 Single Electrolytes at 25 °C
abstract: Abstract The Pitzer model is widely used in process models for determining the thermodynamic properties of concentrated aqueous electrolytes. The main drawback is the need for experimentally determined parameters for each ion pair in the system. The estimation of unknown Pitzer parameters of electrolytes is thus an attractive prospect. This paper investigates machine learning-based models for the task of predicting the Pitzer parameters of binary electrolytes based on the properties of the constituent ions. title: A practical approach to underwater depth and surface normals estimation
abstract: Monocular Depth and Surface Normals Estimation (MDSNE) is crucial for tasks such as three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction, autonomous navigation, and underwater exploration. Current methods rely either on discriminative models, which struggle with transparent or reflective surfaces, or generative models, which, while accurate, are computationally expensive. title: INVESTIGACIÓN VIVA
abstract: Living Research: Understanding Experience to Transform Reality introduces an original methodological and interpretive framework within contemporary qualitative research that integrates phenomenology and action research. The work posits that scientific inquiry is not complete merely by understanding a phenomenon, but when the constructed knowledge returns to its context to enable transformative and reflective action. title: Solving the inverse problem in baseball trajectory
abstract: Inferring the release conditions required to produce a desired baseball trajectory is an ill-posed inverse problem because different combinations of release velocity, spin rate, spin efficiency, spin axis, and release direction can generate similar ball flights. We trained multilayer perceptron (MLP), convolutional neural network (CNN), and gated recurrent neural network (GRU-RNN) models on MLB Statcast data from the 2022–2024 seasons to infer plausible release conditions from scalar, complete-trajectory, and partial-trajectory information. title: Development of Artificial Intelligence Based Model to Predict Crop Yields of Biofertilizers
abstract: The research paper proposes the development and the analysis of an artificial intelligence model that can be used for predicting the crop yield under various biofertilizer treatment, types of soils and environmental conditions. The problem statement is the necessity of the prediction of the efficiency of biofertilizers taking into account the interaction of microbial strains, soil properties, inoculation rate, nutrients, crops, and climatic zones. title: Quantitative ultrasonic inversion of coating bond strength based on a physics-informed neural network
abstract: Abstract The nondestructive quantitative evaluation of the bond strength of metal coatings on marine equipment is crucial for ensuring their safe service. However, due to the inherent high acoustic attenuation of metal coatings and the limited number of destructive pull-off test samples, traditional ultrasonic techniques and purely data-driven deep learning models find it difficult to balance physical interpretability and high-fidelity prediction. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel quantitative characterization method that integrates wideband pulse compression surface waves

title: Review of Applications, Technologies and Future Trends of Maritime UAV Systems for Smart Ocean Operations
abstract: Maritime unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly transforming ocean, coastal, port, and offshore operations through rapid sensing, intelligent communication, autonomous perception, and cooperative decision support. This trend-oriented review analyses 471 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and March 2026, supported by selected foundational pre-2020 studies, to examine the evolution, technological structure, methodological maturity, and deployment readiness of maritime UAV systems. The bibliometric analysis shows rapid publication growth, from 22 papers in 2020 to 160

title: Seeing what students learn: assessing cognitive representations and academic outcomes via EEG image reconstruction
abstract: Abstract Understanding how humans process visual information during learning remains a central challenge in cognitive neuroscience. Traditional approaches typically rely on behavioral observations or indirect neural measures, which limits direct insight into learners’ internal cognitive representations. Recent advances in brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) and deep learning have enabled image reconstruction from electroencephalography (EEG), providing a promising pathway to decode latent cognitive states. journal: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

title: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in schizophrenia: enhancing transparency in clinical decision-making
abstract: Schizophrenia is a chronic and severe psychiatric disorder affecting nearly 1% of the global population, characterized by positive symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions, negative symptoms including avolition and affective flattening, and cognitive impairments that compromise social and occupational functioning. title: A Prompt Elastogravity Signal–Based Rapid Source Characterization Module for Tsunami Warning Support in Alaska
abstract: Abstract State-of-the-art earthquake early warning systems relying on seismic waves tend to underestimate the magnitude of large earthquakes, which typically results in dramatic underestimation of tsunami forecasts. Systems relying on other types of data (W phase, Global Navigation Satellite System) may provide more reliable magnitude estimates for very large seismic events but at the cost of slower warning. title: Bouncing Forward: A Company’s Three-Phase Playbook For True Resilience
abstract: Is your organisation’s approach to disruption one of ‘bounce back’ or ‘bounce forward’? When faced with an external disruption, most organisations try to absorb it and rebound to their previous state. While this ‘bounce back’ is an effective strategy for managing short-term disruptions, is there a better approach for responding to long-term disruptions such as rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) or climate change? title: The CKM–GDM multi-organ precision model: reframing gestational diabetes as an early cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic event in Southeast Asia
abstract: Background Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is amongst the commonest complications of pregnancy and an early marker of lifetime cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) risk. Its burden is heavy in Southeast Asia, where prevalence ranges from about 8% to nearly 30% and a lean phenotype — with marked over-representation of the insulin-secretion-limited subtype — diverges from Western cohorts, yet its definition, timing, and treatment remain contested. title: A LITERATURE REVIEW OF RADIAL BASIS FUNCTION NEURAL NETWORKS FOR BLAST EXPLOSIVE PREDICTION
abstract: This review paper examines the development and application of Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBFNN) for predicting blast explosive effects. Addressing the complexities of nonlinear and multi-physics blast phenomena, it highlights the advantages of data-driven approaches over traditional analytical methods. The paper presents the fundamentals of RBF networks, including their architecture, training techniques, and optimization strategies, emphasizing their capacity for universal function approximation and adaptability. title: Stress corrosion cracking of 316 L stainless steel in simulated Arabian gulf seawater
abstract: Abstract Austenitic stainless steels are widely used in coastal and marine infrastructure for its corrosion resistance, yet failures associated with chloride-induced stress corrosion cracking (SCC) continue to be reported. In this work, the SCC susceptibility of 316L austenitic stainless steel was investigated using test solutions designed to simulate Arabian gulf seawater and compared with a reference standard brine. title: Taxonomy‐Independent eDNA Approaches in Groundwaters: A Prospective Tool for Improved Ecological Assessments
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater continues to be managed predominantly as an abiotic resource for human use, a paradigm that overlooks the biological communities responsible for many indispensable ecosystem services and ultimately the integrity of the global water cycle. A shift towards a holistic ecological perspective is therefore essential but requires innovative techniques to monitor a challenging environment. title: AI-Enabled Climate–Water Governance Linking Aquaculture and Irrigation in The Mekong Delta, Vietnam
abstract: The paper investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance integrated water governance and climate resilience in water-dependent production systems, specifically focusing on aquaculture and irrigation in the Mekong Delta, Vietnam. It addresses a gap in existing literature by integrating technical applications of AI with institutional analyses of water management and climate adaptation. journal: International Journal of Sustainability and Risk Control

title: An interpretable SCA-ANN framework for WTI crude oil price forecasting
abstract: Abstract The recent conflict in the Strait of Hormuz as a critical oil transmit checkpoint combined with the market's inherent instability and the complex, nonlinear interactions among key influencing factors, makes accurate crude oil price forecasting a formidable challenge. Conventional statistical methods often struggle to capture these dynamics, underscoring the need for innovative, data-driven approaches. title: From Necropsy to Molecular Diagnosis: A Review of Evolving Techniques in Veterinary Pathology
abstract: Veterinary pathology has undergone a profound and accelerating transformation, evolving from the purely observational discipline of gross necropsy into a sophisticated, multi-tiered diagnostic science that integrates histopathology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based molecular assays, next-generation sequencing (NGS), and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted digital pathology. title: At the Speed of Light: Can Fleeting Human Leadership Confront Climate Change, Alone?
abstract: Climate change and artificial intelligence (AI) are now accelerating faster than even exceptional human minds were built to manage. This perspective article argues that the deeper risk lies not in technology alone but in the recurring frailty of human leadership during global crises, from the dot-com bust of 2000 to the banking recession of 2008 and the pandemic of 2020. journal: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies

title: Toward interoperable bathymetric data in ocean observing systems: integrating hydrographic standards and FAIR data practices
abstract: Bathymetric data are a fundamental component of ocean observing systems, supporting applications in ocean modelling, coastal hazard assessment, marine spatial planning, and navigational safety. However, these datasets remain highly fragmented due to the diversity of acquisition platforms, including hydrographic surveys, autonomous vehicles, satellite-derived bathymetry, and legacy chart products, which often differ in spatial reference systems, vertical datums, resolution scales, and metadata quality. This heterogeneity creates persistent barriers to interoperability, limiting data integration

title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for sustainable development and policy integration in the shipping industry
abstract: Shipping is a critical industry for global trade but is associated with environmental externalities like air, underwater noise, and light pollution. Transitioning to a sustainable future requires optimizing propulsion systems, which currently suffer from fossil fuel reliance and energy losses. This research develops an AI-assisted evidence-synthesis framework to examine sustainable shipping and propulsion technologies and support a policy framework for a sustainable maritime agenda. title: Postsecularidad y tecnociencia: la redistribución narrativa de la trascendencia en la ciencia ficción contemporánea en español
abstract: This article proposes a reinterpretation of contemporary Spanish science fiction through the lens of postsecularity, understood not as a return of religion but as its functional redistribution within technoscientific dispositifs. Against dominant readings that frame the genre as inherently secularizing, it argues that works such as Jorge Carrión’s Membrana and Elia Barceló’s El efecto Frankenstein reconfigure traditionally religious functions—memory, creation, and identity—within narrative structures mediated by technology. title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF ELECTRICAL TRANSMISSION INFRASTRUCTURE THROUGH SMART GRID TECHNOLOGIES: A SAUDI VISION 2030 PERSPECTIVE
abstract: Electricity transmission networks are changing from being based on individual assets to becoming systems that can be observed digitally, are driven by data and are becoming more adaptive. This shift is particularly important for Saudi Arabia, since the rapid expansion of renewable energy, the great distances across the country, the emergence of new industrial loads and the aims set out in Vision 2030 all mean that the transmission system has to handle greater variability without compromising reliability. title: Comparative evaluation of cycle-based and time history-based intelligent models for predicting the cyclic responses of liquefiable sand: Strengths, limitations, and prospects for advancement
abstract: In this study, an attempt is made to develop deep learning (DL) models using only cyclic laboratory test databases of Ottawa F65 sand to showcase its potential for predicting the cyclic response of soils. Two types of DL-based modelling strategies are proposed herein: (i) cycle-based models and (ii) time history-based models. The DL model, such as long short-term memory (LSTM) network, is considered for predicting the cyclic responses and dynamic soil properties. title: Ancient oysters provide far-field sea-level constraints on ice melt timing and sources during the early–mid Holocene climate transition
abstract: Holocene relative sea-level (RSL) reconstructions from far-field regions constrain past ice volume and global mean sea-level change, yet records from the South China Sea remain debated, particularly regarding the existence of a mid-Holocene highstand. Here, we present a revised RSL history for the Pearl River Delta based on six new radiocarbon-dated index points from an ancient Saccostrea cuccullata oyster reef, integrated into an updated, quality-controlled database of 292 data points. title: Post-Flood Ecosystem Recovery and Policy Zoning in the Chi River Basin, Thailand
abstract: Understanding ecosystem recovery following flood events is critical for sustainable floodplain management, yet causal evidence linking flooding to vegetation recovery remains limited. This study investigated the causal impact of the 2022 flood on ecosystem recovery in the Chi River Basin, Thailand, using 232,172 spatial points with multi-temporal VCI data (2020–2024). We employed Propensity Score Matching (PSM) to control for confounding factors and Difference-in-Differences (DiD) to estimate the causal effect. title: Spatial modeling of soil salinity in hyperarid agroecosystems of northern Peru using a hybrid machine learning ensemble
abstract: Soil salinization poses a critical threat to agricultural sustainability in arid agroecosystems, limiting food security and economic stability. On the northern coast of Peru, the synergy between inefficient water management and extreme climate variability has accelerated soil degradation, demanding precise spatial monitoring tools. This study proposes a Hybrid Smart Ensemble model to map soil electrical conductivity (EC), integrating optical data (Sentinel-2), dual-polarization SAR texture (Sentinel-1), and thermal imagery (Landsat-9 LST). title: Bioinspired Poisson‑actuated gating enabled high-sensitivity and stretchable multidirectional strain sensing
abstract: Abstract Decoupling strain magnitude and arbitrary orientation is a persistent challenge for wearable strain sensors, as conventional layered architectures and monolithic anisotropic networks suffer from issues of interfacial stress concentrations and irreversible signal drift under complex deformations. Inspired by the mechanogating mechanism of tactile sensory cells, we present a fluidic strain sensor with an orthogonal cross-shaped microchannel network and drum-shaped microstructures. title: Recurrent implantation failure: a registry-corroborated, age-stratified definition and pragmatic five-tiered management algorithm
abstract: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remains a significant challenge in reproductive medicine, imposing substantial emotional, clinical, and financial burden on affected couples. RIF is generally defined as failure to achieve pregnancy after multiple transfers of good-quality embryos, yet progress in the field has been constrained by the absence of a universally accepted definition and by the inherent complexity of investigating the embryo–endometrial interface. title: Deep Learning-Based Monitoring of Tension and Fatigue in a Hybrid Mooring System of a Floating Offshore Wind Turbine
abstract: Mooring integrity monitoring of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) is constrained by the cost and limited reliability of subsea tension sensors. This study develops a deep learning framework that predicts the dynamic tension of a hybrid polyester–chain mooring system for a 15 MW semi-submersible FOWT from the platform six-degree-of-freedom motion alone. title: The one-Layer Antarctic model for Dynamical Downscaling of Ice–ocean Exchanges (LADDIE) version 2.0
abstract: Projections of Antarctic mass loss and its contribution to sea-level rise are highly sensitive to the applied ocean-driven melting. As fully coupled continental-scale ocean–ice sheet models are scarce, ice sheet models are typically run in standalone configurations, forced with parameterised sub-shelf melting. To provide a physically more detailed alternative to melt parameterisations, we here present version 2.0 of the one-Layer Antarctic model for Dynamical Downscaling of Ice–ocean Exchanges (LADDIE). title: Polyphonic Aesthetics: Towards a Technopoetry and Sound Poetry Within Expanded Art
abstract: This study explores the polyphonic diversity of technopoetry and sound poetry, tracing their evolution within the expanded field of contemporary art. The 20th century was notably characterized by avant-garde movements—such as Dadaism, Surrealism, Russian Constructivism, Situationism, and Futurism—that influenced the poetic techno-scene. Some notable movements include Fluxus, the happening, and post-punk. title: Machine Learning-Based Discrimination of Pre- and Post-Cleaning Marine Turbocharger Recordings Using Rotational-Speed Signals
abstract: Monitoring marine turbocharger condition under real-ship operation is complicated by operating-condition variability and limited labelled maintenance data. This study assesses whether mean-centred angle-domain rotational-speed fluctuations can discriminate between six recordings acquired before and after one turbocharger cleaning event. The primary evaluation used exhaustive paired complete-record holdout, where one pre-cleaning and one post-cleaning recording are excluded from preprocessing, feature ranking, and model fitting in each split. title: Advances in modelling and optimization of hydrothermal liquefaction for sustainable biofuel production: A review
abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction offers a direct approach to utilizing biomass resources and converting them into biofuel by using water, which acts as a reactant, solvent and catalyst under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions. Hydrothermal liquefaction has been extensively studied to comprehend its mechanisms and kinetics across various batch operation scales. Recent efforts have focused on developing mathematical models for different feedstocks to predict product yields, despite the complexity of the reaction mechanisms and pathways involved. abstract: • Solver-free EO–ML generates 30 m design-event flood-depth and hazard maps. • XGBoost and SHAP reveal strong but basin-specific depth relationships. • Fold ensembles show stable depths, with uncertainty concentrated near boundaries. • Weak-line/WSE-PF screening finds local changes but modest basin-scale effects. • FOEN and ADR7 provide complementary probability–intensity hazard screening. abstract: In this article, we set out what we suggest are three key challenges for critical studies on men, masculinities and organizations in the context of the polycrisis. We first provide an overview some of the major contributions over recent decades of Feminist Studies on Organizations, Critical Studies on Men and Masculinities, Critical Management Studies, Critical Leadership Studies, and Critical Studies on Men, Masculinities and Organizations. title: Quantifying Land–Sea Connectivity Through Remotely Sensed River Plumes
abstract: Abstract Coastal ecosystems are highly influenced by riverine freshwater inputs, but the nature of these influences is dynamic and hard to characterize. Here we present a method that leverages remote sensing data of river plumes to quantify land–sea connectivity. The method uses least‐cost routing across image‐derived cost surfaces, where connected paths have a directional water quality gradient characteristic of a fluvial plume. title: The Plant‐Microbe Alliance for Environmental Restoration: From Nature‐Inspired Solutions to Engineered Ecological Recovery
abstract: According to the United Nations, up to 40% of the world's terrestrial ecosystems are degraded and in need of ecological restoration. Here, we argue that ecosystem restoration requires not only the reintroduction of plant species but also the recovery of the biological interactions that sustain ecosystem functioning. Plants and their associated microbiomes form integrated functional units in which microorganisms contribute to nutrient cycling, stress tolerance, contaminant degradation and ecosystem resilience. title: Emergence of OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST5994, a sister lineage of the high-risk ST307 clone
abstract: Introduction Carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (CP-KP) represents a major public health threat. The global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance is largely driven by high-risk clones (HRCs), such as ST307/OXA-48, ST11/OXA-48 and ST512/KPC-3, which currently dominate the epidemiology of CP-KP in Spain. This study aimed to describe the emergence, dissemination and genomic evolution of an OXA-48-producing K. pneumoniae ST5994 clone in Cantabria, Spain, and to characterize its genomic, phenotypic and epidemiological features. title: Interpretable Machine Learning for NOx Emission Anomaly Detection in Marine Diesel Engines Using Real Operational Data
abstract: Nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions from marine diesel engines remain a major environmental concern in the maritime industry, requiring effective monitoring strategies under actual operating conditions. abstract: Salt marshes are crucial coastal ecosystems that support biodiversity and provide a range of ecosystem services, including nutrient retention, shoreline erosion protection, and carbon storage, through the processes they maintain. However, their dynamic nature, combined with human pressures, has led to their rapid decline, making ongoing monitoring essential. abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a new method which, over the past few years, due to the development of the deep learning technology, has demonstrated significant potential in solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). abstract: Abstract The Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a significant vector-borne threat; however, few models successfully integrate rigorous theoretical guarantees with efficient, reliable predictive tools. abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping hydrogeological modeling. abstract: Accurate shoreline delineation is critical for converting satellite imagery into reservoir bathymetry and storage products, yet its downstream consequences remain poorly quantified. We benchmarked spectral indices, Scene Classification Layer (SCL)-based baselines, pixel-wise machine learning, U-Net, transformer models, and SAM 2 AutoPrompt workflows using Sentinel-2 imagery from five reservoirs in central Mexico. title: A Caribbean bright spot coral reef exceeds thermal limits during the fourth global coral bleaching event
abstract: Marine heatwaves are increasing in both frequency and intensity, exposing coral reefs to prolonged periods of thermal stress and driving recurrent mass coral bleaching. Nevertheless, coral decline remains heterogeneous, with some reefs maintaining unexpectedly high coral cover despite exposure to thermal and other environmental disturbances. This study analysed benthic community change across Banco Capiro in Tela Bay and the south-side reefs of Utila, Honduras, from 2013 to 2025, spanning the 3rd and 4th Global Coral Bleaching Events. title: GIS-based Deep Learning for Identifying and Characterizing Small Community Lagoon Wastewater Treatment Systems
abstract: Wastewater lagoon systems remain a dominant form of secondary treatment for small communities in the United States due to their low energy requirements, operational simplicity, and affordability. Despite their widespread use, national inventories of lagoon systems are fragmented, inconsistently reported, and often outdated, with non-discharging systems particularly underrepresented. These data gaps limit effective infrastructure planning, environmental assessment, and equitable allocation of resources. title: Towards comprehensive academic literacy in the age of generative artificial intelligence
abstract: This article presents a multidimensional analysis of a doctoral seminar taught at a public university in Argentina, in which the use of digital tools and Artificial Intelligence for academic text revision was encouraged. The research aimed to advance the advance the development of the analytical components required for integral academic literacy, grounded in the theoretical-methodological framework of Mediatized Educational Practices in Dynamic Intermedial Devices. abstract: Achieving equitable green growth requires substantial institutional reorganization, often committed to through formal Circular Economy (CE) and Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) transition frameworks. Despite public policy narratives highlighting grassroots sustainability and the inclusion of small enterprises, the underlying political-economic processes and structural barriers that dictate their execution remain insufficiently understood. In contrast to previous approaches to out of distribution problems, which alter the inputs and outputs of an operator, our approach alters the operator itself. title: Taxon‐specific community structure partitions marine particle size spectra into stable and dynamic components
abstract: Abstract Oceanic particle size distributions (PSDs) link plankton community structure to biogeochemical cycling. Although the influence of community composition on size spectra is well recognized in theoretical approaches, long‐term empirical evidence connecting taxon‐specific variability to bulk PSD structure remains limited. Here, we use 9 yr of taxon‐resolved PSDs spanning ~ 7–100 μ m in the surface waters of the oligotrophic North Pacific to show that deviations from canonical scaling are structured, repeatable, and attributable to variability in specific taxa. title: Multiscale pH fluctuations on a stable algal reef community (SE Sardinia, Tyrrhenian Sea)
abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is threatened by ocean acidification and warming, in combination with habitat loss, pollution, invasive species, and overexploitation. Assessing local high-frequency pH variability in the context of relevant basin-scale time series data is essential to understand ecosystem vulnerability. We report the results of the Italian national pH monitoring based on the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, and the pH dynamics observed at Capo Carbonara. abstract: This paper addresses the depth regulation of an inspection-class remotely operated vehicle whose hydrodynamic model is uncertain and whose environment applies a persistent, non-vanishing wave disturbance. A neural-network learning term added to a proportional-derivative feedback can compensate the uncertain dynamics online but, under a persistent disturbance, the classical gradient update never stops adjusting the network weights, so the weights drift without bound and eventually destabilise the loop. title: Técnicas de visión artificial aplicadas a tecnologías asistivas para personas con discapacidad visual: una revisión sistemática de la literatura
abstract: Visual impairment constitutes one of the primary barriers to social inclusion, affecting over 285 million individuals experiencing low vision or blindness, while assistive devices are frequently costly or lack accessibility. Consequently, the present study conducted a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with the main objective of identifying the most efficient artificial intelligence models in the domain of text, color, and object recognition—specifically concerning items such as fruits, banknotes, and facial expressions. title: Probabilistic corrosion prediction of marine steel under future climate change scenarios using physics-informed Gaussian process regression
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a framework of corrosion prediction by utilizing physics-informed Gaussian process regression (PI-GPR) and future climate change simulation. Long-term corrosion prediction of marine steel structures is routinely based on stationary environmental assumptions; however, future sea surface temperature (SST) changes should be taken into account as it may affect corrosion degradation over structural service life. abstract: The current study attempted to predict rainfall on a monthly basis using sequential Long short-term memory (LSTM) algorithm for four selected stations (Kohima, Mon, Phek and Wokha) of Nagaland, India. The LSTM model was built using Python, with data split 80% for training and 20% for testing. Numerous trials with varying LSTM hyperparameters were conducted to identify the best-performing model. title: A rapid-updating method for anthropogenic NO x emissions based on convolutional neural networks and TROPOMI NO₂ observations
abstract: Nitrogen oxides (NO x = NO + NO2) are air pollutants primarily emitted from anthropogenic sources, however, bottom-up anthropogenic NO x emission inventories often suffer from update delays. The TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) provides near-real-time, high-resolution NO2 column densities, offering new opportunities for timely NO x emission prediction. Given the short lifetime of NO x in the lower troposphere, local emissions can influence observations over distances of ~100 km. title: A neuroevolution-driven agent-based model of coral larvae settlement
abstract: Coral reefs face significant threats due to climate change and human activities, which require innovative approaches to study and protect these ecosystems. Successful settlement is the bottleneck linking a reef's free-swimming larvae to the benthic community, ultimately determining the next generation of corals and the long-term resilience of the entire ecosystem. This work introduces an agent-based model (ABM) driven by neuroevolution (NE) to simulate coral larval settlement behavior under various environmental conditions. title: Behavioral Patterns and Identity Expression in University Students’ Uniform-Wearing: A Quantitative Study
abstract: Despite growing scholarly interest in the sociocultural functions of student uniforms, empirical research on uniform-wearing Behavior in Southeast Asian higher education remains limited, particularly regarding the interplay between digital self-presentation and institutional dress norms. This study investigated the Behavior and motivations behind student uniform wearing at Kasetsart University, Kamphaeng Saen Campus. title: Technology integration in Southeast Asian university history education: a qualitative study
abstract: This study investigates how university history lecturers in Vietnam, the Philippines, and Indonesia perceive and integrate technology into history instruction within diverse socio-cultural and institutional contexts. The study was conducted in response to persistent challenges in history education, including lecture-dominated instruction, students’ perception of history as a memorization-based subject, and the limited pedagogical use of digital tools in humanities education. title: Social Representations of Artificial Intelligence from Basic Education Teachers in Aguascalientes
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education has evolved to integrating advanced models such as ChatGPT, and it’s therefore conceived as a complementary tool that promotes personalized learning and processes optimization, despite some ethical challenges related to access inequalities, algorithmic biases, dehumanization, and the fear of teacher replacement. abstract: Hip-fracture registries and audit systems support feedback, benchmarking, and quality improvement, but the public visibility of this infrastructure across Southeast Asia is unclear.This review mapped publicly identifiable registry readiness, audit, care quality, and secondary prevention evidence for hip-fracture care across Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries.We conducted a scoping review and public-evidence implementation gap map across the 10 ASEAN member states.Searches covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL)

title: Propagation-physics-guided channel augmentation and temporal–spectral fusion for domain-robust underwater acoustic target recognition
abstract: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) is essential for ocean-intelligence sensing, but deep learning-based models often suffer from performance degradation under ocean acoustic domain shift. This problem arises because ship-radiated noise recorded under different propagation channels, vessel operating states, background noise levels, and recording configurations may exhibit substantial distribution discrepancies. title: Comparative analysis of the applicability of artificial intelligence models for code generation
abstract: This article analyses the potential for using selected artificial intelligence models in the code generation process during the development of a web application. The analysis was conducted in the Windsurf environment using the Open Data Explorer project as a case study. These models were compared in terms of functional effectiveness, implementation efficiency, the quality of the generated code, project stability, and the types of errors that occurred during subsequent iterations. title: Exploring pre-service teachers’ STEM readiness in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand: Comparative insights from teacher education programs
abstract: STEM education has become a central agenda for enhancing human resource quality and global competitiveness. This study explored pre-service teachers’ readiness to implement STEM teaching in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, with particular attention to their conceptual understanding, implementation ability and experience, perceived barriers and institutional support, and attitudes toward STEM education. title: Challenges and innovations in machine learning-driven hate speech detection on X (formerly Twitter): A methodological and taxonomic review
abstract: Detecting hate talk on public news manifestos, particularly X (formerly Twitter), has enhanced a bigger focus on document excavating and the study of natural language processing (NLP). This systematic literature review (SLR) offers an itemized test of current approaches, machine intelligence forms, challenges, and time engaged in hate talk discovery. title: PINN-Sed: Interconnected Physics-Informed Machine Learning Model for High Resolution Suspended Sediment Transport in River Network
abstract: Abstract There is growing demand for river-network models that can estimate sediment transport at fine temporal resolution. Although coupling physically based sediment modules with hydrological and hydrodynamic models is a logical path forward, these approaches require intensive calibration and substantial computing power, limiting their practical use. title: Ecological recovery, maintenance-dependent protection: a synthesis of three nature-based solutions for coastal resilience in New Jersey
abstract: Hurricane Sandy in 2012 led to an extensive deployment of coastal nature-based solutions (NbS) in New Jersey, providing a unique opportunity to evaluate their physical and ecological performance under multi-year monitoring programs. This study presents a comparative synthesis of documented outcomes across three NbS categories implemented in New Jersey, including beach nourishment and dune restoration on the Atlantic coast, thin-layer placement (TLP) of dredged material for estuarine salt marsh restoration, and living shorelines based on constructed oyster reef systems in Delaware Bay. abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine the content validity of a scale designed to evaluate the use of artificial intelligence in university learning (EPIA-U). The instrument consists of 28 items distributed across four dimensions—Academic support, Study personalization, Satisfaction with use, and Perceived dependence—and was subjected to the judgment of nine experts with backgrounds in education, technology, and research. abstract: This study examines how Gemini, GPT, and Adobe Firefly visualize Islamic worship, sacred space, and Muslim futures. The corpus comprises 72 images generated from ten verbatim English-language prompts submitted to each platform. Every prompt-platform combination was run at least twice, yielding 24 outputs per platform. abstract: Os estudos de comunicação e mídia frequentemente analisam as dinâmicas de poder na inteligência artificial (classificatória, preditiva, generativa, agentiva, etc.). abstract: Background Varicella imposes a sustained public health burden in China, where decades of voluntary single-dose immunization have been associated with recurrent school outbreaks and an age shift toward adolescents. title: Deep learning–assisted coral morphology cover across 742 sites on the Great Barrier Reef (2022–2025): A Great Reef Census citizen science dataset
abstract: Abstract Citizen science can expand the spatial extent of coral reef surveys, but its value is often limited by inconsistent data quality and slow manual analysis. Here we combine volunteer‐collected imagery with deep learning to overcome these constraints, delivering validated coral cover data at scale. We present 46,879 benthic seascape images from 742 sites across 267 reefs on the Great Barrier Reef, collected by Great Reef Census volunteers between September 2022 and February 2025. title: Flood susceptibility in a coastal backwater floodplain: a spatially validated multi-event SAR framework for Alappuzha, India
abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping (FSM) is dominated by studies of upland catchments. At the same time, near-sea-level coastal and backwater floodplains, where inundation is shaped by reclamation, land use, tidal influence and constrained drainage rather than relief, remain comparatively under-explored. abstract: The early detection of production anomalies in petroleum wells is critical for optimizing operational efficiency, reducing downtime, and mitigating environmental risks, particularly in complex and prolific regions like the Niger Delta. This study investigates the application of both unsupervised and supervised artificial intelligence models for anomaly detection using historical well production data. title: Internal Solitary Waves in the Xisha Areas: Evidence From SWOT Observations
abstract: Abstract The Xisha Islands, situated in the northwestern South China Sea, are characterized by diverse topography conducive to a wide range of oceanic dynamic processes. Internal solitary waves (ISWs), large‐amplitude nonlinear waves in continuously‐stratified oceans, are pivotal for oceanic energy transport, vertical seawater mixing, and material exchange. title: How heterogeneous environmental regulations shape marine sustainable development: evidence from coastal China
abstract: Marine sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with environmental protection, making the design and selection of effective environmental regulatory instruments increasingly important under tightening marine ecological constraints. In this study, marine sustainable development is measured by marine green total factor productivity (MGTFP). abstract: Abstract This study investigates and enhances the Forward–Forward (FF) algorithm, a novel neural network training approach recently introduced by Geoffrey Hinton. Unlike Back-Propagation (BP), which relies on separate forward and backward passes, FF performs two forward passes, one with positive (real) data and one with negative data, potentially generated by the network itself. title: Microplastic contamination in edible invertebrate from seafood markets along the Egyptian Red Sea and Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Marine environments contain plastic debris that potentially elicits adverse effects in aquatic organisms. In Egypt, microplastic pollution has been recognized as a significant issue; however, risks associated with human consumption have not been fully elucidated. Here, we evaluated the frequency of occurrence, abundance, and distribution of microplastics (MPs) in edible marine invertebrates (mussel, shrimp, and crab) sold at markets along the Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts of Egypt. title: Eavesdropping on Whales: Hydrophones, Noise and Asymmetrical Listening in the Ocean
abstract: This article concerns the practice of using hydrophones to listen to sperm whales, a species that emits the loudest biological sounds on the planet, in an era of worsening oceanic noise pollution. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork with a whale tourism company in the Norwegian Arctic, the article describes how trained guides track sperm whales with hydrophones that work by amplifying their clicking sounds within a given range. abstract: Monitoring of oil-contaminated land is a pressing challenge for Kazakhstan. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the controls of soil organic carbon (SOC) and soil inorganic carbon (SIC) in humid mountainous landscapes is challenging because of strong topo‐climatic and land‐use heterogeneity. This study assessed SOC, SIC, soil pH and the SIC/SOC ratio across 5964 km 2 in the Eastern Black Sea region of Türkiye using 1310 topsoil samples collected at 0–30 cm depth. title: Environment-conditioned deep learning for severe convection nowcasting
abstract: Severe convection produces localized hazards that often require warnings before radar echoes fully reveal storm development. Convective initiation and the maintenance of intense convection remain challenging for radar-only nowcasting because pre-convective signals may be absent from recent radar observations, and strong echoes often decay rapidly in forecasts. title: Transboundary marine radioactive pollution under China’s ecological and environmental code: implementation gaps and directions for reform
abstract: Marine radioactive contamination can cross national boundaries, limiting the effectiveness of legal responses confined to a single jurisdiction. China has responded by progressively developing its legal framework through successive revisions to the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China and the consolidation of relevant rules in the Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China (EEC). title: Gigantes tecnológicos y poder en plataformas de inteligencia artificial: una revisión crítica
abstract: Estudios críticos, administrativos y técnicos de comunicación y de ciencias sociales suelen diagnosticar vínculos estrechos entre los gigantes tecnológicos (Big Tech) y el nuevo verano de la inteligencia artificial (IA). title: From track to impact: a review of multi-hazard typhoon forecasting and resilience
abstract: While recent advancements in tropical cyclone prediction have been extensively documented, existing review literature remains heavily fragmented into isolated academic domains, such as artificial intelligence, data assimilation, or coastal hydrodynamics. This fragmentation obscures the operational reality of disaster risk reduction. title: Performance of Two Beginner-Accessible AI Image Classifiers for Marine-Debris Identification on Beaches of the Texas Gulf Coast
abstract: Marine debris poses persistent environmental and human-health risks, while recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have expanded the accessibility of image-classification tools. This study investigated the extent to which two beginner-accessible AI image classifiers, trained by a high school student, could distinguish between oceanic debris and natural marine objects on beaches along the Gulf of Mexico coast in southern Texas. title: A review of the effectiveness of solutions to achieve the good environmental status of the marine environment
abstract: Europe’s seas are at the nexus of a “triple crisis” of biodiversity and habitat loss, climate change, and pollution, increasingly eroding the ecosystems’ resilience and capacity to provide ecosystem services. Although essential, existing European Union policies, especially the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD), proved insufficient. title: Research on Copyright Governance and Security Challenges of Training Data for Generative Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Generative AI depends on training with very large volumes of data, and the acquisition and use of that data has become a focal point for copyright infringement and for privacy and security risks. This paper examines how generative AI training data is governed and what security problems it raises. title: Physics-guided Statistical Data Fusion for Reconstructing 3D Current Fields of Oceanic Eddies
abstract: Accurate reconstruction of three-dimensional ocean current fields is critical for understanding ocean dynamics and real-time conduct of modern oceanographic field campaigns, particularly for mesoscale eddy surveys. We propose a physics-guided modeling and learning framework for multi-source data fusion to estimate the three-dimensional (3D) current structure of oceanic eddies by integrating satellite altimetry and temperature data, ocean reanalysis data, and in situ drifting buoy observations. title: Few Annotations, High Accuracy: Transfer Learning and Data Augmentation Improve Passive Acoustic Monitoring of the Vulnerable African Manatee
abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring elusive and threatened species remains a major challenge in ecology and conservation, particularly in turbid aquatic environments.
