title: Climate-driven habitat loss of Chinese sturgeon in the Northwestern Pacific and implications for marine protected area design
abstract: The conservation of endangered anadromous fishes depends on understanding their full-lifecycle habitat requirements, yet the marine phase of Chinese sturgeon ( Acipenser sinensis ) remains a critical knowledge gap despite over 90% of its lifespan occurring at sea. We integrated multi-source occurrence data (satellite tagging, bycatch records, environmental DNA, and online databases) and applied an ensemble modeling framework (Biomod2 with eleven algorithms) to predict habitat suitability across the Northwestern Pacific Ocean (100°E–150°E, 10°N–55°N). title: Cleaner peri-urban agricultural transitions under nitrogen-related water constraints: A teacher-validated evaluation of land-use alternatives in Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands
abstract: Peri-urban agriculture is increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable urban development while reducing the environmental pressures associated with land-use change and water-quality degradation. A key challenge is how to compare alternative agricultural configurations that maintain productive land use while lowering nitrogen-related environmental burdens before implementation. This study develops a teacher-validated framework for evaluating cleaner peri-urban agricultural land-use alternatives, using Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands, as a living-lab case. title: Redes neuronales artificiales en psiquiatría. Generalidades y aplicaciones
abstract: Desde sus primeros tiempos, la inteligencia artificial ha encontrado un campo fértil de aplicación en el dominio médico; quizá por la forma en que se modelan y abordan eventos, y por la apertura del personal sanitario. Lo importante es que ha ayudado a resolver de manera práctica problemas de interés; según la época, se han aplicado algoritmos de tendencia. El objetivo del presente artículo es describir de manera sintetizada la evolución de la inteligencia artificial, algunos detalles históricos, las diferencias entre aprendizaje automático y profundo, el concepto de redes neuronales y su apli

Subsea pipeline vibration and integrity: a review of sensing technologies, mitigation mechanisms, and physics-integrated learning
abstract: Subsea pipeline systems constantly face harsh marine environments, where complex fluid-structure interactions and nonlinear seabed responses cause severe mechanical vibrations threatening long-term structural integrity. Consequently, continuous real-time monitoring is vital. Traditional high-fidelity numerical models remain highly computationally expensive for remote edge devices, while purely data-driven machine learning models lack physical interpretability and struggle generalizing in dynamic underwater conditions. title: A Lagrangian Time‐Series Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Concentrations and Exploring Drivers of Atmospheric Aerosols: Model Development and Application to Cloud Condensation Nuclei in Marine Boundary Layer
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric aerosols play critical roles in climate and air quality. Accurately assessing their environmental impacts requires understanding aerosol abundance, distribution, and the key factors and processes that control them. Although machine learning is increasingly used in predicting aerosol concentrations, its application in exploring underlying processes remains limited, and existing studies often fail to capture processes occurring during preceding days that substantially shape aerosol populations. journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems

title: Artificial Intelligence, Higher Education and Research in Latin America.A Transcomplex Reading
abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly reshaped university management and scientific production. Therefore, this essay aims to reflect on AI, higher education, and research in Latin America from a transcomplex perspective. Through a hermeneutic exercise and critical analysis of specialized literature, it concludes that AI must be understood as a transcomplex, emergent, relational, multidimensional, and uncertain phenomenon, whose effects arise at the intersection of economic, historical, cultural, educational, and technological conditions. journal: Revista Venezolana de Pedagogía y Tecnologías Emergentes

title: Operationalizing the Precautionary Approach in Marine Pollution Control: A Machine Learning Framework to Examine Score Sensitivity in Potentially Polluting Shipwreck Risk Assessment
abstract: Potentially Polluting Wrecks (PPWs) represent a critical global threat to marine ecosystems, requiring proactive risk management aligned with the Precautionary Approach of international environmental law. However, standard multi-criteria risk assessment frameworks frequently suffer from sensitivity to criterion weights, where maximum point allocations determine the relative contributions of criteria to final risk scores. journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

title: MACHINE LEARNING-AIDED GROUNDWATER LEVEL AND CO2 EMISSION ESTIMATIONS IN INDONESIAN TROPICAL PEATLAND
abstract: ABSTRACT Tropical peatlands store a large fraction of global soil carbon and emit large amounts of CO 2 from peat decomposition and root respiration. Accurate quantification of peatland carbon emissions requires a prediction that is sensitive to environmental gradients. This study estimated biweekly total and heterotrophic peat CO 2 emissions (Rs and Rh, respectively) in the peatland hydrological unit (PHU), which represents the whole peatland ecosystem on Rupat Island, Indonesia. title: Automatic grading of HER2 immunohistochemical whole-slide images based on a multi-scale hierarchical graph neural network
abstract: Objective The HER2 immunohistochemical (IHC) score of breast cancer is a critical precursor for determining eligibility for anti-HER2 targeted therapy, as the final HER2 status (positive/negative/low) is determined by IHC results combined with FISH confirmation for equivocal 2 + cases according to ASCO/CAP guidelines. However, most existing artificial intelligence methods separate the detection of invasive cancer regions from HER2 grading and fail to adequately model the spatial heterogeneity of whole-slide tumors. title: Digital economy, green innovation, and high-quality development of the marine economy: evidence from China’s coastal regions
abstract: This study examines the association between the digital economy and high-quality marine economic development using panel data for 11 coastal provincial-level regions in China from 2014 to 2023. Composite indices of digital economy development (DIG) and high-quality marine economic development (MEHD) are constructed, and two-way fixed-effects and panel threshold models are used to examine the overall association and its variation across development conditions. The MEHD index captures selected dimensions of marine economic development and is narrower in scope than a sustainable blue economy. The
institutions: Guangxi University of Finance and Economics

title: Advancing data integration in marine citizen science: insights from a collaborative workshop
abstract: The ocean remains critically under-observed, particularly in coastal zones where traditional monitoring is limited by cost, logistical constraints, and competing regulatory priorities. Marine citizen science offers an emerging and powerful complementary approach to addressing these gaps; however, data management challenges currently limit its full integration into scientific and policy data infrastructures. The inaugural workshop of the Marine Citizen Science Data Network (MCSDN), held in February 2026 in Ostend, Belgium, brought together approximately 200 participants from over 30 countries.

title: Machine Learning–based Earthquake Probability Prediction for Istanbul Province
abstract: Earthquakes represent one of the most destructive natural hazards, causing severe social and economic losses, particularly in tectonically active regions. In this context, estimating the short-term probability of earthquake occurrence is of critical importance for disaster preparedness and risk mitigation. This study focuses on Istanbul province, located along the North Anatolian Fault Zone in the Marmara Region, which is considered one of the most seismically active areas in Türkiye. journal: International Journal of New Findings in Engineering Science and Technology

title: Remotely sensed vegetation resilience in the four major estuarine ecosystems of eastern China
abstract: Introduction Estuarine wetlands are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth, but they have been experiencing severe degradation induced by human activities and climate change worldwide. Traditional assessments of degradation mostly rely on static indicators, which are insufficient to reflect dynamical ecosystem properties such as systemic resilience. title: A CNN-ConvLSTM Deep Learning Model with Axial Attention for Radar Reflectivity-based Precipitation Nowcasting in Southern Vietnam
abstract: Precipitation nowcasting plays a critical role in early hazard warning, especially for rapidly evolving convective systems. This study proposes a radar-based deep learning model that combines convolutional neural networks (CNN) for spatial feature extraction, a recurrent spatiotemporal module (ConvLSTM) for image sequences, and axial attention to capture spatiotemporal context. The experiments use reflectivity fields derived from the CAPPI radar product during the 2022 rainy season (April–October) at the Nha Be radar station. institutions: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

title: A Self‐Powered Ocean Energy Platform Enabling Green Hydrogen Production and Smart Ocean Monitoring From Irregular Wave Energy
abstract: ABSTRACT Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising for harvesting low‐frequency, stochastic ocean‐wave energy, yet their limited power output and inefficient energy utilization hinder practical marine applications. Here, we present an in‐phase dual‐layer oscillating float triboelectric nanogenerator (IDOF‐TENG) that directly converts irregular ocean‐wave energy into electricity for simultaneous green hydrogen production and smart ocean monitoring. title: Artificial intelligence cooperation and domestic absorptive capacity: evidence from ASEAN economies
abstract: Abstract Cross-border artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation is expanding, but evidence on its effect on domestic technological capability in recipient economies is scarce. Drawing on absorptive capacity theory, we create a composite AI absorptive capacity index for 10 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) economies, encompassing innovation foundations, application foundations and industrial support. institutions: Southwest University of Science and Technology

title: Optimized machine learning models for identification of autism spectrum disorder
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) relies heavily on identifying critical behavioral and clinical markers within high-dimensional datasets. However, standard feature selection methods frequently struggle with premature convergence and suboptimal feature identification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an approach based on an Improved White Shark Optimizer combined with Machine Learning classifiers (IWSO-ML). journal: International Journal of Cognitive Computing in Engineering

title: Diversity assessment of Western Indian Ocean whiprays (Himantura spp.) through a molecular species delimitation approach
abstract: Abstract The Himantura species complex consists of large demersal whiprays vulnerable to coastal fisheries, yet unresolved taxonomy within the genus hinders conservation efforts, making molecular assessments crucial for effective fishery management. This study clarified genetic relationships among Himantura species in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) using species delimitation techniques. title: Understanding Land Surface Temperature Patterns in Istanbul: The Role of Blue–Green and Built-Environment Predictors Using Explainable Machine Learning
abstract: Rapid urbanization and the replacement of vegetated surfaces by impervious materials can substantially alter urban thermal environments, while water bodies, topography, and coastal setting may further modify these patterns. Understanding how these factors contribute to land surface temperature (LST), particularly across large and geographically heterogeneous cities, is important for spatially targeted heat mitigation. title: Spatial Data Fusion and Machine Learning Bias Correction for Convection-Permitting Atmospheric Downscaling and Multi-Criteria Site Feasibility Mapping in Complex Coastal Terrains
abstract: High-resolution atmospheric modeling over topographically complex coastal zones requires multi-source spatial data fusion to bridge the scale gap between satellite-assimilated global reanalysis and localized boundary layer dynamics. This study presents a spatial data fusion framework coupling convection-permitting Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations (3 km grid spacing) with machine learning calibration and GIS multi-criteria decision analysis across continuous computational grids (24,871 cells). title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Teaching Support System for Personalized Learning in Higher Education
abstract: The aim of this study was to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence-driven teacher support system capable of translating multidimensional learning profiles into instructional and assessment recommendations for higher education. The proposal integrated five diagnostic dimensions: VARK, for preferences in accessing information; FSLSM, for processing and representation traits; ICAP, for levels of cognitive engagement; SRL, for self-regulated learning; and EBSI, for study habits. title: Nano clay mitigation of wind induced soil loss across aggregate sizes through wind tunnel experiments and explainable machine learning
abstract: This study aimed to investigate, under wind-tunnel conditions, the effects of different nano-clay application rates (0, 0.94, 1.88, and 3.75 g m⁻²) on wind-induced soil loss across different aggregate sizes (0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 mm) and wind speeds (8, 10, and 12 m s⁻¹). In addition, the study aimed to model wind-induced soil loss processes using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence methods. title: Coupled adaptive neural network control for active suspension of deep-sea mining tracked vehicles under hydrodynamic effects and multiple parametric uncertainties
abstract: Deep-sea mining tracked vehicles are subject to substantial parametric uncertainty from hydrodynamic effects, soft-seabed interaction, suspension nonlinearities, and actuator degradation. This paper proposes a coupled adaptive neural network (CANN) strategy for an 8-DOF six-wheel half-vehicle active suspension. Unlike channel-wise suspension controllers, the method reconstructs a two-dimensional body-level force-tracking error from bounce and pitch accelerations. title: Perceptions of Communication Directors Regarding the Professional Conflicts Posed by Generative Artificial Intelligence
abstract: A adoção de ferramentas de inteligência artificial generativa na comunicação corporativa está a transformar a prática profissional e a gerar novos conflitos de natureza ética, estratégica e organizacional. Este artigo explora as perceções dos diretores de comunicação relativamente a estes desafios, num contexto de mediação entre a automatização de processos, a gestão das audiências e a reputação organizacional. title: A hybrid deep learning–based OCR model for handwritten medical prescriptions
abstract: The current trend involving the use of paper-based medical prescriptions and the exchange of such by the social media is a major problem in automated and accurate text extraction in healthcare processes. This paper suggests a complete smart pipeline to digitize the images of medical prescriptions with lightweight deep learning-based classification, specialized Optical Character Recognition (OCR) engines, and comparative benchmarking of results using a large language model (LLM). title: A Multi‐Region Deep Learning Framework for Low‐Frequency Earthquake Detection: Application to the Guerrero Seismic Gap
abstract: Abstract Low‐frequency earthquakes (LFEs) provide key constraints on slow earthquake processes but remain difficult to detect because of their low signal‐to‐noise ratios (SNR) and emergent onsets, particularly in offshore environments where seismic networks are sparse. In this study, we develop a deep learning framework for LFE detection trained on a curated multi‐region data set spanning six tectonic environments. journal: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation

title: From pixels to runoff: integrating high-resolution remote sensing and deep learning for hydrologically meaningful urban land-use classification
abstract: Accurate urban land-use classification is essential for hydrological modeling, yet most studies evaluate classification schemes solely by pixel-level accuracy rather than their hydrological consequences. This study examines whether conventional classification accuracy is sufficient to identify land-use maps suitable for hydrological modeling. title: Storybooks and Wordwalls in Problem Based Learning to Improve Critical Thinking and Environmental Awareness
abstract: Exploration and reflection on problem-based learning building critical thinking. Implementation constrains problem-based learning in elementary schools, students' ability to understand problems is crucial. Media are needed to stimulate the ability to analyze real-world problems, express logical opinions, and implement solutions as critical thinking skills that foster an attitude of environmental concern. The purpose of this study was to analyze the influence of the use of storybooks and wordwall deep problem-based learning on critical thinking skills and environmental awareness simultaneously.

title: A Regional Intercomparison of Ice Sheet Mass Balance Estimates of the Northwest Greenland Ice Sheet
abstract: Abstract Changes in ice sheet mass manifest as changes in ice flow, ice thickness, and gravitational attraction. These parameters can be measured from space and used to track Greenland's contribution to sea level rise independently from each other. While an excellent level of agreement between these satellite techniques has been demonstrated at the ice sheet scale, less attention has been paid to whether this agreement is maintained at regional and local scales. institutions: Centre for Polar Observation and Modelling

title: Intelligent Surveillance System for Knife Detection Based on YOLOv8 Neural Networks
abstract: Cold weapon violence in urban environments represents a growing problem that demands innovative technological solutions for its prevention and control. This article presents the design and implementation of an intelligent surveillance system based on the YOLOv8nano architecture for real-time detection of sharp objects, specifically knives, in images and video streams. title: Recent advances in oil spill recovery technologies
abstract: Marine oil spills pose persistent threats to ecosystems and economies. This review systematically evaluates research advancements in marine oil spill recovery over the past decade, focusing on the last five years. After outlining oil spill impacts and traditional strategy evolution, the paper analyzes breakthroughs in three mainstream approaches: physical/mechanical methods (highlighting nanostructured adsorbents), chemical methods (emphasizing eco-friendly dispersants and gelling agents), and biological methods (focusing on nano-enhanced and enzymatic bioremediation). title: Heterogeneous urban decarbonization pathways revealed by typological and machine learning frameworks: A global analysis across Annex I cities
abstract: Cities are central to global climate mitigation, yet existing projections often rely on coarse-grained assessment models that overlook the interplay between urban typology and socioeconomic dynamics. Here, we harness a context-aware deep learning framework combined with typological clustering to project CO₂ emissions for 46,833 cities in Annex I countries through 2050 under Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. title: Deep learning driven smartphone system for fish disease diagnosis in Indian major carps
abstract: Abstract Fish disease poses a substantial threat to the productivity and sustainability of Indian major carps (IMCs) in aquaculture. Early and accurate fish disease detection is crucial to minimizing economic losses and ensuring fish health management. In this study, we developed a lightweight deep learning model, FishMoViT, for real-time detection of seven major IMCs diseases. It integrates two state-of-the-art deep learning networks, MobileNetV2 and MobileViT-Small, as a dual backbone, leveraging an ensemble strategy to combine complementary feature representations. title: Minería 4.0 y educación universitaria: revisión sistemática, análisis bibliométrico y marco curricular MC4 para la formación avanzada de capital humano
abstract: Este artículo presenta una revisión sistemática (PRISMA 2020) y bibliométrica de 157 documentos (Scopus/WoS) para determinar la estructura intelectual, las brechas de competencias y la arquitectura curricular en la educación universitaria. Los resultados revelan un crecimiento anual de 18.4% y un núcleo de nueve revistas Q1. El análisis conceptual identifica nueve clústeres, destacando gemelos digitales, sostenibilidad/ESG, inteligencia artificial, sistemas ciberfísicos, Educación 4.0 y reskilling. abstract: Marine engineering materials experience coupled and nonstationary environmental actions that cannot be fully reproduced by accelerated laboratory tests, making long-term field exposure necessary for reliable service-state assessment. abstract: Artificial intelligence tools are essential for effective time management. Given that many students work alongside their studies, saving and managing time effectively can significantly increase their efficiency. A total of 791 students from Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University took part in the study. Quantitative research methodology was chosen, enabling the authors to generalise the obtained results. The data were processed using the SPSS software package. title: Análise de isótopos estáveis em ciências forenses: fundamentos teóricos, aplicações e avanços.
abstract: Os isótopos estáveis constituem importantes traçadores naturais utilizados em estudos ambientais, ecológicos e forenses, pois suas variações refletem processos físicos, químicos e biológicos que ocorrem no ambiente e nos organismos vivos. title: Physics-enhanced deep learning for dual-branch single-pixel vision via highly scattering media
abstract: Single-pixel imaging (SPI) offers sensitivity for optical sensing, but dynamic scattering media severely degrade the captured 1D bucket signals, causing traditional image reconstruction algorithms to fail and hindering target recognition. To overcome the resulting sim-to-real gap, we propose a physics-enhanced dual-branch digital twin framework for single-pixel vision in highly scattering environments. title: Mapping disappearance: spatial analysis of vulnerable coastal destinations
abstract: Abstract Many coastal regions around the world face increasing risks from both natural and anthropogenic drivers, including climate change, rising sea levels, and rapid, unauthorized urbanization. This study presents an integrated geospatial approach to evaluate the coastal vulnerability of Visakhapatnam and Uppada Village, both located in coastal Andhra Pradesh, India. These areas are exposed to multiple natural hazards and disasters but lack comprehensive multi-temporal analysis. This research uniquely integrates remote sensing and GIS with a multi-parameter coastal vulnerability assessment

title: Discovery and promotion of unknown sounds into operational detection targets for underwater passive acoustic monitoring under false alarm constraints
abstract: Abstract Earth’s oceans cover 70% of the planet yet remain among the least observed regions. Underwater acoustics is a primary sensing modality, but recordings span biological, anthropogenic and natural sounds while labels remain sparse. title: Economía azul e inteligencia artificial: innovación, sostenibilidad y nuevos mercados
abstract: La economía azul propone conciliar la actividad económica sin destruir los recursos marinos. En este contexto, el presente trabajo sostiene que la inteligencia artificial (IA) no debe verse solo como una herramienta de eficiencia, sino un elemento clave para redefinir las condiciones de viabilidad ambiental oceánica. A partir de una revisión crítica de la literatura reciente, se argumenta que la (IA) puede contribuir a la gestión sostenible de los ecosistemas marinos, aunque su impacto depende de marcos institucionales capaces de evitar la reproducción de desigualdades tecnológicas y prácticas

title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting the Mechanical Properties of Polymer Composites
abstract: This paper presents the results of an investigation into the feasibility of applying ensemble machine learning algorithms to predict the mechanical properties of nanofilled epoxy composites, aimed at enhancing the reliability of water transport facilities. The study is positioned as a validated proof-of-concept demonstrating the applicability of ensemble ML models for property prediction tasks in epoxy composites, rather than as the formulation of a universal predictive framework. title: Severity prediction of traffic accidents with recent machine learning paradigms and SHAP
abstract: Abstract Traffic-related fatalities are among few leading causes of death worldwide. Crash severity prediction of traffic crashes has become a widespread research subject in recent years. Severity outcomes of crashes are usually influenced by factors such as humans, vehicles, roadway, weather, environment, and their interactions. A better understanding of crash-contributing circumstances and crash severity risk predictors is vital for the timely and effective implementation of appropriate mitigation measures. title: Resource-aware residential load forecasting: A cross-platform evaluation on embedded edge devices
abstract: This work presents a systematic, deployment-oriented evaluation of residential load forecasting models on resource-constrained embedded edge devices. In comparison to previous work, this study jointly analyses forecasting performance, memory footprint, inference latency, and directly measured on-device energy consumption. title: A deep neural network for CrIS cloud detection and transfer to HIRAS via implicit contrastive learning
abstract: Accurately identifying whether a field of view of satellite hyperspectral infrared sounders is clear or cloudy is critical for geophysical parameter retrieval and meteorological applications. In this study, a deep neural network is developed for cloud detection in Cross-track Infrared Sounder (CrIS) data and subsequently transferred to the High-spectral Resolution Infrared Atmospheric Sounder (HIRAS) onboard the Fengyun (FY)-3D satellite. title: Emerging Technologies and the Future of Warfare: A Strategic Analysis for Naval Power in the Indian Ocean Region
abstract: The character of warfare is being reshaped by artificial intelligence, unmanned systems, and quantum computing at a pace that outstrips the doctrinal and institutional habits of most navies. This paper argues that technological change, geopolitical multiplexity, and institutional inertia together constitute the central strategic problem facing maritime forces in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR), and Pakistan in particular. title: A systematic framework for assessing conservation effectiveness of migratory marine species: Integrating biomass, habitat quality, and functional traits
abstract: The global expansion of Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) under the "30×30" target necessitates rigorous effectiveness assessments. Traditional evaluations for migratory marine species often rely on static biomass metrics, which fail to capture spatiotemporal mismatches between dynamic migration patterns and static reserve boundaries, deceptively masking structural population crises. Addressing these gaps, we developed a systematic framework integrating biomass, habitat quality, and functional traits. title: Automated and Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Predicting the Fracture Toughness of Fiber-Reinforced Ultra-High-Performance Concrete Subjected to Freeze–Thaw Damage
abstract: The extended longevity of fiber-reinforced ultra-high-performance concrete (FR-UHPC) in frigid regions remains incompletely comprehended, especially concerning the deterioration of mode-I fracture toughness (KIC) due to repeated freeze–thaw cycles (FTCs). title: Cross-scale influences of habitat and urbanisation on terrestrial vertebrates in coastal wetlands
abstract: Abstract Context Biodiversity in wetlands is impacted by expanding and intensifying urbanisation. While aquatic species spatial use of mangroves and saltmarshes is well established, little is known about how terrestrial vertebrates use these habitats in Australia and under what contexts. abstract: El siguiente artículo tiene como objetivo mostrar los fundamentos de los generadores de lenguajes naturales dentro de las inteligencias artificiales, desde la elucidación de las Redes Neuronales hasta las arquitecturas Transformers de los modelos GPT. abstract: Stainless steels are widely used in marine engineering, nuclear power, and automotive applications because of their excellent mechanical properties, processability, and corrosion resistance. abstract: This paper analyzes ten cases of AI integration in data journalism (two global, eight Latin American). AI expands operational capacity (volume and speed) but does not replace epistemic decisions, which remain under editorial control. The automation gradient —signaling, predictive scoring, large‑scale classification, total output validation— is proposed as an alternative to the automatic/semiautomatic binary. In Latin America, the main constraint is data governance: the lack of public information in processable formats limits the reach of AI, regardless of the models’ capabilities.

abstract: Welded metal sheets are used across automotive, aerospace, marine, and civil infrastructure applications for their high strength and light weight, yet fatigue failure remains a persistent concern in relation to their long-term structural stability. This study investigated whether chlorophyll fluorescence spectral indices could discriminate healthy (SA, n = 361), asymptomatic infected (AS, n = 284), and symptomatic infected (SY, n = 161) cocoa leaves. title: Developing an Object‐Based Climatology of Tornadic Storms Over the United States Using Machine Learning and Radar Reanalysis
abstract: Abstract Tornado climatologies over the contiguous United States have traditionally relied on report‐based data sets, which are subject to biases related to population density, time of day, and evolving observational practices. This study presents an object‐based machine learning framework for constructing a tornado climatology using storm cluster data derived from a radar reanalysis data set within the Multi‐Radar Multi‐Sensor framework spanning 2005–2011. abstract: Introduction. Studying the reproductive processes and spatial characteristics of the formation of sustainable agricultural development potential is a pressing issue given the persistent imbalance between economic, social, and environmental priorities. The purpose of this article is to assess the potential for sustainable development (PSD) of regional agricultural production based on an analysis of the reproduction of artificial, human, and natural capital using neural network tools.Materials and Methods. title: Development of an artificial intelligence-based adaptive digital twin method for early fault detection and energy loss reduction in solar photovoltaic systems
abstract: This article examines the scientific and conceptual foundations for developing an artificial intelligence-based adaptive digital twin method aimed at early fault detection and the reduction of associated energy losses in solar photovoltaic systems. An adaptive digital twin model is proposed by integrating real-time monitoring data, environmental parameters, electrical indicators, technical condition characteristics, and time-varying operational data into a unified information environment. abstract: This study presents a first-order assessment of natural hydrogen prospectivity of the Jeju Basin and Hupijiao Rise in the Northern East China Sea Shelf Basin by integrating seismic, wireline logs, and geochemical data. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based fault detection was applied to 3D seismic volumes to delineate basement-involved faults and igneous intrusions, while wireline logs and Rock-Eval pyrolysis data from exploration wells were analyzed to evaluate reservoir conditions and thermal maturity. abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks introduce a fundamentally new communication paradigm by integrating heterogeneous Space–Air–Ground–User–Sea Surface–Underwater (SAGSU-U) domains into a unified architecture. Although this integration significantly enhances network connectivity and coverage, it also expands the cyberattack surface, creating new security challenges for physical-layer intrusion detection. abstract: Abstract The Aurora hydrothermal vent field (AVF) is the first confirmed active vent system on the Arctic Ocean seafloor, located at the western end of the ultraslow spreading Gakkel Ridge. It marks a distinctive endmember among ridge‐axis hydrothermal systems, where volcanic construction and ultramafic influence co‐exist. abstract: Introduction In the north-eastern Pacific, high-value abalone fisheries, which are sensitive to pH variations, require in situ pH data to properly assess the bioeconomic effects of their possible dynamic trajectories under alternative fishing mortalities. Methods In situ pH data were collected every 15 min using a HOBO® MX2501 sensor in the La Bocana pink abalone fishing grounds and compared them with Argo float and Copernicus Marine Service observations. title: Climate stress priming of juvenile Southern California giant kelp (Macrocystis pyrifera) to marine heatwaves
abstract: Introduction Seaweed aquaculture production is expanding globally but threatened by increasing climate stressors, including extreme events. Ocean-based aquaculture is especially vulnerable to marine heatwaves, which can rapidly raise temperatures above the physiological limits of organisms, including macroalgae. title: Surface-water-quality dynamics in the Mekong Delta: impacts of pollution sources and altered flow regimes
abstract: The Mekong Delta is experiencing surface-water-quality degradation driven not only by increasing pollution loads but also by altered flow regimes, salinity intrusion, sediment starvation, and shifting hydraulic operation. This paper synthesizes and analyzes monitoring records for 2016–2024, a database of 3,117 samples, supplementary surveys conducted in 2022–2024, and hydrodynamic–salinity–morphological studies to clarify surface-water-quality dynamics in the Mekong Delta through two linked dimensions: the direct impacts of pollution sources and the amplifying role of altered flows. abstract: Introduction The rapid expansion of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has increased the cyberattack surface of industrial infrastructures, creating demand for intrusion detection systems (IDS) that combine predictive performance with deployment efficiency. Methods This study proposes a Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO)-guided fixed top-k feature-ranking framework for multi-class IIoT intrusion detection using candidate-dependent redundancy regularization, class-weighted learning, stratified cross-validation, repeated runs, and independent holdout evaluation. title: Patterns of association between carbon sinks and multidimensional human driving factors in China: a hybrid machine learning framework
abstract: Regarding the urgency of carbon neutrality, the necessity to investigate the dynamics of carbon sinks and their human drivers is overwhelming. However, most of existing literature only examines the nexus between carbon sinks and their human drivers by the traditional econometric regressions with predetermined function forms. Such predefined functions may undermine the asymptotical property of estimation and thus yield potentially biased results. title: Algal overgrowth disproportionately undermines fish species richness in coral‐rich reefs
abstract: Algal overgrowth on coral reefs threatens reef fish species richness worldwide, yet the variation in this pressure across gradients of coral cover remains unclear. Using a global dataset spanning 2006-2023, we examined how cover by low-lying algae and macroalgae modulates the relationship between live hard coral cover and fish species richness. title: AI-Enabled Cultural Heritage Preservation and a Browser-Based Virtual Museum: Design and Implementation of a Kenya Coastal Heritage Platform
abstract: Coastal Kenya holds a wide-ranging cultural heritage expressed in material artefacts, oral traditions, indigenous and local languages, historical knowledge, and everyday community practices. Yet these resources are increasingly strained by modernisation and global circulation, shifting modes of cultural transmission, and gaps in systematic documentation. This study reports the design and implementation of the Kenya Coastal Heritage Digital Platform produced under the Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for the Preservation and Promotion of Coastal Cultural Heritage in Kenya (LAIPCH-K) project.

title: Predicting the initial cracking time of beam bridges in subtropical coastal area using field measured data
abstract: Accurate prediction of the initial cracking time (ICT) of reinforced concrete (RC) bridges is critical for durability assessment and maintenance planning. Conventional ICT models, predominantly calibrated on laboratory data, often fail to capture the complex degradation of in-service bridges in subtropical coastal environments. This study develops a dual-track prediction framework integrating a field-calibrated numerical model with eight machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on 756 field records. title: The impact of climate risk on forestry ecological total factor productivity: evidence from double machine learning
abstract: Extreme climate events associated with climate change pose a growing threat to forestry production efficiency, yet systematic empirical evidence on their effects on ecological total factor productivity in forestry (forestry TFP) and the underlying transmission pathways remains limited. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provinces from 2012 to 2023, we measure provincial physical climate risk, dominated by acute extreme events, with a composite physical climate risk index (CPRI) comprising exposure to extreme cold, extreme heat, extreme rainfall and extreme drought. title: From deterministic to stochastic: A hybrid framework coupling machine learning with Bluecat for probabilistic satellite-based precipitation estimation over Greece
abstract: Study region: This study focuses on Greece, characterized by complex topography and strong spatial and temporal variability in precipitation variability, which challenge accurate rainfall estimation and hydrological applications. Reliable precipitation data are essential for hydrological modeling, water resource management and rainfall extremes assessment, while satellite products provide extensive spatial coverage but are subject to systematic biases relative to ground observations. title: Assessing urban water consumption dynamics using machine learning and spatial variables under normal and pandemic conditions: A case study
abstract: Abstract This study developed a spatially explicit framework to estimate household water consumption (HWC) and the number of household water subscribers in each consumption class (NHWSCC) using land surface temperature (LST), land value, and elevation. Three machine-learning (ML) models were applied: symbolic regression (SR), an extreme learning machine (ELM), and an ELM hybridized with the artificial bee colony algorithm (ELM-ABC). title: Microbial community dynamics mediate rapid biomass loss and phosphorus recycling in pelagic Sargassum
abstract: Sargassum blooms in the tropical North Atlantic have surged to unprecedented levels, causing massive algal tides that severely impact coastal ecosystems. To improve the current understanding of Sargassum biomass dynamics and the contribution of this productive algal bloom to carbon and nutrient fluxes between the Atlantic and the Caribbean, we characterized the growth and decomposition rates of this pelagic alga, nutrient release rates during litter decay, and the bacterial microbiome at several stages of this decay. abstract: For matched field localization using ship radiated noise as sources of opportunity, replica libraries are often incomplete because vessel trajectories cannot fully cover the observation region. The completion problem can be formulated as recovering missing replica entries from partial observations, for which Bayesian matrix completion methods provide a probabilistic framework. title: Learning the Path to Ion Separation: A Proof-of-Concept for Machine Learning-Assisted Inverse Design (MLAID) of Nanofiltration Membranes
abstract: Abstract Advancing the design of polymeric membranes through material screening and discovery offers a powerful strategy to guide future membrane fabrication tailored to a wide range of separation challenges. Traditional trial-and-error methods often fall short in navigating this large monomer and process-design space, whereas machine learning-assisted inverse design (MLAID) can provide an extensible workflow for translating literature-derived membrane knowledge into ranked experimental candidates. title: Explainable Machine Learning-Based Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment and Upazila-Level Intervention Prioritization in the Chattogram Region, Bangladesh
abstract: The increasing occurrence of natural hazards, either individually or in combination, has intensified disaster risk worldwide, with the Chattogram Region of Bangladesh representing a prominent multi-hazard hotspot where earthquakes, landslides, and floods frequently coexist. An interpretable GIS–ML-based multi-hazard risk assessment (MHRA) framework was developed to generate earthquake, landslide, and flood susceptibility zones (EQSZ, LSSZ, and FSZ) using ensemble machine learning algorithms, with model predictions explained through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). title: Integrating mRMR and PSO–machine learning with SHAP interpretation for UAV-based maize aboveground biomass and carbon estimation
abstract: Accurate estimation of crop aboveground biomass (AGB) and aboveground carbon (AGC) across growth stages is pivotal for evaluating agroecosystem carbon sequestration. Nevertheless, the integration of feature selection, model optimization, and interpretability for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based crop AGB estimation remains underexplored. We propose a comprehensive interpretable machine learning framework for whole-season crop AGB estimation. title: Integrated diagnostic framework for resolving distinct ozone formation mechanisms via observations, modeling, and machine learning
abstract: Abstract Ozone (O3) pollution in relatively high-latitude industrial cities shows spatiotemporal patterns associated with coupled meteorological, transport, and chemical processes, yet its dominant formation mechanisms remain unresolved. This study developed an interpretable diagnostic framework integrating process-resolved Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with Chemistry (WRF-Chem) simulations, observations, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) interpreted using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) for Changchun, Northeast China (September 2023–August 2024). title: Research on the BiSpikeNet classification model for tea plant pests and diseases
abstract: Background Fast and accurate identification of tea pests and diseases with lightweight, efficient, and resource-friendly computation is a key challenge in smart tea gardens. While deep learning models like ResNet extract strong features, their high computational cost limits application. Conversely, lightweight models like BiRealNet reduce complexity but suffer from unclear intermediate features and weak discrimination. abstract: Purpose: This article aims to examine the role of digital innovation in enhancing the competitiveness of coastal Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) within the framework of the blue economy. Coastal MSMEs play an important role in generating employment, supporting local livelihoods, and utilizing marine and coastal resources. However, these enterprises frequently face challenges related to limited market access, low technological capabilities, inadequate infrastructure, environmental pressures, and intense competition. abstract: Introduction Driven by the dual forces of global climate change and sea-level rise, storm surge disasters have emerged as a primary external shock constraining the sustainable development of coastal socio-economic systems. title: Marine organic waste valorization on seafood-based industry development: A review on circular bioeconomy and Technology Readiness Level (TRL) perspectives
abstract: Marine organic waste, including fish processing byproducts, shellfish residues, aquaculture waste, aquatic plant biomass, and coastal beach wrack, represents an abundant yet underutilized biomass resource with significant potential for supporting a circular bioeconomy. This review comprehensively evaluates recent advances in the valorization of these marine waste streams through sustainable biotechnological and thermochemical approaches. abstract: Abstract In CNC milling processes, vibration signals are a crucial data source that directly reflects machining dynamics and changes in cutting conditions. This study aims to classify material type, feed rate, and depth-of-cut using data-driven vibration signals obtained during CNC milling of Al6061 and Al7075 aluminum alloys. Vibration data were collected from the bed and tool holder areas; a sensor-fusion approach, in which these two data sources are evaluated together, was also investigated. title: Radiosonde-informed machine learning correction of ERA5 integrated water vapor: spatiotemporal generalization and external GNSS evaluation
abstract: Accurate integrated water vapor (IWV) estimates are essential for atmospheric monitoring, yet reanalyses can retain systematic discrepancies relative to in situ observations. This study develops a radiosonde-informed machine learning framework to correct ERA5-derived IWV over Europe and assess spatial and temporal generalization. Radiosonde profiles from the University of Wyoming and the Integrated Global Radiosonde Archive were collocated with ERA5 and VMF3 products at 116 stations from November 2021 to November 2025. abstract: As key spatial carriers for regional economic growth and ecological protection, urban agglomerations’ ecological resilience is critical to regional risk adaptation and sustainable development. This study examines 92 prefecture-level and above cities in China’s five major urban agglomerations from 2007 to 2021. An ecological resilience evaluation system is constructed under the resistance–adaptability–recovery framework and measured using the CRITIC method. abstract: Coastal subsea tunnels often traverse shallow heterogeneous strata, creating significant deformation risks. Deformation control is therefore essential for safe urban construction. This study integrates FLAC3D, SSA-LSSVM, and NSGA-II for multi-objective excavation-support optimization. The Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Second Subsea Tunnel serves as the case study. title: Reservoir Water Level Prediction and Gate Operation Optimization Using Machine Learning: A Case Study of Shetrunji Reservoir, Gujarat
abstract: Control over reservoir water levels and gate settings at the spillways is key for preventing floods, protecting people living downstream, and efficient utilization of stored water especially when the reservoir is nearing its maximum capacity. This research project centers on the Shetrunji Reservoir in Gujarat, India, investigating the potential of machine learning to improve operations. Daily and event-based hydrological records for the reservoir covering the period 2020 to 2024 were compiled, digitized, and used to train and test predictive models. abstract: Introduction Maritime transport carries the predominant share of cross-border agricultural trade, and geopolitical conflicts, climate anomalies, port congestion, and proliferating trade barriers have intensified uncertainty for the coastal enterprises that depend on seaborne logistics. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new pathways for building resilient supply chains through multi-source data fusion and risk prediction capabilities. title: Coastal vascular plant diversity of the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve: Rare plants, vegetation mosaics, and conservation priorities
abstract: The coastal margin of the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve (DDBR) forms a dynamic ecological interface between the delta, the Razim-Sinoe lagoon system, and the Black Sea. We synthesized project-derived floristic, phytocoenological, spatial, and pressure records collected during 2009-2018 from Musura Island to Corbu, including 86.92 km covered during the final detailed mapping stage. abstract: The practical application of rechargeable zinc-air batteries (R-ZABs) is critically limited by high-performance bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, as their intrinsic activity directly governs the efficiency and longevity of air cathodes. Recently, biomass-derived carbon materials are compelling candidates for bifunctional electrocatalysts, benefiting from their renewable nature, low cost, inherently porous architecture, and naturally doped heteroatoms. title: Infrastructure-based prioritization and cost analysis of offshore freshened groundwater: a Northern Adriatic case study
abstract: Offshore Freshened Groundwater (OFG) represents a potential unconventional water resource for water-stressed coastal regions. However, its development is hindered by a lack of systematic, cost-effective methods for regional-scale screening and prioritization, which are necessary before expensive site-specific surveys can be justified. This study addresses this gap by developing and applying an integrated, two-step data-driven framework. abstract: Background Urban blue–green environments are vital components of the urban exposome, shaping daily opportunities for physical activity, stress mitigation, and broader public health. However, these benefits depend on daily accessibility. In compact coastal metropolises, extensive nature may coexist with highly unequal residential access. This study investigates whether socially vulnerable residential areas in Shenzhen experience reduced exposure to public green and coastal blue spaces. abstract: This study developed a risk-based integrity management strategy for aging marine pipelines, emphasizing corrosion degradation, structural reliability, failure risk, and life extension of the Uyeghe–Stubb Creek buried oil pipeline system in Rivers State, Nigeria. The study used a case-study approach, drawing on historical inspection data and operating parameters, along with Melchers tri-linear and Paik non-linear corrosion models, marine-growth modelling, time-dependent reliability analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation. title: Learning from the past, building the future: AI in geotechnical engineering through the FOMLIG 2025 NextGen initiatives
abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping engineering disciplines, and geotechnical engineering is no exception. The next generation of geotechnical engineers must not only learn to use AI tools, but understand where they come from, what assumptions they rest on, and where they may fail. This paper reports on three intertwined NextGen initiatives hosted at the 3 rd workshop on the Future of Machine Learning in Geotechnics (FOMLIG3 2025) in Florence, Italy. title: Single-photon lidar observation process modeling and physics-driven virtual data generation
abstract: Single-photon lidar possesses significant advantages in underwater weak-signal target detection. However, the complex underwater light propagation environment leads to highly random and non-uniform observation noise. Furthermore, the limited scale of real data, constrained by experimental conditions and acquisition costs, makes it difficult to meet the training requirements of deep learning detection models. title: Reservoir Porosity Prediction in the Koroshina Dolomite Formation, Sadad Gas Field, Syria, Using Seismic Inversion and Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: The Koroshina Dolomite Formation is an important gas-bearing carbonate reservoir in the Sadad Gas Field, central Syria, where strong structural heterogeneity and limited well control make the prediction of reservoir properties challenging. This study aims to predict the spatial distribution of reservoir porosity within the Koroshina Dolomite Formation by integrating well-log data, two-dimensional (2D) post-stack seismic data, seismic inversion, and artificial neural network modeling. title: Empowering Young Minds through Environmental Education on Marine Litter: Evidence from a School-Based Intervention in Japan
abstract: Marine litter remains a major global environmental challenge, and long-term mitigation depends not only on policy and waste management systems but also on public awareness and behavior change. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a school-based environmental education intervention in improving elementary school students’ knowledge, awareness, and behavioral intentions regarding marine litter. abstract: Purpose. This study develops a reproducible, precision-first framework for targeting gold mineralization in arid environments, addressing both bedrock and placer deposits at the Wadi Umm Eish El-Zarqa area in Egypt, the first such investigation in this region. Methods. The methodology combines machine learning applied to hyperspectral EnMAP data and spatial geomorphometric analysis of ALOS-PALSAR DEM. abstract: Sandstorms are a major aeolian hazard in arid environments, significantly affecting ecological stability, infrastructure and human health. abstract: Marine litter (ML) has attracted attention from international and national regulatory bodies because of its impact on biodiversity, water quality and the blue economy. title: The impact of rural population shrinkage on cultivated land non-grain conversion—dual causal inference based on machine learning
abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid advances in new urbanization and continued rural population contraction, the expansion of cropland non-grain use poses a potential challenge to national food security. Based on 3,598 observations from 257 prefecture-level cities in China over the 2011–2024 period, this study introduces a double machine learning approach and combines two-way fixed-effects models, threshold models, and spatial Durbin models to systematically examine the mechanisms through which rural population contraction affects cropland non-grain use. title: SceneContextNet: an integrated multi-stage deep learning framework for context-aware scene understanding using multi-object detection and spatial relationship modelling
abstract: Deep learning, especially CNN- and transformer-based approaches, has significantly impacted computer vision techniques such as object detection, segmentation, and scene classification. Despite the many successful scene understanding pipelines currently in use, most still rely primarily on global image features or object-level predictions and have little capacity to explicitly model object relationships, spatial arrangements, and structured contextual dependencies. abstract: Carbon emission prediction of coastal port-industrial zones integrates industrial production, maritime logistics and spatial environmental governance. Existing models fail to simultaneously capture multi-scale temporal fluctuations and spatial correlations of industrial units under meteorological and policy interference. This paper constructs an interpretable dual-branch framework combining Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition–XGBoost (EEMD-XGBoost) and a Temporal Graph Neural Network (T-GNN). abstract: Introduction Jellyfish possess the biochemical and physiological capabilities that enable them to survive from the beginning of the animal era to the impacts of global warming (ocean warming and deoxygenation) on the seas today. Despite their confirmed ability to bloom, significant gaps remain about the molecular basis of specific physiological responses, and limited data allow us to understand the metabolic pathways that enable medusozoans to transform energy and successfully cope with the challenges the marine environment imposes. title: Sinkhole susceptibility and genesis at the southwestern slope of the Mount Sirino (Basilicata, Southern Italy): insights from field survey and machine learning modeling
abstract: The southwestern slope of the Mount Sirino (Basilicata, Southern Italy) is characterized by complex geological conditions favouring heterogeneous sinkhole phenomena. abstract: Coastal urbanization is reshaping land-use patterns in many developing countries, particularly in rapidly developing coastal areas. This study analyzes land-use dynamics across coastal gradients in Vietnam during 2017–2025 using ESRI annual data, GIS analysis, and panel regression models. abstract: Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine transportation are fundamental to modern human life, but vehicle collisions with wildlife inadvertently kill hundreds of millions of animals across 2000 vertebrate and invertebrate species annually; however, a comprehensive framework to assess and mitigate these mortalities is missing. abstract: Urban green spaces (UGSs) are among the most important settings for high-quality soundscapes in cities, yet tools for spatially explicit identification and characterization of soundscape quality remain limited for green space planning. abstract: Background Insulin resistance (IR) underlies many chronic diseases. abstract: This study addresses the early and accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, a key challenge in clinical neurology. abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodule provinces host distinct benthic prokaryotic communities, yet viruses that regulate them remain largely unknown. abstract: Abstract. Determining the climatic conditions under which the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) was smaller than present is important to quantify GrIS sensitivity to climate change. abstract: Food preservation challenges have positioned packaging as a rapidly evolving, innovation-driven field, with smart packaging offering transformative solutions. Among advanced materials, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted growing attention due to their permanent porosity, structural tunability, high surface area, and chemical stability. It analyses the processes shaping security dynamics -ranging from traditional military risks to contemporary hybrid, cyber, and cognitive threats. title: Satellite-based vessel detection under turbulence and jitter: a degradation-aware comparison
abstract: Maritime domain awareness increasingly relies on satellite-based Earth observation (EO) for wide-area vessel monitoring. Low Earth orbit (LEO) platforms enable flexible acquisition, but optical imagery can be degraded by atmospheric turbulence and platform jitter. abstract: Abstract Traditional directional regulation metasurfaces redirect reflected waves into prescribed directions, limiting their effectiveness in broadband and multistatic underwater detection. title: Physicochemical and urban land-use characteristics associated with resistance to precipitation in estuaries vary across scales
abstract: Estuaries are subject to frequent stressors, including elevated nutrient loading and extreme hydrologic events, which impact water quality and disrupt ecosystem stability and function. The capacity of an estuary to resist changes in function in response to precipitation events is an important descriptor of ecosystem response dynamics, especially when interpreted within the context of baseline system condition and ecological state. abstract: Mineral prospectivity mapping is difficult in regions where confirmed deposits are few and available geological data vary widely in type and quality. abstract: The high-dimensional Fokas model can describe a wide range of complex nonlinear wave phenomena; however, traditional analytical methods struggle to obtain a diverse set of exact analytical solutions, which limits the theoretical analysis and engineering applications of such models. abstract: The operation of centrifugal pump systems driven by AC motors is crucial for industrial fluid transportation, particularly in energy and logistics facilities where stable pressure and flow regulation are essential to maintaining operational efficiency. abstract: Coastal ecosystems face increasing challenges due to environmental degradation, declining community welfare, and limited local capacity to manage natural resources sustainably. Understanding how climatic and site-specific drivers regulate the start, end, and length of the growing season, and how these phenological shifts translate into productivity responses, remains a key challenge for predicting forest carbon dynamics. abstract: Rural-coastal settlements in developing nations suffer from immense energy poverty, climate vulnerability and lack sustainable livelihood options. abstract: In a sea environment, the localization of ships is very important for traffic management. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) dataset is widely used to get information about ships. abstract: Mediterranean coastal regions face increasingly interconnected climate risks that require adaptation across sectors and governance levels. Despite growing policy commitments and a widening portfolio of adaptation initiatives, implementation often remains fragmented. This study examines the governance conditions under which diverse climate adaptation initiatives can be integrated to support coordinated regional and local resilience. abstract: This study investigates the techno-economic feasibility of coupling a reverse osmosis (RO) desalination plant with a nuclear-renewable hybrid energy system (Nu-R HES) consisting of a 150 MWe small modular reactor (SMR), a 100 MWe solar photovoltaic (Solar PV) plant, and a 600 MWe hydroelectric power plant (HPP) for the seaport region of Durrës, Albania. abstract: Abstract Parasitic fungi of the phylum Chytridiomycota are known parasites of phytoplankton yet little is known about drivers of their diversity and host interaction dynamics in marine and brackish habitats. abstract: Carotenoids play a crucial role as accessory pigments in plant photosynthesis and are closely associated with physiological responses to environmental stress. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) holds transformative potential to decode urban climate resilience (UCR) complexities, yet its unguided expansion risks amplifying systemic biases. abstract: Cost-per-click (CPC) in paid search is an auction-generated outcome shaped by a competitive landscape that is only partially observable from any single advertiser’s history. From 1.66 billion Google Ads log records for a concentrated car-rental market (2021–2023), we construct a weekly panel of 1,811 keyword series over 127 weeks (218,924 keyword–week observations) and build competition-aware proxies from keyword text, CPC trajectories, and geographic market structure. title: Transversal Pooling Neural Networks
abstract: Many learning tasks require stability to small transformations while retaining sensitivity to larger ones. We introduce \emph{transversal pooling neural networks}, which generalize spatial max pooling to affine group actions. We establish equivariance to a chosen subgroup and derive explicit stability bounds for individual pooled wavelet coefficients under affine perturbations of the input. Experimentally, we demonstrate the utility of our networks in low-data environments and for predicting tropical cyclone intensification.

title: The limits of exactness: On the failure of automatic differentiation in physics-informed machine learning
abstract: Automatic differentiation (AD) lets neural networks compute derivatives of governing equations to machine precision, and this precision has made it the computational backbone of physics-informed machine learning. Yet exactness in the mathematical sense is not the same as fidelity to the physics. Here I argue that a derivative can be numerically perfect and still be the wrong derivative for the problem at hand, because AD, by construction, has no notion of the physical structure a solution must obey. title: Warm-starting PDE solvers with any-dimensional machine learning
abstract: Any-dimensional machine learning models, such as graph neural networks (GNNs), can be naturally trained and evaluated on inputs of different sizes and dimensions. Inspired by the GNN transferability literature, we show mathematical conditions under which a partial differential equation (PDE) learning-based solver can be trained in small dimensions and directly applied to solve a higher dimensional PDE in a zero-shot fashion. title: How can AI accelerate the green transition?
abstract: In his essay The Gift, published in 1925, the sociologist Marcel Mauss emphasised the 'total' scope of the phenomenon of gift-and counter-gift-giving, noting that it 'expresses, simultaneously and all at once, all manner of institutions: religious, legal and moral (...)\,; economic (...)\,; not to mention the aesthetic phenomena to which these facts give rise (...).'' The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), which is suddenly and profoundly disrupting individual and collective lives, bears a resemblance to the ''total social fact'' described a hundred years ago. title: Toward Enhanced Water Detection in SWOT Pixel Clouds using Dynamic Graph Neural Networks
abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission offers unprecedented freshwater monitoring capabilities through its innovative wide-swath measurement system, which generates several data products, including the high-resolution pixel cloud (PIXC) product. However, the native PIXC water classification remains prone to systematic misclassification in urban environments, where strong radar returns from non-water surfaces are the predominant error sources. We present a deep learning approach that enhances land-water classification directly on SWOT PIXC data based on a dynamic graph convolutio

title: Nesterov-Accelerated Concurrent Learning for Lyapunov-Based Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Concurrent learning (CL) has recently been extended to Lyapunov-based deep neural networks (DNNs) to obtain parameter convergence under finite rather than persistent excitation. However, the existing first-order law converges slowly, especially for high-dimensional systems and overparameterized networks. To address this problem, this paper develops a Nesterov-accelerated concurrent learning (NACL) adaptation law for uncertain second-order control-affine systems. title: TaiJi: State-Conditional Adaptive Combination of Machine-Learning and Physics-Based Global Weather Forecasts
abstract: Data-driven machine-learning weather models now rival, and in some respects surpass, operational numerical weather prediction (NWP), yet no single model dominates across variables, pressure levels, lead times, or regions, and the marginal returns from developing ever-larger individual models are diminishing. We present TaiJi (after the Chinese concept of yin-yang harmony, the complementarity of opposites), a spatiotemporal adaptive ensemble framework that recasts optimal model-weight combination as a learned prediction problem: a lightweight convolutional neural network, conditioned on the rec

title: AquaBEV-Nav: Learned BEV Occupancy for Underwater Navigation and Exploration
abstract: Safe underwater exploration requires a robot to understand where surrounding structures are located and which regions are available for motion. Existing vision-based underwater exploration systems commonly obtain this information indirectly by estimating monocular depth, unprojecting the geometry into 3D space, and accumulating it into a 2D bird's-eye-view occupancy map. This reliance on intermediate depth estimation is particularly problematic underwater, where scattering and wavelength-dependent attenuation degrade visual cues and limit the reliability of monocular depth estimates. title: CoralPlan: Observation Skill Selection and Execution for Underwater Robotic Inspection
abstract: Underwater robotic inspection depends on acquiring views that reveal task-relevant structure. For a structurally complex coral colony, recognising the target is only the starting point: the robot must select and execute a viewing motion suited to the inspection task. We present CoralPlan, a vision-language system that selects an observation skill from a current camera image and task text supplied by an episode manifest. title: Coral Grow-out Robotic Assessment System (CGRAS): Scaling Coral Recruit Monitoring Through Robotics and Computer Vision
abstract: Climate change is the largest threat to coral reefs, with increasing global impacts accelerating the need for scalable reef restoration technologies. Large-scale reef restoration depends on the mass production of corals, such as through coral aquaculture. Coral seeding with recruits grown in aquaculture facilities is a feasible restoration approach, but effective production requires consistent, high-frequency monitoring of tens of thousands of macroscopic (0.5-2mm diameter) recruits, making conventional manual assessment prohibitively labor-intensive. To address this monitoring bottleneck, we

title: Learning Provable Neural Network Observer for Uncertain Dynamical Systems
abstract: In many safety-critical applications, control of uncertain dynamical systems relies on observers that estimate states and external disturbances. Neural network observers can improve estimation accuracy, but certifying their Lyapunov stability via Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) constraints leads to large-scale semidefinite programs (SDPs) that are difficult to solve for large networks. To overcome this scalability bottleneck, we propose a novel two-stage training framework for provably stable neural network observers. title: Explaining El Niño Forecasts with the Average Gradient Outer Product
abstract: An important and unresolved problem in the physical sciences is explaining the predictions made by neural networks. Several explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods have been proposed to address this problem, including gradient XAI, Integrated Gradients, and GradientSHAP. We evaluate the baseline XAI methods according to four scores: sensitivity (XAI patterns strongly affect predictions), attribution (XAI patterns reproduce the change in prediction relative to a baseline), robustness (XAI patterns remain stable for nearby inputs), and coherence (XAI patterns are spatially smooth). title: Does High Signal-to-Noise Ratio Identify Better Training Data for Seismic Deep Learning?
abstract: Hard signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) screening removes weak seismic records, but does retaining clearer waveforms improve learning enough to compensate for the discarded data? We test this question in phase picking and ambient-noise dispersion, first matching training counts and then restoring the full eligible dispersion pool at fixed compute. title: A Model-Agnostic Physics-Guided Adapter for Few-Shot Transfer of Coastal Flood Prediction Models to Unseen Regions
abstract: Deep learning surrogates can produce high-resolution coastal flood maps orders of magnitude faster than physics-based hydrodynamic simulators, yet transferring them to new coastal regions remains costly, since generating target-region data for fine-tuning typically requires numerous time-consuming simulations. To tackle this bottleneck, we introduce the Physics Adapter (PA), a compact, architecture-agnostic adaptation interface that enables efficient few-shot transfer of flood prediction models across diverse coastal regions. title: AquaWAM: A Dynamics-aware World Action Model for Underwater Embodied Agents
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) are becoming increasingly important and useful for embodied intelligence, as they enable robots to anticipate the consequences of candidate actions before interacting with the physical environment. However, underwater robots are usually subject to passive dynamics, such as inertia, buoyancy, hydrodynamic drag, and persistent drift, which can continue to affect the vehicle even after an action is completed. title: PIC-UIE: Predicting Image-Adaptive Corrections for Lightweight Underwater Image Enhancement
abstract: Underwater image enhancement (UIE) aims to restore visibility, color fidelity, and structural detail from images degraded by wavelength-dependent attenuation and backscatter. State-of-the-art UIE methods often rely on large backbones and dense image-to-image prediction, limiting their practicality for edge deployment. Moreover, operating entirely in a single color space couples degradation estimation with luminance and chroma correction. title: A PyTorch Library for Hyperspectral Image Models: Technical Report
abstract: Hyperspectral remote sensing has advanced across diverse deep learning paradigms, including spectral spatial CNNs, Vision Transformers, Mamba, graph neural networks, Kolmogorov Arnold networks, and self supervised masked autoencoding. Yet progress remains hindered by fragmented repositories, incompatible tensor conventions, and non standardized evaluation. title: DeepMIDE: A Multivariate Spatio-Temporal Method for Ultra-Scale Offshore Wind Energy Forecasting
abstract: To unlock access to stronger winds, the offshore wind industry is advancing with significantly larger and taller wind turbines. This massive upscaling motivates a departure from univariate wind forecasting methods that traditionally focused on a single representative height. To fill this gap, we propose DeepMIDE—a statistical deep learning method which jointly models the offshore wind speeds across space, time, and height. title: Detecting Nighttime Anomalies from NASA Black Marble Using a Generalized Spatio-Temporally Robust Framework of Machine Leaning Ensembles
abstract: Nighttime lights from NASA's Black Marble product suite capture thermal and light emission signals from anomalous events including fires, volcanic eruptions, and gas flaring. Existing detection approaches rely primarily on thermal bands, limiting sensitivity to weaker signals. We propose a novel machine learning framework that jointly models Black Marble M-band and Day/Night Band (DNB) signals to derive a generalized, spatio-temporally robust ensemble of anomaly detectors. title: Butterfly Effect Confirmed in Global AI Weather Models: Evidence from Tropical Cyclone Forecasting
abstract: A paradox recently emerged in artificial intelligence (AI) weather prediction research. While some claim AI weather models cannot simulate atmospheric butterfly effect, this conflicts with AI models' limited predictability and advances in AI ensemble forecasting. This study demonstrates via counterexamples that the butterfly effect does exist in AI weather predictions. For Super Typhoon Khanun, AI predictions are constrained by a double-attractor system. title: SEA-CLIP-Tiny: Efficient Multilingual Text-Vision Embedding for Southeast Asian Languages
abstract: Multilingual text-vision embedding models are essential for cross-lingual image-text retrieval, but Southeast Asian languages remain poorly supported due to the region's linguistic diversity and limited data and computing resources. In this paper, we introduce SEA-CLIP-Tiny, a compact multilingual text-vision embedding model for Southeast Asia with fewer than 50M parameters. title: Learning Hierarchical Causal Representations of the Effects of Forcings on Temperature in Climate Models
abstract: Machine learning (ML) emulators provide a fast and cost-effective method to simulate climate change scenarios after being trained on Earth System Models projections. However, the black-box nature of those data-driven approaches limit the usability and trustworthiness of their outputs and in particular their use as causal attribution tools. Here, we develop a hierarchical causal representation learning framework applied to sea surface temperature fields from a state-of-the-art global climate model. title: Evaluating Dynamical Fidelity through Predictive Structure in Physical Representations
abstract: Machine-learning models for physical systems are currently evaluated primarily through errors between predicted and reference states and, increasingly, through tests of physical consistency. These metrics assess whether predictions are accurate and satisfy selected physical requirements, but provide limited insight into whether learned trajectories reproduce the underlying dynamics. title: Coarse-to-fine multi-resolution hash encoding for implicit full waveform inversion
abstract: Implicit full waveform inversion (IFWI) reparameterizes the velocity model with a neural network, but it suffers from spectral bias and requires many iterations to converge. Multi-resolution hash encoding uses a learnable feature grid to recover high wavenumber details at multiscales and provides strong local representations. title: Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models
abstract: When recalling lists of concepts (e.g., animals) during the semantic fluency task (SFT), both humans and large language models (LLMs) organise their output into clusters of related items (e.g., sea animals) that are punctuated by strategic switches between clusters. In humans, this pattern can be explained by a semantic foraging process, whereby distinct neural and behavioural signatures accompany within-cluster production ("exploit") and between-cluster switching ("explore"). title: Low latency global carbon budget reveals strong land sink recovery in 2025
abstract: The atmospheric CO2 growth rate fell sharply in 2025, from a record 3.76 $\pm$ 0.09 ppm yr-1 in 2024 to 2.06 $\pm$ 0.09 ppm yr-1 (NOAA marine boundary layer observations), below the 2015-2022 mean of 2.47 ppm yr-1, even as fossil CO2 emissions rose by 0.7% to 10.38 GtC yr-1.
