title: Latitudinal changes in moist heatwaves across the Northern Hemisphere during 1950–2023
abstract: The intensification of moist heat extremes under global warming represents a critical hazard to human health and ecosystem stability. However, the distinct spatiotemporal evolutionary patterns of moist heatwaves (MHWs; relative humidity ≥40%) versus extreme moist heatwaves (EMHWs; relative humidity ≥70%) across different latitudinal zones remain insufficiently understood. title: Generation and Propagation of Eastern Subpolar North Atlantic Salinity Anomalies
abstract: Abstract The Eastern Subpolar North Atlantic (E‐SPNA) upper ocean experiences pronounced interannual salinity variations that influence the global overturning circulation, yet a quantitative understanding of their life cycle remains lacking. Based on an ocean circulation state estimate, we combine budget analysis with particle tracking to quantify the generation and propagation of E‐SPNA salinity anomalies. abstract: Mesh-free Lagrangian methods including smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) are ideal for complex ocean engineering involving large free-surface deformations, yet their high computational cost in 3D large-scale domains remains a barrier. Hybrid coupling strategies combine mesh-based far-field solvers with near-field SPH to offer a solution; however, a core challenge has been maintaining consistent free-surface tracking along 3D interfaces under multi-directional waves. title: Predicting winter cold surge scenarios using ensemble forecasting and clustering techniques
abstract: East Asian cold surges develop through several distinct spatiotemporal evolution patterns, each characterized by a different intensity and duration. Beyond forecasting whether a cold surge will occur, anticipating which type will develop would allow the likely evolution scenario to be foreseen in advance, providing valuable lead time for disaster preparedness. abstract: Abstract Dynamic bedforms, such as sand waves, may pose a threat to offshore energy infrastructure. Due to their impact on seabed mobility, dredging is often required to reduce risks, for example, to avoid cable exposure. However, commonly used data‐driven methods cannot predict the evolution of partially dredged sand waves. title: A VFIFE-based non-contact monitoring approach for mooring line tension in floating offshore wind turbines
abstract: The safety of mooring systems is critical for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs), yet contact-based tension monitoring suffers from difficult installation, susceptibility to damage and limited long-term reliability. This study proposes a non-contact monitoring method based on the Vector Form Intrinsic Finite Element (VFIFE), which determines mooring tension from the measured motion of the floating platform. abstract: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) increasingly support long-duration ocean observation, yet their mission endurance remains constrained by limited onboard energy storage. Wave energy offers a continuous, weather-independent supply, although most pendulum-based harvesters respond to only a single motion axis. abstract: Ports play a critical role in global trade infrastructure, however they are also a significant source of GHG emissions, energy use as well as marine environmental damage. The shift towards “green ports” has become a strategy to lessen the ecological footprint and enhance the efficiency of port operations by incorporating renewable energy sources, sustainable water management, and climate-resilient infrastructure. abstract: Managing high-salinity reject brine, CO₂ emissions, and declining oil recovery presents interconnected challenges across the water–energy nexus. This study investigates an integrated waste-derived hydroxyethyl cellulose–electrocoagulation–CO₂ (HEC─EC─CO₂) platform for brine treatment, gas-phase CO₂ uptake, solid recovery, and enhanced oil recovery (EOR). abstract: Environmental remediation has started to take advantage of all the advantages of Industry 5.0: sustainabililty, resilience and human-centric techologies. The role of nanocatalysts has a privileged part on it, as they allow the remediation of numerous pollutants present in atmosphere, water or soils. abstract: Semantic 3D city models (s3DCM) are a key component of urban digital twins (UDT) because they integrate geometry and semantic information in three-dimensional environments. abstract: Airborne microplastic (MP) particles are transported through the atmosphere, yet direct measurements at altitude remain scarce. We developed a novel uncrewed aerial system (UAS)-based method for in situ MP sampling within and above the atmospheric boundary layer. abstract: The increase in the frequency of devastating hurricanes has led to heightened interest in evaluating the vulnerability of coastal infrastructure by structural engineers, insurance companies, and government agencies involved in disaster mitigation efforts, such as the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). title: Changes in bioclimatic indices in the Arctic in 1991–2025
abstract: In the context of a changing climate, a comprehensive assessment is required of the impact of climatic conditions on the comfort of the living environment. This study evaluates changes in bioclimatic indices assessed on the basis of model reanalysis across the marine and land Arctic within the boundaries of the WMO Arctic Regional Climate Center — Network under ongoing climate change. abstract: To address the growing complexity between the built environment and urban life, modern urban planning has increasingly relied on digital technologies for decision-making, including City Information Modeling (CIM). While CIM has matured from standards and data integration to real-time analytics and digital twins, most initiatives optimize physical systems while struggling to incorporate “intangible” citizen-generated data. abstract: Autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) are increasingly deployed for hydrographic survey, coastal observation, and unmanned maritime monitoring. abstract: Abstract Motivated by an observed asymmetry in boundary layer convergence lines (BLCLs) between the Kubuqi and Ulan Buh desert borders of the Hetao Oasis in northern China, this work aims to document the differences in BLCL frequency and convective initiation and their potential drivers. abstract: The Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) is a crucial component of the global climate system, significantly influencing weather patterns, agriculture, and water resources across India. However, accurately simulating and predicting key aspects of the ISM—such as its onset, intensity, and variability—remains a challenge due to the intricate interactions between atmospheric, oceanic, and land surface processes. abstract: Armoured Fighting Vehicles (AFVs) must survive distinct but interacting threat classes, including kinetic-energy and armour-piercing projectiles, shaped-charge jets, high-velocity fragments, top-attack munitions, and buried mine/IED blast. abstract: Atmospheric water generation (AWG) yield is typically treated as a fixed hardware property. abstract: Abstract Turbulence in the free atmosphere has been widely estimated using the Thorpe method, which identifies vertical inversions in potential temperature profiles as evidence of overturning. However, the mechanisms driving Thorpe‐detected turbulence remain poorly understood, due largely to limitations in spatial and temporal resolution of observational and reanalysis datasets. title: Heat stress and heatwave trends across Türkiye (1975–2024) using the Extended Heat Index
abstract: Heat stress is an increasingly important climate-related hazard in regions experiencing rapid warming and changing temperature–humidity interactions. This study examines heat stress and heatwave trends across Türkiye during 1975–2024 using ERA5 reanalysis data aggregated to the provincial scale. Heat stress was quantified using the Extended Heat Index (EHI), which integrates air temperature and relative humidity to represent physiologically meaningful thermal exposure. abstract: Abstract Planetary boundary layer (PBL) turbulence modulates tropical cyclone (TC) intensity through competing mechanisms: (a) frictional dissipation that weakens TCs and (b) frictional convergence that drives stronger low‐level inflow and intensifies TCs. abstract: In the State of Maine, USA, tidal stream energy resources over a large swath of coastline have remained largely under-evaluated. abstract: China produces approximately 91.5% of the world’s Saccharina japonica (the species denoted by “kelp” herein) and its kelp farms collectively constitute one of the largest populations of floating marine structures anywhere. abstract: Abstract Lightning is an Essential Climate Variable, yet long‐term detection records may be compromised by changes in detection technology. abstract: Abstract Using satellite‐derived dust optical depth (DOD), reanalysis meteorology, and a global topsoil flash drought (TSFD) inventory for 2003–2022, we find that TSFD events are associated with increased dust loading at the global scale. abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable forecasting of extreme rainfall remains a critical challenge for flood management in climate‐sensitive regions. abstract: Introduction: Yellowfin tuna, Thunnus albacares , a commercially important pelagic species widespread across the Indian Ocean, plays a critical role in Indian fisheries. Understanding regional variation in biometric and demographic parameters is essential for achieving effective stock assessment and fisheries management. This study evaluated regional differences in growth patterns and condition of yellowfin tuna across the Indian Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). title: Thermal Amplification of Drought and Hydroclimatic Regime Shift in the Pantanal Wetland
abstract: Abstract The Pantanal, the world’s largest tropical wetland, is experiencing increasing hydroclimatic stress under sustained warming. Drought duration, severity, and intensity increased significantly after the early 2000s, resulting in the most persistent multi-year drought within the study period. This study assesses whether drought dynamics are becoming increasingly thermally amplified. abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme precipitation and atmospheric moisture transport are closely linked components of the Tibetan Plateau (TP) hydroclimate, but statistical covariability should be distinguished from causal control. We analyse extreme‐precipitation and integrated vapour transport (IVT) indices over 1979–2015 using APHRODITE precipitation and ERA5 reanalysis. abstract: Abstract Weather is a key driver of bird migration, particularly near ecological barriers, where migratory species often converge before crossing. While its effects on individual timing are well documented, how weather reshapes the temporal assemblage of migratory bird communities remains unexplored. abstract: Accurate estimation of design wave heights is paramount for the safety and resilience of coastal infrastructure. abstract: Abstract. Land-atmosphere interactions play a fundamental role in regulating climate variability, ecosystem productivity, and air quality through coupled exchanges of energy, water, carbon, and reactive trace gases. title: Lake Urmia desiccation drives building heating and cooling energy demand in northwestern Iran
abstract: Abstract The progressive desiccation of terminal lakes under global climate change represents an emerging environmental challenge with significant implications for regional climate and building energy demand. This study investigates the impact of Lake Urmia desiccation on building energy consumption across 13 cities in the Lake Urmia Basin in northwestern Iran during 2001–2023. abstract: Since the declaration of the Monsoon Onset over Kerala (MOK) involves subjective assessment by forecasters, an objective approach based on a dynamical model can provide forecasters with appropriate guidance to reduce errors in MOK declarations. abstract: This study examines the modulation of precipitation variability and its implications for potential predictability over mainland Ecuador and its relationship with the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) during the period 1981–2018. The analysis integrates homogenized and gap-filled daily precipitation observations with multiple satellite-based datasets (MSWEP, CHIRPS, and IMERG), enabling a comparative assessment of seasonal precipitation characteristics, dry and wet spell indices, and extreme rainfall metrics. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric refractivity model accuracy is important for refraction correction, starlight refraction navigation, and related optoelectronic applications. abstract: Water utilities increasingly depend on Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) sensors to support infrastructure planning, predictive asset maintenance, operational asset monitoring, and digital-twin applications. However, physical IIoT sensors remain vulnerable to sensor drift, calibration degradation, device failure, and communication outages, creating data observability gaps that can reduce confidence in analytics-driven operational decisions. title: Reassessment of post-breeding migratory passage of the Critically Endangered Balearic Shearwater at the Strait of Gibraltar
abstract: Abstract The Balearic Shearwater ( Puffinus mauretanicus ), Europe’s most threatened seabird, is classified as Critically Endangered. Previous migration counts at the Strait of Gibraltar suggested substantially higher population estimates than breeding colony surveys, but no updated assessment has been conducted for more than 15 years. We reassessed post-breeding migratory passage through the Strait using the same census framework and analytical approach applied during 2008–2010. title: Propagation of Subduction Polarity Reversal Along Arc‐Continent Convergent Margin: Insights From 3D Geodynamic Simulations
abstract: Abstract Subduction polarity reversal (SPR) driven by arc‐continent collision stands as a crucial process to establish new subduction zones throughout the Phanerozoic. Despite its inherent 3D nature, investigations of SPR along extensive arc–continent collision margins have largely been confined to 2D models, providing limited perspectives on the collision‐perpendicular propagation of SPR and the associated tectonic evolution. In this study, we establish a 3D numerical model to examine the geodynamic viability and tectonic responses of SPR propagation in the context of arc‐continent collision.

abstract: Abstract. Extreme weather hazards are increasing and stakeholders need rapid, transparent information during unfolding events. abstract: Water vapour exchange into the upper troposphere (UT) remains poorly understood over the Third Pole region. Previous studies have mainly focused on monsoon related moistening of the UT using reanalysis and satellite data. In this study, we employ km-scale (Dx = 3.3 km) ICON-CLM simulations to investigate the role of convection in transporting water vapour into the UT over the Third Pole. abstract: Wildfire danger assessment relies heavily on meteorological data and is challenged by the mismatch between real-time needs and the coarse spatial resolution of weather prediction outputs. abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated framework for estimating Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP)‐equivalent return levels under climate change, addressing two critical challenges: sampling uncertainty for rare events and the validation of bias correction under different global warming scenarios. abstract: Climate change and extreme weather are increasing the vulnerability of power systems globally, particularly in emerging economies such as Indonesia. Yet, existing studies often assess these impacts in isolation, focusing on individual components or specific hazards, leaving system-level effects—at provincial and national scales—under-examined. abstract: Circulation factors determine forest fire risk and the likelihood of catastrophic flooding in northern Siberia and the Russian Far East. abstract: On 10 April 2025, a severe thunderstorm impacted eastern India, causing disastrous impacts across 19 of Bihar's 38 districts. abstract: Riverbank erosion is an important geomorphological process that significantly influences river morphology, ecological systems, and infrastructure stability. Existing morphodynamic modelling approaches are generally unable to fully reveal the underlying hydro-mechanical mechanisms governing riverbank erosion because of the lack of suitable numerical models capable of simultaneously modelling free-surface flow, seepage, soil deformation, and large-deformation failure processes. abstract: Abstract. Renewable energy production is strongly influenced by climate variability and change, making the energy sector sensitive to fluctuations on decadal timescales. abstract: Abstract The topic of underground hydrogen storage brings microbial processes into the focus. Underground porous structures provide excellent living conditions for microorganisms because their habitat is protected but still allows a supply of substrates and nutrients. abstract: Abstract The intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ) is a central component of tropical climate, yet the conditions under which a tropical rain belt remains zonally extended or becomes unstable to zonal organization remain poorly understood. abstract: The Weather and Climate Science for Service Partnership (WCSSP) India, launched in 2017, builds long-term research partnerships between the UK and India to strengthen weather and climate science. abstract: Understanding regional wetting and drying under global warming remains challenging. Here we show, using global climate simulations and 191 records of past climate, that terrestrial moisture changes over the past 21,000 years follow a pronounced latitudinal pattern. abstract: In eastern India, thunderstorms and frequent lightning during the pre-monsoon season (March-May) result in significant human fatalities. abstract: Fatigue damage limits the service life of metallic structures, including mobile working machines. title: Tree-ring-derived April–July drought variability in the western Loess Plateau of China over the last four centuries and its linkage to the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation
abstract: Short instrumental records limit assessment of long-term drought variability on the western Loess Plateau of China. In this paper, we reconstructed April–July self-calibrating Palmer Drought Severity Index (scPDSI) variability for the last four centuries (1610–2016 CE) using a tree-ring width chronology obtained from Pinus tabuliformis in the Kongtong Mountains. Tree growth was strongly moisture limited, and the chronology was most strongly correlated with April–July scPDSI ( r = 0.74, p < 0.01). title: A physics-guided integrated global to regional method for high-resolution weather forecasting
abstract: High-resolution regional forecasts support disaster mitigation and sectoral decisions, yet numerical regional models remain costly. Here we introduce AERO-ODE, a physics-guided framework that combines global dynamical information, parameterization increments, and regional terrain constraints. From global initial conditions, AERO-ODE generates 72 h regional forecasts at hourly intervals and 3 km resolution in approximately 21 s, covering pressure-level Z , T , S , U and V and near-surface MSLP, U 10 , V 10 and T 2 m , without separate global surface lateral-boundary inputs. title: Michoacán Seismic and Tremor (MIST) Network: Perspectives, preliminary results and future directions to understand the role of the Cocos plate and the monogenetic volcanism
abstract: The Michoacan Seismic and Tremor (MIST) network is a follow-up project of the Middle America Subduction Experiment (MASE) and the Veracruz-Oaxaca Network (VEOX). These former experiments consisted of linear arrays perpendicular to the trench that generated large waveform datasets to characterize the subduction of the Cocos plate better. While the MASE array focused mainly on the flat segment of the subduction zone in the state of Guerrero, Mexico the VEOX array examined the changes in geometry towards a steep subduction in the Tehuantepec Isthmus. title: History of anthropogenic Phosphorus inputs (HaPi) to the terrestrial biosphere from 1860 to 2020
abstract: Abstract. Nitrogen and Phosphorus (P) are essential nutrients for sustaining life on Earth and have been increasingly applied in global agriculture to meet the growing demand for food production. Quantifying the spatial and temporal dynamics of nutrient inputs to the terrestrial biosphere is crucial for analyzing nutrient flows in crop-livestock systems, managing nutrient resources sustainably, and mitigating nutrient-related environmental impacts. title: A Fermatean fuzzy fault tree and Bayesian network hybrid for collision and grounding risk in a congested strait
abstract: Collision and grounding remain the dominant accident categories in congested straits, where dense crossing traffic, sharp bends and strong currents act together with human and technical failures. Quantitative risk assessment in such waters is hampered by scarce failure data and by the vagueness of expert judgement. This study proposes a hybrid model that couples Fermatean fuzzy fault tree analysis with a Bayesian network for the assessment of collision and grounding risk during the transit of a congested strait. title: Optimum dosage and long-term sulfate resistance of cement-based materials modified by nano-SiO₂ and nano-CaCO₃
abstract: To enhance the durability of cementitious composites in sulfate-rich environments, this study investigates the effects of varying dosages of nano-silica (NS) and nano-calcium carbonate (NC) on their macroscopic behavior and microstructural evolution during a 180-day sulfate exposure period. By integrating measurements of mass change, compressive strength, and rupture strength with X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), the underlying modification mechanisms of both nanomaterials are systematically revealed, and their optimal contents

title: Thermodynamic Drivers of Rapid Transition From Drought to Flood in Siberia, Russia
abstract: Abstract Siberia is a warming hotspot under the impact of climate change, and faces growing threats from hydroclimatic extremes. The rapid transition from drought to extreme wet conditions (hereafter RTDFs) could exacerbate compound hazards, as intense rainfall on drought‐weakened surfaces may increase runoff and permafrost instability in vulnerable cold regions. While some studies have examined RTDFs, understanding of them as a continuous physical process, particularly the dynamics of the transition, requires further investigation. title: Uncertainty in Precipitation Estimates Warrants Greater Consideration in Debris‐Flow Research
abstract: Abstract Quantitative precipitation estimates (QPEs) may provide a valuable data resource for investigations of postfire debris flows. In mountainous regions where debris flows typically occur, gauge coverage can be sparse; gridded QPEs offer remotely sensed and/or physics‐based precipitation estimates where no direct measurement is available. However, different gridded QPEs often tell contrasting stories about the magnitude, timing, and location of precipitation during a storm, which can lead to biases or misrepresentations of triggering rainfall in debris‐flow studies. title: Halogen behaviour during mantle melting and metasomatism recorded by peridotite xenoliths from Tariat, Mongolia
abstract: Peridotite xenoliths from the Tariat region of Mongolia are representative of the MORB-source mantle in terms of trace element patterns and radiogenic isotopic ratios, with rare metasomatic enrichments. A selection of 21 lherzolites with MgO of 37–44 wt% were analysed for halogens (F, Cl, Br, I) by a combination of ion microprobe in clinopyroxene (CPX) orthopyroxene (OPX), olivine (OL), and spinel (SP), and bulk rock methods. title: Characterization of geological samples and their influence during CO2 storage capacity in meter scale porous media
abstract: The rise of atmospheric CO 2 driven by anthropogenic activities is the main contributor to greenhouse gases and climate change. To address these emissions, Carbon, Capture and Storage (CCS) technologies are implemented and their effectiveness depends on the geological and sedimentological context that defines the physical properties of reservoir and seal rocks. This study aims to assess the influence of the physical properties of sediment samples from river–beach sands and supermature quartz sands by constructing a base geometry within a porous medium to analyze their CO 2 storage capacity. title: Towards an optimisation of mooring design for floating offshore wind turbines: Mathematical formalisation of a novel physically-based motion-related constraint
abstract: Early-stage mooring design for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs) relies on empirical poorly standardised motion-related constraints that neglect system dynamics. This work proposes a novel performance-driven methodology that dynamically links allowable offsets to the physical response of the system. A validated OpenFAST model of the NREL 5 MW wind turbine on the OC3 Hywind spar-type floating platform, Magnitude-Squared Coherence, and Pearson’s correlation analyses, were used to investigate FOWT dynamics and identify key physical relationships underpinning the proposed motion-related desi

title: How Predictable Was the Extreme Precipitation Preceding the May 2019 Arkansas River Floods?
abstract: Abstract In May 2019, unprecedented extreme rainfall over the central United States (US) facilitated severe flooding along the Arkansas River. The well‐documented relationship between atmospheric rivers (ARs) and central US heavy precipitation motivated investigation into AR relevance to this event and its predictability on extended timescales. title: Offshore wind profile characteristics and their impact on floating wind turbine power production
abstract: Abstract. In this study, we investigate the impact of vertical wind shear and wind speed inversions on the power production of a floating offshore wind turbine. Using nacelle-mounted wind lidar data from a 6 MW turbine at the Hywind Scotland wind farm, we analyse inflow conditions and turbine performance during summer and autumn. The wind climatology shows that 33 % of examined cases exhibit non-standard wind profiles within the rotor-swept area, including negative shear and wind speed inversions. title: TYPOLOGY OF CALENDAR YEARS AND THERMAL REGIME DYNAMICS UNDER GLOBAL WARMING: RISK ASSESSMENT FOR ALMATY
abstract: The aim of this work was to develop a statistically substantiated typology of thermal conditions of calendar years for Almaty and a quantitative analysis of its transformation against the background of ongoing climate change. A two-stage approach was used for the study. The first stage: dimensionality reduction using principal component analysis (PCA) followed by k-means clustering to identify integral year types. title: Anthropogenic aerosol reduction contributes to faster flash drought onset in a changing climate
abstract: Flash droughts have emerged as severe hazards, posing growing challenges to natural and socioeconomic systems, yet the influence of recent aerosol reductions on their onset remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impacts of aerosols and their underlying mechanisms using multi-source observations and large-ensemble climate simulations. Lower aerosol levels are increasingly linked to severe soil moisture deficits, with aerosol effects on onset-speed variability intensifying across 69.2% of regions. title: Assessing the Sustainability Performance of Fishing Harbors Under Uncertainty: A Gaussian‐Neutrosophic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Fishing harbors are increasingly required to meet sustainability expectations associated with the environmental, social, and economic development goals. Accordingly, assessing their sustainability performance has become an important concern for both policymakers, harbor operating organizations, and harbor managers. This study develops a decision support system (DSS) within a neutrosophic environment to evaluate the sustainability performance of small‐scale fishing harbors. title: Anthropogenic aerosol forcing of European windstorms in CMIP6 climate models
abstract: A recently developed set of historical storm reconstructions were extensively validated by insurance loss data and revealed how European windstorm damages were three times higher in the 1980s and '90s compared to a few decades before and since. A better understanding of these slower fluctuations could improve how this costly risk is managed. Here, we explore the impacts of anthropogenic aerosols (AA) on European property damage using results from DAMIP (Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project) climate model experiments. journal: Natural hazards and earth system sciences

title: Simulating jökulhlaups from an ice-marginal lake within a 2D model of subglacial drainage and basal sliding
abstract: Abstract. Ice-marginal lakes are an increasingly common feature of glacierised landscapes, and their sudden drainage beneath glaciers (a jökulhlaup) can threaten downstream communities and infrastructure. Numerous efforts to model jökulhlaups have been made, however, because these models are 1D representations of a single channel connected to a lake, they cannot simulate lateral jökulhlaup propagation through the subglacial system. title: European Climate Signals in Water Budget Dynamics
abstract: Monitoring the water budget helps us understand and manage the available water in a specific area, as well as track its use. Knowing the water budget (i.e., the difference between water inflow and outflow) allows us to predict water shortages or surpluses. In these times of climate change, the risk of extreme events such as droughts and floods is rising. The study considered the area of the European continent, classified according to the Koppen-Geiger climate zones, as it features a highly diverse climate. title: Interlocking, rearrangement and progressive failure in rubble‑mound breakwaters
abstract: Rubble-mound breakwater stability is commonly assessed through Hudson- and Van der Meer-type empirical formulae, which relate wave loading, armour properties and geometry to global stability and damage parameters. These formulae remain the design basis, but they do not explicitly describe how inter-block contacts reorganise under repeated wave loading. A testable contact-network interpretation of progressive rubble-mound failure is developed here. The armour layer is treated as a granular assembly whose load-carrying capacity depends on the redundancy and persistence of load-bearing contacts.

title: Dependence of Neutralized Charge Amount on Meteorological Conditions in Summertime Lightning Discharges in Japan
abstract: Abstract Lightning discharges in Gunma Prefecture, Japan, from June–September 2023 were analyzed to explore the dependence of the neutralized charge amount on cloud structures embedded in weather systems, mainly based on in situ measurements of the ground‐based electric field, radar and satellite remote sensing, and numerical simulations using a bulk lightning model. title: Spaceborne multi-sensor tracking reveals hydrologic decoupling during the record-breaking Sahara flood
abstract: Satellite remote sensing enables large-scale quantification of extreme hydrologic events in data-scarce regions, yet the integration of multi-sensor observations to resolve hydrologic responses remains limited. The record-breaking 2024 Sahara flood presents a unique opportunity to evaluate satellite-based characterisation of hydrologic extremes in hyper-arid environments. By integrating multi-sensor satellite observations of precipitation, surface inundation, and terrestrial water storage, we provide a comprehensive assessment of this event’s hydrologic scope. title: Quantifying Groundwater–Surface Water Exchange on a River Island: A Comparative Analysis of Direct and Indirect Methods
abstract: Abstract Groundwater–surface water exchange is a key hydrological process that governs river water quality and aquatic ecosystems. However, the quantification of such exchange remains uncertain, especially within river island aquifers where exchange processes are highly heterogeneous. In this study, direct seepage meter measurements and indirect Darcy‐based estimates of exchange fluxes were compared under consistent spatiotemporal conditions within the aquifer of Jungsa Island, a river island in the lower West Nakdong River, South Korea. title: Economic-boom-driven electricity demand linked to urban air pollution and health in India
abstract: Abstract Rapid economic growth in India since 2000 has been accompanied by rising electricity demand and worsening urban air pollution. Here we show that a threefold increase in GDP per capita was associated with a nearly fourfold rise in electricity demand, with coal supplying approximately 76% of total generation. This coal-dependent expansion increased energy-sector SO 2 emissions and contributed to a twofold increase in urban aerosol loading, with sulfate accounting for approximately 46% of the urban aerosol burden. title: Process based modelling of breaker bar evolution with submerged vegetation under regular waves
abstract: This study investigates how submerged vegetation influences breaker bar development using the process based IH2VOF-SED model, which couples a two-dimensional vertical Reynolds averaged Navier–Stokes solver with sediment transport and bed evolution. The model is evaluated against laboratory measurements for bare and vegetated beach profiles under regular erosive waves. It reproduces the principal measured features of wave transformation, pointwise velocity signals, and beach-profile evolution, although agreement varies among cases and variables. title: Explainable AI-based spatial downscaling and water balance-guided temporal disaggregation of GRACE terrestrial water storage anomalies over the Ganges River Basin
abstract: GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) observe terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA), but their coarse resolution and monthly sampling limit direct use at finer scales. We develop a GRACE-constrained framework for the Ganges River Basin that refines the JPL RL06 mascon product to 0.1° and disaggregates it to daily values while preserving the monthly storage constraint. Mascon-specific level and long-term trend are retained from GRACE, whereas the residual anomaly is modelled from ERA5-Land hydroclimatic variables and static covariates, keeping observed and inferred information separable. title: In Situ Measurement of Dust Particle Transport to the Tropopause Layer over the Northern Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Abstract Previous satellite observations and simulations have shown that dust particles can be transported to the upper troposphere, but there is very little evidence from in situ observations. This study provides the first balloon-borne measurements of dust particle transport to the tropopause layer during a dust event over the northern Tibetan Plateau (TP). title: Assessment of Small-Scale Wind Power under Different Climatic Conditions in Aliero, Northwestern Nigeria
abstract: The endemic electricity shortage across the counties in Nigeria requires continuous progress in renewable electricity in mix of electricity sources in Nigeria. The rapid increase in installed capacity of wind power requires continuous progress in wind power prediction techniques in addressing the intermittent effect of wind in electricity generation, which is address in the novel approach adopted in this research. title: Hydro-morphological investigations on local scour around inclined piles under wave conditions
abstract: Scouring is a problem that should be considered while designing bridges; scour around inclined piles in the presence of waves has rarely been researched. However, in reality, many inclined braces are used for aesthetic reasons, which alters the flow properties depending on their exposure to the flow field. The purpose of this work is to numerically examine the flow behavior and local scour evolution around inclined piles downstream under wave conditions. title: Mediterranean cyclones from pre-industrial to future climate: changes in extreme wind, precipitation and compound precipitation–wind events
abstract: Abstract. The Mediterranean storm track is characterized by small but intense cyclones that can cause extreme weather events across the region. Thus the aim of this study is to investigate the impact of future climate change on extreme wind, precipitation and compounding cyclones. Using a regional climate model simulation, we show that the mean cyclone frequency is reduced by roughly a third in the Mediterranean by the end of the 21st century under the representative concentration pathway RCP8.5. title: The Growing Role of Evaporative Demand in Driving Record‐Breaking Droughts in the Amazon Basin
abstract: Abstract Amazon droughts have historically been driven by precipitation deficits, but recent escalating drought events highlight a regime shift toward “hot droughts.” By decomposing historical drought drivers (1979–2024), we show that rising evaporative demand (represented by potential evapotranspiration, PET) now acts as a primary driver of drought intensification. While rainfall deficits remain the dominant contributor to the record‐breaking 2024 drought, escalating atmospheric thirst almost doubled its severity. title: Global climate impact of land-surface change driven by radiative effects
abstract: Abstract A robust proportionality between radiative forcing and global-mean temperature has been established for most climate drivers. However, land-surface changes are considered an exception due to their potential to alter surface hydrology, introducing non-radiative effects that may rival those from surface albedo changes. title: Physics-guided thermal infrared and multispectral fusion for Land surface temperature monitoring
abstract: Accurate land surface temperature (LST) monitoring increasingly depends on the integration of complementary Earth observation modalities. Thermal infrared observations provide direct evidence of land-atmosphere energy exchange and night-time thermal patterns, whereas optical and multispectral imagery supplies land-cover, vegetation, and structural context. title: Long-term climatology of vertical profiles of polarimetric variables and ice-microphysical retrievals at X-band – Part 1: Radar calibration
abstract: Abstract. In a two-part series of papers, a climatology of quasi-vertical profiles (QVPs) of polarimetric variables and ice-microphysical retrievals such as ice water content, total number concentration and mean volume diameter is presented. QVPs are generated from plan position indicator scans at 18° elevation angle measured with the X-band radar located in the city of Bonn in western Germany between 2013 and 2023. title: A State‐of‐the‐Art Study of Vortex‐Excited Vibration Problems in Large‐Span Flat Steel Box Girder Bridges
abstract: ABSTRACT Windborne vibration of large‐span bridges occurs from time to time, especially the abnormal windborne vibration of urban bridges, which often causes public panic. The paper consists of four parts. Specifically, the first part analyzes the wind challenges of large‐span bridges, including the formation mechanism of wind‐induced vibration disaster of large‐span bridges and typical cases, as well as the limitations of the current wind design codes. title: Satellite evidence of unequal basin-scale recovery from severe droughts
abstract: Abstract Severe droughts deplete terrestrial water storage, jeopardizing ecosystems and human well-being. Yet, the pace and extent to which large river basins recover from such events remain unknown at the global scale. Here, integrating GRACE/FO water storage observations with state-of-the-art water availability estimates, we disentangle hydrological recovery following 468 basin-scale severe droughts with discernible impacts globally from 2003 to 2025. title: Improved multi-class drought classification through climate data analysis and advanced imbalanced data handling
abstract: Study region The Urmia Lake Basin, a terminal endorheic system in semi-arid northwestern Iran, faces severe hydrological decline. 51 years of monthly precipitation records (1971–2021) from four upper sub-basin rain gauges are analyzed alongside 11 climate teleconnections. Study focus Detecting rare, extreme drought events in terminal basins is frequently hindered by class imbalance in historical hydroclimatic records, biasing machine learning classifiers toward normal conditions. title: Framework for systematic monitoring of roadside litter emission and transport at the river catchment scale
abstract: The negative impact of macrolitter, especially plastics, on ecosystems is well known. River catchments serve as critical environmental conduits, transporting water alongside natural and anthropogenic sediment from terrestrial features, such as slopes and terraces, into aquatic ecosystems including river channels and floodplains. Existing literature shows that riverine macrolitter transport is increasingly well understood, whereas local terrestrial sources and delivery pathways remain underexplored. title: Probabilistic fatigue assessment and optimal heading design of FOWT mooring systems under wind–wave misalignment
abstract: Floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) mooring fatigue accumulates under ordinary operating conditions, where wind and waves are often misaligned. Previous studies typically represent this misalignment by a relative angle or a few fixed directional cases. Yet the three-line mooring is directionally anisotropic, making fairlead fatigue dependent on the absolute wind and wave directions. This study develops a probabilistic fatigue framework that preserves absolute directionality and exploits it to optimize platform heading. abstract: Abstract. Aerosol particles contain complex mixtures of polar and non-polar species that can undergo organic-inorganic phase separations. In phase-separated aerosol particles, the phase state of the outer organic coating can modulate heterogeneous chemistry. Heterogeneous chemistry leading to isoprene epoxydiol (IEPOX)-derived secondary organic aerosol (IEPOX-SOA) is encoded in the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model and has been the focus of previous aerosol phase separation and phase state work. title: Macroscopic and mesoscopic mechanical behavior of the interface between piles and unsaturated sand under vertical cyclic loading
abstract: Understanding the degradation of pile bearing capacity under vertical cyclic loading requires an in-depth investigation of the pile–unsaturated sand interface. This study employs a multi-scale approach—combining visualized cyclic loading tests, particle image velocimetry (PIV), and discrete element method (DEM) simulations—to elucidate the underlying macro–meso evolutionary mechanisms. title: Impact of VR-based climate change education on awareness and water use behavior
abstract: Climate change has increased the need for effective educational approaches that can promote climate-related awareness and environmentally responsible behaviors. This study investigates the effects of a passive 360-degree virtual reality educational intervention on climate change awareness and operational water consumption in a real industrial setting. The study was conducted with 17 cafeteria workers at an operating factory in Türkiye. title: H2CHAIN: Integrated Web Platform for Energy-Balance-Constrained Planning of Green Hydrogen Value Chains
abstract: Planning a green hydrogen project couples siting, generation, electrolysis, storage, conversion and cost decisions that are usually assessed in separate tools. This paper presents an integrated web-based decision-support platform for the planning and analysis of green hydrogen value chains. The platform combines geospatial analysis, techno-economic modeling, and system-level scenario assessment within a modular architecture that is accessible through a standard web browser. title: Salinity-driven controls on arsenic mobility in naturally coated sands: multi-mineral sorption, kinetic limitations, and metal-facilitated transport
abstract: Arsenic mobility in groundwater is sensitive to hydrodynamic and hydrochemical perturbations, yet the coupled mechanisms controlling arsenic transport in natural sands remain poorly constrained. This study uses a series of column experiments, combined with chemical extractions, surface microscopy, and reactive transport modeling, to explore how transient pore-water chemistry and co-existing mineral surfaces in sandy porous media control arsenate transport under oxic conditions. title: Prediction of Electric Arc Furnace End‐Point Temperature via Fusion of Physical Mechanism and Stacking Ensemble
abstract: Accurate endpoint temperature prediction in electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking is critical for energy efficiency and product quality; however, it remains fundamentally challenged by severe nonlinearity and dynamic variations. Traditional machine learning models lack interpretability and robustness against industrial noise, whereas purely mechanistic models fail to capture nonlinear deviations. title: An approximately 70-year core-related modulation of Earth rotation and its implications for the leap second
abstract: Recent observations of Universal Time (UT1) indicate an acceleration in Earth’s rotation. If sustained under the current leap-second framework, this behavior could eventually prompt consideration of a negative leap second. We examine whether the recent acceleration is consistent with an approximately 70-year, core-related modulation of length of day (LOD). title: Evaluation of different equations of state for simulating fluid-solid interaction with the material point method
abstract: The simulation fidelity of Fluid–Structure Interaction (FSI) is critical for predicting multi-phase (solid-liquid-gas) interactions that involve large deformations and failure evolution. While the Material Point Method (MPM) offers a robust numerical procedure for those problems, the choice of the Equation of State (EOS) for weakly compressible fluids remains a subject of compromise between computational accuracy and efficiency. title: Enhanced WCSPH modelling of 2-D and 3-D granular flows using μ(I) rheology with rheology-aware boundary treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a weakly compressible smoothed particle hydrodynamics (WCSPH) framework for granular materials incorporating δ -SPH pressure stabilization, μ ( I ) rheology, a rheology-consistent extrapolated boundary condition (EBC), and a rheology-aware particle shifting technique (PST). title: Vision-assisted optimization of coagulation–flocculation parameters using a joint YOLOv11 and U-Net + + framework
abstract: This study investigates a defined coagulation–flocculation–sedimentation unit for variable-composition chemical wastewater rather than treating wastewater treatment as a single universal process. A joint YOLOv11 and U-Net + + perception model was developed to identify suspended particles, oil films, flocs, and foam and to quantify their spatial coverage before periodic adjustment of pH, flocculant dosage, and hydraulic retention time. title: Fire carbon emission constraints from space-based carbon monoxide retrievals during the 2019 intense burning season in Brazil
abstract: Abstract. In 2019, Brazil experienced an intensive fire season, despite the absence of major climate anomalies to enhance fire activity. Existing carbon monoxide (CO) emission estimates from state-of-the-art fire emission inventories differ by a factor two for the period and region. abstract: This study assessed flood hazard and risk in Semarang City, where increasing hydrometeorological pressures and rapid urban development have heightened flood impacts. abstract: Abstract We present a revisited Cartesian-diver experiment in which a small air-filled balloon, loaded with a metal sphere and plasticine, undergoes a metastable sinking motion in a water column. title: Model output statistics for enhancing dynamically downscaled temperature prediction from FuXi-ENS over South Korea
abstract: While machine learning (ML) weather models are emerging as promising tools for predicting weather conditions on a global scale, their coarse resolution and systematic biases limit practical applicability in regional contexts. This paper assesses the role of model output statistics (MOS) in post-processing temperature ensemble forecasts that are dynamically downscaled from the state-of-the-art ML weather model FuXi-ENS. title: Hydrodynamic and ecological modeling for water quality assessment in Lake Qaroun, Egypt
abstract: Lake Qaroun is a closed saline lake located in Fayoum Depression in Egypt. The hexagon figures, found in the Summary for Policymakers (SPM), were a key part of this presentation. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric non‐methane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) are important trace species with anthropogenic and natural sources including fugitive emissions from fossil fuel mining and distribution, biomass burning, biofuel combustion, and biogenic emissions from microbes and plants. abstract: Abstract. abstract: This study explores how corrosion unfolds in aluminium hybrid structures created by integrating Selective Laser Melting (SLM) with conventional casting techniques. title: Relationship of tropical cyclone wind-field and cloud-band metrics with extreme rainfall events over Mexico
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) are the most important hydrometeorological phenomena affecting Mexico, accounting for approximately 86.5% of the country’s most costly disasters, where extreme rainfall is the main TC-associated hazard. This study analyzes two TC size metrics during the 2000–2024 period: R34, defined as the mean radius of 34-kt winds, and ROCLOUD, a satellite-derived metric that represents the spatial extent of TC cloud bands. abstract: Accurate forecasting of net electrical power output (PE) in Combined Cycle Power Plants (CCPP) is a requisite for grid stability and strategic bidding in deregulated energy markets. While Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) architectures offer superior predictive precision compared to traditional physical simulations, their black-box opacity often hinders industrial adoption. abstract: Abstract Recent work has demonstrated that convection‐permitting models often produce a greater number of precipitating convective cells compared to radar observations. Congestus‐depth cells contribute most to the bias, which are colloquially termed “popcorn convection.” This study explores warm‐phase microphysical contributions to the bias using simulations spanning a field campaign hosted in the mountains of central Argentina. abstract: Abstract Long-term soil temperature changes in high-latitude regions have been reported mainly focusing on the near-surface air and sub-surface soil temperature because of limited observational data. This gap still obscures spatiotemporal changes and associated processes of vertical thermal changes at multiple soil layers over such climate-sensitive regions. abstract: Reliable precipitation and streamflow data are essential for hydrological modelling and water resources management, yet observational networks in many African regions remain sparse. abstract: Sensitive skin is shaped by intrinsic physiology and environmental exposures, yet how concurrent lifestyle factors modulate its expression remains poorly characterized. This study examined how differing environmental and lifestyle conditions influence sensitive skin phenotypes through clinical evaluation, biophysical measurements, and biomarker profiling. abstract: Abstract Compound climate vulnerability—the geographic co-location of climate exposure, concentrated employment and residential socio-economic disadvantage—remains methodologically underdeveloped at the sub-municipal scales required for operational adaptation planning. abstract: Drought is a significant climate-related hazard in Sierra Leone due to the countrys reliance on seasonal rainfall, rain-fed agriculture, and climate-sensitive water resources. abstract: Abstract A strong westerly wind burst (WWB) event that occurred from November 6 to 16, 2023 has been suggested to have substantially influenced the development of the strong 2023/24 El Niño, yet the mechanisms governing its genesis remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract This study investigated scour-induced degradation of shallow and intermediate strip foundations subjected to vertical, horizontal, and moment loading using adaptive finite element limit analysis. title: Global Characterization of Precipitation Peaks in the Seasonal Cycle
abstract: Abstract Precipitation seasonality is commonly described using wet and dry periods, but this framework can obscure multiple rainfall maxima within a rainy season. Here we introduce a global framework for identifying the number of precipitation peaks (NPP) during rainy periods from daily precipitation using optimal harmonic seasonal fits and reproducible peak‐selection criteria. abstract: Abstract We investigate the role of the elasticity and density of the forearc mantle wedge corner on the stress distribution in the forearc region of subduction zones, using numerical quasi‐2D lithospheric deformation models for the Cascadia, Nankai, NE Japan, and Costa Rica subduction zones. title: Applications of Earth Observation for Monitoring and Management of Natural Hazards and Emergency Situations in Central Asia
abstract: Central Asia is highly vulnerable to a wide range of natural hazards due to its complex mountainous terrain, glacierized catchments, and highly variable climate. Hazards such as glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs), mudflows, snow avalanches, river floods, and droughts pose significant risks to communities, infrastructure, and water resources across the region. title: Discrepancies in Extreme Daily and Monthly Precipitation Trends Between Observations and Earth System Models
abstract: Abstract While extreme precipitation is expected to intensify globally in a warming climate, changes in extreme precipitation on regional scales remain uncertain. To understand how well Earth system models (ESMs) capture recent changes in regional extreme precipitation, we compare trends in daily and monthly extreme precipitation across multiple observational data sets and three ESM ensembles. title: Inter-station measurements redundancy and bias structure for optimising closely spaced radiosonde thermodynamic profiling networks
abstract: Accurate and internally consistent radiosonde temperature and relative humidity profiles are fundamental to numerical weather prediction (NWP), boundary-layer studies, climate monitoring, and satellite data validation. However, in closely spaced upper-air profiling networks, unresolved inter-station redundancy and systematic bias structures may obscure true atmospheric variability and complicate evidence-based station spacing decisions. title: Understanding Heat Waves in Rajasthan: Spatio‐Temporal Analysis, Hazard Assessment, and Hotspot Mapping
abstract: ABSTRACT Heat waves (HWs) cause substantial loss of life and economic damage globally, and in Rajasthan, India's most climatologically exposed state, their intense and prolonged nature poses a severe threat to human health. Despite this, comprehensive studies examining heat wave (HW) characteristics, hotspot identification, and management frameworks for Rajasthan remain scarce. abstract: Paediatric asthma hospitalisations have marked seasonal peaks, but it remains unclear whether associations with environmental exposures vary under different local climatic conditions. This study aimed to quantify regional- and season-specific associations between environmental factors and paediatric asthma hospitalisations. abstract: Abstract Near-surface (10-m) wind speed over land decreased on average over the Northern Hemisphere between 1980 and 2010, a phenomenon that has become known as global stilling. We show that the multi-model decadal predictions are able to capture the aforementioned decrease in wind speed from one to ten years ahead. abstract: This study developed and evaluated a spatial consistency quality-control method for daily surface air temperature observations from 186 SYNOP stations across Vietnam during 1961–2023. The variables examined included daily mean (Tavg), minimum (Tmin), and maximum (Tmax) temperatures. The proposed framework combines inverse distance weighting (IDW) with a machine-learning (ML) model. title: Increasing Extreme Negative Vegetation Responses to Drought‐Related Compound Events
abstract: ABSTRACT Vegetation growth is increasingly threatened by both extreme climate events and anthropogenic disturbances. Although considerable attention has been given to detecting large‐scale vegetation anomalies, comprehensive analyses of the spatiotemporal dynamics of negative extreme anomalies in vegetation growth (NEGs) and their underlying drivers remain limited. abstract: Sloshing dynamics in partially-filled rectangular tanks remains a computationally demanding phenomenon in applications such as tuned liquid dampers, largely due to high computational costs of using high-fidelity sloshing models. abstract: Abstract Drought impacts in large river basins depend not only on precipitation deficits but also on how terrestrial water storage (TWS) buffers climate anomalies through hydrological memory, which is the persistence of past storage conditions. abstract: Global seafood production generates millions of tonnes of nutrient-rich processing side-streams that remain underutilised despite their potential as sustainable sources of high-value compounds and renewable resources. This review critically examines emerging engineering strategies for transforming seafood residues into value-added products within the framework of the blue circular economy. abstract: Abstract. For analysing karst hydrogeological systems, observations of karst springs and cave drips are considered indispensable. title: Reliability Analysis of Electro-Swing Adsorption Carbon Capture Onboard Ships
abstract: The maritime sector accounts for approximately three percent of global greenhouse gas emissions, a share expected to increase in the coming decades. To comply with increasingly stringent emission regulations, onboard carbon capture (OCC) technologies are being investigated as a short- to medium-term mitigation option for existing ship fleets. abstract: This study aims to systematically analyze and evaluate the fault sealing properties in the Zhuhai Formation of the Pearl River Estuary Basin using an in-situ stress calculation model. abstract: Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is a core indicator for quantifying atmospheric pollution, and its spatiotemporal variation is strongly influenced by meteorological factors, including water vapor, a critical driver of atmospheric moisture transport and energy balance. title: Research on the reliability assessment method for Gas Insulated Switchgear based on composite risk assessment model
abstract: Fault diagnosis in safety–critical industrial infrastructure is often hindered by the data scarcity of catastrophic failures and subjective uncertainty inherent in domain knowledge. abstract: Abstract Communities around the globe are experiencing great difficulty in constraining their water consumption within the limits of available, renewable freshwater supplies. abstract: Abstract The Lancang–Mekong River Basin (LMRB), a crucial transboundary region that sustains millions of people across Southeast Asia, faces growing threats from compound hydrological extremes under climate change. title: Changing Antecedent Land‐Surface Conditions Can Amplify Future Heat Extremes Across New Zealand
abstract: Abstract Extreme heat in New Zealand is projected to intensify faster than mean warming, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Using dynamically downscaled CMIP6 projections, we investigate whether land–surface moisture constraints contributes to future heat‐extreme intensification in a maritime climate. title: Urbanization-Induced Groundwater Contamination in Barjisiyah Area, Southern Iraq: Hydrochemical, Isotopic, and Microbial Assessment
abstract: Recent urbanization and overexploitation have significantly degraded groundwater quality in the shallow unconfined aquifer in Barjisiyah. The study area is located within the discharge area and is exposed to natural salinization from the underlying layer and anthropogenic sources with limited rainfall recharge. Six groundwater samples have been collected from the unconfined aquifer across urbanized zones. title: Modelling of blade root and tip losses in horizontal axis wind turbines
abstract: This study investigates how alternative blade-root and blade-tip loss corrections influence steady aerodynamic predictions for a 200-kW horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT) within a Blade Element Momentum (BEM) framework. A controlled comparison is performed using theoretical, semi-empirical, and performance-based loss formulations and three related RISØ-A1 blade configurations. title: UTILIZATION OF BRACKISH WATER IN AGRICULTURE: POTENTIALS, CHALLENGES, AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: Brackish water offers compelling opportunities for agricultural use, especially in regions experiencing water scarcity and limited freshwater resources. However, its utilization requires careful supervision, considering factors such as crop salinity tolerance and soil composition to prevent adverse effects. Utilizing brackish water reduces yield of salt sensitive crops; however, strategic measures such as efficient leaching, blending with freshwater, and selecting salt tolerant crop varieties can mitigate these impacts. title: Anticipatory Smart Governance: Public Policy Strategy for Urbanization Mitigation and Public Services in the IKN Buffer Zone
abstract: The relocation of Indonesia's capital to the Nusantara Capital City (IKN) has fundamentally transformed the administrative and socio-economic landscape of Balikpapan City as its primary buffer zone and gateway. This study addresses the core research problem of how local government institutional capacity and public service frameworks adapt to rapid urbanization pressures driven by national-scale capital relocation. title: Satellite-based global monitoring of urban-scale methane emissions
abstract: Abstract. Quantifying and understanding methane emissions of cities are of great importance given their role in current and future mitigation efforts to combat climate changing emissions. However, it remains challenging to routinely and accurately characterize and verify city-scale methane emission inventories. Previous studies of urban methane emissions have employed a range of emission quantification methods, leading to inconsistent estimates and different associated uncertainties. title: Advancing grapevine phenology predictions: a comparison of regression-based statistical learning approach and conventional models in mediterranean environment
abstract: Climate conditions can significantly affect plant dormancy and growing season, impacting crop development and its productivity. Temperature is considered the primary driver of grapevine phenology, with endodormancy and ecodormancy largely regulated by chilling and forcing accumulations, respectively. title: Global Inequality and Potential Trade‐Offs in Community Resilience to Compound Climate Extremes
abstract: Abstract The resilience of human society to multiple climate disasters is crucial for supporting sustainable development progress and promoting human well‐being in an era of climate change. Yet little research has attempted to assess global spatial‐explicit capacity of communities to deal with compound extreme climate disasters simultaneously, and the relationship between resilience to different climate extremes remains unknown. abstract: Bridgmanite, the main mineralogical phase in the Earth's lower mantle, is intrinsically anisotropic and may therefore generate seismic anisotropy in actively-deforming regions, particularly subduction zones. The bulk of the lower mantle is widely regarded as well-mixed but recent seismic observations suggest structures at mid-mantle depths whose origin remains unclear. title: Ecosystem Complexity and Climate Adaptation in Oman: Climate-Water-Ecosystem Nexus
abstract: This study examines the relationships among climate variability, water-related variables, and vegetation dynamics across the Sultanate of Oman. Using six decades of climatic and hydrological data, the study evaluates long-term climate variability patterns, identifies the main climatic and ecohydrological factors associated with native vegetation dynamics, and proposes a Climate–Water–Ecosystem framework to explore interactions, trade-offs, and synergies within arid environments. title: The Altitude Effect of Stable Isotopes in Rivers Over the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Abstract The altitude effect of stable isotopes in river water is key to paleoelevation reconstruction, yet remains poorly quantified at regional scales due to monitoring challenges. This study compiled river water isotope data across the Tibetan Plateau and used a decision‐tree‐based random forest model to simulate high‐resolution δ 18 O patterns. We produced the first systematic, spatially explicit map of the δ 18 O altitude effect over the entire plateau, revealing strong spatial heterogeneity. title: Transtibial Bone-Anchored Prosthesis: Experimental and Theoretical Study
abstract: In this study, an experimental and numerical approach is used to evaluate a transtibial bone-anchored prosthesis system that includes an osseointegration implant composed of Ti-6Al-7Nb. The work addresses three factors that are critical to clinical and biomechanical performance: (1) the mechanical properties and corrosion behavior of the implant materials, (2) enhancement of bioactivity via hydroxylapatite (HAp) surface coatings, and (3) structural response of the tibia-implant construct under physiologically representative gait loads. title: Localized analysis of Cloudburst dynamics over Indian Himalayan Region during 2022
abstract: In this research, the focus is on examining the occurrence of localized Cloudburst events in the Indian Himalayan region (IHR). Specifically, in the year 2022, a total of 66 cloudburst cases were observed in the region, indicating a rise in the severity of extreme rainfall events (ERE) in recent times. Due to limited information and awareness, the mountainous hazards often go unnoticed. title: Forecasting European temperature-related mortality in Summer 2024: data-driven vs. physics-based forecast approaches
abstract: Abstract. Heat has emerged as a major public health concern. Over 62,000 heat-related deaths were estimated to have occurred during the European summer of 2024, exemplifying the pressing need to develop effective early warning systems. Such systems depend critically on the quality of the underlying forecasts, and recent work has focused on developing impact-based forecasts for heat-related mortality, which provide impact-oriented information. title: The Three Musketeers of Coevolutionary Circular Design
abstract: ABSTRACT The transition from a linear to a circular economy necessitates systemic changes in product design, data sharing, and material flows. Applying a coevolutionary framework, this study shows how these three dimensions interact dynamically in circular economy transitions. Drawing on semi‐structured interviews with experts in sustainability, procurement, R&D, and suppliers engaged in circular product design, we analyze the mutual adaptation of product design practices, data sharing initiatives, and material flows within three industrial companies. title: Physics-guided interpretable ensemble learning for daily reference evapotranspiration estimation in arid regions
abstract: Dependable estimates of reference evapotranspiration (ETo) are fundamental to managing water sustainably across arid regions, yet conventional empirical methods have limited capacity to represent the complex non-linear interactions among meteorological variables governing ETo dynamics. This study develops a physics-guided interpretable ensemble learning framework that integrates rule-based (RuleFit) modeling, Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Generalized Simulated Annealing (GenSA) optimization, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). title: Digital Transformation for Enhancing Port Competitiveness, Resilience, and Sustainability: Evidence from Tanjung Perak Port, Surabaya
abstract: Indonesian ports are under sustained pressure to reduce dwelling time, logistics costs, and environmental exposure while maintaining operational resilience in the face of supply chain disruptions. This study examines digital transformation as a strategic intervention influencing port competitiveness, resilience, and sustainability. A qualitative case study was conducted at Tanjung Perak Port, Surabaya, using policy documents, operational reports, and observations of digital systems implemented during the 2019–2024 period. title: Fairytale Physics
abstract: A careful analysis of generally accepted physical theories, most of which are included in physics textbooks, shows that they are often purely mechanistic and therefore poorly correspond to reality. As a result, it turns out that both scientists and graduates of educational institutions are essentially both carriers and disseminators of distorted ideas about the real world. In an attempt to draw attention to this state of affairs, issues arising from attentive analysis of some generally accepted physical theories or their practical application are discussed here.

The impact of climate change on human health and pharmaceuticals
abstract: Climate change and air pollution affect every major organ system, altering both the disease burden and patient responses to pharmaceutical treatments. However, current knowledge on how health systems, patients, healthcare professionals, and governments should prepare for these challenges remains fragmented. This review synthesises evidence on the potential impact of climate change on human health and pharmaceuticals, with the aim of identifying the diseases, populations, and medications most vulnerable, and assessing potential implications for pharmacotherapy. abstract: The stability of tunnel surrounding rock in deep-mine fault fracture zones is poor, significantly affecting safe and efficient mining operations. Thus, exploring the deformation and failure mechanisms of tunnel surrounding rock and researching reinforcement measures for tunnels passing through fault zones are important. title: Path planning for logistics UAVs considering energy consumption and safety under wind field uncertainty
abstract: Wind disturbances at low altitudes increase energy consumption and safety risks for multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in densely built urban environments. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is too expensive for online path planning, while threshold methods represent hazardous regions as binary no-fly zones. abstract: Abstract Subseasonal-to-seasonal precipitation forecasts are highly relevant for a wide range of practical applications and risk management, but their skill decreases substantially at longer lead times. Although statistical post-processing is widely regarded as a key step for improving forecast reliability, the skill of post-processed daily precipitation forecasts up to one month remains poorly quantified at a global scale. abstract: A evolução da topografia após o término dos processos orogênicos responsáveis pela formação de cadeias montanhosas tem intrigado as geociências há mais de um século. title: Future Urban Heat Risk Assessment in Sydney: Integrating Satellite-Derived UTCI with Population Projections
abstract: Urban heat stress poses an intensifying public health challenge in Australian cities, with Sydney facing increasingly severe summer thermal conditions. We present a reproducible framework for metropolitan-scale future heat risk assessment that integrates satellite-derived Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) with demographic projections to 2031. title: Groundwater regulates the spatial pattern of photosynthesis in the contiguous United States
abstract: Abstract Plants can access water stored in aquifers to sustain their activity, releasing moisture into the atmosphere—a critical survival mechanism during drought. Understanding the role of groundwater in regulating photosynthesis is thus key for modelling land-atmosphere interactions. However, the contribution of groundwater to spatial variation in mean annual photosynthesis remains poorly quantified, particularly relative to well-known factors like climatic aridity. abstract: This study investigates the synergistic effects of abrasive concentration and WC grain size on the cavitation erosion behavior of cemented carbide (WC-Co). abstract: La actual pérdida de la biodiversidad demanda ciudadanos capaces de comprender y actuar frente a problemas ambientales complejos, por lo que es necesario formarlos en dicho sentido desde edades tempranas. Este estudio explora el potencial del Pensamiento Computacional (PC) y la Realidad Extendida (XR) como herramientas innovadoras para la enseñanza y el aprendizaje de la biodiversidad. Mediante una revisión sistemática apoyada en plataformas digitales (Litmaps y NotebookLM), se identificaron y analizaron aplicaciones, beneficios y desafíos de ambas metodologías. title: Twenty years of Kilimanjaro observations across 5000 m reveal tropical elevation-dependent warming under clear-sky conditions
abstract: Abstract Mountain regions are experiencing rapid climate change. However, temperature trends along elevation gradients remain poorly understood in the tropics, where long-term high-elevation air temperature ( T air ) observations are sparse. Here, we examine elevation-dependent warming (EDW) on Mount Kilimanjaro by combining a unique long-term in situ T air transect with Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) land-surface temperature (LST), surface and topographic datasets. Using machine learning, we map clear-sky T air at four MODIS overpasses at 1 km resolution for 2004–2024.

abstract: Implicit information on land use conflicts in territorial spatial planning texts directly affects the coordination and implementability of planning schemes. Traditional manual interpretation approaches have low efficiency, high omission rates, and inadequate standardization, making them difficult to use for full-process review of massive multi-source planning texts under multi-plan integration. title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of vegetation responses to compound drought and heatwave events in Central Asia
abstract: With climate warming intensifying, compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events have become more frequent and intense in arid Central Asia, severely affecting vegetation growth. However, systematic quantitative assessments of vegetation responses and their drivers under such compound extremes remain limited. Using meteorological and remote sensing data, we identified growing-season CDHW events across Central Asia from 1982 to 2023. title: Brief communication: Rise of the Guadalupe River – a multifaceted post event analysis of 4 July 2025, flood in Central Texas
abstract: Abstract. The flash flooding across Central Texas on July 4th, 2025, caused more than 130 fatalities and property losses exceeding 20 billion dollars. The objective of this study is to diagnose the drivers of this catastrophic event and to analyze the temporal variability in forecasting flood inundation dynamics in the hours leading up to and during the event. title: Dating the key structures of the Guge ancient city through integrated 14C and literary research
abstract: This study integrates AMS 14C dating of 12 plant specimens, Bayesian modeling, and Tibetan texts to establish the first high-resolution construction chronology for key structures of the Guge ancient city in western Tibet. To ensure chronological precision and mitigate the old-wood effect, sampling prioritized short-lived annual plants and the outermost growth layers of small-diameter timber. Radiocarbon data were processed using the IntCal20 calibration curve and constrained by independent historical termini ante quos derived from mural inscriptions and prayer texts. title: Observation, analysis and numerical simulation of a low-level windshear case at Beijing Daxing International Airport
abstract: A case of low level windshear at Beijing Daxing International Airport is studied in the present paper. It is related to the synoptic scale/mesoscale changes of the airflow pattern over northern China. The shear was captured well by the Doppler LIDAR at the airport and timely alerts had been issued. This study considers the technical feasibility of forecasting the shear feature using a high resolution numerical weather prediction model with a lead time of several hours. It turns out that the shear feature could be forecast well, and is generally consistent with the actual observations.

title: Dynamic Rupture Modeling with a Rate and State Friction Law in a Discontinuous Galerkin Method
abstract: Earthquake rupture modeling has proven to be a useful tool to understand the physics behind different slip sequences inferred from observations. title: Integration of fiber-optic sensors into wrought alloys using a confined rolling process
abstract: Abstract This study presents a novel confined hot rolling technique for embedding optical fiber sensors into wrought metallic components, with the goal of enabling real time strain monitoring in extreme environments such as advanced nuclear reactors. Finite element analysis (FEA) was used to investigate the stress-strain response of embedded fiber assemblies under various rolling conditions. title: Geostatistical and Spatial Clustering Analysis for Wildfire Monitoring in Türkiye
abstract: The wildfire situation has become increasingly dangerous to the eastern Mediterranean’s forest lands and human life. Among these are wildfires in Türkiye that have had one of the largest impacts on the country in the region. A pipeline consisting of five steps was applied using an integrated methodology to analyze MODIS Collection 6.1 data for the fires occurring in Türkiye during the three years of 2018 through 2020. abstract: The weld efficiency, fracture position and microstructure of dissimilar friction stir welded joints between Al-Mg and pure Fe, produced at rotational speeds of 300-1100 rpm and a constant welding speed of 100mm/min, were investigated using finite-element simulation, tensile tests, microhardness tests, scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) techniques. abstract: With the accelerated industrialization, the emission of emerging pollutants has increased in aquatic systems, which poses a risk to the integrity of ecosystems, water security and human health.
