abstract: This work addresses a common problem: technology projects often run late, go over budget, or fail because risks are found too late. Before this framework, managers relied on manual reports and gut feeling, which meant problems were spotted only after damage was done. We built a system that reads project data (like progress, defects, and team speed) every two weeks, uses machine learning to predict which projects are likely to delay, and explains why using simple scores. abstract: Abstract Biological invasions increasingly threaten tropical montane forests, yet the environmental drivers shaping invasion risk in African Afromontane landscapes remain poorly understood. Gishwati‐Mukura Biosphere Reserve in Rwanda exemplifies this challenge, where invasive species threaten forest recovery and native species conservation. abstract: Agricultural drainage networks increasingly function as distributed pollution control systems for mitigating non-point source phosphorus (P) export to aquatic ecosystems. However, the spatial heterogeneity of P retention and its specific drivers across varying ditch orders remain poorly understood, as most studies focus on isolated, single-order segments. abstract: Abstract Ratios of linear trends are used to measure amplification ratios for warming and cooling rates in atmospheric layers relative to the surface. title: Reliability Engineering Framework for Cloud Based Government and Financial Information Systems
abstract: The accelerated adoption of cloud computing by government institutions and financial organizations has transformed public service delivery, fiscal management, and financial intermediation. However, the migration of mission-critical information systems to cloud environments introduces complex reliability challenges with far-reaching implications for economic stability, public trust, and national security. abstract: Abstract Lightning is a major source of nitrogen oxide radicals (NO x ≡ NO + NO 2 ), but large uncertainties in NO x yields per flash hinder accurate quantification of emissions and impacts on oxidant chemistry. abstract: The increasing need for renewable energy has resulted in the swift proliferation of wind power, both onshore and offshore. In order for the adequate development of off shore wind industry, it is necessary to resolve some uncertainties with regards to foundation employed for these structures. With wind turbines becoming larger and more powerful, the need for strong, stable, and efficient foundation systems is more critical than ever. abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change projections for Mexico remain subject to substantial regional and inter‐model uncertainty, particularly for precipitation. Here, we assess 21st‐century changes in temperature and precipitation over Mexico using 36 CMIP6 models under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1‐2.6, SSP2‐4.5, SSP3‐7.0 and SSP5‐8.5). abstract: The rheological behavior of paste, particularly regarding pumpability and in-situ dispersion, is critical for the safe and efficient disposal of mine tailings using paste technology. Therefore, when designing paste mixtures, both rheological and physical mechanical properties must be well defined. The flow behavior of paste is mainly governed by the physical and chemical characteristics of the tailings, among which the particle size distribution (PSD) plays a decisive role. title: ENGLISH SLANG IN THE DIGITAL AGE: LEXICAL INNOVATION, PRAGMATIC CHANGE AND CROSS-PLATFORM VARIATION
abstract: This article examines contemporary English slang as a dynamic form of lexical innovation shaped by digital communication. Rather than treating social media as a neutral channel through which pre-existing slang is simply transmitted, the study approaches platforms as linguistic environments that influence the formation, circulation, reinterpretation, and partial normalization of slang units. abstract: Abstract Driven by the global energy transition and China's dual-carbon goals, oil and gas field development faces challenges in achieving sustainable development. Oilfield-geothermal co-development (OGC) offers a pathway for revitalizing mature oilfields and supplying low-carbon energy. This article describes the resource endowment, genetic mechanisms, and oil-heat-water co-occurrence relationships of geothermal resources in oilfields, examines the theory and key technologies for OGC, and proposes an integrated technical system. title: IoT-Based Instrumentation for Urban–Rural Thermal Comfort Assessment Using Temperature Humidity Index
abstract: Urbanization alters land surface characteristics and may contribute to the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, affecting outdoor thermal comfort. This study presents an Internet of Things (IoT)-based instrumentation system for microclimate monitoring and thermal comfort assessment using the Temperature-Humidity Index (THI). The system integrates calibrated DHT22 sensors, an ESP32 microcontroller, a 20×4 LCD, Firebase Realtime Database, and a web dashboard. abstract: The digital documentation of riverside cliff grottoes has long been hindered by acquisition blind spots caused by steep terrain and irregular cliff faces. Conventional close‑range photogrammetry relies on preset flight paths, which are difficult to safely execute in complex scenarios with vegetation occlusion and no available space for setup along the riverbank. title: Research on thermodynamic performance of a gas-steam combined cycle with rotating detonation combustion
abstract: Conventional gas-steam combined cycles are constrained by the substantial irreversibility of constant-pressure combustion, whereas integrating a rotating detonation combustor (RDC) may lower the turbine exhaust temperature and thereby impair the steam bottoming cycle. In this study, a thermodynamic model of a methane-fueled RDC-based gas-steam combined cycle is developed and compared with a conventional constant-pressure-combustion combined cycle. title: Probabilistic tropical cyclone rainfall generator for flood hazard assessment along the U.S. Atlantic and Gulf Coasts
abstract: Abstract Statistical tropical cyclone rainfall (TCR) models based on historical observations have the potential to support flood hazard assessment by efficiently generating rainfall fields for large ensembles of TC tracks. Despite efforts to improve the characterization of TCR, existing models exhibit limited performance. title: Self-Adaptive Edge-Intelligent IoT Framework for Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring and Predictive Control
abstract: Monitoring water quality is important for environmental safety and public health in places with fast-changing or unstable water conditions. Conventional monitoring approaches are slow to respond, not scalable, and lack real-time decision-making ability. To address these limitations, a research framework is proposed based on an intelligent edge-IoT architecture for real-time monitoring and assessment of water quality parameters. abstract: Abstract Understanding the spatial and seasonal redistribution of temperature and precipitation is essential for climate adaptation in arid regions. Although recent studies in Iraq have applied statistical downscaling and CMIP6 projections to selected watersheds and water-resource systems, province-scale assessments of how seasonal temperature and precipitation classes may spatially redistribute across Anbar Province under multi-model CMIP6 scenarios remain limited. title: Using climate models in climate assessments: a Bayesian perspective
abstract: Outputs from complex Earth system models (ESMs) participating in the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP) are a major source of information for policy-relevant assessments of climate change. The way we view and interpret the CMIP archive shapes our understanding of the real world, yet many assessments present analysis choices only implicitly. title: Deformation-enhanced fluid evolution and skarn–IOCG transition in the Paleoproterozoic Elaine Dorothy Cu–Au system, Mount Isa Inlier, Australia
abstract: Abstract The Elaine Dorothy Cu-Au deposit, located in the Mary Kathleen Domain of the Mount Isa Inlier, Australia, records the interaction of Paleoproterozoic skarn metasomatism, fluid evolution, and deformation. title: Dynamic Inference of Regional Traffic States in a Dense Waterway Using AIS Window Sequences
abstract: Regional vessel monitoring requires both a description of current traffic and an estimate of its near-term evolution. This study evaluates a lightweight approach to dynamic traffic-state inference using sequences of Automatic Identification System (AIS) observations. A lower Yangtze waterway case area is divided into spatial cells, and vessel-level observations are aggregated into 10-minute windows. abstract: The structural integrity of aging high-rise concrete infrastructure requires frequent, high-precision inspections, yet traditional manual methods remain heavily reliant on labor-intensive, costly, and inherently dangerous techniques such as gondolas or rope access. This research aims to address these critical industry challenges by developing an innovative, autonomous cyber-physical framework that integrates Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) tactile scanning with advanced Vision-Language AI Models (VLM). title: Beyond bare metal: Next-generation industrial control via resource slicing on commodity platforms
abstract: The adoption of virtualization/containerization technologies in industrial control systems promises improved deployment flexibility, scalability, and resource efficiency. However, migrating time-critical control logic to shared virtualized environments poses significant challenges in meeting strict real-time requirements. title: Non-stationary time series attribution for heatwaves over Europe
abstract: The increasing occurrence of extreme weather events since the beginning of the 21st century has led to the development of new methods to attribute extreme events to anthropogenic climate change. The way in which the extreme event is defined has a major influence on the attribution result. A frequently overlooked aspect concerns the temporal dependence of extremes. abstract: Abstract This study presents the digital documentation of traditional Fijian architectural heritage through an in-depth investigation of the bure , Fiji’s indigenous house, focusing on three distinct bure types in Navala village. title: Geometric priors for reinforcement learning-based multi-robot ecological monitoring
abstract: Autonomous ecological monitoring requires robotic systems capable of efficiently exploring large natural environments while minimizing redundant traversal under limited communication and partial environmental knowledge. Although reinforcement learning provides adaptive decision making for multi-robot exploration, sparse rewards often result in inefficient exploration and slow policy convergence. abstract: Post-microbial therapeutics is proposed here as an integrative, function-centered framework rather than a new therapeutic class. It asks whether a defined microbial perturbation can produce a reproducible change in a microbial function, biochemical output, and clinically relevant host phenotype. abstract: Natural hazards can adversely impact society, environment, and human well-being. The development of mitigation strategies is typically based on estimates of economic losses, but such estimates are difficult when high-resolution post-disaster data are scarce. abstract: Damage to arch dams during a powerful earthquake can result in significant loss of life and property. Therefore, in order to prevent damage or destruction that may develop during a major earthquake, it is extremely important to determine how the arch dams will behave under the influence of earthquakes with different characteristics. abstract: Accurate estimation of the rainfall erosivity factor (R-factor) is fundamental for soil erosion prediction and informed land conservation. abstract: Freshwater degradation in semi-arid regions can simultaneously affect river ecological condition and the reliability of water resources for irrigated food production. This study integrated ecological, irrigation-water, hydroclimatic, and crop-specific assessments across the Euphrates, Shatt Al-Hillah, and Al-Diwaniyah river systems in central Iraq over 5 years (2020–2024). abstract: Accurate prediction of the burst pressure of pipelines subjected to internal pressure is essential for pipeline integrity assessment. This study proposes a theory-data hybrid model for burst pressure prediction of corroded pipelines within the framework of Unified Strength Theory. abstract: Abstract Synchronous flooding across distant regions can amplify socioeconomic impacts. As the hydrological cycle intensifies, flood synchronization appears to be expanding, yet predictive understanding beyond gauged basins remains limited. We analyze the global synchronization of annual peak runoff (a proxy for flooding) using gridded data sets and complex network approach, and evaluate 13 CMIP6 (Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6) models in reproducing spatial synchronization patterns. title: A modular framework for quantifying the impact of multi-domain modelling assumptions on urban building energy demand
abstract: Urban Building Energy Modelling (UBEM) is an established approach for evaluating urban energy demand and informing infrastructure planning and policy. However, UBEM workflows often rely on simplified modelling assumptions and input representations that overlook evolving urban and climate conditions. This study presents a modular multi-domain framework that quantifies the impact of three urban factors on energy demand: urban context, climate variability (including site-specific monitored weather and future weather projections), and electric vehicle (EV) adoption. abstract: This paper presents an experimental study of the effects of polyurethane (PU) capsule position on heat gain in hollow brick walls in real outdoor environments. abstract: Background Gut metagenomic classifiers for colorectal cancer (CRC) are often evaluated with random splits that place samples from the same studies, countries, or processing workflows in both training and test sets, potentially inflating apparent performance. abstract: The increasing complexity, volatility, and sustainability pressures affecting global supply chains have accelerated the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies in logistics management. abstract: Traditional all-steel helical piles suffer from excessive steel consumption. This paper proposes a novel helical-ribbed thin-walled steel tube-encased concrete pile to enhance bond-slip performance and economic efficiency. Eight pile specimens with varying rib widths and pitches were tested under vertical uplift loading to characterize failure modes, ultimate bearing capacity, and stress distribution. abstract: This study presents a sensitivity based optimal control framework for enhancing solid particle transport in petroleum pipelines. A nonlinear dynamic model is developed to describe particle velocity evolution under the effects of drag force, mixture density, particle size, and bounded ﬂow disturbances. abstract: Abstract Intraplate volcanism in Northeast Asia, located in a distant back‐arc setting, challenges conventional models of mantle convection and volatile cycling. abstract: Abstract The aim of this work has been to investigate the application of two popular atmospheric water status measurements, namely, vapour pressure deficit (VPD) and atmospheric water potential (AWP). abstract: ABSTRACT Amlexanox, a 5H‐benzopyranopyridine derivative with emerging therapeutic potential in metabolic and inflammatory diseases, lacks a validated analytical method for pharmacokinetic studies in beagle dogs. abstract: Abstract Land surface models are fundamental for simulating coupled carbon, water and energy exchanges in Earth system models, yet their performance remains poorly constrained across Africa's diverse hydroclimatic gradients. We evaluate the Joint UK Land Environment Simulator (JULES) using eddy covariance observations from 16 flux towers spanning major African ecosystem types. abstract: Abstract High seismic velocity keels extending to depths greater than 200 km underlie the oldest parts of continents, the Precambrian cratons. abstract: ABSTRACT The study examines how hard and soft power influence the organizational effectiveness of State corporations (SCs) in Kenya, a public‐sector context characterized by complex political dynamics and competing interests. Using a mixed‐methods approach, the study surveyed 366 employees across 33 SCs and interviewed eight Chief Executive Officers (CEOs). abstract: Abstract Synthesizing fully developed three-dimensional turbulence remains a long-standing problem in fluid mechanics and an open challenge for generative modeling. title: The operational perspective in business process management: towards holistic task execution support
abstract: Abstract This paper redefines the operational perspective in Business Process Management (BPM). While BPM inherently operates at the operational level, its traditional focus on automation, standardization, and software execution has historically overlooked a holistic understanding of task execution, particularly manual tasks and the tools and materials required for them. abstract: We present a new record of Actinopterygii from continental Triassic rocks from southern South America, Argentina. We studied three specimens preserved in black finely laminated mudstones with different grades of preservation, most of them incomplete but articulated or in casts. abstract: This study explores the effect of automation technology on the level of service quality and customer satisfaction in the logistics industry. A case study method was employed to investigate the problems faced by a logistics company in terms of operational and service efficiency and how the integration of an automated scanning and sorting system can streamline these issues. abstract: Abstract Urbanisation fundamentally alters the sensory landscape, creating novel acoustic environments where anthropogenic noise acts as a rigorous filter on wildlife communities. While birds are known to adjust their songs to cope with noise, the limits of this plasticity and the role of fine‐scale habitat structure in buffering these constraints remain poorly understood, particularly in intensely urbanised megacities. abstract: Convergence in parameter estimation classically requires ``persistency of excitation," which is a non-degeneracy condition on a trajectory-dependent signal. This paper develops, to the best of our knowledge, the first such excitation theory for a nonlinear partial differential equation. title: HalifaxDT: A Wireless Digital Twin from Open Geospatial Data
abstract: Wireless digital twins can support site-specific analysis, planning, and experimentation for future wireless networks. However, constructing them at city scale remains challenging when accurate 3D city models are unavailable. This paper presents HalifaxDT, a wireless digital twin of the Halifax Peninsula in Nova Scotia, Canada, constructed from heterogeneous open geospatial and spectrum data. title: Baroclinic Annular Mode Modulates Global Atmospheric Rivers and Extreme Precipitation
abstract: The Baroclinic Annular Mode (BAM) strongly influences extratropical circulation, yet its role in the global hydrological cycle remains unclear. Using ERA5 reanalysis and a global atmospheric river (AR) database, we show that BAM systematically reorganizes AR occurrence and extreme precipitation in both hemispheres. abstract: Sub-Neptunes orbiting M dwarfs are commonly interpreted either as rocky cores beneath primordial H/He envelopes (gas dwarfs) or as volatile-rich bodies formed beyond the water-ice line (water worlds). abstract: We investigate fully nonlinear water waves and fluid-particle dynamics generated by the horizontal motion of a seabed obstacle with prescribed time-dependent velocity. title: Flow dynamics of cryolava or impact melt on Titan's surface
abstract: Titan, a unique body in the solar system, resembles a life-size Miller-Urey experiment where pockets of liquid water might interact with abundant organic matter. Its young surface (less than a billion years) shows signs of material exchange with the interior, and an isotopic signature is detected in the atmosphere. abstract: Three-dimensional flood propagation through the Bhote Koshi--Langtang Khola junction at Syabrubesi, Nepal, is studied using an incompressible free-surface model. The calculation is motivated by the August 2026 flood and examines the passage of an imposed inflow through the local bends and changes in channel width. abstract: Slender flexible structures such as mooring lines, aquaculture netting, and aquatic vegetation are too thin to be resolved economically by a body-fitted mesh, yet they exchange momentum with the flow in both directions. abstract: Existing trajectory designs for covert communications with uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) typically rely on point-mass kinematics, which overlook the inherent coupling between flight maneuvers and antenna orientation. Motivated by recent studies linking UAV acceleration to attitude, we investigate dynamics-consistent trajectory and attitude co-design for rotary-wing UAV covert communications. title: Beyond Tomorrow -- Electrification of Hard-to-Abate Sectors
abstract: Reaching net-zero greenhouse-gas (GHG) emissions requires deep electrification beyond ground transportation, buildings, and conventional industry automation. This article discusses direct electrification pathways for hard-to-abate sectors, which today account for 30% of global GHG emissions and include steel, cement, chemicals, aviation, and shipping. abstract: The anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) is a widely used tool to infer rock fabrics, yet quantitative interpretation is limited by sparse single-crystal magnetic properties for rock-forming minerals and by the difficulty of separating intrinsic diamagnetism from impurity-related magnetism. Here we use density-functional theory (DFT) combined with perturbation theory to compute the diamagnetic susceptibility and AMS of calcite-group carbonates (calcite, magnesite, and dolomite) and to quantify the additional paramagnetic contribution from transition-metal doping. abstract: Abstract Assembly theory predicts that a distinguishing signature of life is its ability to produce complex molecules in abundance, opening new possibilities for life detection. abstract: Bacterial swarming is the collective expansion of dense populations of motile cells across hydrated soft surfaces, yet gravity is usually treated as a fixed background condition in standard horizontal assays. We used surface inclination to examine how agar-surface orientation relative to gravity affects the expansion of Enterobacter sp. SM3 swarms. abstract: Advances in several physics domains open up novel paths to smaller scale, higher energy density opportunities to advance small systems for nuclear fusion. abstract: Generative models for multivariate weather series are routinely evaluated with pooled distributional metrics computed after marginal calibration. abstract: Continuous monitoring of intraocular pressure (IOP) is essential for the diagnosis and management of glaucoma, yet existing clinical methods rely on intermittent in-clinic measurements that miss critical diurnal fluctuations. title: Strategic Environmental Assessment for the Ukrainian Community Development Strategies: European Union Practice
abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is an important tool for integrating environmental considerations into territorial planning and sustainable development. This study compares SEA practices in the United Kingdom, Poland, Romania, and Ukraine to identify best European practices and formulate recommendations for Ukraine. abstract: There is now a growing recognition internationally that the impacts of Artificial Light at Night (ALAN) on marine biodiversity require regulation. Here, we develop an ocean narrative that integrates physical, ecological, and societal indicators, to illustrate polar ocean change. abstract: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) have become an important methodological tool in contemporary archaeological research because they enable researchers to integrate, visualize, analyze, and interpret archaeological data in their spatial context. abstract: Despite rapid advances in AI, big data analytics, GIS, real-time monitoring, and predictive modeling, their integration into environmental impact assessment (EIA) practice remains poorly documented. abstract: Organic alkalinity has been recognized as a potentially substantial fraction of total alkalinity in coastal waters. title: Status of Sea Bamboo (Isis hippuris Linnaeus, 1758) in Bunaken National Park, North Sulawesi, Indonesia
abstract: Isis hippuris Linnaeus, 1758, commonly known as sea bamboo, is a gorgonian octocoral of the family Isididae that plays a vital structural and ecological role in coral reef ecosystems. It is also recognised for producing unique bioactive secondary metabolites, particularly hippuristanol, which exhibits potent antiviral and cytotoxic properties. Despite its conservation and pharmacological importance, baseline demographic data for I. hippuris across North Sulawesi marine protected areas remain scarce. This study assessed the distribution, abundance, and population density of I. hippuris within B

title: Silicate accumulation in taxonomically diverse seaweeds: morphology, uptake, visualization and environmental responses
abstract: Abstract Silicon is required by some microalgae but use and accumulation by seaweeds has been quantified in few taxa. This study aimed to examine biogenic Si (bSi) in taxonomically and morphologically diverse seaweeds, measure Si uptake rates, assess the effects of environmental conditions on bSi, and visualize Si within seaweed tissues. bSi was determined in 57 seaweed taxa across 17 taxonomic orders collected around Tasmania, Australia. title: Spatial disparities in surf-resource sustainability: Implications for coastal policy and marine education in Taiwan
abstract: This study situates global surf sustainability within the Taiwanese context, where recreational surfing has developed since the 1980s and expanded internationally after 2010, yet region-wide assessments of surf-resource sustainability remain limited. Little is known about how sustainability conditions vary across Taiwan’s coastal regions, which sustainability dimensions contribute most strongly to these disparities, and what implications such patterns have for coastal governance and marine education policy. title: Measurements of the Size and Physical Properties of Marine Particles Using Atomic Force Microscopy: Implications for Marine Biogeochemical Cycles
abstract: Abstract Particle size and physical properties such as stiffness and adhesiveness affect sinking velocity and flux in the ocean, yet conventional two‐dimensional measurements lack accuracy and mechanical information. In this study, we applied atomic force microscopy (AFM) to quantify three‐dimensional size and physical properties of marine particles. Three hundred and sixty‐eight particles were collected using a marine snow catcher from the pycnocline and benthic boundary layer at three coastal‐to‐offshore stations in the northwestern Pacific. title: Combined effects of elevated temperature and fluoxetine exposure on early development of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus
abstract: Temperature rise associated with climate change increases the vulnerability of coastal species, which are also exposed to pharmaceuticals. We investigated the effects of thermal stress and fluoxetine (FLX), alone and in combination, on early developmental stages of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus, a key coastal species. Gametes, zygotes and embryos were exposed to ambient (18°C) and near-future projections (21°C, 24°C) to identify the most sensitive developmental stage to warming. In parallel, environmentally relevant FLX concentrations were tested under near-future temperature scenarios.

title: Projecting Impacts of Marine Heatwaves and Their Effects on Long‐Term Changes in Marine Ecosystems Over the 21st Century
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasing in frequency, duration and intensity under climate change. Although current MHWs trigger broad ecological impacts, such as coral bleaching, mass mortality of seagrass meadows, and declines in important fish stocks, the cascading effects of MHWs on ecosystem structure and functions in the 21st century remain unclear. In this study, we utilise a global biomass flow modelling framework to analyse these impacts. title: Navigating coastal futures: Harnessing GIS and multi-criteria decision analysis for sustainable resilience in Kerala's vulnerable Shores
abstract: Extreme weather occurrences, particularly in densely populated coastal places like India, cause loss and devastation, hindering disaster preparedness and long-term viability of vulnerable populations. Research shows that hybrid models, such as Bayesian Networks and Coastal Vulnerability frameworks, outperform traditional methods for measuring coastal vulnerability to Sea Level Rise (SLR). However, their extensive geographical coverage has considerable limitations, including data scarcity and challenges in effectively capturing differences in tiny locations. title: ANOVATS: a subsampling-based test to detect differences among short time series in marine studies
abstract: Assessing marine ecosystems is important for understanding the impacts of climate change and human activity, as well as for maintaining healthy oceans and ecosystems. In marine science, it is common for biologists and geologists to identify regional differences based on expert knowledge, frequently through data visualization. However, time series data collected through surveys in marine studies typically span only a few decades, limiting the applicability of classical time series methods. Additionally, without expert knowledge, detecting significant differences becomes challenging. To address

title: Environmental occurrence and source apportionment of synthetic phenolic antioxidants in typical coastal bays: Drivers and source-specific risk assessment
abstract: Synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) are emerging contaminants whose occurrence, sources, and risks in marine ecosystems remain poorly understood. This study assessed the occurrence, associated factors, potential sources, and ecological and human health risks of 16 SPAs in seawater, sediments, and clams from coastal bays of the Shandong Peninsula based on a single sampling campaign conducted in August 2024. Given the limited data available for SPAs, the driver, source, and risk analyses were exploratory and aimed to identify potential environmental and health implications. Σ₁₆ SPA concentrat

title: Where do the monsters come from? Visualizing marine pollution through biological mutation and game threat design
abstract: Marine pollution is difficult to communicate because much of it is gradual, distributed, and hidden below the surface. Plastic fragments, chemical residues, and damaged habitats may be present long before the sea looks visibly different. This creates a problem for games: players need to understand danger quickly, while the process itself is slow and difficult to see. This paper examines biological mutation as a design language for making that hidden damage visible. title: Tecnologías de información geográfica y gerencia pública en salud: hacia una vigilancia epidemiológica territorial de la enfermedad diarreica aguda en Perú y América Latina
abstract: La enfermedad diarreica aguda (EDA) persiste como problema prioritario de salud pública en Perú y América Latina. Mediante una revisión sistemática PRISMA de 30 estudios (Scopus y SciELO, 2000-2026), se analizó cómo las Tecnologías de Información Geográfica (TIG) —autocorrelación espacial e indicadores LISA— identifican clústeres de riesgo de EDA. Se concluye que estas herramientas constituyen activos estratégicos de gerencia pública en salud, con potencial para optimizar la planificación territorial, la asignación presupuestaria y la capacidad de respuesta institucional ante brotes.

title: Environmental Factors Have a Stronger Influence on the Coral Holobiont in Comparison to Geographic Distance Along a 15,000‐km East‐to‐West Transect Through the Coral Triangle, Pacific and Indian Oceans
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To determine the factors that structure coral‐associated microbial communities (bacteria and Symbiodiniaceae). These microbial communities play critical roles in reef ecosystem function, yet the relative importance of environmental versus geographic drivers in structuring these communities across large spatial scales remains poorly understood, particularly across broad Indo‐Pacific gradients that include biodiversity hotspots such as the Coral Triangle. title: Tracing Groundwater–Seawater exchanges using geochemical tracers (radon, radium, stable isotopes of water) in a seasonally frozen beach
abstract: Groundwater–seawater exchanges remain poorly documented in subarctic and arctic regions, particularly during winter, when coastal ice alters hydrogeology conditions and limits sampling opportunities. This study investigates winter groundwater dynamics at a seasonally frozen beach by combining the use of various geochemical tracers. title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. title: Constraint-Based Adaptive Grids for Compact Representation of Marine Scalar Fields
abstract: Fixed-block representations can obscure heterogeneous local variability in marine scalar fields. We present a deterministic adaptive representation in which anchored dyadic tiles merge under a field-normalized local-range rule and a realized-tile diameter cap. Area-weighted tile values provide lossy reconstruction, whereas exact tile-to-cell membership preserves the link to the authoritative source grid. title: 4-MBC in Australian sunscreens as an unmonitored discharge pathway into Great Barrier Reef coastal waters
abstract: Abstract 4-Methylbenzylidene camphor (4-MBC, also known as enzacamene), a chemical UV filter prohibited or never permitted across the EU, UK, China, ASEAN, US, and Japan, remains legal in Australian therapeutic sunscreens at concentrations up to 4% w/w. The European Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety concluded in 2022 that no safe concentration could be established, and the UK Scientific Advisory Group on Chemical Safety confirmed this in 2025. title: Rheumatic Heart Disease Burden and Sex Differences in China and ASEAN Countries, 1990–2030: A Comparative Analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
abstract: Background: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) remains a major public health concern in low‑ and middle‑income countries. Systematic comparisons between China and the ten ASEAN member states examining sex disparities are scarce. Methods: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 data, we analyzed RHD burden in China and ten ASEAN countries from 1990 to 2023. Key measures included age‑standardized prevalence (ASPR), mortality (ASMR), and disability‑adjusted life‑years rates (ASDR). title: Mathematics anxiety and problem-solving ability in numerical methods courses: A repeated cross-sectional study across two Southeast Asian universities
abstract: Mathematics anxiety (MA) impedes mathematical learning by taxing cognitive resources, negatively affecting problem-solving ability (PSA). Some evidence suggests that the strength and nature of this negative association may vary across educational and cultural contexts. However, cross-cultural studies on MA and PSA, especially in Southeast Asia, remain limited. This study investigated cohort-level patterns of MA and PSA in a transnational Numerical Methods course at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) and Universitas Pahlawan (UP), Indonesia. title: Marine habitat use and movement of sympatric anadromous Dolly Varden and Arctic Char in the Canadian Arctic
abstract: Abstract Objective Inuit subsistence fishers in Kugluktuk, Nunavut, Canada, have noticed changes in the timing and locations of their catches of Arctic Char Salvelinus alpinus and northern form Dolly Varden S. malma malma (collectively referred to by the community as “char”) in the past ∼20 years. In response, an ongoing research program was formed to study char in partnership with the Kugluktuk Hunters and Trappers Organization. title: Landscape of Targetable Genetic Alterations in Advanced Cholangiocarcinoma among Patients in Southeast Asia
abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a heterogeneous form of biliary tract cancer, for which treatment options remain limited; however, molecular profiling technology has helped in uncovering genomic mutations that can be used in precision oncology. This molecular profiling study has been carried out retrospectively in order to investigate the genomic alterations that are targetable in advanced cholangiocarcinomas of Southeast Asia. title: Winter disturbances drive community change in subarctic eelgrass meadows
abstract: The dynamics of winter sea ice and icefoot play a fundamental role in structuring intertidal ecosystems in subarctic environments. However, ongoing climate warming is altering ice regimes across northern shorelines. In the St. Lawrence marine estuary (Canada), reduced formation of icefoot increasingly exposes benthic habitats to winter-related disturbances. We investigated how such disturbance influences eelgrass ( Zostera marina L.) meadows and associated benthic communities using a before-and-after comparison spanning the 2024-2025 winter season. title: Three decades of marine bioregions evolution through analysis of phytoplankton phenology
abstract: Abstract. Ocean biogeochemistry is undergoing significant modification in response to climate change. To better understand these evolution, we present a novel ocean monitoring indicator approach that tracks the temporal evolution of marine bioregions of similar phytoplankton phenologies. Chlorophyll-a concentration observations from remotely sensed ocean color describe seven distinct marine bioregions characterized by their unique patterns of phytoplankton biomass seasonality. title: Assessment of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion Potential in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia: Energy Performance, Techno-Economic Feasibility, and Environmental Considerations
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion as a renewable electricity source in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia. Ocean temperature data from the World Ocean Atlas for 1955-2018 at station 21576 were analyzed to characterize the surface and deep-water thermal conditions and to assess the performance of an open-cycle Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion system. The assessment covered thermodynamic efficiency, electrical power generation, production cost, freshwater production, and potential environmental impacts. title: Balancing blue growth and the ecosystem approach: policy coherence in Sweden’s Marine Spatial Plan for the Baltic Sea
abstract: There is growing expectation within the European Union (EU) that Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) – the public process for allocating marine space among competing uses – can support environmental restoration and economic development through the Ecosystem Approach (EA), which seek to balance ecological, social, and economic objectives. This article examines how effectively MSP implements the EA in practice, using Sweden’s Baltic Sea plan as a case study. title: Remobilized volcanogenic sediments boost photophysiological activity in three symbiotic reef-building coral species
abstract: Abstract Coral reefs that surround volcanic islands are continually influenced by run-off carrying remobilized volcanogenic sediments. Although unaltered volcanic ash is known to supply trace metals that enhance coral holobiont productivity, the impacts of long-term exposure to weathered tephra, a far more likely scenario in island settings, are less understood. title: Pyropia haitanensis cultivation enhances water quality and reshapes microbial communities in coastal water and connected aquaculture ponds
abstract: Seaweed cultivation offers nature-based bioremediation for aquaculture effluents, yet its cascading effects on microbial ecosystems remain poorly understood. This study evaluated Pyropia haitanensis cultivation impacts across four phenological stages in nearshore marine (Cultivation Area, PS; Control Sea, CS) and connected aquaculture ponds (Influenced Pond, PA; Control Pond, CA). Results showed that P. haitanensis cultivation significantly improved water quality in PS and PA by increasing dissolved oxygen and pH while reducing NH₄⁺-N, TN, TC, and TOC. title: Global triazine herbicide pollution impairs marine phytoplankton nutrition through disruption of acetyl-CoA-related metabolism
abstract: Herbicide contamination impairs marine primary productivity, yet its subcellular impact on phytoplankton carbon allocation remains poorly understood. Global monitoring (1990–2023) revealed triazine herbicides as the dominant coastal pollutants, with atrazine and simazine exceeding 80% detection frequency; their combined toxicity corresponded to a median atrazine-equivalent concentration of 0.68 nmol L −1 . title: Meandering shorelines: The potential for multi-level habitat complexity to ecologically enhance artificial coastal defences
abstract: Artificial coastal defences simplify, linearize, and homogenize the coast, leading to reduced species diversity, ecological functioning, and ecosystem services. Previous active management research has shown that greater habitat complexity at millimeter to decimeter scales increases the diversity of fauna and flora living on constructed shores, however, little is known regarding the potential effects of increasing the scale of complexity on larger marine species. title: From shark hunters to sea guardians: Environmental literacy transformation and socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people in Sapeken Islands, East Java-Indonesia
abstract: The Bajo people are known for their closeness to and dependence on the sea. Over the past few decades, the Bajo people have undergone significant changes that are worth examining. This study aims to analyze the socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people who inhabit Sadulang Besar Island, Sapeken Archipelago, East Java, with particular attention to how environmental literacy, intergenerational learning, and shifting livelihood strategies have contributed to changes in marine practices and ecological identity. title: Hydrodynamics of bio-mimetic sponge arrays with non-uniform triangular arrangement under wave actions
abstract: Bio-inspired marine structures have attracted increasing attention as nature-based solutions for modifying coastal hydrodynamics and enhancing momentum exchange. Previous studies on isolated and dual sponge-inspired elements have shown limited hydrodynamic effectiveness under relatively low-height waves, where velocity redistribution and turbulence generation remain weak. To address this limitation, the present study proposes and experimentally fabricates a bio-mimetic pillar coral composed of non-uniform triangular sponge elements arranged in a progressive three-line configuration. title: Dietary shift from marine to agriculture in coastal Lower Yangtze Delta during Neolithic revealed by isotopic evidence from Jingtoushan
abstract: Neolithic agriculture is considered to have reduced marine food reliance among coastal populations, yet whether this dietary transition occurred in Neolithic China remains unclear. The lower Yangtze River Delta, central to both marine adaptation and rice agriculture origins, provides key evidence. In this study, stable isotope data from human and faunal bone collagen from the Jingtoushan site (8300–7800 BP), combined with published regional data, were used to investigate the dietary patterns and shifts. title: Biomass and Carbon Allocation in Tree Components of Beech-Chestnut Mixed Forests in Coastal Western Black Sea Region
abstract: Aim of study: Estimating C storage using biomass data is a widely used method for forest ecosystems. In most studies, the content of biomass is calculated by destructive methods such as cutting and sampling of trees on sampling plots. However, tree biomass can be estimated using diameter and height data without disturbing the site. The aim of this study is to determine the content of above-and below-ground biomass and their carbon (C) stocks in an eastern beech (Fagus orientalis Lipsky) and Anatolian chestnut (Castanea sativa Mill.) mixed forest. title: Macrobenthic community turnover along a compressed depth gradient in the East Sea
abstract: The East Sea of Korea is a semi-enclosed marginal sea characterized by a steep bathymetric gradient, creating a compressed environmental gradient that provides an ideal study area for investigating benthic macrofaunal communities. Still, quantitative assessments of community patterns across the continuous coastal-to-deep-sea gradient remain limited in the East Sea of Korea. This study analyzed the distribution and community transition patterns of macrobenthic communities along the continuous coastal-to-deep-sea depth gradient in the East Sea. title: Environmental assessment of shrimp farming in coastal Tamil Nadu of India: a case study of Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai districts
abstract: Shrimp aquaculture is a major economic activity in Tamil Nadu, with the Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai districts together accounting for nearly 45% of the state’s licensed shrimp farms. Although the sector has periodically attracted concern regarding its environmental sustainability particularly with respect to shrimp farm discharge water quality and coastal ecosystem health there remains a paucity of empirical, field-based assessments from this region. title: Phosphate-Modified Co/BaTiO₃@Vulcan Nanocomposite for Stable Seawater Oxygen Evolution
abstract: This study presents a design strategy for developing corrosion-resistant anode materials, establishing a successful baseline for further optimization in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) during direct seawater splitting. Cobalt nanocomposites supported on BaTiO₃ and Vulcan XC72R carbon black were synthesized via a combined sol-gel and microwave-assisted methodology using cellulose phosphate (CP) as a structural template and phosphorus source. title: Environmental Security of the Gulf During Armed Conflict: Marine Pollution Risks, GCC Preparedness, and a Regional Emergency-Response Framework
abstract: The Gulf is a strategically crucial and environmentally vulnerable semi-enclosed marine system supporting petroleum industries, international shipping, desalination facilities, coastal ecosystems, and urban centers. Alongside chronic industrial and maritime pressures, armed conflict introduces severe risks via direct military operations, targeting of energy infrastructure, drone and missile strikes, hazardous material releases, and disruption of monitoring networks. title: Long-Term Shoreline Dynamics and Their Implications for Coastal Spatial Management
abstract: Coastal development increasingly takes place in environments where dynamic shoreline processes undermine the permanence of spatial planning and infrastructure. This research investigates long-term shoreline change along the Tanjung Pandan coast, Indonesia, and assesses its implications for coastal management, with Tanjung Pendam serving as a strategic urban waterfront. A quantitative spatial-descriptive methodology, combined with planning interpretation, was employed using multi-temporal shoreline data from 2000, 2013, and 2025. title: Marine renewable energy and cumulative effects assessments: Summary of the state of play
abstract: Cumulative effects result from interacting human activities across space or time, potentially involving multiple sectors, which can affect ecosystem components. Cumulative effects assessments (CEAs) systematically identify and evaluate the compound effects of multiple pressures that may occur within and across industries (and via interaction with climate change induced ecosystem shifts), causing large-scale environmental change. title: Seascape genomics reveals high genetic diversity and apparent panmixia in endemic Southern Ocean phytoplankton
abstract: Abstract The adaptive potential and resilience of cold‐adapted phytoplankton to climate change have the potential to impact polar marine food webs and global biogeochemical cycles. Two central but poorly constrained facets of adaptive potential in polar phytoplankton are standing genetic diversity and its spatial structure. Here, we partially sequenced 30 field isolate genomes of a commonly‐occurring endemic Southern Ocean (SO) phytoplankton, the diatom Actinocyclus actinochilus , and analyzed patterns in standing genetic diversity and geographic structure. title: Shell characteristics and Sr–Nd–Pb isotope signatures of Creseis acicula during its 2020 outbreak near Daya Bay Nuclear Power Station
abstract: Abstract China ranks second in the world in terms of nuclear power generation, making significant contributions to China’s green economic and social development. Chinese nuclear power plants are located in coastal areas, which are prone to frequent outbreaks of marine organisms due to inputs from terrestrial sources. These outbreaks have led to shutdowns of varying severity at nuclear power plants. However, there is currently limited research on the processes involved in marine-organism outbreaks. Daya Bay Nuclear Power Station (DBNPS) is the first large-scale commercial nuclear power station

title: Reproductive thermoregulation in marine mammals: mechanisms, adaptations and evolutionary implications
abstract: Marine mammals inhabit thermally challenging environments in which maintaining internal body temperature is essential for survival, metabolic function, and reproductive success. Unlike terrestrial mammals, many marine male species lack external reproductive structures (e.g. scrotum), raising questions about how reproductive temperatures are regulated in the absence of conventional cooling mechanisms. This review synthesizes current knowledge of reproductive thermoregulation in marine mammals, with a focus on cetaceans and pinnipeds, and highlights key anatomical and physiological adaptations.

title: Anthropized environments as reservoirs of hidden and exotic diversity in marine annelids: sicilian ports as a case study
abstract: Marine annelids are key components of benthic ecosystems, yet their diversity remains unevenly documented, particularly in anthropized habitats. In Sicily (Mediterranean Sea), significant knowledge gaps persist regarding port benthic communities and their role in the spread of non-indigenous species (NIS). This study provides the first characterization of polychaete assemblages in Sicilian ports in over three decades, with a specific focus on biodiversity patterns and NIS occurrence. title: Environmental Communication and Multi-Stakeholder Collaboration for Sustainable Fisheries Livelihoods and Coastal Resource Governance on Labengki Island, Indonesia
abstract: The goal of this study was to analyze multi-stakeholder collaboration in environmental communication in developing sustainable marine tourism in Labengki Island, North Konawe Regency, as a means of supporting coastal fisheries livelihoods and improving the social economy of Labengki Island’s small islands. A qualitative exploratory approach was used, with a case study design. Thematic analysis was conducted in NVivo using software, whilst Actor-Network Analysis (ANA) — an approach adapted from Actor-Network Theory (ANT) — was used to map relationships between human and non-human actors. title: Effects of the summer season and religious holiday periods on tropospheric NO₂ levels in Türkiye’s coastal tourism destinations: A Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI and GIS-based analysis (2023–2025)
abstract: This study investigates tropospheric NO2 variations observed in the Mediterranean and Aegean regions—Türkiye’s prominent coastal tourism hubs—during the 2023–2025 period, within the context of seasonal summer intensity and short-term mobility during Eid al-Fitr (Ramadan Feast) and Eid al-Adha (Feast of Sacrifice). title: Determination of seasonal groundwater recharge potential in the coastal mining town of Jose Panganiban, Philippines
abstract: Coastal groundwater resources are highly vulnerable to the combined risks of heavy metal contamination and saltwater intrusion where artisanal small-scale gold mining is active. This study used a GIS-based analysis to identify susceptible coastal aquifers in the municipality of Jose Panganiban, Philippines, by examining the reduction in groundwater potential coincident with the seasonal oscillation of precipitation, the main driver of recharge. title: Dashboard e Indicatori sul Climate Change per i Planning Decision Support Systems
abstract: What are geospatial dashboards, and how can they support planning and Planning Decision Support Systems (PDSS) addressing Climate Change (CC)? Starting from the literature, the paper analyses dashboards and their indicators as used in planning, proposing criteria for an integrated, dynamic, and operational PDSS for diverse plan recipients at local and global scales. title: Spatial prioritization of urban green infrastructure for heat mitigation: a gis-mcda approach in Chennai, India
abstract: Urbanization and loss of vegetated land have amplified the Urban Heat Island (UHI) phenomenon which severely worsens urban climate in the main cities of the developing nations. This research develops a GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis (GIs-MCDA) framework to quantify green space shortfalls, surface thermal exposure, and urban microclimates across the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC), India. title: Functional Identity Drives Directional Shifts in Freshwater Plankton Biomass–Size Relationships
abstract: Body size is a master variable in ecology that can predict ecosystem-level processes and reflect environmental conditions across diverse ecosystems. In freshwater ecosystems, the relationship between body size and biomass provides a powerful tool for characterizing community structure and trophic transfer efficiency. While these relationships are well established at the whole-community level, responses within plankton functional groups with distinct ecological characteristics have yet to be explored. abstract: Coastal regions are increasingly under compounded pressures from climate change and rapid socioeconomic development, and integrated approaches to sustainability assessment are needed. This study assesses coastal sustainability in Ho Chi Minh City by developing a composite sustainability index (CSI) structured around three key dimensions: socioeconomic, ecoenvironmental, and institutional management. title: Visualizing the Nuclear: Visibility and Invisibility in U.S. Photographic Representations from the Pacific
abstract: This article examines the visual culture of U.S. nuclear imperialism in the Pacific through an analysis of several widely circulated photographs: two images of atomic testing at Bikini Atoll published in Life magazine in 1946, and a photograph of the nuclear-powered USS Enterprise produced during Operation Sea Orbit in 1964. Drawing on theories of coloniality, whiteness, and militourism, this article traces the shift from the hypervisibility of the atomic explosion to the increasing invisibility of nuclear power within Cold War visual discourse. title: Visualizing Reversible Uranyl (UO 2 2+ ) Capture and Release With Self‐Indicating Porous Organic Polymers
abstract: Seawater uranium extraction is a promising sustainable energy pathway; however, practical application requires advanced adsorbents that combine reversible, high uranium‐uptake capacity with the ability to track sorption cycles. Herein, we report self‐indicating porous organic polymers (POPs), Sal‐POP and Im‐POP , containing uranyl (UO 2 2+ ) ion‐coordinating salphen and o ‐hydroxy imine cores with UO 2 2+ binding energies up to −71.94 kcal mol −1 as uranium adsorbents, and demonstrate their reversible, high uranium extraction capacities up to 0.114 g g −1 h −1 . title: New records of the rare deep-sea snailfish Acantholiparis opercularis (Cottoidei: Liparidae) in the western North Pacific, with notes on the morphology and distribution of the species
abstract: An unusual snailfish with spines on its head was sampled by the SokhoBio expedition in the southern Sea of Okhotsk at a depth of 3305 m. We identified it as Acantholiparis opercularis Gilbert et Burke, 1912, a rare deep-sea fish described from the Avacha Gulf (southeast of Kamchatka) and the Shumagin Islands (Aleutians) and known from several additional records in the North Pacific (Bering Sea, Oregon, Northern California). title: Spatial Variability and Long‐Term Trends in Winter Phytoplankton of the Warming Eastern Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Abstract The Eastern Mediterranean Sea (EMS) is among the fastest‐warming ocean regions, but the impacts of this warming on phytoplankton are unclear. Here, wintertime field observations were conducted across the EMS. These observations showed that small photosynthetic eukaryotes (<20 μm) dominated phytoplankton communities, collectively accounting for >60% of total chlorophyll a (Chl‐a) despite severe nitrate‐ and phosphate‐depleted conditions. title: Measuring Dry Deposition of Sea Spray Aerosol and Height of Aerosol Plume Using a Controlled Wave Pool
abstract: Abstract Deposition of sea spray aerosols facilitates atmospheric corrosion of materials, requiring maintenance and replacement over time. However, the dimensions of sea spray aerosol plumes produced from breaking waves have not been well‐characterized, limiting useful prediction of particle transport downwind and atmospheric corrosion. Therefore, this project aimed to measure sea spray aerosol production from breaking waves in a controlled environment at several elevations to obtain the height profile of an aerosol plume. title: Climate change and biological traits: interglacial stability and higher glacial functional diversity in Late Quaternary molluscan assemblages of the Adriatic Sea (Italy)
abstract: Abstract Studies on the effects of long-term climate change on marine communities are crucial to our understanding of ecosystem resilience. The Late Quaternary fossil record, dominated by extant taxa, provides a valuable archive of past biotic responses to major climate fluctuations. While most studies on faunal turnover so far have focused on taxonomic identity, trait-based approaches are becoming increasingly common as they provide a stronger link to ecosystem functioning. title: Prorocentrum pseudonux sp. nov. ( Prorocentrales, Dinophyceae ): A new nanoplanktonic dinoflagellate from the open tropical Pacific Ocean
abstract: SUMMARY While phytoplankton from the coasts of temperate seas has received considerable attention, phytoplankton from the open tropical ocean, especially the smallest fraction, remains understudied. Here, we describe a new nanoplanktonic dinoflagellate from the tropical Pacific Ocean. Prorocentrum pseudonux sp. nov. is slightly oval in thecal view, measuring 6–9 μm long and 5–8 μm deep. The theca is smooth with a few pores of different size classes. title: Small‐Scale Topographic Variability Shapes Molecular Diversity of Organic Matter in Coastal Dune Soils
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays a crucial role in carbon and nutrient cycling across terrestrial, aquatic, and marine ecosystems. Most terrestrial OM originates from litter and soils, where it is mobilized by percolating rainwater before entering the groundwater. Consequently, groundwater OM composition can be influenced by soil processes such as organic matter processing above the groundwater surface. title: A review on visualization of flexible VOC sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are ubiquitously present in the natural environment and are produced by human activities, serving as key indicators of the chemical state of substances. The integration of flexible sensors and visualization technologies offers novel solutions for on-site, in-situ, and real-time VOC detection. title: Ocean predators as indicators of nano- and microplastic prevalence in pelagic food webs
abstract: Quantifying nano- and microplastics (NMPs) in ocean predators is fundamental to understanding the prevalence of these contaminants and potential impacts on ecosystem health. Pyrolysis gas chromatography tandem mass spectrometry with lipid correction was used to determine NMP concentrations and polymer composition in the muscle tissue of two pelagic predators (dolphinfish [ Coryphaena hippurus ], yellowfin tuna [ Thunnus albacares ]) across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. title: Território quilombola e fragilidades ambientais
abstract: Coastal systems are dynamic spaces where natural elements and human actions interact in complex ways, generating varying degrees of environmental fragility. Thus, this paper aims to assess the environmental fragility of the Quilombo do Cumbe Territory, using the sub-watershed in which the territory is located as the spatial unit of analysis. The methodological approach is based on an integrated analysis, supported by General Systems Theory (Bertalanffy, 1975) and an adaptation of Ross’s proposal (1994, 2012). It was carried out in the following stages: literature review; collection and process

title: Application of eDNA metabarcoding for high-resolution reconstruction of the trophic web of an Arctic fjord
abstract: Abstract In a rapidly changing Arctic, the Kongsfjorden marine ecosystem was investigated to explore its community composition and structural dynamics using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding. Samples were collected with metaprobes , passive eDNA samplers deployed within fish traps in the coastal zone and towed along a transect in the mid-fjord zone. Mitochondrial COI and ribosomal 18 S SSU (V8-V9 region) genes were amplified to characterize metazoan and protist communities, respectively. title: Quantitative Text-based Shrinking-society Risk Index for Multidimensional Assessment in Coastal Regions
abstract: In this study, the shrinking-society risk index (SSRI), utilizing unstructured textual big data to detect and quantify the shrinking-society crisis facing coastal regions in South Korea, is proposed.Recognizing that traditional indicators based on demographic statistics have limitations in the immediate measurement of latent functional degradation within communities, large-scale textual data are defined as environmental and social input signals and a marine softsensor framework for multidimensional analysis is designed.The architecture of this framework curated 15 years of news big data and mu

title: Volcanic stratigraphy offshore East Montserrat: Selective preservation and subaqueous remobilisation in marine records
abstract: Abstract In tectonically active regions, volcanic eruptions generate large volumes of material that are transported offshore through processes such as pyroclastic density currents, turbidity currents, and secondary sediment remobilisation. These deposits form key stratigraphic markers for reconstructing eruptive histories, yet their preservation, correlation with onshore events, and modification by mass wasting remain insufficiently understood. title: PREFERENCES OF DIGITAL NOMADS: ANALYZING POPULAR DESTINATIONS AND DECISION-MAKING FACTORS THROUGH INTERACTIVE DATA VISUALIZATIONS USING PUBLIC ACCESS DATABASES
abstract: Digital nomadism is a rapidly spreading form of location-independent work that is fundamentally transforming the global labour market, economy, and tourism. The aim of this study is to quantitatively explore and model the destination preferences of digital nomads and to present an innovative, interactive data visualization framework. Our research analyses the structural changes of the period 2021-2024 following the logic of the PEST model (Political, Economical, Social, Technological). title: Antifungal potential and ecological perspectives of selected seagrass species from tropical coastal meadows
abstract: Seagrasses have gathered increasing attention due to their multifaceted ecological roles. Apart from their ecological significance, seagrasses have exhibited potent antifungal properties, indicating potential for diverse applications. The antifungal efficacy of methanolic extracts derived from five seagrass species ( Cymodocea serrulata , Cymodocea rotundata , Halodule pinifolia , Halophila ovalis , and Syringodium isoetifolium ) was assessed against pathogenic fungal strains using the agar well diffusion method. title: Integrating Environmental DNA ( eDNA ) Approaches to Enhance Fisheries Advisories Through Marine Food Web Reconstruction: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental DNA (eDNA) transforms marine ecological research through non‐invasive assessment of ecosystem structure with higher taxonomic resolution. This study explores the potential of eDNA metabarcoding to enhance fisheries advisories through food web reconstruction, bridging ecological insights with ecosystem‐based fisheries management. This review elucidates the concepts of eDNA and explores its applications in food web studies and Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) dynamics. title: Molecular approaches to phylogeny and species boundaries in Lethrinus (Teleostei, Lethrinidae): insights from a taxonomic complex along Mozambique coast
abstract: Abstract Accurate species delimitation is essential for understanding the evolutionary processes that generate and maintain biodiversity, particularly in marine systems characterized by high connectivity and widespread distributions. Reef-associated fishes of the Indo–West Pacific provide an ideal framework to investigate these dynamics, yet many taxa remain poorly resolved due to morphological conservatism and cryptic diversity. title: Multi-decadal trends in abundance reveal a dramatic decline in wild Norwegian Atlantic salmon
abstract: Understanding changes in population abundance is critical for conservation of fish populations. Here, we estimate abundance of wild Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar L.) in Norwegian rivers at national and regional levels using catch statistics encompassing nearly 450 populations. Estimates based on body size were reconstructed nationally (1983–2023) and for five geographic regions (1989–2023). Abundance of one-sea-winter (1SW) and multi-sea-winter (MSW) salmon was reconstructed regionally over 1989–2023. title: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Surface Water and Fluvial Sediments of a Rural Gulf Coast Watershed: A Year-long Spatiotemporal Assessment
abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants of significant health concern. This study quantified the spatiotemporal occurrence of 40 PFAS in surface water and fluvial sediments across the Lavaca Watershed and Lavaca Bay, Texas, a rural Gulf Coast system with limited potential point sources. Monthly sampling was conducted at 12 sites from January to December 2025, and samples were analyzed following U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Method 1633A. title: Metabolomic profiling and anticancer effects of Red Sea sponges Liosina granularis and Callyspongia crassa on prostate and ovarian cancer cells
abstract: Abstract Marine sponges are rich sources of bioactive secondary metabolites with potential relevance to anticancer drug discovery. This study investigated the metabolomic profiles and preliminary anticancer activity of methanolic extracts from two Red Sea sponge species, Liosina granularis (LGE) and Callyspongia crassa (CCE), using prostate (PC3) and ovarian (SKOV-3) cancer cell models. LC-MS/MS analysis annotated 44 metabolites, including alkaloids, long-chain amides, fatty acids, polyketides, and terpenoids. title: A coupled water-quality–Ecopath with Ecosim model incorporating sand-lance aestivation dynamics in the Harima-Nada Sea
abstract: Sand lance ( Ammodytes japonicus ) is an important forage fish in the Harima-Nada Sea, Japan, but its stock has declined markedly in recent decades under concurrent changes in nutrient availability and water temperature. To clarify the mechanisms underlying these changes, we developed a region-specific coupled water-quality–Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE) model that explicitly incorporates sand-lance aestivation dynamics. title: Self-organized hummock-hollow patterns redistribute salinity stress in coastal meadows
abstract: Self-organization theory predicts that ecosystem functioning and resilience can emerge from feedbacks that generate spatial patterns. These emergent properties have commonly been explained by local positive feedbacks that concentrate limiting resources within productive patches. Here, we identify a stress-redistribution feedback underlying self-organized hummock-hollow patterning. title: Thermal resource characterization for regional OTEC site screening in the Caribbean using AHP–TOPSIS
abstract: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) offers a sustainable option for improving energy security in the hurricane-prone Caribbean region. This study established a regional screening framework for identifying offshore OTEC candidate sites based on a high-resolution (∼1 km) characterization of the Mean Sea Water Temperature Difference (ΔT m ) and thermal persistence over a 19-year period under hurricane and non-hurricane seasons. title: Shear strength evolution and multi-factor coupling friction model of coral sand-structure interface
abstract: The shear strength of coral sand-pile interface affects the bearing capacity of pile foundation in island and reef engineering. However, there is still a lack of interface shear strength prediction model that can comprehensively consider the influence of multiple factors. In this paper, the influence of roughness of pile (concrete, steel and aluminum alloy), normal stress and relative density of soil on the shear characteristics of pile-soil contact interface is systematically studied by using a large-scale interface shear apparatus developed independently. title: Web-Based Extreme Weather Monitoring and Early Warning System for Traditional Fishermen Using IoT Sensor Data
abstract: Extreme weather can disrupt traditional fishing activities and increase safety risks, particularly when local weather information is difficult to access before departure. This study develops a web-based extreme weather monitoring and early warning system for traditional fishermen using Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data. The system integrates an ESP32 microcontroller with a DHT22 sensor, rain sensor, and anemometer to acquire temperature, humidity, rainfall, and wind-speed data at ten-second intervals. title: Softening mechanism and fatigue performance analysis of heat affected zone in welding of microalloyed submarine flexible pipes
abstract: Subsea flexible pipelines are key equipment in deep-sea resource development, serving as the "lifeline" connecting underwater production systems with surface treatment facilities. Its core function is to safely and efficiently transport various marine resources. The welding Heat Affected Zone (HAZ) is a weak link in the welding joints of submarine flexible pipelines. title: Spatial patterns and environmental associations of plankton communities in the Karst free-flowing Chishui river: Insights from eDNA metabarcoding and network analysis
abstract: Understanding the mechanisms governing plankton community assembly and spatial heterogeneity is fundamental for freshwater ecosystem conservation, yet such knowledge remains scarce for free - flowing rivers in Karst regions facing compounding anthropogenic pressures. Here, we investigated the spatial patterns, community – environment relationships, and co-occurrence network architecture of phytoplankton and zooplankton communities along the mainstem of the Chishui River, the last undammed tributary of the upper Yangtze River and a biodiversity hotspot of global conservation significance. title: Spatial organization and coordinated development of offshore wind industrial chains under governance decentralization: evidence from China's coastal provinces
abstract: Offshore wind industrial chains, encompassing upstream component manufacturing, midstream project development and operation, and downstream grid integration, underpin large-scale utilization, yet their spatial organization, structural linkages, and coordinated development remain underexamined. title: Sea Turtle Nesting Beach Fidelity Revealed by Satellite Tracking
abstract: ABSTRACT Site fidelity describes the tendency to return to or reuse familiar sites, yet some animals may use alternative sites while maintaining fidelity to primary locations, with consequences for population estimates as well as resilience to changing environments. Here we assessed and compared nesting beach fidelity of hawksbill turtles ( Eretmochelys imbricata ) on Frégate Island, Seychelles using data from beach foot patrols (2017–2025; n = 575 turtles) and satellite telemetry (2023; n = 10 turtles) and then examined the implications of fidelity strategies for population estimates. title: Delta morphology reveals timings of early ocean regression and hydrologic shift on ancient Mars
abstract: Abstract Mars’ ancient hydrologic history remains a subject of debate, with competing interpretations suggesting either a large ocean or scattered lacustrine environments. Here, we show that delta morphology on Mars records a shift between these hydrologic regimes. Through controlled tank experiments, we identify two distinct delta types: “lobe-extruding deltas” formed during water-level falls and “stepped fan-deltas” formed during rising water levels. title: Fluid–substrate coupled controls on mineral‑phase selection in the Kunlun hydrothermal system
abstract: Abstract Mineral precipitation at submarine hydrothermal vents transfers redox‑sensitive elements from the lithosphere to the ocean. However, conventional plume and sediment‑trap sampling poorly preserves particle‑scale signatures generated at reactive interfaces, hindering robust interpretation of near‑vent mineralization. Here, we deployed open‑cell Fe, Ni, Cu, and Fe–Ni foams within diffuse low‑temperature alkaline fluids of the serpentinization‑driven Kunlun hydrothermal field. title: Mosaic Accumulation of Somatic Genetic Variation and Estimates of Age in the Long‐Lived Reef‐Building Coral Acropora palmata
abstract: Somatic genetic variation (SoGV) accumulates during an organism's lifetime and is traditionally viewed as detrimental rather than adaptive due to links with cancer and senescence. However, in modular organisms like corals, deleterious mutations can be purged at the cellular or polyp level, while adaptive mutations may rise in frequency as polyps create genetically distinct modules. title: Assessment of water quality and anthropogenic impacts on surface and groundwater in the Zhambyl region using GIS-technology
abstract: An integrated hydrochemical and geospatial assessment was performed to access the water quality of wastewater accumulation basins and adjacent aquatic systems in the Zhambyl region (southern Kazakhstan) under conditions of increasing anthropogenic impact. Monitoring was carried out at eight sampling points (P1-P8) during three seasonal campaigns (September 2025, November 2025, and January 2026). The measured parameters included pH, oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), dissolved oxygen (DO), salinity, total dissolved solids (TDS), electrical conductivity (EC), and chemical oxygen demand (COD).

title: Design and Implementation of a Centralized Vessel Monitoring System Using API Harmonization
abstract: Vessel tracking is critical for ensuring the safety and operational efficiency of the maritime industry. However, the reliance on tracking devices from disparate commercial vendors (e.g., Vendor A, Vendor B, and G-Track) introduces severe data fragmentation, forcing operators to navigate multiple proprietary dashboards. Furthermore, custom-built Internet of Things (IoT) tracking devices lack interoperability with these existing commercial platforms. title: Optimising renewable hydrogen hub locations: A GIS-based spatio-temporal integration framework
abstract: This paper presents a Geographic Information System (GIS)-integrated spatio-temporal optimisation framework for the design of renewable hydrogen hubs. This framework embeds high-resolution spatial datasets directly into an hourly Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation to co-optimise the siting, sizing, and hourly operation of system components, thereby minimising the Levelised Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH 2 ). title: Hydrometeorological and hydrogeological trends and drought dynamics in a cold-humid, coastal region
abstract: Quantifying groundwater response to droughts remains challenging, as aquifers typically respond to meteorological conditions with delays, and long-term groundwater records remain limited. This study investigated statistical relationships among meteorological, hydrogeological, and hydrological datasets in the Canadian province of Nova Scotia. title: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
abstract: Abstract The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. title: Estimation of Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) over the Hiramandalam Reservoir Catchment Using GIS
abstract: Reliable estimation of the Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) and the resulting Probable Maximum Flood (PMF) is essential for fixing the design flood of high-hazard hydraulic structures such as spillways and flood-control dams. This paper presents a GIS-based estimation of one-day PMP and the corresponding PMF for the catchment of the Hiramandalam Reservoir, located in Hiramandalam mandal of Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh.
