title: Local Environmental Habitat Templates and Hydroperiod Contingency Jointly Shape Benthic Macroinvertebrate Dynamics in Tropical Choked Coastal Lagoons
abstract: Abstract Coastal lagoons are highly dynamic transitional ecosystems in which benthic macroinvertebrate communities are shaped by spatial and temporal environmental filters. However, the relative importance of lagoon-specific conditions versus temporal variation remains poorly resolved, particularly in the tropics. title: Ontogenetic shifts, trophic differentiation, and predator–prey size relationships in Oxyrhopus false coral snakes from Bahia, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Although snakes of the genus Oxyrhopus are generally regarded as opportunistic predators, the relative roles of interspecific dietary differentiation, ontogenetic variation, and predator morphology in their feeding ecology remain poorly understood. We analyzed the diet of 253 preserved specimens representing four Oxyrhopus species from Bahia, Brazil. title: Underwater hybrid ESD versus conventional ESD for colorectal laterally spreading tumors: a retrospective study
abstract: Background and aims Conventional endoscopic submucosal dissection (C-ESD) is standard for colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) but is time-consuming. abstract: Abstract Magma oceans represent a pivotal stage in the early evolution of terrestrial planets. title: Field sampling guidelines for sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) research in lacustrine and coastal systems: from field collection to laboratory subsampling
abstract: Abstract Sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) has emerged as a powerful proxy for reconstructing past biodiversity and environmental change in lacustrine and coastal systems, yet standardized field guidance remains limited, particularly for researchers working in tropical and coastal depositional environments. Here, we present a practical sampling framework covering the key field protocols of sedaDNA research, from field collection to laboratory subsampling, with emphasis on contamination control at each step. title: Artificial light at night causes unequal and species-specific shifts in infection risk by a generalist marine parasite
abstract: Abstract Light pollution, in the form of artificial light at night (ALAN), changes the normal physiology and behaviour of animals, leading to alterations in interspecific interactions. Parasitism is likely to be impacted, ranging from altered parasite proliferation and transmission to altered host exposure or susceptibility to infection. title: Large-scale marine eDNA database reveals seasonal latitudinal diversity gradients in Japan driven by vagrant fish
abstract: Abstract The spatial and temporal patterns of marine diversity are essential for the sustainable use and management of marine ecosystems. Here, we investigated latitudinal and seasonal diversity gradients of fish genera in Japanese waters using environmental DNA (eDNA) data from 1,765 surveys conducted between 2017 to 2022. We found a negative relationship between genus richness and latitude, consistent with latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG). abstract: Biluhu Timur Village and its surroundings, located in Batudaa Pantai District, Gorontalo Regency, have a topography ranging from hills to coastal plains and relatively high rainfall, which makes them prone to landslides. This study aims to analyze the geological and geomorphological conditions and to map landslide susceptibility zones in Biluhu Timur Village and its surroundings at a scale of 1:25,000. title: Spatial Assessment of Heat Health Risk in Brussels Through GIS and Local Climate Zone Analysis
abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization are increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events, posing significant risks to public health in cities. Although numerous studies have investigated urban heat islands and heat vulnerability, spatially explicit assessments integrating environmental, demographic, and urban morphological characteristics remain limited, particularly in European cities. title: Flood susceptibility assessment using GIS and an analytical hierarchy process in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara, Nigeria
abstract: Flooding remains a major environmental challenge in Ilorin Metropolis, Kwara State, Nigeria. title: GIS-Based Flood Risk Assessment in the Johor River Basin Using AHP and Weighted Overlay
abstract: Flood-risk studies in Malaysia have often concentrated on hydrological hazard, although the consequences of flooding also depend on where people and assets are located and how well communities can cope. This study develops a basin-wide flood-risk index for the Johor River Basin by integrating hazard, exposure and vulnerability within a geographic information system-based multi-criteria decision analysis. abstract: Research on natural disasters requires analytical procedures that are rapid, reproducible, and based on sound scientific principles. Such procedures should also be accessible to institutions responsible for environmental monitoring, land-use planning, and disaster risk reduction. abstract: This paper describes a dataset of drone-based optical 3D mesh models of geological outcrops across South Korea, developed by the Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources (KIGAM). abstract: Ion-conducting elastomers combine large deformability with charge transport but often exhibit trade-offs among mechanical robustness, self-healing, conductivity, and environmental stability. Here, we develop a partially reduced graphene oxide (GO)-reinforced ion-conducting elastomer through thermally induced ring-opening polymerization of α -lipoic acid in the presence of dopamine methacrylamide. abstract: The marine-associated crane fly subgenus Idioglochina Alexander, 1921 of the genus Dicranomyia Stephens, 1829 comprises coastal species whose immature stages are associated with shoreline habitats, but its diversity and ecology in Japan remain insufficiently documented. abstract: ABSTRACT In Coastal Bangladesh, community-based water management groups (WMGs) and water management associations (WMAs) have been central to participatory water governance, yet their postproject sustainability remains uncertain. This article examines how WMGs and WMAs shape participatory water governance and local adaptive capacity in two coastal polders after the withdrawal of project-based support. abstract: ABSTRACT Organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials for flexible and aquatic applications are limited by triplet exciton instability under deformation and environmental perturbation. title: GIS-Based Modelling for Evaluating Soil Erosion Patterns in Ravine-Affected Regions of the Yamuna River, India
abstract: Soil erosion poses a significant environmental challenge, particularly in ravine-affected areas where high-intensity rainfall leads to substantial soil loss, resulting in declining soil fertility and the conversion of productive agricultural land into wasteland. The present study focuses on estimating the rate of soil erosion in one of the severely ravine-affected lands along the Yamuna River and examines changes in soil erosion rates over the years. The Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) Model was employed using various soil erosion estimation parameters in the ArcGIS 10.5 platform.

abstract: Nigeria's mining sector was once a major driver of national economic growth during the 1960s and 1970s, but its prominence declined sharply following the rise of the crude oil industry, leaving it with a marginal GDP share of just 0.17% between 2018 and 2022. Reports from the Development Agenda for Western Nigeria Commission highlight that the country's Southwestern states possess rich mineral reserves such as gold, tin, zircon, rutile, feldspar, and quartz giving the region strong potential to emerge as a global mining hub. abstract: Reducing CO 2 emissions from residential space heating is critical to achieve carbon neutrality, particularly in urban areas. However, effective climate action is often hindered by the lack of precise location-specific emissions data. This study introduces the first web tool for estimating direct (i.e., scope 1) carbon dioxide emissions resulting from space heating of residential buildings at a sub-city scale (100-m resolution). abstract: Coastal sand dunes, which support numerous valuable plant species, are experiencing severe decline and degradation driven by development and coastal erosion. abstract: Marine ecosystems harbor diverse microbial communities with considerable potential for the discovery of environmentally sustainable agents for hydrocarbon remediation. The present investigation compared bacteria isolated from three distinct marine ecological niches: marine algae, ascidians and oilcontaminated marine sediments, to identify efficient biosurfactant-producing strains and to evaluate their crude oil bioremediation potential. abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐term fishery‐dependent datasets for threatened marine fishes are exceptionally rare, yet critical for reconstructing pre‐collapse population states. We analyzed an extensive archive of biological and fishery records for Pogonias courbina collected in southern Brazil during the 1970s–early 1980s, when the stock remained still abundant. abstract: Coastal mangrove sediments are critical reservoirs of antibiotic and heavy metal resistance genes (ARGs/HMRGs). Yet, how pollution history shapes their dissemination remains unclear. abstract: Soil macroinvertebrates mediate key soil processes, but field evidence is scarce in coastal Neotropical pastures. abstract: Groundwater resource protection is a worldwide issue because groundwater plays a crucial role in meeting water supply demands for both natural ecosystems and human activities. abstract: The Brazilian Landform Classification System (Sistema Brasileiro de Classificação de Relevo — SBCR) has organized a new geomorphological structure, placing macro-compartments at the first level and morphostructural domains and subdomains at the second. abstract: Flooding has become one of the most urgent climate-related threats to cities, especially in African coastal cities like eThekwini Municipality, South Africa. abstract: Abstract Biodiversity loss threatens ecosystem services on which humanity depends, yet the strength, form and context-dependency of biodiversity–ecosystem service and biodiversity–ecosystem function relationships remain poorly quantified. abstract: Drought constrains seedling establishment and ecological restoration in tropical coastal forests, where native pioneer species are needed to diversify vulnerable shelterbelt plantations. Mallotus paniculatus is a common pioneer tree with broad environmental adaptability, but its drought-response mechanisms remain poorly understood. abstract: ABSTRACT Dual biodiversity and climate crises have exacerbated declines in global fisheries, resulting in food insecurity for communities that depend on subsistence fishing. As fish populations change and shift their geographic distributions under a changing environment, long‐term planning of fisheries management becomes critical for ensuring food security. title: Complementary Data Sources for Mapping Target Mediterranean Non-Native and Cryptogenic Species: The Role of Local Knowledge and Citizen Science
abstract: Citizen Science (CS) and especially Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK) play an increasingly crucial role in assessing the impacts of climate change on the biodiversity of Mediterranean shallow waters. We explored the use of multiple data sources - including CS, and particularly, LEK and social media - to assess the distribution of selected, especially non-native and cryptogenic thermophilic, marine species in the Mediterranean. This case study aims to test the complementarity and reliability of adequately validated participatory and informal knowledge systems in documenting species occurrences.

title: How Well Can the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) Satellite Mission Observe Irrigation Canals?
abstract: Abstract The capability of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite for observing irrigation canals has remained relatively unexplored. Here, we assess SWOT observability of irrigation canal networks across 22 Asian countries using a new confidence level (CL) metric. Validation against in situ gauge observations showed that higher CL corresponds to significantly lower water‐level retrieval error. Of approximately 795,110 km of canals analyzed, 37.5% (297,799 km) show high confidence, 46.9% (373,035 km) moderate confidence, and 15.6% (124,276 km) low confidence of observability.

title: Stress-dependent shifts in genotoxic sensitivity of zooplankton
abstract: The ocean is increasingly exposed to multiple stressors, including rising temperatures and metal pollution. Zooplankton are central components of the marine food web and understanding lethal responses and underpinning molecular mechanisms across species from different habitats is essential for predicting ecosystem resilience. This study compares two zooplankton species from an Arctic fjord, the near surface-dwelling Acartia longiremis and the lipid-rich, deeper-dwelling Calanus finmarchicus , for their molecular responses to acute and sub-acute temperature and copper (Cu) stress. title: Water Quality Index Evaluation and GIS-Based Suitability Assessment of Groundwater and Surface Water for Domestic Use in Otuabagi Community, Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: Access to potable water in oil-producing communities of the Niger Delta remains constrained by decades of hydrocarbon exploration and inadequate environmental management. abstract: Saturn’s icy moon Enceladus features chemical signatures consistent with an alkaline soda ocean with H 2 production via hydrothermal water-rock reactions. abstract: The term sinkhole refers to sudden ground subsidence caused by natural or anthropogenic factors and represents a locally significant geological hazard. abstract: Understanding seabird diet is fundamental to assessing trophic interactions and predicting responses to environmental change. abstract: One of the distinguishing features of hybrid infrastructure is the need to find balance between multiple functional performances. Multi-criteria decision analysis is an ideal tool for exploring this balance and identifying an ideal solution, but there are few examples of its application to coastal infrastructure. abstract: Pinnipeds, including seals, sea lions and walruses, are marine mammals susceptible to a variety of pathological conditions. Although neoplastic lesions in these species are receiving increased attention, relatively little information is available compared to neoplastic studies in domestic animals. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are highly vulnerable to coastal environmental change and anthropogenic disturbance. The mangrove forests distributed along the eastern and western coasts of Shenzhen experience contrasting environmental regimes. abstract: The confirmation of species distributions and taxonomic identification is critical for documenting biodiversity under increasing anthropogenic pressures. This objective is challenging for gelatinous plankton due to logistical constraints related to safety and preservation. This study documents and validates the taxonomic identity of live individuals of Chiropsalmus alipes from Bahía de Banderas (Mexican Tropical Pacific), using high- resolution in situ video and photographic records. abstract: Abstract Island‐induced eddies from the Canary Islands region propagate southwestward along the Canary Eddy Corridor, exporting biological and biogeochemical properties to the oligotrophic open ocean. abstract: Benthic organisms have relatively limited mobility and long life cycles, enabling them to comprehensively reflect long-term changes in water quality, sediment conditions, and hydrological conditions. This study integrates survey data on benthic animals in Dongting Lake from 2001 to 2025, with a particular focus on reviewing publicly available data from 2016 to 2025, and conducts stage-based visualization of three categories of indicators: phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic animals. abstract: Abstract Ecotypic divergence in Atlantic cod ( Gadus morhua ) is well established for adult fish, but the extent to which juveniles differ is still poorly understood. abstract: Plant biodiversity plays a pivotal role in buffering ecosystems and human societies against the impacts of natural disasters. abstract: The study examined impact of perennial pluvial flooding on the architectural quality and performance of residential buildings in selected Areas of Port Harcourt Metropolis. Resilience Theory guided the theoretical framework of this study. The methodology integrates both primary and secondary data sources. With a population of 1,416, a sample frame of 708, and a sample size of 512 determined using the Taro Yamane method, the study employed field observations, surveys, and statistical analysis, including descriptive statistics. abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral imaging is an information-rich, reflectance-based spectroscopic method for non-intrusive investigation of physiological and biochemical properties of various organisms from cellular to ecological levels. Although several recent works have used hyperspectral imaging combined with predictive models to estimate algal biomass and valuable pigments, utilizing the advantages of hyperspectral sensing to reveal key physiological spectral indices remains far less definitive in microalgae. title: Inherited Carboniferous to Permian zircons constrain the continuity of the Gondwanan continental arc beneath the central Chilean Andes (32-34° S)
abstract: This study investigates the crustal architecture and tectonomagmatic evolution of the central Chilean Andes (32-34° S) through new U-Pb zircon geochronology. Results from the western border of the Principal Cordillera (32-33° S) reveal a dominant late Carboniferous to early Permian inherited signature, accounting for 60-62% of zircon populations in Late Cretaceous and Miocene units. abstract: Abstract Background Forensic DNA phenotyping (FDP) provides vital investigative leads by predicting externally visible characteristics (EVCs). However, a significant “genomic gap” exists as most FDP models are calibrated on European or East Asian datasets, limiting their reliability in the genetically diverse Southeast Asian (SEA) region. title: Nonlinear loss of recalcitrant organic carbon in saltmarsh sediments following Spartina alterniflora eradication: Evidence from microbial metabolic shifts
abstract: Large-scale eradication of the invasive Spartina alterniflora on China’s coasts is implemented to restore wetland ecosystems, yet it introduces a critical yet overlooked environmental trade-off: massive plant residue input may destabilize sediment organic carbon (SOC), the core part of coastal blue carbon. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems along the Guangdong coastline serve as a vital blue carbon sink, yet their carbon sequestration potential under changing climatic conditions requires rigorous assessment and forward-looking evaluation. This study develops an integrated framework combining remote sensing techniques and spatial modeling approaches to quantify historical changes and project future trajectories of mangrove blue carbon stocks in Guangdong Province, China. abstract: This study presents an automated pre-classification data filtering method that increases confidence in the classification of cetacean acoustic events lacking visual verification, while minimizing bias and reducing the need for manual review. The study tests the approach on false killer whale (Pseudorca crassidens) acoustic data from the North Pacific Ocean. abstract: Balikpapan City was pivotal in the pre-independence petroleum industry. As a vital geopolitical asset, it became a strategic WWII theater between Japanese and Allied forces. Military defense remnants including bunkers, trenches, artillery, and military bases are extensively concentrated in East Balikpapan District. title: Digital Terrain Model: An Approach to Evaluating Climate Change in Oko
abstract: This study examines the application of Digital Terrain Models (DTMs) as a geospatial approach to assessing climate change impacts in Oko, Anambra State, Nigeria. Oko, located in Orumba North Local Government Area, has been severely affected by climate-induced hazards, particularly gully erosion and flooding. abstract: This paper presents the comprehensive results of recent archaeological research conducted in the Ain Naga region of Biskra (Algeria), an area notably characterized by a high density of Protohistoric funerary monuments locally known as "Nechaz" or Mounds (Tumuli). title: Effect of environmental conditions on two vibriophages and their host
abstract: Bacteriophages play a key role in regulating Vibrio populations in marine environments, and environmental conditions may influence their replication and interactions with bacterial hosts. This study aimed to isolate and characterize the bacteriophage PvVp2, which infects the pandemic Vibrio parahaemolyticus strain KX, and to compare its environmental performance with that of phage CHOED, a lytic phage infecting Vibrio anguillarum . abstract: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the generalized variable-coefficient Gardner equation without an external force, which models wave propagation in coastal internal solitary waves and plasma physics. title: From Rainless Days to Systemic Drought Risk in Indonesia: Climate Drivers, Drought Propagation, Food–Water Vulnerability, and Adaptive Resilience
abstract: Prolonged rainless periods are an increasingly important climate-risk signal in Indonesia, but their societal significance cannot be understood from rainfall duration alone. This qualitative literature review synthesizes recent evidence on how meteorological dryness evolves into agricultural, hydrological, and socioeconomic drought and examines the implications for food production, water security, rural livelihoods, and drought governance in Indonesia. abstract: Background EuroSCORE II, the Additive EuroSCORE, and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS PROM) are widely used cardiac surgery risk models, but their performance has not been evaluated in a cardiac surgery centre located at high altitude (≥2,500 m asl). Methods We conducted a retrospective external validation study using prospectively collected registry data from consecutive adult cardiac surgery procedures performed at Hospital Universitario Mayor-Méderi (2,600 m asl), Bogotá, Colombia, between January 2019 and February 2026 ( N = 1,486). title: Microeukaryotic Diversity and Habitat Structuring in a Desiccating Alkaline Maar Lake (Central Mexico)
abstract: Microeukaryotes are important components of microbial food webs in saline and alkaline lakes, yet their diversity and distribution across distinct microhabitats remain poorly understood. We characterized microeukaryotic communities associated with microbialites, microbial mats, hypersaline waters, and sediments in the desiccating maar lake Rincón de Parangueo (central Mexico) using 18S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. title: Codon-aware multi-scale feature fusion for metagenomic sequence classification
abstract: Microorganisms exert profound influences on both natural ecosystems and human society. As the cornerstone of microbial research, metagenomics relies on the precise analysis of large-scale, multi-source genomic data. However, discriminating among diverse sequence types remains a formidable challenge. To address this, we present CamFi (Codon-aware Multi-scale Feature Fusion), a unified framework integrating overlapping nucleotide-triplet representations with multi-scale dilated convolutions for classifying prokaryotic chromosomes, eukaryotic chromosomes, plasmids, and viruses. title: Uncovering regional differences in plastic pollution distribution along the Norwegian coast
abstract: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms behind coastal plastic accumulation is crucial for more targeted clean-up actions and policy-making. We used a systematically collected dataset for plastic pollution along the Norwegian coast, added physical and socio-environmental response variables to it, and used linear regression to identify the most important factors that influence plastic accumulation. title: Rapid CFU-equivalent quantification of Enterococcus in environmental waters via a competitive lateral flow assay
abstract: Rapid and quantitative assessment of fecal contamination in environmental waters is essential for effective public health protection and timely water quality management. However, conventional monitoring based on membrane filtration requires 18–24 h incubation to enumerate culturable Enterococcus as colony-forming units (CFUs), resulting in delays between contamination events and management decisions. abstract: This article investigates the spatial distribution of public toilets in the city of Recife-PE and its relationship with public leisure spaces and sociodemographic variables. The provision of public toilets can stimulate urban life in the city's free space and influence the model of building sustainable, accessible, and equitable cities. There is a gap in the area of urban planning related to the offer of public toilet equipment, its location, and socio-spatial aspects. title: An Integrated Geospatial and Socio-economic Assessment of Flood Risk in North-western Nigeria Using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis
abstract: Flood disasters have become increasingly frequent and severe in Nigeria, driven by a combination of climatic shifts and anthropogenic pressures. This research paper assesses flood risk vulnerability across the seven states of the Northwest geopolitical zone (Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kano, Jigawa, and Kaduna). abstract: The current work presents a probabilistic seismic hazard assessment (PSHA) for engineering bedrock conditions (Vs30} = 760 m/s) across the Jizan region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. For this purpose, we compiled a homogenised earthquake catalogue covering 827–2022 CE, including historical and instrumental records from multiple authoritative sources. abstract: Autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) require reliable encounter assessment to support remote supervision in restricted and coastal waters. This paper proposes a shore-side collision-risk surveillance approach based on Closest Point of Approach (CPA) and Time to Closest Point of Approach (TCPA). The proposed framework combines own-ship telemetry, target-track data, relative-motion estimates, and communication status to produce a four-tier alert status for the monitoring operator. abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable estimates of abundance are fundamental to conservation assessments and measuring the success of conservation actions, especially where populations are in decline or recovery. Here we present an approach that improves statistical precision and biological value of estimates of population size by integrating multiple data sources in a marine system. title: Elevated temperature exacerbates red sore disease caused by Vibrio vulnificus in American eels (Anguilla rostrata)
abstract: The marine pathogenic bacterium Vibrio vulnificus is linked to epizootics of a dermal ulcerative disease, causing high mortality in European and Japanese eels. American eels ( Anguilla rostrata ) experience a similar condition, commonly referred to as red sore disease (RSD). Field studies indicate that V. vulnificus infections highly correlate with RSD in American eels, but causation remains un-established. abstract: Lignin is a key structural polymer in seagrass cell walls, supporting tissue rigidity, mechanical resilience, and resistance to hydrodynamic forcing. title: Optimal duration of anticoagulation after successful catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: insights from recent randomized trials
abstract: The optimal duration of oral anticoagulation (OAC) after successful catheter ablation (CA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) remains controversial. Current guidelines recommend indefinite OAC based on stroke risk profiles, but long-term therapy adherence is suboptimal due to bleeding concerns. abstract: Aquaculture governance in Norway has largely developed around the rapid expansion of Atlantic salmon farming, while repeated efforts to establish cod aquaculture have resulted in limited and discontinuous production. Recent improvements in breeding, biological performance, and market conditions have, however, renewed commercial interest in cod farming and raised a central policy question: to what extent can regulatory frameworks developed for salmon be transferred to cod aquaculture? abstract: Conventional agricultural practices face increasing scrutiny due to their environmental impact, including soil degradation, water pollution, and high reliance on synthetic inputs. Sustainable agriculture seeks to mitigate these issues by integrating ecologically sound and economically viable methods. Marine macroalgae, commonly known as seaweed, have emerged as a promising natural resource with multifaceted applications in sustainable farming. abstract: Riverbank erosion and accretion are natural and ongoing geomorphological processes in the huge delta of Bangladesh, driven by the mighty Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna river systems. abstract: Integrated Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and Big Data Analytics (BDA) offer substantial potential to improve visibility, trust, coordination, and decision-making in maritime logistics. abstract: Information on heat-related health risks that is based on meteorological data and forecasts is important for outdoor workers, farm managers, and many other stakeholders, but visualization and interpretation of climate data in a user-friendly way remains a challenge. This proof-of-concept research developed Sol, an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to conveniently interpret and communicate heat stress risks through smartphones and other devices. abstract: Purpose of Study: The study analyzed the effect of strategy implementation on growth of registered Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Mombasa County, Kenya. abstract: Urban fragmentation as a process of spatial differentiation is increasingly shaped by the internal boundaries and discontinuities that segregate identified parts of the metropolitan areas from within. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are dynamic coastal habitats that support distinctive microbial communities capable of producing structurally diverse and biologically potent secondary metabolites. Among these, endophytic fungi residing asymptomatically within mangrove plants represent an underexplored resource with substantial potential for the discovery of novel antimicrobial agents. abstract: A deeper understanding of the enzymatic machinery operating in the gastrointestinal tract of Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ) can aid nutritional research and the development of future aquafeeds. Current knowledge does not fully capture the diversity of digestive enzymes, their temporal and compartmental dynamics, and how the enzymatic repertoire is shaped by the feed. abstract: Background: Focusing on Manado, Indonesia, a coastal destination balancing growth and ecological risk, we develop and test an integrative model grounded in stakeholder and legitimacy theories that links environmental management accounting (EMA), CSR commitment, and environmental disclosure quality (EDQ). abstract: Climate change is leading to more frequent and extreme salinity fluctuations in marine environments, and the presence of emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl contaminants (PFAS) is attracting increasing attention. abstract: This study examines how rural tourism supports sustainable development, economic recovery, social stability, and cultural preservation in post-conflict regions, using Transcarpathia, Ukraine, as a case study for 2022–2024. It applies a mixed-methods approach combining satellite remote sensing, GIS-based spatial analysis, and socio-economic indicators to assess land-use change, infrastructure recovery, ecological stability, and socio-economic resilience. abstract: Abstract Coccolithophores are unicellular marine phytoplankton that produce complex and intricately shaped mineralized scales called coccoliths. Coccoliths are produced in an intracellular vesicle where crystal nucleation occurs, from which several individual calcite units develop with anisotropic crystallographic facets, prompting studies into the cellular mechanisms that control crystal growth within the cell. title: Resource‐Based Carrying Capacity Estimates for the Florida Manatee ( Trichechus manatus latirostris ) in a Subtropical Estuary
abstract: ABSTRACT Resource‐based carrying capacity can constrain abundance and population dynamics of large herbivores, including in aquatic ecosystems. Seagrass decline in the Indian River Lagoon (IRL) has raised concern that reduced forage availability may limit foraging opportunities for large marine herbivores, particularly the Florida manatee ( Trichechus manatus latirostris ). We applied a resource‐based carrying‐capacity model to evaluate how long‐term changes in seagrass availability may have affected the number of manatees the IRL can support. title: Evaluating Kelp Feedstock for Alginate-Based Materials: Physicochemical Characterization of Sodium Alginate and Aquaculture Considerations
abstract: Abstract Cultivated kelps are a scalable marine feedstock for renewable polymers, but regional aquaculture supply chains lack engineering benchmarks for the alginate yield and quality. Here, we apply a lower-hazard citrate-based process to quantify bioplastics-relevant alginate metrics across cultivated northeast Pacific kelps from commercial farms in British Columbia (Canada) and Alaska (USA). Ten blade biomass samples spanning five species were screened. title: Acoustic recognition of tilapia feeding intensity via LoRA-fine-tuned multimodal large language models
abstract: Real-time assessment of fish feeding intensity is essential for demand-based feeding in intensive aquaculture, yet existing methods rely on external spectrogram preprocessing and large annotated datasets, limiting practical deployment. This study proposes an end-to-end approach that reformulates feeding intensity recognition as an audio instruction-following task using the multimodal large language model Qwen2.5-Omni-3B. title: Effectiveness of experiential practice on environmental awareness and pro-environmental behavior: evidence from junior high school students in Toride City, Japan
abstract: Abstract This study verified the effects of “experiential practice” and “visualizing” carbon dioxide reduction on the transformation of junior high school students' environmental awareness and pro-environmental behavior (PEB). We sought to propose measures for sustaining high environmental awareness and choice of appropriate actions. title: The Empire Under One Umbrella: Espionage, Reporting and the Communications System of the Mauryan State in the Aśokan Edicts, the Contemporary Textual Sources and Recent Scholarship
abstract: This paper argues that the Mauryan empire could not have been held together under a single authority without a system for acquiring, moving and verifying information, and that this proposition — which no surviving document states in so many words — can be established by correlating four independent bodies of evidence: the Aśokan inscriptions, the Arthaśāstra, the Greek testimony as transmitted by later authors, and the Buddhist literary tradition. title: Multi‐Scale Assessment of Population Exposure to Landslides in Vietnam
abstract: ABSTRACT Vietnam's complex terrain and monsoon climate create extensive landslide‐prone conditions, yet the population exposure patterns of its urban, rural, and demographic groups remain insufficiently quantified. title: Economic Drivers and the Dynamics of Inclusive and Sustainable Urbanization: An Assessment of Medan with Comparative Insights from Bangkok and Marseille
abstract: Urbanization can drive economic growth but also increases spatial pressure, environmental risks, and disparities in access to urban services. This research examines how economic structure, investment orientation, and governance capacity shape inclusive and sustainable urbanization in Medan, using Bangkok and Marseille as comparative cases. title: Can Passive Samplers Replace Biota in Risk Assessment of Resuspended Contaminated Sediments?
abstract: Resuspension of contaminated sediments elevates turbidity and mobilises sediment‑bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) into the water column, increasing their bioavailability and toxicity to aquatic organisms. Passive samplers (PS), which accumulate the freely dissolved fraction of contaminants, have the potential to replace biota as a non‑invasive tool for estimating exposure and toxicity. title: Instantaneous heating rate forcing differentiates tropical high-cloud adjustments across greenhouse gases
abstract: Tropical high clouds are central to large-scale circulation and the hydrological cycle. The consensus expectation is that they rise and contract under surface warming, but their fast adjustment to greenhouse gas (GHG) concentrations is diverse. All GHGs reduce atmospheric longwave loss, yet tropical high clouds can increase or decrease depending on the gas. title: Station-Area Accessibility and Rail-Property Value Capture for Urban Regeneration in Yangon
abstract: Urban rail can support local economic development when station areas are accessible, connected and integrated with surrounding land uses. This study examines Ma Hlwa Gone Station on the East Wing of the Yangon Circular Railway as a case of railway-led urban regeneration. It applies an implementation-oriented TOCC framework combining TOD principles, compact urban form, Rail + Property mechanisms and institutional coordination. title: New traveling wave solutions for the extended (3+1)-dimensional KdV-Calogero-Bogoyavlenskii-Schiff and the fourth-order nonlinear Ablowitz-Kaup-Newell-Segur water wave equations using efficient techniques
abstract: This study develops novel solitary wave solutions for the recently introduced extended (3+1)-dimensional KdV-Calogero-Bogoyavlenskii-Schiff (KdV-CBS) equation and the fourth-order nonlinear Ablowitz-Kaup-Newell-Segur (AKNS) water wave equation with a perturbation parameter. title: Spatiotemporal analysis of land use change in the Eastern Slopes of the Jerusalem Area
abstract: Abstract Urban expansion is one of the main drivers of land use changes in the Central Palestinian Mountains. It influences the basic environmental components, including water, soil, and specifically vegetation cover. In the present study, the study area has experienced noticeable land use changes over the past three decades, resulting in many adverse impacts on the environment. This study aims to examine land use changes and identify the main drivers and consequences of these changes on vegetation cover during the period 1997 and 2022. title: Using spatio-temporal models to assist ecosystem-based fisheries management: a New Zealand case study
abstract: Tools to understand or predict ecosystem changes (e.g., fish community analyses) and the impacts of management measures on ecosystem components (e.g., ecosystem simulation models) are instrumental to the success of ecosystem-based fisheries management (EBFM). We developed a workflow using vector autoregressive spatio-temporal (VAST) models to assist EBFM in the Chatham Rise middle depth (CHAT MD) region, located in New Zealand waters. title: Mapping land-use/land-cover change and associated predictors in Cambodia from 2000 to 2020: Landsat-based SVM mapping and random forest analysis
abstract: Introduction Land-use/land-cover (LULC) change in Cambodia is relevant to forest conservation and land management in the Lower Mekong region. Methods This study describes mapped change between three national LULC snapshots (2000, 2010, and 2020) using Landsat TM/ETM+/OLI imagery, supervised support vector machine (SVM) classification, post-classification transition matrices, and random forest (RF) predictor-importance analysis. abstract: Introduction Seagrass meadows have undergone substantial declines in Vietnam over recent decades owing to habitat loss, climate change, nutrient enrichment, and other anthropogenic disturbances. Enhalus acoroides , a dominant large tropical seagrass, has experienced marked reductions in distribution and abundance, yet information on its population genetic structure remains limited. title: Smartphone-based mapping of home ignition zone attributes for wildland–urban interface fire risk assessment
abstract: Background Assessing home ignition zone attributes is essential for reducing wildfire risk in wildland–urban interface (WUI) communities; however, traditional satellite imagery often lacks sufficient spatial resolution and timely updates to capture localized fuel conditions near structures. Aims This study develops and validates a smartphone-based framework for real-time detection, mapping and 3D visualization of building features and defensible space fuel to support wildfire risk assessment and mitigation in WUI environments. title: SAFEBORDERS (DIGITAL CONVERSATIONAL AGENT): PREVENTION OF SMUGGLING OF CIGARETTES, DRUGS AND CONTROLLED GOODS AT MALAYSIAN BORDERS
abstract: This study presents the design, development, and usability evaluation of SafeBorders, an AI-powered bilingual digital conversational agent developed to support public advocacy and community engagement in preventing the smuggling of cigarettes, drugs, and controlled goods at Malaysian borders. title: Complete mitochondrial genome of Arcuatula japonica (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) and its phylogenetic analysis
abstract: Arcuatula japonica (Dunker, 1857) (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) is a marine mussel distributed primarily in the northwestern Pacific. To clarify its evolutionary position and evaluate the taxonomic status of Crenellinae, we sequenced and characterized the complete mitochondrial genome of A. japonica. title: Building on sand: state capacity, livelihoods, and the limits of environmental governance in Cabo Verde
abstract: Cabo Verde has built an extensive environmental policy framework, ratifying major multilateral agreements and enacting decree-laws that formally regulate the exploitation of natural resources. Yet on Santiago Island, small-scale illegal extraction of development minerals by low-income households continues to cause severe degradation of beaches, watersheds and hillsides. title: Industrial Development in Protected Zones: A Four-Gate Legal Assessment of the Tahura Ngurah Rai Factory Case in Bali
abstract: The reported construction-material factory linked to Russian investment near Bali's Tahura Ngurah Rai highlights a recurring difficulty in environmental governance: the coexistence of land certificates, business registrations, spatial restrictions and conservation boundaries. This article examines the legal consequences of that overlap through normative legal research using statutory, conceptual and documentary case approaches. title: Building adaptive capacity of US Gulf Coast city practitioners to extreme weather events
abstract: Abstract Building city practitioners’ capacity to prepare for and respond to climate change-driven events can increase coastal cities’ resilience. We conducted a first-of-its-kind mixed methods research project from 2021 to 2023 with 46 US Gulf Coast small and midsize cities to measure the effectiveness of an adaptive capacity-building intervention: a stormwater planning tool called FloodWise Communities (FWC) deployed through the engagement between researchers and practitioners in each city. City practitioners were surveyed pre- and post-intervention between September 2021 and December 2022.

title: Archaeological micromorphology in Latin America: an overview
abstract: Micromorphology helps to reveal fundamental aspects of archaeological sites and landscapes that are invisible to the naked eye. Apart from discerning human contributions from patterns of natural sediment/soil formation, deposition, and alteration, this technique, coupled with others, has been able to showcase specific human activities hidden in the archaeological record. Over the last couple of decades, micromorphology has slowly entered the realm of archaeological techniques in Latin America and neighboring regions. title: The Evolutionary History of Early Ray‐Finned Fishes (Pan‐Actinopterygii)
abstract: One out of every two vertebrate species is a ray-finned fish (Actinopterygii). The ~380-million-year fossil record of ray-finned fishes provides a window into the evolutionary history of actinopterygian diversity in deep time. The actinopterygian fossil record shows that the ray-finned fish crown group (Actinopterygii) lived alongside speciose members of now extinct lineages, collectively referred to as early actinopterygians. abstract: ABSTRACT Global wild‐sourced wildlife trade is structured not only by the intensity and composition of traded species, but also by the routes, hubs, and redistribution pathways that connect countries/territories into an intricate network. Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of trade networks over time is essential for identifying emerging governance challenges and conservation priorities. title: A novel bacterial symbiont in the seaweed Gracilaria tenuistipitata and its promising anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative potential in relation to special secreted metabolites
abstract: Marine macroalgae host compositionally complex microbiomes that constitute an evolutionarily refined, yet largely unexplored source of structurally diverse natural products. Thus, the bioactivities of the algae may be related to those of their associated microorganisms. Here we describe the discovery of strain S.100, an endophytic bacterium isolated from the red alga Gracilaria tenuistipitata and displaying remarkable anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative activities, through a primary screening on ethyl acetate (EtAc), chloroform and n-hexane extracts of its culture. title: Circulating in the oyster immune system: multi-compartment modeling reveals dynamic intercellular trafficking of biodegradable nanoplastics
abstract: Studies of the cellular fate of nanoplastics (NPs) in bivalves commonly overlook the dynamic trafficking of particles among immune cells. Here, we established a multi-compartment kinetic framework using time-resolved measurements of hemocyte populations for 2-h following a 1-h in vitro exposure to polylactic acid biodegradable nanoplastics (PLA-NPs). title: Spatial Analysis of Atmospheric Pollutants in An-Najaf Governorate Based on Sentinel-5 Satellite Observations
abstract: Sentinel-5P satellite imagery, in combination with Geographic Information Systems (GIS), was utilized to analyze the spatial distribution of the atmospheric pollutant gases—ozone (O₃), sulfur dioxide (SO₂), and carbon monoxide (CO)—across An-Najaf Governorate in central Iraq. abstract: Orthopedic implant biofilms are not only antibiotic-tolerant bacterial communities but metabolically active niches that reshape host immunity. Compared with planktonic infection, mature biofilms impose spatial and metabolic constraints that can uncouple leukocyte recruitment from sterilizing activity. abstract: Traditional early medieval historiography frequently treats the early Saxons as a homogeneous, migrating ethnic entity. This paper explores this paradigm by conducting an exploratory quantitative textual and spatial analysis of early medieval identity construction, focusing on the maritime networks of the North Sea and the territorial river systems of the Rhine-Meuse delta in Northwest Europe. abstract: This thesis sought to determine to what extent photogrammetry can reduce the time and resources required for property assessment when parcels are affected by expropriations linked to infrastructure projects taking the district of Ventanilla during 2025 as the case study. The work followed an applied approach with a quasi experimental design combining drone flights GIS based geoprocessing and document review. abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. title: Macroevolutionary dynamics and predictors of tropical rain forest plant diversity
abstract: Tropical rain forest is the most diverse terrestrial biome, yet the drivers of its diversification across space and time remain poorly understood. Although heterogeneous diversification rates, including both ancient and recent radiations, have been reported, these dynamics have rarely been examined within a single lineage across deep evolutionary timescales. abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) change is a major driver of rangeland degradation, threatening grazing resources and pastoral livelihoods in the Guinea and Sudan savanna ecosystems of northeastern Nigeria. This study evaluates the impact of LULC change on grazing resources in Dauchi Grazing Reserve, Song LGA, Adamawa State, Nigeria, using multi-temporal satellite imagery covering forty years. abstract: Abstract Digital traces from social media increasingly shape how tourist preferences are observed and interpreted, yet attraction-related attention is often treated as a single aggregate indicator, with limited consideration of where this attention comes from and how attractions are discursively framed. abstract: Halimeda is a genus of green macroalgae found in Indonesian waters, including the waters around Ternate Island. Coastal communities typically consume algae as a food source. However, over time, knowledge about algae has expanded, and people have become more aware of their nutritional content. abstract: ABSTRACT Many engineering courses are still organized according to a predominantly deductive and content‐oriented approach: theoretical foundations are introduced first, while authentic disciplinary activity is often postponed to later stages of the curriculum. abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a practical, standardized ophthalmic examination protocol for teleost fish using captive rockfish (Family Sebastidae) as a pilot population. abstract: Hypersaline brines (salinity >10 wt%) generated by the water, energy, and agricultural sectors present a significant challenge for sustainable wastewater management. Although solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers an energy-efficient route for brine treatment and zero-liquid-discharge operation, persistent salt accumulation hinders long-term performance and operational stability. abstract: Biological invasions have been defined as one striking indicator of the Anthropocene epoch, with more species being translocated beyond their native range by human activities. The inventory of non-native species in a region provides basic information for further exploration of biological invasions. title: Redesigning boat owner-crew labor relations in Kupang fisheries: a systems and behavioral analysis
abstract: Informal patron-client arrangements in capture fisheries can combine vessel finance, employment, social assistance, and market control, creating both protection and dependency. This study examined how boat owner-crew labor relations are reproduced and how a feasible transformation could be designed at Tenau Coastal Fishing Port and Oeba Fish Landing Base, Kupang City, Indonesia. title: Targeting Flood Resilience Investments Through a Readiness Gaps Index: Evidence from Mississippi
abstract: Flooding is among the most costly and recurrent disasters globally, including in the United States. The Southeastern United States is vulnerable to billion-dollar climate disasters. In Mississippi, high flood exposure coincides with uneven institutional capacity and socioeconomic constraints, yet existing assessments largely emphasize hazard or social vulnerability in isolation while overlooking integrated readiness for resilience planning. abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive aquaculture practices heavily reliant on conventional energy sources have contributed significantly to environmental degradation, primarily through greenhouse gas emissions. abstract: This study explains the living conditions of the coastal Bajo tribe in Muna Regency, Indonesia, and examines their potential for improving housing quality through a community-led self-help approach. Adopting a convergent parallel mixed-methods design, fieldwork was conducted across three purposively selected vulnerable settlements: Tapitapi, Lagasa, and Pasikuta villages (N = 259). abstract: The southern region of East Java is part of the Sunda Subduction Zone, which has high seismic activity due to the convergence of the Indo-Australian and Eurasian Plates. This study aims to analyze the probability of earthquake occurrences in the southern offshore of East Java using the Poisson distribution and the Gutenberg–Richter law. abstract: Beyşehir Lake, located within the provinces of Konya and Isparta, is Turkey’s third-largest lake and the country’s largest freshwater resource. title: Nicotinium-based surface-active ionic liquids as antimicrobial surfactants: Micellization properties, antibiofilm activity, and biocompatibility
abstract: A new family of nicotinium-based surface-active ionic liquids (CₙNicBr, n = 10-16) was synthesized by N-alkylation of nicotine and characterized by NMR, MS and thermogravimetry (stable to 215 °C). abstract: The marine realm, which covers approximately 70% of Earth’s surface, harbours a vast diversity of untapped bioactive resources. abstract: When discussed together, menstrual and socioenvironmental health often focus on questions of hygiene and risk management, centering the materialities, distribution, and disposal of menstrual products. abstract: This study examines agricultural land-use change, socio-economic transformation, and food security implications in Aimas District, Sorong Regency, Indonesia. abstract: Rainfall measurement with high spatial and temporal resolution is critical for flood forecasting, drought mitigation, and disaster preparedness. Rainfall patterns are highly variable, both geographically and over time. This variability presents a significant challenge for monitoring, as rain gauges can accurately capture temporal patterns only at a single location. abstract: The current study evaluated the genetic characterization and differentiation of oil families in the units of the Yamama, Nahr Umr, and Mishrif reservoirs of the Ratawi oil field, south of Iraq. abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of certification for Indonesian-flagged ships at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority and Harbor Master Office (KSOP Utama Tanjung Priok), identify the constraints encountered, examine its contribution to maritime safety and security, and formulate optimization efforts. abstract: Cyclones remain a serious threat to Bangladesh's coastal communities. However, their impacts are not felt equally across all geographical locations and sociodemographic groups. The community of Bauphal, Patuakhali, is especially vulnerable because its livelihoods are tied to rivers, boats, fishing, and seasonal mobility rather than fixed land-based settlement. title: The Role of Geographical Indications in Sustainable Coffee Tourism in Forest Areas: Lessons from Lemukih Coffee
abstract: Geographical Indications (GIs) protect distinctive local products while supporting community development and sustainable tourism. However, their effectiveness depends on regional government capacity to integrate product protection, economic development, environmental conservation, and tourism. This study examines the potential of Lemukih Robusta Coffee as a regional flagship product, evaluates the effectiveness of the Buleleng Regency Government’s policies in managing and protecting its GI in areas adjacent to forests, and explores how GI protection can support sustainable coffee tourism. abstract: Accurate software defect prediction is essential for identifying fault-prone modules early and reducing software testing and maintenance costs. However, Within-Project Defect Prediction (WPDP) models may perform poorly when the target project has limited labeled defect data. Cross-Project Defect Prediction (CPDP) addresses this limitation by transferring knowledge from other projects, but heterogeneous feature distributions, source–target mismatch, and negative transfer remain significant challenges. abstract: This study evaluates four breeding lines of the Carniolan honey bee, Apis mellifera carnica, across distinct ecological zones of Serbia and Montenegro. The objective was to assess phenotypic, morphometric, and isoenzyme polymorphism of local populations adapted to contrasting climatic and altitudinal conditions. abstract: This study integrates remote sensing and spatial econometric techniques to identify pixel-level wind energy corridors in West Bengal, India. Weibull scale (A) and shape (K) parameter rasters at 100 m resolution were combined with Dynamic World land-cover data to evaluate how landscape characteristics influence wind resource potential. abstract: A novel β-cyclodextrin-modified silica composite (β-CD-SiO 2 ) was prepared by in situ thermal esterification for selective elimination of cholesterol in tuna oil refining. Characterisations revealed the effective immobilisation of β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) onto mesoporous silica (mean pore size 24.40 nm). abstract: Settlement represents a key transition from dispersal to recruitment, during which predation can strongly influence population dynamics through both consumptive and non-consumptive effects. Predation generates chemical cues that convey information about the presence of predators, attacks on prey, ingestion of prey and post-attack conditions. abstract: Climate change is intensifying drought vulnerability in northern Ghana, posing serious risks to crop production, food security, and rural livelihoods in semi-arid regions. abstract: ABSTRACT Pyrethroid insecticides are largely exploited in Italy to reduce Aedes albopictus nuisance and to discontinue autochthonous transmission of exotic arboviruses. abstract: Kinematic graph interpretation is a basic physics competency that often challenges students because of abstract vector representations and weak geometric transformation skills. This study analyzes the influence of vector animation videos on kinematic graph learning, with spatial skills as a mediating variable. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design was applied to 60 Grade X students of SMAS Ta’miriyah Surabaya. abstract: Abstract In this article, I examine how I embed algorithms in instrumental and electroacoustic compositional practices to organise numerical data drawn from extra-musical environmental and cosmological contexts within musical materials and structures. I explore such material-semiotic exchanges between music and surrounding environments to sonically reconfigure the matter of the life stories suggested by Ursula Le Guin, stories that challenge anthropocentric narratives. abstract: High-quality Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are essential for accurately estimating lake storage variations, but the high cost of in-situ measurements limits their large-scale application. Reconstructing DEMs from remote sensing-derived lake contours is a promising low-cost alternative. abstract: Delamination is a critical failure mode in glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) laminates used in artisanal boatbuilding, particularly under dynamic loading associated with slamming phenomena. This study evaluates the effectiveness of interlaminar aramid fiber stitching as a reinforcement technique to improve the interlaminar shear strength and damage tolerance of GFRP laminates manufactured using traditional hand lay-up processes. abstract: This article proposes vegetal reproduction and photographic reproduction as analytical models for accounting for the ways in which the past survives in the present. These models propose non-linear temporalities, defined by latency, germination, and fragmentary reproduction that destabilize narratives of closure and progress. abstract: Climate change is fundamentally altering the geographic ranges of plant-pathogenic microorganisms, with profound implications for global food security and agricultural sustainability. abstract: Abstract Inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) is a ubiquitous phosphate biopolymer involved in diverse cellular processes. Despite its significance, selective detection of polyP remains challenging because of its simple and highly charged structure. abstract: Introduction Larimichthys crocea is an economically important marine aquaculture species, and improving growth performance while maintaining lipid metabolic homeostasis is important for its sustainable production. This study investigated the effects of dietary Eucommia ulmoides supplementation on growth performance and lipid metabolism in L. crocea and explored the underlying molecular basis using integrated transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses. abstract: Abstract Mountainous transport corridors are increasingly exposed to interacting natural hazards that intensify infrastructure, socio-economic, and land-use risks. abstract: Objectives Zinc is widely present in the oral microenvironment and can influence the growth of oral bacteria. ZccR is a MerR-type transcriptional regulator that controls zinc efflux in Streptococcus mutans ( S. mutans ), but its role in biofilm virulence and interspecies competition with oral commensals remains unclear. abstract: Debates on the future of smallholder farming in sub-Saharan Africa often interpret rural youth mobility and non-farm work as withdrawal from agriculture. This article examines how rural youth in coastal Guinea-Bissau engage with labour- and knowledge-intensive, climate-vulnerable mangrove swamp rice farming, and the conditions under which agriculture remains part of their imagined futures. title: Nature-based flood assessment for vulnerable educational infrastructure under tropical urban conditions
abstract: Worldwide, urban rainwater flooding is increasingly affecting small-scale public infrastructure in tropical cities. Consequently, drainage decisions are often made with limited hydrometric data. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate flood control alternatives using the Nature-based Solutions (NBS) approach through participatory assessment and modeling with the Stormwater Management Model (SWMM) at a vulnerable educational infrastructure (VEI) in Durán, Ecuador. abstract: Overtourism is increasingly understood as a multidimensional sustainability challenge, yet local decision-makers still lack replicable tools for assessing where tourism pressure may translate into territorial vulnerability. This paper develops a municipal impact-assessment framework for diagnosing overtourism vulnerability regimes. The analysis follows a two-step logic. abstract: The Wazwaz–Kaur equation is a significant nonlinear partial differential equation. This equation is used to describe nonlinear wave propagation in fields including fluid dynamics, plasma physics, and other areas of mathematical physics. abstract: This study examines how Chinese high school students perceive and respond to online misinformation and how their responses are shaped by school, family, and wider social contexts. Four focus group discussions were conducted with 24 students aged 15-17 from two public high schools in a southeastern coastal city. abstract: Abstract The River Wave Concept is a theoretical interpretation of river ecosystem processes that links flow to multiple river ecosystem concepts and contextualizes how a river functions with or without anthropogenic impacts. Here we propose a framework that can map the River Wave Concept to ecosystem concepts and wave metrics using widely available flow data from gauging station networks. abstract: This study examines the integration of concept mapping and authentic assessment in pre-service elementary science education using a four-phase professional development model. An embedded mixed-method design was employed, involving 82 seventh-semester students in a primary school teacher education program at a state university in Indonesia. abstract: Environmental literacy requires learning environments that enable students to explore complex ecosystem interactions and evaluate the consequences of environmental decisions, yet conventional online science learning often provides limited opportunities for such experiences. This study developed and evaluated a Roblox-based immersive learning system designed to support environmental literacy, particularly in the context of peatland conservation. abstract: Habitat structure can affect species detectability and the performance of bird survey meth-ods, particularly in heterogeneous habitats, as variation in vegetation complexity can affect both visual detection and sound attenuation. abstract: As the population of persons living with HIV (PLWH) ages, the Peruvian National HIV, STI and Hepatitis Program (NHSTIHP) faces the question of how best to provide care for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) among PLWH. abstract: The environmental behavior of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in tropical nearshore sediments remains poorly understood, particularly with respect to the contamination characteristics of emerging PFAS and precursor-related compounds. title: Visibility on Terrains
abstract: This chapter surveys terrain visibility models, algorithms, and applications. It introduces basic definitions, from line-of-sight, single-viewpoint viewsheds to cumulative and total viewsheds, on both Triangulated Irregular Network (TIN) and regular grid terrains. Reviews exact and approximate algorithms and highlights key application domains including archaeology, visual exposure to greenery, scenic route management, and land conservation.

abstract: Nowadays, Virtual Reality (VR) systems are more helpful for making decisions, training, and rehabilitation. abstract: Understanding the Earth’s deep interior remains challenging, as traditional geophysical methods face ambiguities in linking seismic observations to temperature, composition, or mass density variations. abstract: Richard Christopher Carrington carried out extensive sunspot observations from 1853 to 1861 and left numerous scientific legacies. abstract: Small Island Developing States (SIDS) depend fundamentally on the ocean for their societies, economies and livelihoods, yet they are among the regions most exposed to ocean changes. abstract: Anisakidosis is a parasitic zoonosis transmitted through the consumption of raw or undercooked fish. This condition represents an important epidemiological concern in Sangihe Islands Regency, where the prevalence of parasites in fish intended for consumption is 10.7% and the seroprevalence of human antibodies is 52.67%, potentially reflecting local dietary practices involving raw fish dishes such as Kinilo. title: Species distribution models of ESA-listed corals highlight niche differences among taxa that may guide recovery planning
abstract: Abstract Understanding the biogeography of living marine resources is essential for informed management, particularly in data-limited environments. Here, we use two corals listed under the U.S. Endangered Species Act (ESA) around Tutuila, American Samoa, to evaluate a transferable workflow that combines presence-only occurrence records, open biodiversity repositories, and open-access environmental data to extend existing survey records and support species monitoring. title: Killing the Antarctic Krill: Assessing State–Corporate Environmental Crime in the Southern Ocean
abstract: Antarctic krill is a keystone species in the Southern Ocean ecosystem, in that it plays an essential role in healthy marine food webs and carbon sequestration. However, its survival is increasingly being threatened by a growing industrial fishery dominated by powerful corporations alongside habitat changes caused by climate change. This article examines how states enable and/or fail to prevent the large-scale depletion of Antarctic krill by corporate actors, questioning whether this constitutes state–corporate environmental crime. title: Shellfish as Bio-indicators of Petroleum-related Pollution in a Tropical Oil-producing Estuarine Ecosystem of the Niger Delta, Nigeria
abstract: Petroleum-producing estuaries of the Niger Delta support shellfish harvesting while receiving complex, spatially variable mixtures of hydrocarbons and other contaminants. Shellfish can integrate biologically accessible exposure, but their interpretation is complicated by differences in habitat, taxonomy, physiology and analytical practice. This critical narrative review evaluates the conditions under which shellfish provide reliable evidence of petroleum-related contamination, biological effects and potential dietary exposure. abstract: Microplastic pollution in coastal sediments is a growing concern in tropical Southeast Asia, yet published data for the north coast of West Java remain scarce. This study reports a preliminary survey of microplastic occurrence in surface sediments (0 to 5 cm) at four sites along the northern Cirebon coast, West Java, Indonesia: Kejawanan, Mundu, Gebang and Losari. abstract: This study investigated the morphological and molecular characteristics of Scomberoides commersonnianus and Scomberoides lysan from the Sudanese Red Sea. abstract: Abstract. This manuscript presents a comprehensive and evolving novel in situ dataset of water levels and wave parameters collected from March 2023 onward in the St. Lawrence Estuary and Saguenay Fjord (Quebec, Canada), supporting validation activities for the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite mission. abstract: Sea urchins (Echinoidea) play important ecological and economic roles in coastal ecosystems, but morphological identification is often unreliable due to overlapping diagnostic traits among closely related taxa. This study used DNA barcoding of the mitochondrial COI gene to identify a sea urchin specimen from Kumu Beach, North Sulawesi, and determine its phylogenetic relationship with GenBank reference sequences. title: Polystyrene nanoplastics impair mitochondrial function, quality control, and ER–mitochondria crosstalk in HeLa cells
abstract: Introduction Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) represent persistent environmental contaminants derived from the degradation of plastic debris and are increasingly detected in biological systems, raising concerns regarding their potential effects on human health. Emerging evidence suggests that, following cellular internalization, PS-NPs can induce intracellular stress responses and interfere with mitochondrial homeostasis, highlighting mitochondria as key targets of nanoplastic-induced cellular dysfunction. title: Harnessing macrogenomics to study changing marine ecosystems under global climate change
abstract: Abstract Climate change is reshaping marine ecosystems at an accelerating pace. Predicting its impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem functions is therefore crucial to developing effective conservation strategies. Integration of genomic tools, habitat modelling and simulations offers a transformative approach to forecast these impacts. Yet, current frameworks remain limited to single-species analyses. title: The power and potential of blue philanthropy
abstract: Abstract Blue philanthropy has quadrupled in the past 15 years, growing to over USD 2.2 billion annually. We spotlight areas in which it has resulted in significant impacts and is poised to generate more. Introducing a five-part research agenda, we describe the power, pitfalls and potential of blue philanthropy, and how scientists can contribute to shaping an increasingly impactful future for marine science and ocean conservation in concert with blue philanthropy.

abstract: Marine environments and seafood are potential reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance, but genome-level data linking antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and metal tolerance genes (MTGs) in these matrices remain fragmented. abstract: Marine ecosystem assessments use indicators and various integration methods to conclude on ecosystem state. The integration methods vary in their structures, which will influence the number of indicators required. Thus, the choice of an assessment method will have cost consequences, but if the indicator pool is fixed, it is important to select a suitable method to ensure scientific robustness of the results. abstract: The Black Sea is an area of significant geostrategic importance, bridging Europe to Asia, with untapped potential for economic development, strategic transit routes especially for access to energy resources and critical raw materials. abstract: Abstract The transition to alternative marine fuels is often framed through fuel choice decisions, technical feasibility, or specific policy measures such as pricing, subsidies, standards, and training. abstract: Background: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants of increasing concern due to their widespread occurrence, environmental persistence, and potential adverse health effects. The analysis examines whether models reproduce the mean climate, trends (accounting internal-variability), extremes, and key circulation/process diagnostics. Despite strengths, several limitations persist across key aspects. Precipitation biases include annual-mean wet-bias over the southern AP and dry-bias over the central AP, and models underestimate the frequency and intensity of heavy-precipitation-events. title: Levels and Health Risk Assessment of Heavy Metals in Selected Skin-Whitening Creams Marketed in Lafia Town
abstract: The rising popularity of skin-whitening creams in Nigeria raises alarms about potential exposure to harmful metals that may occur either as impurities or as intentionally added ingredients. This study assessed the levels of cadmium, chromium, copper, iron, and lead in various skin-whitening creams available in Lafia Town. abstract: Introduction Potentially hazardous element (PHE) contamination threatens agroecosystem sustainability and food security, particularly in irrigated regions. abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. abstract: Background. Athletic performance genomics is dominated by studies conducted in European and African populations, leaving Southeast Asian (SEA) populations systematically underrepresented. abstract: Salt production in Kabupaten Kupang has strong natural potential, but weak downstream processing limits local value capture. This study evaluates how comparative advantage can be converted into competitive advantage through value-chain upgrading and salt industrialization. title: In the World of Aquatic Parasites, Microsporidia Matter!
abstract: Microsporidia are highly diverse, widespread parasites related to fungi and several groups of zoosporic protistan parasites. They infect a broad range of hosts, from protists to vertebrates, in many environments including most, if not all, aquatic habitats. Their genomes range from relatively conventional to highly reduced, yet they share key cellular structures and traits underlying infection and host association. abstract: Axenic and gnotobiotic aquatic animals provide direct experimental access to the causal roles of microorganisms in host physiology, nutrition, immunity and disease. Fish are particularly suitable vertebrate models because fertilization and embryogenesis commonly occur externally, allowing embryos to be disinfected before hatching and maintained under microbiologically controlled conditions. Traditional ageing by counting annuli on their ear stones (otoliths), is labor-intensive, lethal, and can be inaccurate for long-lived fishes. abstract: Abstract Future imaging spectrometers will expand contemporary data volumes by orders of magnitude, requiring automated methods to upscale labor-intensive detection of trace gas point sources. abstract: Introduction The organization of school time has been a focus of recent education reform, yet which school time reform practices appear in the official social media narratives of district education bureaus remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Focusing on areas of Ukraine’s Donetsk and Luhansk regions occupied by Russia since 2014, this article examines occupation as a cultural infrastructure assembled through heraldry, monuments, popular music, cinema, education policy, school materials, and literature. It shows how these media share a repertoire that stages conquest as “reunification” and dependence as local sovereignty, recasting violence as anti-fascist defence and historical restoration. Because polymer types differ by orders of magnitude in the toxicity of their constituent monomers and additives, particle abundance alone is an incomplete measure of hazard. abstract: Automated snow depth retrieval from time-lapse cameras is constrained by site-specific annotation and manual image quality screening, thus limiting scalability across deployments. abstract: Saudi Arabia’s industrial growth offers two key materials challenges: reducing the embodied carbon of construction and diverting mineral, glass, polymeric, metallurgical, and construction-and-demolition waste from disposal. This review analyzes how recycled materials and sustainable construction chemicals can be integrated as a unified low-carbon strategy, rather than as separate innovations. abstract: Abstract Fish-killing harmful algal blooms (HABs) continue to inflict severe economic losses on marine aquaculture worldwide, yet monitoring systems designed around microalgal cell counts frequently fail to anticipate acute mortality events. The dominant surveillance paradigm was inherited from shellfish-toxin monitoring, where a filter-feeding bivalve integrates exposure to intracellular phycotoxins and toxin burden in tissue triggers regulatory action. abstract: Abstract. These effects can bias the interpretation of vertical air motion and hydrometeor fall speeds, leading to systematic errors in cloud and precipitation retrievals. abstract: The Maritime Labour Convention (MLC, 2006) was designed to harmonise minimum standards of working and living conditions at sea across jurisdictions. Despite its near-universal ratification, significant disparities in labour conditions persist, indicating limited effectiveness in the implementation of the regulatory framework. abstract: PT XYZ is a business entity operating in the marine product processing sector, with pasteurized canned crab meat as its flagship product. abstract: Background The Literacy scale for Excellent Traditional Chinese Culture (ETCC-LS) is an important measurement instrument for assessing college students’ cultural accomplishment and the effectiveness of university cultural education.
