As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered as decision-support tools, their reliability in guideline-concordant surgical triage requires systematic evaluation. abstract: Satellite retrieval of chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) is central to monitoring eutrophication in inland reservoirs, yet the atmospheric-correction processors it depends on, trained on oceanic and large-lake conditions, are systematically biased over small water bodies. abstract: To explore cultivation techniques for improving winter wheat yield in saline-alkali soils, this study investigated the effects of seedling-stage drought priming on salt tolerance and related physiological mechanisms during later growth stages. abstract: OBJECTIVES: Lebanon is a low-burden tuberculosis (TB) country with a complex demographic context shaped by migration, socioeconomic instability, and recent healthcare disruptions. We aimed to characterize the population structure, drug resistance, and transmission dynamics of Mycobacterium tuberculosis using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). abstract: Background. Ginger is a horticultural commodity and a biopharmaceutical crop with many benefits and high economic value. Ginger is widely used as a raw material in the functional food, cosmetics, and herbal pharmaceutical industries. Water content is a critical parameter affecting the quality, storage stability, and activity of bioactive compounds in ginger rhizomes. Purpose. abstract: This review examines how the Malaysian Vocational Diploma Program (DVM), particularly Welding Technology, contributes to the development of graduate competence and employability. title: Application of Pollution Load Index (PLI) and Geo-Information Techniques for Evaluating Heavy Metal Distribution in Soils of the Toro Mining District, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates the geochemical characteristics and spatial distribution of heavy metals in soils within the Toro mining district, Bauchi State, Nigeria, to evaluate the environmental impact of prolonged artisanal tin mining. A total of ten (10) composite soil samples were collected from depths of 10–15 cm across active, abandoned and control sites. Samples were analysed using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) at the Nigerian Geological Survey Agency (NGSA) Laboratory, Kaduna, with quality control protocols observed throughout the analytical process. title: Effectiveness of Planting Pattern Systems and Types of Varieties on the Growth and Production of Rice Plants (Oryza sativa L.)
abstract: Jajar Legowo planting pattern technology is a planting technique designed to arrange the planting pattern in order to increase production. The purpose of this study is to analyze the Jajar Legowo planting system and different varieties on post-harvest rice production and proximate content. There are 2 types of research methods: quantitative analysis of post-harvest rice, which includes proximate content, and rice cultivation using a Randomized Block Design (RBD) with 5 repetitions. title: Hepatoprotective effects of natural polysaccharides: molecular mechanisms, structure–activity relationships, sources, applications in functional foods, and prospects
abstract: Natural polysaccharides from plants, fungi, algae, microorganisms, and animals have attracted increasing interest as food-derived candidates for liver protection. This critical review integrates preparation identity, structural attributes, mechanistic evidence, disease-model specificity, and translational readiness rather than treating these dimensions independently. title: Evaluation of micro-litter pollution in the Antarctic asteroid Odontaster validus Koehler, 1906 at Deception Island (South Shetland Islands)
abstract: Micro-litter (ML) pollution is increasingly being reported in Antarctic benthic ecosystems and the organisms inhabiting them. In this study, we assessed ML abundance and characteristics in the Antarctic asteroid Odontaster validus at Deception Island (South Shetland Islands), an area with significant human presence. Additionally, we considered the potential influence of local factors, including proximity to research stations and the bay entrance, as well as depth (5 and 15 m), on ML pollution. title: Plasmodium falciparum parasite density and its association with malaria rapid diagnostic test positivity among school-aged children across diverse malaria transmission settings in mainland Tanzania
abstract: Malaria rapid diagnostic tests (mRDTs) are widely used for malaria diagnosis and surveillance; however, their performance is influenced by parasite density. This study assessed the relationship between parasite density and mRDT positivity among school-aged children (SAC) across diverse malaria transmission settings in mainland Tanzania. Data were obtained from 17,131 school-aged children participating in a nationwide malaria survey. Malaria infection was assessed using mRDT and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) targeting the Plasmodium falciparum lactate dehydrogenase (PfLDH) gene.

title: An Analysis-Ready Dataset of Sentinel-2 Water and Vegetation Indices for River Basin Monitoring: STAC and COG Based Data Access and Cloud-Native Organization
abstract: River basins integrate hydrological, water-quality, and vegetation processes, requiring consistent observations of surface water and surrounding vegetation. Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument imagery provides frequent observations at spatial resolutions of up to 10 m. However, long-term basin-scale analysis requires repeated data discovery, retrieval, preprocessing, and quality control. This study presents an analysis-ready, cloud-native dataset of Sentinel-2-derived environmental indices for the Hwangnyonggang River Basin, South Korea (674.8 km2), covering January 2017 to August 2026. title: Polychaete (Annelida) diversity in the impacted Berg River Estuary, South Africa
abstract: Abstract Although Ramsar-listed, the Berg River estuary (South Africa) is anthropogenically impacted and severely understudied. Four studies conducted between the 1950s and 2000s found that polychaetous annelids in the estuary are represented predominantly by capitellid, spionid and nereidid species. This study provides an updated taxonomic inventory of polychaetous annelids in this estuary, with COI, cytb and 16S DNA sequence data to facilitate future molecular-based biodiversity studies. 3840 specimens (16 species from seven families) were collected from 9 sites from the mouth of the estuary

title: Fermented Sargassum-Based Seafood Rice Seasoning: Prototype Development and Mix Design Optimization
abstract: Direct incorporation of brown-seaweed biomass into foods is limited by its fibrous texture and by the challenge of retaining desirable marine and umami notes without an excessive fishy odor. This study evaluated whether fermented commercial Sargassum spp . biomass could be incorporated into a dry seafood seasoning for rice and whether a constrained mix design could identify a formulation with high preliminary hedonic acceptability.Commercial dried Sargassum spp . biomass was rehydrated for 6 h, washed, pretreated with 1.5% sodium bicarbonate at 90–100°C for 2 h, reduced to 1–2-mm fragments, an

title: Effects of temperature fluctuations on quality deterioration and flavor evolution of pre-packaged tofu during cold-chain logistics
abstract: Introduction To investigate the effects of temperature fluctuation during cold chain logistics on quality deterioration and flavor evolution of pre-packaged tofu. Methods This study simulated stable cold chain (CK) and two temperature fluctuation modes (T1 and T2), and systematically analyzed the microbial changes, spoilage metabolism, water status, texture properties, and volatile flavor composition of tofu under different storage conditions. title: Climate-driven shifts in lumpy skin disease risk across Iran: Insights from ensemble species distribution models
abstract: This study aimed to identify the environmental determinants influencing the distribution of lumpy skin disease and to predict changes in its spatial distribution risk and potential geographic range across Iran under future climate change scenarios using ensemble Species Distribution Models (SDMs). To this end, following data cleaning and quality control of 3654 disease occurrence records, a total of 2849 presence points recorded between 2013 and 2024 were retained for model development. title: Analysis of microplastic abundance, polymer composition, and the effect of natural filtration on traditionally produced cooking salt from Watu Asa Village
abstract: Produksi garam laut tradisional sangat rentan terhadap sampah laut, namun data komprehensif mengenai kontaminasi mikroplastik dan peningkatan kualitas melalui teknologi filtrasi pada sistem berbasis perebusan di wilayah pesisir berkembang seperti Sumba Tengah masih sangat terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menentukan kualitas fisik-kimia, kelimpahan ternormalisasi, karakteristik morfologi, dan komposisi polimer spesifik dari mikroplastik pada garam laut dan air tua (brine) dari wilayah pesisir dekat estuari Desa Watu Asa. title: Occurrence characteristics of plastic waste on beaches and the influencing factors of mercury enrichment: a case study of Qingdao
abstract: Abstract Plastic pollution has become a research hotspot. To explore the occurrence characteristics and influencing factors of mercury (Hg) in plastic waste on beaches, plastic debris samples were collected from the intertidal and supratidal zones of four typical beaches in Qingdao. Polymer types of the plastics were identified, and Hg concentrations in the plastics were determined to investigate the effects of physicochemical properties (plastic color, polymer type, and degree of aging) on Hg enrichment. title: Geographically close nearshore sites exhibit contrasting dissolved oxygen dynamics and ecosystem metabolism in eastern Lake Taihu
abstract: Diel dissolved oxygen (DO) dynamics integrate biological metabolism and physical forcing and provide a powerful tool for investigating ecosystem metabolism in shallow lakes. However, whether geographically close sites exhibit similar metabolic behavior and environmental controls remains poorly understood. Here, three years (2022–2024) of high-frequency DO observations from three contrasting nearshore sites in eastern Lake Taihu were used to quantify diel and seasonal variability in net ecosystem production (NEP), gross primary production (GPP), and ecosystem respiration (R). title: Distribution and life-history of spurdog (Squalus acanthias) along the Norwegian coast inferred from a five-year fishery-independent longline survey
abstract: Abstract Northeast Atlantic spurdog ( Squalus acanthias ) has recently shown signs of recovery from overfishing following international conservation measures. As the fishery slowly reopens, ensuring its sustainable long-term trajectory will require an understanding of its contemporary population structure, habitat use, and life-history traits across its distribution range. journal: Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries

title: Prevalence and clinical significance of α-globin gene subtypes in prenatal thalassemia screening: a focus on the -α3.7III variant in Sanya, Hainan, China
abstract: Introduction Alpha-thalassemia is a common genetic disorder in southern China. The - α 3.7 deletion has three subtypes (I, II, III), among which type III has been rarely reported in the Chinese population. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, genotypic distribution, and hematological phenotypes of the - α 3.7III subtype in Sanya, Hainan. Methods A total of 474 reproductive-age individuals undergoing prenatal thalassemia screening were enrolled from February 2022 to April 2025. Peripheral blood samples were collected, and genetic testing was performed using next-generation sequencing

title: The Nuances of Conflicts in the Arctic and the Level of Analysis Problem
abstract: This article examines conflict dynamics in the Arctic using a framework that includes the state, regional, and systemic (international) analysis levels. While public and political narratives often depict the Arctic as an emerging arena of geopolitical rivalry, these interpretations often overlook the analytical complexity of conflicts in the region. Drawing on the levels of analysis approach, the study employs qualitative content analysis of academic literature, policy documents, and institutional agreements to explore how conflict dynamics emerge and interact across levels. title: Blue Transformation Pathway for Nigeria and Africa: A Strategic Framework for Transitioning to 90%–95% Aquaculture Dominance by 2050
abstract: ABSTRACT The global fisheries sector is undergoing a structural transformation, with aquaculture surpassing capture fisheries in 2022 (51% of global aquatic animal supply) and reaching 53% by 2024, when aquaculture production topped 100 million tonnes for the first time. Despite vast aquatic resources, Africa produces only approximately 1.9% of global aquaculture output and remains dependent on declining capture fisheries. title: Effects of Antibiotic and Temperature Treatments on Phycosphere Bacterial Communities of Kelp Gametophytes
abstract: Microbiome dysbiosis represents a critical bottleneck in sustainable kelp aquaculture, yet the distinct regulatory mechanisms of antibiotics and temperature remain poorly characterized. This study systematically elucidates the divergent effects of penicillin-streptomycin exposure and temperature gradients on Saccharina japonica gametophytes and their epiphytic microbiota. title: The Gruesomeness of Microplastics: Food Contamination, Human Exposure, and Health Risks
abstract: Plastics, once addressed as a revolutionary, effective, and beneficial invention, have now become a global environmental nightmare due to the alarming rise of microplastic pollution. This form of pollution is increasingly being recognized as a serious global disorder. Microplastics, whether originating directly from primary sources or from the degradation of larger plastic waste, are now pervasive in the air, soil, and aquatic environments. title: Evaluating sediment color as a paleoceanographic proxy in Santos Basin continental slope sediments, SW Atlantic
abstract: Abstract Sediment color is a valuable proxy in paleoceanography, reflecting chemical and mineralogical composition influenced by biogeochemical processes and depositional environments. This study investigates the relationship between sediment color (RGB and CIE L*a*b*) and metals in three radiocarbon-dated sediment cores from the Santos Basin continental slope (SW Atlantic). The cores, located within the Upper Circumpolar Water domain, span different time intervals. Results show significant color variation, especially after the Bølling–Allerød event. title: State of the art of diffusive gradients in thin films for in situ speciation analysis and chemical fractionation of metals and metalloids in water
abstract: Diffusive Gradients in Thin Films (DGT) has become an established passive sampling technique because it provides time-integrated, in situ measurements of labile metal(loid) species. Its capacity to support metal(loid) speciation and correlate labile fractions with ecotoxicological thresholds has further increased its relevance in environmental monitoring. Given the growing number of publications and the expanding scope of applications, a critical overview of recent developments is justified. journal: Critical Insights in Environmental Science and Technology

title: Integrating operational emission management into SMS: A bibliometric and conceptual perspective on the ISM Code
abstract: The maritime industry is undergoing a paradigm shift driven by stringent decarbonization regulations, such as the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI). Despite the proliferation of technical solutions, a conceptual divide persists between emission compliance and the established safety management culture governed by the International Safety Management (ISM) Code. title: Environmental factors associated with abundance and bioindicator potential of Australomicrodeutopus in tropical brackish water ponds
abstract: Amphipods are recognized as important ecological components of brackish water ecosystems, yet empirical evidence linking their distribution to environmental conditions in tropical aquaculture ponds remains limited.This study investigated the environmental factors associated with abundance influencing the distribution of the amphipod genus Australomicrodeutopus and evaluated its potential as a bioindicator of environmental quality in tropical brackish water ponds.Field observations were conducted in two shrimp ponds located in Suppa District, Pinrang Regency, Indonesia, with weekly sampling per

title: Analysis of Multiple Tire Rubber-Derived Chemicals in Fish Bile and Plasma: Analytical Method and Field Assessment in Puget Sound, WA, USA
abstract: Abstract Tire rubber-derived chemicals (TRCs) are known to be highly toxic to fish, but understanding of their environmental levels and fate is still limited. This study presents a new method for the analysis of 18 TRCs, including phenylenediamines (TRC-PDs), their quinone derivatives (TRC-Qs), and rubber vulcanizing and curing-related chemicals (TRC-VCRs) in fish bile and plasma samples. We applied this method in bile and plasma samples from English sole collected in urban, near-urban, and nonurban sites in Puget Sound, WA, USA. title: Unlocking the mechanical, physical, and antimicrobial properties of gelatin-based films via chitosan nanoparticle reinforcement for active food packaging applications
abstract: The growing ecological concerns over plastic packaging have driven interest in biodegradable film materials. This study evaluates the mechanical, physical, and antimicrobial properties of chicken skin gelatin films reinforced with varying concentrations (0–8%) of chitosan nanoparticles (CNPs). CNPs significantly enhanced the films’ performance, increasing the tensile strength from 1.35 to 5.81 MPa, Young’s modulus from 0.42 to 5.61 MPa, and decreasing the elongation at break from 319.11% to 106.72%. title: Underestimation of plastic pollution and implications for water quality assessments in urban lakes
abstract: Plastic pollution is increasingly recognized as a pervasive threat to water quality, yet most studies quantify only microplastics (<5 mm), potentially biasing estimates of environmental contamination. Here, we formally evaluated the underestimation bias associated with the intentional exclusion of plastics >5 mm from samples collected across a system of urban freshwater lakes (n = 20). We first conducted surveys of predominant single-use plastics to identify common forms and likely sources (e.g., food containers, tobacco products) present in these environments. title: Nutritional and Economic Potential of Needle Cuttlefish (Sepia aculeata): Unlocking an Underutilized Seafood Resource in Bangladesh
abstract: Needle cuttlefish ( Sepia aculeata ), an abundant yet underutilized cephalopod species in Bangladesh, remains a non-conventional seafood resource with limited nutritional information. This study evaluated the proximate composition, amino acid profile, fatty acid composition, micronutrients, and heavy metals of both edible and non-edible portions of S. aculeata , while recommended nutrient intake (RNI) contribution and economic efficiency were assessed using edible portions only. journal: Journal of Food Composition and Analysis

title: Anthropogenic risk assessment of riverine habitat using an ecosystem-based risk approach for river management prioritization: A case study from the Biyonga River, Indonesia

title: Traceability and Supply Chain Dynamics of Fish Commodities in the Tolo Bay and Banggai Region, Indonesia
abstract: This study examined the production capacity, household and industrial consumption, and supply chain traceability of fish commodities in the Tolo Bay region, encompassing Banggai, Banggai Laut, and Banggai Kepulauan Regencies of Central Sulawesi Province, part of the Republic of Indonesia's National Fisheries Management Area 714 (WPPNRI 714). title: Rare earth elements and yttrium in water sources of the Distrito Federal, Central Brazil: baseline data for water quality monitoring
abstract: Rare earth elements and yttrium (REY) were evaluated in water supply sources of the Distrito Federal, Central Brazil, to establish baseline data for water quality monitoring. Tap water was collected from the distribution system of two water sources: Lakes Paranoá and Descoberto, while groundwater samples were obtained from porous and fractured aquifers. Sampling was carried out during the rainy and dry seasons. title: Effects of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Supplementation on Growth, Survival and Fatty Acid Composition of Anadara tuberculosa Spat
abstract: ABSTRACT This research assessed the feasibility of using the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a complementary feed for the mangrove cockle Anadara tuberculosa spat. The nutritional impact of five mix diets was tested: (1) Tisochrysis lutea + Chaetoceros gracilis , (2) C. gracilis + S. cerevisiae , (3) S. cerevisiae , (4) T. lutea + S. cerevisiae and (5) T. lutea + C. gracilis + S. cerevisiae . In addition, fatty acid (FA) profiles of the diets and of spat tissues were analysed. title: Reconciling Competing Natural Resource Interests for Sustainable Development: The Role of Law in Balancing Oil Exploitation, Water Resource and Ecosystem Services in Nigeria
abstract: Oil exploitation remains important to the economy and development of Nigeria, but its interaction with the ecosystem and interconnected water resources create conflicts between competing forms of resource use. This paper examines whether Nigerian law provides a coherent and balanced framework for reconciling oil development with the continued impairment on water resources and associated ecosystems. journal: JOURNAL OF LAW AND GLOBAL POLICY

title: Effect of storage time on release of microplastics (MPs) from different milk packaging
abstract: The growing detection of microplastics (MPs) in the human body has raised concerns about the potential entrance of MPs into the food chain and subsequently into humans. Due to wide consumption of milk by different age groups, investigating the MPs release into milk during storage time from different commercial milk packaging materials is crucial. MPs release in three common packaging types of ESL milk (bottles and packets) and sterilized milk (multi-layer carton) during storage periods (expiration date) was studied. title: Toxicological impacts of sulfamethoxazole on freshwater organisms – toxicity and oxidative stress
abstract: The continuous expansion of the pharmaceutical sector has intensified aquatic contamination, as persistent active compounds enter water bodies through urban, industrial, and agricultural runoff. Among these contaminants, sulfamethoxazole (SMX)—a widely used sulphonamide antibiotic—raises ecological concerns due to its persistence and potential for bioaccumulation. title: Variability of toxic Microcystis blooms and bacterial communities in freshwater bodies with different anthropopressure and climate zones: a novel comparative study in Guatemala and Poland
abstract: Abstract The global rise of harmful cyanobacterial blooms (HCBs) in freshwater systems is driven by anthropogenic pressure and climate change, yet limited information exists on how these factors shape HCBs and their phycosphere-associated bacterial communities (PBCs). We examined the influence of eutrophication (nutrient concentrations and land use), climate zone, and seasonality on phytoplankton and PBCs across three freshwater bodies: hypertrophic Lake Amatitlán with urban and agricultural catchments, mesotrophic Laguna del Pino with a forested/agricultural catchment (both tropical, Guatemal

title: Method of meal delivery influences estimates of postprandial metabolism and alkaline tide in a benthic fish
abstract: Intragastric gavage is widely used in studies of digestive physiology to deliver standardised meals, yet it remains unclear whether it elicits postprandial metabolic and acid-base responses comparable to voluntary feeding. Here, we tested whether the method of meal delivery affects the magnitude and timing of the postprandial rise in metabolic rate known as specific dynamic action (SDA) and the associated alkaline tide (transient rise in blood pH and bicarbonate following feeding) in sand flathead (Platycephalus bassensis) using a standardised 1.5% body-weight ratio either as intact pellets (v

title: A cost-benefit analysis of small-holder floating-house fish farming in Chau Doc City, Vietnamese Mekong Delta
abstract: Smallholder floating-house aquaculture supports vital riverine livelihoods in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta but faces increasing environmental and hydrological pressures. This study conducts an empirical Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) to evaluate the economic viability, cost drivers, and adaptation strategies of smallholders in Chau Doc City in An Giang Province. Primary data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 35 fish farmers across three distinct river reaches. title: Humans and disasters: Examining the disaster mitigation knowledge of the Kaili tribe in Central Sulawesi
abstract: The natural disasters of earthquakes, liquefaction, and tsunamis marked the activation of the Palu Koro Fault on September 28, 2018, resulting in numerous casualties. However, the Kaili people, as the indigenous community, possess local knowledge of disaster mitigation, thereby minimizing risks. Therefore, this study was conducted to explore historical values and traditional knowledge related to disaster mitigation. title: Hong Kong’s Water Quality Governance: A Historical PerspectivePolicy Instruments and Priorities
abstract: Based on 112 water quality-related proceedings of the Hong Kong Legislative Council from 2014 to 2025, this study employed an analytical framework of policy tools, policy issues, and time evolution to investigate Hong Kong’s water-quality governance agenda. The findings indicate that command and control were mentioned most frequently, followed by public information, participation and collaboration, public investment, and economic incentives. title: An AI-Enabled Predictive Procurement Model for Forecasting and Inventory Optimization
abstract: This paper presents an AI-enabled predictive procurement model that integrates probabilistic demand forecasting, supplier lead-time prediction, and multi-echelon inventory optimization to secure target service levels while lowering working capital. The framework couples hierarchical time-series forecasting with gradient-boosted trees and lightweight sequence models, capturing seasonality, promotions, and regime shifts. title: Solid waste management practices in riparian communities are a key driver of microplastic concentrations in the Mekong River, Cambodia
abstract: Rivers are major conduits of plastic pollution, however the role of community level waste collection on riverine microplastic concentrations remains poorly understood. We investigated seasonal patterns and drivers of microplastic pollution along the Lower Mekong River, Cambodia, with a focus on riparian waste collection services. Surface water samples were collected during dry and wet seasons using a pump and filter method (100 µm minimum aperture), and more than 15,000 particles were chemically identified using Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). title: Source apportionment and health risk assessment of PAHs in commercial fish from Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia
abstract: Abstract This study measured polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) contamination in ten commercially important fish species from the Al-Jubail industrial coastline, Arabian Gulf, Saudi Arabia. Muscle tissue concentrations were quantified by GC-MS. Source apportionment used diagnostic molecular ratios, positive matrix factorization (PMF), and hierarchical clustering, and health risk was assessed separately for adults and children. title: Redox distribution of Asgard archaea and co-occurring taxa in microbial mats from an early Proterozoic ecosystem analog
abstract: Abstract Increasing evidence supports that eukaryotes originated from the symbiosis of an Asgard archaeon, the alphaproteobacterial ancestor of mitochondria, and possibly additional bacterial contributions. Eukaryogenesis likely occurred in redox-transition environments such as microbial mats or shallow sediments ~2 billion years ago, when atmospheric oxygen was far lower than today. title: THE EFFECT OF SPRAYING WITH DIFFERENT CONCENTRATIONS OF KELPMAX SEAWEED EXTRACT ON THE GROWTH AND CHEMICAL COMPOSITION OF THE YIELD OF TWO BARLEY VARIETIES (HORDEUM VULGARE L.)
abstract: This study was conducted to determine the effect of foliar spraying with different concentrations of the Kelpmax seaweed extract on the growth and chemical composition of two barley varieties (Hordeum vulgare L.), namely Al-Jazira 1 and Rayhan, under greenhouse conditions. The plants were sprayed with three concentrations of the extract (0.0, 2.5, and 5) mL L⁻¹ at three growth stages. The results showed that spraying with the Kelpmax seaweed extract had significant effects on a number of growth traits and the chemical composition of the yield. title: The Multiplying Worlds of Ma Joie
abstract: This essay explores the environmental and spatial afterlives of plantation colonialism in the Seychelles through an ecofeminist auto-theoretical approach. Drawing on family archives and field philosophical research, the author reflects on her position as the granddaughter of a former plantation owner while tracing the material and spatial legacies of the Plantationocene. title: Gene expression, Antioxidant Responses, and metabolomic Profiling Reveal Chlorella vulgaris Mediated Protection against acetaminophen and microplastic Co-toxicity in Oreochromis niloticus
abstract: Abstract Emerging water pollutants such as pharmaceutical (PhACs) and microplastics (MPs) are progressively detected in aquatic environments, raising alarms about their mutual toxicological effects on non-target biota, particularly fish. Although the individual effects of these pollutants have been investigated, there is little data available on their interactions and potential strategies to reduce toxicity. title: Corrosion-induced degradation of rock bolt–grout systems in subsea tunnel primary support
abstract: Rock bolt–grout systems are critical load-transfer components in the subsea tunnel primary support, but its material deterioration and structural damage under aggressive groundwater remain insufficiently understood. In the article, the properties of rock bolt–grout specimens exposed to chloride, sulfate and chloride–sulfate environments were tested. An impressed-current protocol was combined with pull–out tests, open–circuit potential, linear polarization resistance (LPR), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), depth-resolved ion profiling and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP). journal: Journal of Railway Science and Technology

title: Robust trajectory tracking of an underactuated ROV under compound flow disturbances using ADRC-GISMC
abstract: Abstract Trajectory tracking of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) remains difficult when hydrodynamic coupling, plant uncertainty, actuator constraints, and spatially varying flow disturbances act simultaneously. This study presents a simulation-based evaluation of an ADRC-GISMC strategy for an underactuated ROV under an engineering-oriented compound disturbance model combining background-current and local outfall-plume components. title: ANALYSIS OF THE IMPACT OF PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE FAILURES ON FLEXIBLE PIPELINE CONNECTORS IN OFFSHORE OIL PRODUCTION
abstract: Oil plays a significant role in the Brazilian and global energy matrices. Brazilian oil production is predominantly offshore, particularly in pre-salt fields. In oil and gas production systems, both rigid and flexible pipelines are employed. During retrieval operations, special attention must be given to permeated gas trapped within the annular space of the flexible pipeline. Controlled gas release, as required by API 17B, is performed by opening pressure relief valves installed in the end connectors. title: Stakeholder perceptions of seafood supply chain resilience and sustainability: an Australian case study
abstract: Abstract Seafood supply chains face increasing disruption from climate change, pandemics, and changing market conditions, creating challenges for maintaining both resilience and sustainability. Understanding the perspectives of people working in the industry and supply chain (i.e. stakeholders) are crucial to developing context-specific and practical pathways for supporting continued seafood supply, livelihoods and profitability. title: From lab to field: case study of predicting the capability of accelerated weathering for protective coatings in Qatar
abstract: This study evaluates the ability of accelerated laboratory testing to represent the field performance of four commercial multilayer protective coating systems. Coated carbon-steel panels were exposed to 4,200 h of ISO 12944-9 cyclic aging and compared with panels subjected to two years of natural exposure at a C2 corrosivity site in Qatar. title: Compliance and non-compliance patterns among listed and non-listed ship recycling facilities: a comparative assessment of 22 facilities evaluated for the EU List
abstract: Ship recycling plays a central role in the circular economy of the maritime industry, yet significant disparities persist in safety, environmental performance, and regulatory compliance across global Ship Recycling Facilities (SRFs). This study analyzes 22 official inspection reports conducted by DNV for the European Commission under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation (EU SRR 1257/2013), comparing listed and non-listed facilities. title: Physicochemical and microbiological qualities of shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) coated with pectin incorporated with green tea spent extract during refrigerated storage
abstract: This study developed and characterized a pectin (PEC) based coating incorporated with green tea spent extract (GTSE) and/or nisin. Further, Pacific white shrimp were treated with the developed coating and investigated for physicochemical, textural, microbial, and melanosis formation during refrigerated storage for 12 days. Among the four coating solutions, PEC-2 had higher homogeneity (583.6 nm) and antioxidant activity (DPPH: 76.73% and ABTS: 70.95%). title: Reviews and syntheses: Snow algae on the move – biased motility and snowpack interaction from a biophysics perspective
abstract: Abstract. Snow algae are psychrophilic and psychrotolerant photosynthetic microorganisms found on every continent, predominantly in polar and alpine environments. Along with contributing to terrestrial carbon cycling and food webs, colourful snow algal blooms formed on snow surfaces can substantially reduce albedo and accelerate snowmelt. Despite their ecological importance, the mechanisms governing snow algae motility and migration within snow remain poorly understood. title: Groundwater Exploitation and Domestic Water Supply Challenges in Yenagoa Metropolis
abstract: The quantity of water derivable from groundwater could be affected by overexploitation, which also promotes negative impact on the quality. This study investigated groundwater exploitation, treatment methods, and domestic water supply challenges in Yenagoa metropolis, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. A survey of 350 households was conducted to assess sources of water, facility ownership, treatment practices, maintenance frequency, and supply-related challenges. title: 3D Reconstruction of Dinoflagellate Chromosomes from Hi-C Data Challenges the Cholesteric Liquid Crystal Hypothesis
abstract: Dinoflagellates have permanently condensed chromosomes that are often described as cholesteric liquid crystals (CLCs). The CLC model proposes that DNA is organized into parallel fibers within stacked discs, such that the fiber orientation rotates between adjacent discs. Extrachromosomal loops extending from the discs are hypothesized to be more accessible and thus to contain transcriptionally active genes. title: The 2026 U·S·–Iran War and Its Implications for Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Exports and Global Energy Markets: The State of Qatar as a Case Study
abstract: This study analyzed the 2026 United States–Iran War and its impact on global LNG exports, using Qatar as a case study. Qatar was chosen because it is a major exporter of liquefied natural gas and depends heavily on the Strait of Hormuz to export LNG to other countries. The study also examined the political and geopolitical aspects of military conflict and its consequences for LNG production and exports, as well as its broader impact on global energy security and energy markets abroad. title: Assessing Earth system responses in mitigation scenarios with activity-driven simulation of carbon dioxide removal
abstract: Abstract. Assessing Earth system responses arising from carbon dioxide removal (CDR) requires developing and simulating pairs of scenarios – a mitigation scenario with deployment of CDR and a corresponding no-CDR baseline. The latter describes a world where no CDR is deployed, such that net carbon emissions are higher and a given temperature target may be missed. While over the past years a rich literature on deep mitigation scenarios with CDR has been emerging, no-CDR baselines have mostly been explored in stylized Earth system model (ESM) experiments. title: Health Risk Assessment and Heavy Metal Contamination in Canned Tuna Fish from the Libyan Market
abstract: This study investigated the concentrations of selected heavy metals in canned tuna products commercially available in the Libyan market, given the widespread consumption of canned tuna as an affordable source of protein and the potential health risks associated with the bioaccumulation of chemical contaminants in fish tissues. We randomly obtained eight canned tuna samples from different brands and production batches from supermarkets and local markets in Tripoli, Libya. title: Rainfall homogeneity, variability, and trends across unimodal and bimodal regimes in the Wami Basin, Tanzania
abstract: ABSTRACT The graphical abstract links rainfall data, statistical tests, spatial outputs, and hydrological implications for the Wami basin. Rainfall regime coexistence influences hydrological variability in semi-arid regions, but is rarely treated explicitly in basin-scale assessments. This study evaluates rainfall homogeneity, variability, anomalies, seasonality, and trends across unimodal and bimodal regimes in Tanzania's Wami basin from 1985 to 2014. title: Integrated adaptations of muscle structure and mitochondrial function to locomotion demands in teleost fishes
abstract: Abstract Teleost fishes display diverse swimming modes supported by functional specialization of skeletal muscle. However, the ultrastructural adaptations and molecular mechanisms regulating mitochondrial homeostasis in relation to divergent locomotion remain unclear. We compared muscle fiber composition, mitochondrial ultrastructure, and regulatory pathways in two teleosts with contrasting swimming strategies: the sustained swimmer Pseudocaranx dentex and the burst swimmer Paralichthys olivaceus. title: Evaluating the Courier and Delivery Services Company's Efficiency Using an EBM Model
abstract: The market for courier and delivery services is changing favorably as a result of the most recent and continuous technical developments in logistics. Thanks to real–time monitoring technology, which provides transparency and peace of mind, customers can now effortlessly keep a watch on their deliveries at every stage. This study aims to assess the efficiency of nine significant delivery and courier services. title: Sexual dimorphism shapes the plasma metabolome of the endangered Iberian lynx
abstract: Sexual dimorphism is a key but still incompletely resolved determinant of mammalian systemic metabolism, particularly in endangered species where physiological organization remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrate untargeted plasma metabolomics to dissect hierarchical determinants of systemic metabolic organization in the Iberian lynx ( Lynx pardinus ), one of the world’s most endangered felids. title: Assessing the Socioeconomic Challenges Affecting Economic Development in Puntland
abstract: Puntland, a self-governing federal member state in north-eastern Somalia, occupies a distinctive position within one of the world's most fragile economies. Since declaring autonomy in 1998, Puntland has built functioning public institutions, a working seaport at Bosaso, and a livestock-led export economy, even as it has remained exposed to drought, clan-based insecurity, weak public revenue, and limited access to international finance. journal: Horn of Africa Journal of Social Science

title: 16S rRNA amplicon profiling of Salvadora persica -associated rhizosphere bacterial communities under saline agricultural conditions
abstract: Salvadora persica (Arak) is a facultative halophyte adapted to arid and saline environments, yet its rhizosphere microbiome remains poorly characterised. We profiled bacterial communities associated with S. persica at Arak Farm, Rabigh, Saudi Arabia, using Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V3–V4 16S rRNA region and ASV-based analysis. Three rhizosphere composites and one adjacent bulk-soil composite were analysed. title: Benzothiazoles and benzotriazoles in the dust and human urine samples from the e-waste recycling industry: occurrence, distribution, and occupational exposure assessment
abstract: Benzothiazoles (BTHs) and benzotriazoles (BTRs) are high production volume chemicals widely incorporated into electronic products, yet their environmental occurrence and potential occupational exposure during e-waste recycling remain poorly characterized. In this study, four BTHs and three BTRs were quantified in 113 dust samples collected from a modern e-waste recycling facility and 15 household dust samples, as well as in urine samples from 121 e-waste dismantling workers and 20 rural residents. title: Bacteriological Quality and Physicochemical Properties of Drinking Water Sources in Slums of Lagos State, Southwest, Nigeria
abstract: Water is very essential and widely used by humans, animals and for the success of agricultural products. The inhabitants resort to use of borehole, sachet and bottle water for drinking and domestic use. There is paucity of information on bacterial contamination and phytochemical properties of drinking water sources in major slums of Lagos city. Such contaminants may be the cause of frequent febrile illnesses experienced amongst the inhabitants of these slums. title: Molecular Insights Into the Effects of Global Warming and Pollutants on Crustacean Reproduction and Immunity: Protein–Pollutant Interactions via Molecular Docking
abstract: ABSTRACT Global warming and environmental pollutants represent escalating threats to crustaceans, with serious implications for aquaculture sustainability and ecosystem stability. This review synthesises and advances current understanding by integrating physiological, biochemical, and molecular evidence on the effects of elevated temperature and diverse contaminants—including endocrine‐disrupting chemicals (EDCs), heavy metals (HMs), nanoparticles (NPs), pesticides, and microplastics—on crustacean reproduction and immunity. abstract: This study aimed to identify Salmonella spp. and Escherichia coli contamination associated with foodborne diseases in fishery commodities from Bali, Indonesia. A total of 216 samples representing commercially important fish and shrimp species were collected from suppliers, fish processing units, micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), traditional markets, and modern markets across regencies in Bali. title: Mapping the Biodiversity, Climate, and Health Nexus: an Analysis of Horizon Europe research projects
abstract: Addressing the interconnected challenges of climate change, biodiversity loss, and human health requires a shift from fragmented governance toward integrated actions. This study applies an analytical framework combining Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modelling and network analysis to systematically map the Biodiversity, Climate, and Health (BCH) nexus within the Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe research portfolios. title: Induction versus maintenance: EEG evidence for two-stage limitations of electrical stunning in tilapia and catfish
abstract: Billions of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) and African sharptooth catfish ( Clarias gariepinus ) are slaughtered annually, often without stunning. This study evaluated a prototype in-water electrical stunning system under semi-commercial farm conditions, separating the immediate induction of insensibility from its maintenance. Fish received short electrical exposures to assess induction of insensibility and longer exposures, with or without exsanguination and ice-slurry immersion, to assess recovery during a 10-min period. title: High diversity but limited expression of biosynthetic gene clusters in a peatland microbial community
abstract: Abstract The in situ relevance of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remains poorly understood. We apply meta-omics to characterize BGC diversity and activity along a peatland redox gradient. From seven metagenomes, we recover 9,694 BGCs, spanning diverse taxa, most lacking close relatives in reference databases, indicating extensive novelty. title: Overtime Drivers and Work–Rest Compliance among Indonesian Deck Seafarers: Implications for Maritime Traffic Safety
abstract: Work-rest compliance is an important component of maritime safety because deck seafarers are responsible for watchkeeping, lookout, vessel traffic monitoring, bridge communication, and navigational decision-making. Although international regulations emphasize adequate rest to reduce fatigue risk, overtime may still occur due to operational, technical, administrative, and regulatory demands. This study examines overtime drivers and work-rest compliance among Indonesian deck seafarers and discusses their implications for maritime traffic safety. title: Multi-method non-parametric assessment of river water-quality trends and change-points in the Danshui River basin, metropolitan Taipei (2010–2026)
abstract: The Danshui River drains metropolitan Taipei, where two decades of expanding sewer connection and riparian constructed wetlands have targeted river pollution. title: Asynchronous Changes in Tempo‐Spatial Patterns of the Younger Dryas Hydroclimate in Northeastern China
abstract: Abstract The Younger Dryas (YD, 12,900–11,700 years before present) event offers a key opportunity to investigate climate system responses to abrupt perturbations, yet regional hydroclimate responses in northeastern China remain debated. Here we reconstruct the spatial fingerprint of YD hydroclimate variability using a comprehensive fossil pollen data set. Our results show regionally coherent cooling but strong spatial heterogeneity in precipitation. At YD onset, northern regions became drier, whereas southern areas experienced slight wetting. title: Fabrication and in vitro toxicity assessment of PET microplastic fibers with diameter and aspect ratio control
abstract: Microplastics (MP) are widespread anthropogenic pollutants present in the air we breathe, the food we eat and the water we drink. Their presence has been reported in almost all ecosystems and several human organs and tissues. Despite their pervasiveness, our knowledge regarding their effects remains in its infancy. Current understanding is largely limited to the assessment of a few specific particle types, even though MP exist in a variety of shapes, sizes, and materials. title: Evolutionary game analysis of scientific research data sharing under the open science context
abstract: Scientific data sharing is central to open science, yet its development is constrained by fragmented data resources, heterogeneous stakeholder incentives, privacy risks, and limited regulatory capacity. This study develops a bounded-rationality, four-population evolutionary game framework involving data providers, data users, government agencies, and sharing platforms. title: Water retention strategies for drought-prone aquaculture ponds: Technologies, effectiveness, challenges, and future prospects
abstract: Water scarcity threatens earthen pond aquaculture's viability and profitability. Drought, variable rainfall, rising air and water temperatures, decreased groundwater availability, and inadequate pond soils deplete stored water through evaporation, seepage, and operating losses. This review synthesises drought-prone pond water retention solutions from engineering, hydrological, aquaculture, and climate-adaptation literature. title: Heavy Metal Contamination in Macrobrachium rosenbergii From the Khulna Division of Bangladesh: A Human Health Risk Assessment
abstract: This study aimed to determine the concentrations of heavy metals (As, Cr, Cd, Pb, and Hg) in Macrobrachium rosenbergii from prawn farms in Khulna division, Bangladesh, and to assess the associated human health risks. Twenty-four farms in different upazilas of Khulna division were selected for sampling, and heavy metal concentrations in prawns were determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). abstract: Well log interpretation faces significant challenges due to data scarcity, distribution shift across geological basins, and a lack of physics-informed representations in current foundation models. While recent masked autoencoder approaches show promise for self-supervised pretraining on subsurface data, they fail to consider fundamental petrophysical constraints that govern measurement relationships. title: Impacts of South Asian aerosol inflow over Mount Qomolangma on downstream cloud–precipitation processes through a long-range ice-crystal “seeding” effect
abstract: Abstract. Mount Qomolangma (MQ) serves as a natural laboratory for investigating aerosol–cloud–precipitation interactions over the Tibetan Plateau (TP). Using satellite and comprehensive ground-based observations, we identify pronounced ice-cloud activation associated with transported exogenous aerosols. Under different large-scale atmospheric circulation regimes, ice-phase cloud activated over MQ can be efficiently transported downstream through distinct pathways, exerting a pronounced ice crystal seeding effect on cloud–precipitation conversion. title: A harmonized dataset for dams and reservoirs in West Africa
abstract: Abstract. Most existing datasets that could support dam and reservoir management and assessments of their impacts in West Africa are limited by inaccurate georeferencing, inconsistent accessibility, heterogeneous data records, and a lack of validation against field observations. In this study, we review and assess existing datasets containing information on dams and reservoirs in West Africa and subsequently integrate them into a harmonized and consolidated regional dataset. title: Structural, biological and nutritional properties of biopolymer-coated nanoliposomes containing poppy-pollen peptides prepared by two-step hydration method: membrane stability and gastrointestinal release
abstract: Bioactive peptides (BPs), despite their multiple biological and nutritional effects, suffer from low bioavailability, instability, and high reactivity. Therefore, in this study, stabilization and preservation of the biological activities of poppy pollen peptides (PPPs) within coated Nanochitosomes (NCs) with different concentrations (0.1–0.5% w/v) of chitosan were evaluated. title: Injection-based microbially induced carbonate precipitation: soil improvement and restructuring of native microbial communities
abstract: Abstract Purpose Microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) is increasingly applied as an environmentally oriented soil-improvement technique; however, its ecological effects on native soil microbial communities remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated injection-based MICP for soil improvement and the associated restructuring of soil microbial communities. title: Can conventional energy-saving technologies keep ships operating in European waters compliant with maritime climate regulations? A simulation-based assessment
abstract: Maritime transport is subject to increasingly strict emission regulation. Ships operating in European waters must comply with the International Maritime Organization’s Carbon Intensity Indicator, the European Union Emissions Trading System, and the FuelEU Maritime regulation, raising regulatory and financial pressure on the existing fleet. To stay compliant, shipowners can adopt conventional energy-saving technologies, such as hull and propeller upgrades. title: New radiocarbon determinations for the late Pleistocene site of Badanj (Bosnia and Herzegovina): Implications for the Upper Palaeolithic sequence of the Adriatic basin
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the results of a new radiocarbon dating program for the Upper Palaeolithic site of Badanj, Bosnia and Herzegovina. After putting together older dates originating from the 1970s and 1980s with recent ones acquired as part of new fieldwork, we then combine the available radiocarbon record with the present understanding of the stratigraphy to create two alternative Bayesian models. title: Breeding on a Tropical Island Proves More Difficult Than Expected: The Ongoing Breeding Failure of Laysan Albatross on Clarion Island
abstract: ABSTRACT In the 1980s, the Laysan Albatross ( Phoebastria immutabilis ) expanded its breeding range into the eastern Pacific and established colonies on several islands off the coast of Mexico. Colony growth has varied widely among these islands, likely reflecting differences in immigration rates and local conditions, such as food availability and predation risk, which can influence breeding success and population dynamics. title: Constitutive Behavior and Tangent Modulus Evaluation of Polyamide Multifilaments Under Post-Impact Conditions
abstract: This study investigates the constitutive behavior and tangent modulus of polyamide multifilaments in post-impact rupture. Polyamide is widely used in applications such as offshore mooring systems due to its excellent mechanical properties. However, its performance under dynamic conditions, especially after impact events, has not been extensively studied. title: Bioaccessibility and health risk evaluation of heavy metals in commercial fruit juices of Pakistan using an in vitro simulated digestion model
abstract: In recent years, fruit juice consumption has increased worldwide due to its potential health benefits. However, there is concern regarding heavy metals (HMs) in commercial fruit juices, posing significant health risks to their consumers. The current research was carried out to assess the concentrations of HMs in commercially available packaged fruit juices in Pakistan and evaluate their potential health risks through an in vitro digestion model. title: GUYASOILeDNA: a trans-kingdom and functional eDNA dataset on soil biodiversity from diverse land-cover types in French Guiana
abstract: Soil biodiversity represents approximately 60% of all described species on Earth and plays a critical role in terrestrial ecosystem functioning. However, knowledge of tropical soil biota and their roles remains highly fragmentary, especially in hyperdiverse tropical regions that remain largely undersampled relative to their temperate counterparts. Recent non-invasive methods, such as environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, have enabled large-scale data collection across kingdoms of life and habitats, including understudied compartments such as soils. title: From Hazard to Intervention: A Global Systematic Evidence Synthesis of Spatially Targeted Nature-Based Solutions for Urban Climate Resilience
abstract: In urban areas, a range of hazards are being exacerbated by climate change, such as extreme heat, flooding, drought and air pollution. Spatial solutions like NbS (Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems, green spaces, urban forests and wetlands) provide effective solutions to mitigate these risks with multiple functions and low costs. But knowledge of where and when, and who, such interventions work best is still incomplete. title: Genomic Vulnerability of a Threatened Possum in a Biodiversity and Climate Change Hotspot
abstract: Spatial variation in the magnitude and pace of climate change impacts means some species will be more affected than others. This includes those occurring within global biodiversity hotspots, regions with exceptional concentrations of endemic species that have often been shaped by long-term climatic stability. abstract: We present an evaluation and future projections of ten Global Climate Models (GCMs) dynamically downscaled using Rossby Centre Regional Atmospheric model version 4 (RCA4) under the Coordinated Regional Climate Downscaling Experiment (CORDEX) framework. abstract: The anthropocentric consciousness of human beings has induced the belief that humans are the most significant and only important entity in the ecosphere. title: High-resolution mangrove mapping in Guatemala using PlanetScope imagery and a SWIR-free moisture index
abstract: Mangrove forests are ecologically and socioeconomically important ecosystems that require accurate and timely monitoring. This study presents a high-resolution mangrove mapping approach along the Pacific coast of Guatemala using PlanetScope imagery integrated with a machine-learning framework. Sentinel-2 and Landsat data were used to derive the Modular Mangrove Recognition Index (MMRI), which depends on shortwave infrared (SWIR) bands. title: GEDI canopy cover assessment using airborne LiDAR across eco-climate regions of the United States
abstract: Information about woody plant density and canopy cover is central to our definition of terrestrial ecosystem types and crucial for understanding ecosystem state, dynamics, biogeochemical processes, and biodiversity. The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) LiDAR on the International Space Station (ISS) samples 3-D structural information on woody vegetation structure, including an estimate of canopy cover in each 25 m diameter footprint. title: Assessing the impact of climate change on wind energy potential in Brazil’s capitals: a long-term Weibull parameter analysis (1960–2020)
abstract: Abstract Brazil’s vast territory and favorable wind conditions have positioned it as a global leader in wind energy development. Accurate assessment of wind resources is essential for the feasibility of wind farms, particularly in the context of climate change. This study analyzes wind speed data from 27 Brazilian capitals (1960–2020) obtained from the CRUA database, using the two-parameter Weibull distribution to estimate the shape ( k ) and scale ( c ) parameters. title: Green Transition in New India: Issues and Remedies
abstract: Environment plays vital, instrumental and pivotal role in the existence and development of the human society. The world community has been exploiting the environment for speedy development and extremely neglecting the protection and preservation of the environment. Modernization, industrialization and globalization have not only accelerated the process of development but also polluted and destroyed the green environment worldwide including India. abstract: This research assessed the monitoring and evaluation (M&E) practices of the Brigada Eskwela Program across select public elementary schools in the District of Santa Fe, Division of Cebu Province, during School Year 2025–2026 to establish an empirical basis for program enhancement. Anchored on the CIPP Evaluation Model, Deming’s PDCA Cycle, General Systems Theory, and Stakeholder Theory, the investigation utilized a descriptive-evaluative quantitative design. title: Commercial Ambition and State Power of the British East India Company: The Rise of the "Company-State"
abstract: The British East India Company presents a typical case of the fusion between commercial expansion and state power in the history of the British Empire. The Company was initially established to secure a commercial monopoly, but its objectives were gradually converted to the de facto domination of South Asia. This paper examines the principal stages and mechanisms through which the EIC was transformed from a commercial enterprise into a "Company-State." title: Histological Based Biomonitoring of Odimodi River Basin Using the Liver of Sarotherodon melanotheron (Blackchin Tilapia)
abstract: The use of fish Liver as a histological bioindicators is an important environmental biomonitoring tool. Histological biomarkers were adopted to evaluate the health conditions of different organisms and to indicate potential environmental hazards. Histotoxicology is applied as an effective method to evaluate the influence of contaminants and other stressors in surface waters. Therefore, histological changes in the liver tissue of Sarotherodon melanotheron were evaluated and adopted as a bioindicator to measure environmental quality in Odimodi river basin, Delta state Nigeria. title: Fuel Heating for Reduce Emission of Diesel Engine
abstract: Diesel engines offer the highest efficiency compared to other internal combustion engines, and are therefore widely used in industry and transport. However, exhaust emissions from the combustion of diesel fuel pose a threat to the environment and human health. As a preventive measure, research has been conducted with the aim of modifying the fuel system or combustion system to reduce exhaust emissions. abstract: ABSTRACT The transportation sector contributes over 25% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from the use of fossil fuels. GHGs are one of the primary causes adversely affecting all three pillars of sustainable development. This rapid degradation has led to an urgent call to embrace “responsible transportation.” Responsible transportation advocates the speedy transition to alternative eco‐friendly modes of transportation and the use of renewable fuel sources—solar or electric power. title: Seasonal and spatial distribution of microplastics in the Upper Bhima River basin, Western Ghats, India
abstract: Microplastics (MP) are recognized as emerging global pollutant with significant ecological consequences for freshwater ecosystems. Information regarding MP pollution in rivers originating from the Western Ghats is insufficient and underreported, including from one of the largest rain-fed riverine systems, the Bhima River. The present study was undertaken across seasons to understand the seasonal variations of MP in the upper stretch of the Bhima River. title: Food Safety Risk Assessment of Wet-Salted Hilsa from Bangladesh: Physical, Chemical, and Biological Hazards
abstract: Wet-salted hilsa is a traditional fish product of Bangladesh, yet scientific evidence regarding its food safety remains limited. This study assessed the physical, chemical, and microbiological hazards associated with wet-salted hilsa. Physical hazards, namely filth, foreign substances, insect remnants, blowfly eggs, and live larvae, etc., revealed hygienic violations, with filth showing the highest (83–93.75%) contamination frequency and insect remnants showing the lowest (5–33.33%). title: Occurrence of Escherichia coli as an Indicator of Pollution in Groundwater Wells in Tobruk City, Libya
abstract: The issue of water scarcity has become increasingly severe, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions like those in the Arab world, where water resources are limited. Tobruk, a city facing such challenges, also grapples with water shortages due to the limited capacity of its desalination plant. This study aims to detect the presence of E. coli as an indicator of pollution in groundwater wells in the city of Tobruk. abstract: ABSTRACT Aquaculture is one of the fastest‐growing food‐production sectors in the world, with the potential to supplement fish protein from the dwindling capture fisheries and bridge the supply and demand gap of aquatic food in most regions of the world. As a result, the government of Kenya promoted aquaculture through an economic stimulus program and achieved significant milestones in the sector's development over the last decades. abstract: The study comparatively analyzed crayfish marketing across selected markets in Akwa Ibom State. The objectives of the study were to: estimate the factors influencing gross margin of crayfish marketing and identify constraints militating against crayfish marketing in the study area. Multistage sampling was employed to select one hundred respondents for the study. title: CRITÉRIOS DE DIAGNÓSTICO E TRATAMENTO SANITÁRIO NA AVALIAÇÃO DA QUALIDADE DO PESCADO
abstract: O controle de qualidade e a segurança sanitária do pescado são fundamentais para resguardar a saúde pública, dada a elevada perecibilidade da matriz e sua suscetibilidade a perigos biológicos e químicos ao longo da cadeia produtiva. Este estudo objetivou revisar os critérios de diagnóstico, controle e tratamento sanitário empregados na avaliação da qualidade do pescado. A metodologia consistiu em uma revisão narrativa com seleção de publicações recentes abarcando parâmetros sensoriais, físico-químicos, microbiológicos, parasitológicos e toxicológicos. title: Using grey literature to document and track climate change adaptation
abstract: While some large-scale and government-led adaptation is recorded, small-scale adaptations (e.g., in homes or businesses) are unreported, giving a partial view of national adaptation. Knowing how people adapt enables governments to incentivise and harness individual and bottom-up adaptation to support resilience. Grey literature (e.g. community-group and private sector reports) offers a rich source of adaptation information. Mining this using AI-tools and expert review would support evidence-based adaptation policy and evaluation.

title: Metagenomic analysis of rhizosphere soil microbiota in wild and cultivated Notopterygium incisum, an umbelliferae medicinal herb
abstract: Notopterygium incisum is not only a traditional Chinese medicine but also an endemic herb. Artificial domestication and large-scale cultivation are crucial for resolving the crisis of wild resources and the supply-demand imbalance of N. incisum, yet current techniques have failed to stably provide the herb medicine in good quality. Metagenomic analyses revealed significant differences in the rhizomicrobiota between wild and cultivated N. incisum, particularly in microbial composition, gene functions, and community assembly. abstract: Abstract Dendrocephalus brasiliensis Pesta, 1921 is an anostracan characteristic of temporary aquatic environments whose persistence depends on the viability of dormant cysts accumulated in the sediment. This study tested the hypothesis that nauplii are more sensitive to malathion than cysts and that exposure to the latter may alter hatching dynamics. title: Trends in Construction and Demolition Waste Management in Residential Buildings: Innovative Methods and Current Challenges
abstract: The Galapagos Islands face significant environmental challenges associated with increasing urbanization and the generation of Construction and Demolition Waste (CDW) from residential buildings. This study analyzes current CDW management practices on San Cristóbal Island using a quantitative approach based on municipal construction records from 2019 to 2024, complemented by spatial analysis and field inspections. title: A simple method for enhancing the spatial independence of regional partial duration series in extreme, short-duration rainfall frequency analyses
abstract: Abstract Regional frequency analyses (RFA) using partial duration series (PDSs) generally produce more reliable rainfall depth-duration-frequency (DDF) estimates than those based on annual maxima. A common implementation of this approach, the station-year method, pools threshold exceedances across multiple sites within a region to construct a regional PDS (rPDS). title: Occurrence and seasonal distribution of persistent organic pollutants in air and soil across agricultural urban and industrial landscapes
abstract: Soil represents a major terrestrial reservoir of persistent organic pollutants (POPs) that influence their atmospheric concentrations through volatilization processes. This study examines the distribution, seasonal variability, and air–soil exchange of key organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) (i.e., ΣDDTs, ΣHCHs), and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) in soils and air from industrial, agricultural, and urban areas in three Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cities (Peshawar, Swabi, Haripur), Pakistan. abstract: Background: Microplastics (MPs) are widespread environmental contaminants that have entered human biological systems, raising concerns for oral and systemic health. Saliva offers a convenient, non-invasive matrix for assessing exposure. However, standard detection methods such as Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) and Raman spectroscopy remain costly, preparation-heavy and limited to specialized laboratories. abstract: Shandong provides a concrete case for examining whether higher vocational education (HVE) can keep pace with industrial upgrading. Since the new and old kinetic energy conversion (NOKEC) strategy began in 2018, provincial policy has prioritized high-tech manufacturing and the “ten strong industries,” while HVE program structures have adjusted more slowly. This study evaluates the coordination between industrial upgrading and HVE program structure across 16 prefecture-level cities from 2016 to 2023. title: Multiple lines of evidence reveal rapid, seasonal watershed responses to enhanced weathering
abstract: A whole-watershed experiment revealed rapid streamwater alkalinity increases within weeks of basalt application, with strong seasonal cycling and the export of ~10% of theoretical carbon removal as alkalinity over 2 years, underscoring that temperature and hydrologic variability critically govern enhanced weathering effectiveness and monitoring.

abstract: Abstract Mapping the impurity distribution in 2D with laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (LA‐ICP‐MS) has provided valuable insights into the micro‐chemistry of a broad range of environmental samples. However, technical limitations have largely restricted mapping to millimeter‐sized maps as “snapshots.” Especially for stratigraphic archives with layers on the cm to mm scale and finer, much could be gained from increasing the map size to encompass the layer scale. title: Transportation Safety, and Supply Chain Resilience in Road-Based Crude Oil Logistics: Evidence from a Conflict‐Affected Region
abstract: Abstract Crude oil transport is a vital component of global energy supply chains; however, it is riddled with systemic risks, including human error, infrastructure fragility, security vulnerabilities, and regulatory deficiencies. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of crude oil transport, with particular emphasis on the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRG), a semi-autonomous territory that has emerged as a significant oil producer despite enduring geopolitical instability. title: Occurrence, concentration profiles, and human health risks of 18 phthalate esters in tap water and community direct-drinking water in Bengbu, China
abstract: Introduction Phthalate esters (PAEs) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants and endocrine-disrupting chemicals that have raised growing public health concerns. title: A Sharp Melt‐Bearing Lithosphere–Asthenosphere Boundary Beneath the Korean Peninsula: Evidence From Teleseismic Receiver Functions
abstract: Abstract The lithosphere–asthenosphere boundary (LAB) provides key constraints on how continental lithosphere responds to tectonic processes. Located between the East Asian cratonic blocks and the western Pacific subduction system, the Korean Peninsula (KP) provides an important setting to examine continental lithospheric evolution, yet seismic constraints on its LAB structure remain limited. We use P‐ and S‐receiver functions to investigate crustal and lithospheric structure beneath the southern KP and adjacent volcanic islands. title: Influence of thermal stratification on aquatic community structure and water quality across freshwater ecosystems
abstract: Climate change intensifies thermal stratification in lakes, altering oxygen, nutrients, and habitats, which reduces aquatic biodiversity, modifies biological communities, and compromises the ecological resilience of these ecosystems. In this context, the objective was to evaluate, through a systematic review, the impact of thermal stratification on aquatic biodiversity in lake systems, analyzing changes in richness, abundance, and biological composition associated with thermal stratification. title: A survey study on seaport modernising in Algeria as a driver for facilitating export and import operations
abstract: The modernisation of seaports has emerged as a strategic imperative in the contemporary global economic landscape, driven by the accelerating pace of globalisation and the sustained expansion of international trade volumes. As maritime transport remains the backbone of global commerce, the efficiency and responsiveness of port infrastructure directly influence a nation’s trade competitiveness. In light of these developments, this study aimed to investigate the role of seaport modernisation in Algeria as a key driver for facilitating export and import operations. title: Physical controls dominate stream metabolism and carbon cycling over nutrients and stoichiometry
abstract: Abstract Streams process and transport vast carbon quantities along the aquatic continuum. The balance between processing and downstream export is governed by metabolism, which in turn is regulated by distinct physicochemical controls that vary through space and time. However, macronutrient stoichiometry is rarely considered over absolute concentrations. Here, we examined physical, chemical, and stoichiometric controls on stream metabolism, organic carbon mineralization, and carbon spiraling over 2 years. title: Technological evolution and emerging research hotspots in earthquake monitoring from 1990 to 2024 revealed by bibliometric evidence
abstract: Earthquake monitoring has changed substantially over the past three decades, yet its technological evolution has rarely been examined through a systematic bibliometric lens. Existing review and scientometric studies have mainly focused on overall publication trends or adjacent disaster domains, with limited attention to how advances in sensing and analysis have reshaped earthquake monitoring itself. title: Spatial And Temporal Assessment of Atmospheric Nitrogen Using Hypnum Cupressiforme Mosses and Kjeldahl Analysis
abstract: This study aimed to explore the experiences of Palestinian Nitrogen content in mosses was investigated in a semi-rural area in Lebanon. CALPUFF dispersion model was used to estimate the annual average NOx and NH3 concentrations. Three sampling campaigns were conducted over the course of a year where 33 samples of the moss Hypnum cupressiforme were collected during each campaign. Kjeldahl method was used to determine the total nitrogen content in the collected samples.

abstract: Biosecurity screening of synthetic DNA orders is a key defense against malicious actors and careless enthusiasts producing dangerous pathogens or toxins. It is important to evaluate biosecurity screening tools for potential vulnerabilities and to work responsibly with providers to ensure that vulnerabilities can be patched before being publicly disclosed. abstract: Motivation: Logistics companies are a vital link in most global supply chains and improve the performance of their partners by optimising costs, increasing delivery reliability and flexibility of operations, and improving logistics organisation. It is important to note that the logistics industry, through its role in serving other sectors of the economy, is susceptible to any disruption that causes the slowdown in those sectors. title: Groundwater Sustainability in Hard Rock Terrains and Related Health Risks Assessment in Semi-Urban Nigeria
abstract: Ten representative groundwater samples were randomly collected from public hand dug wells in the Igarra Town and analyzed to assess their quality for drinking purpose and associated health risks following established methodological standards. The results revealed that pH values ranged from 5.25-6.63, indicating slightly to moderately acidic conditions and deviation from World Health Organization (WHO) and Nigeria drinking water standards (NSDWQ). title: Future of edge AI in biodiversity monitoring
abstract: Abstract Many ecological decisions are slowed by the gap between collecting and analysing biodiversity information. Edge computing moves data processing closer to the sensor, with edge artificial intelligence (AI) using AI models for data processing and selective data transfer. edge AI extends the scope of biodiversity monitoring by complementing retrospective ecological analysis with real‐time sensing, enabling responsive and adaptive decision‐making. However, the adoption of edge AI systems in ecological research remains fragmented because deploying efficient and reliable systems is complex.

title: Metagenomic insights into viral community restructuring and microbial interactions in waste stabilization ponds
abstract: Abstract Waste stabilization ponds (WSPs) operate as sequential ecological compartments in which physicochemical gradients, microbial succession, and trophic interactions increase toward the final polishing stage. Among these units, the maturation pond represents the terminal control point for pathogen attenuation and effluent quality; however, its role in shaping viral community structure remains insufficiently resolved. title: Quantifying metal transferability in soil and its relationship to metal-related health risks in the strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa)-human food chain
abstract: Understanding metal transfer in soil-strawberry systems is indispensable for sustainable strawberry production. To date, much attention has been paid to metals in strawberries, while metal transferability in strawberry-growing soil has been ignored. In this study, the availability, mobility, and bioavailability indices established based on BCR-extracted metal fractions and previously used for metal bioavailability evaluation in sediments were utilized to estimate metal transferability in soil sampled from strawberry orchards in the Yangtze River Delta, China, and predict metal-related health r

title: Integrated modelling framework for predicting microplastic build-up on urban surfaces
abstract: Urban impervious surfaces are major accumulation zones for microplastics, with deposited urban dust as a key carrier matrix facilitating their retention, redistribution, and transport from terrestrial to aquatic environments. However, processes governing microplastic build-up and the ability to predict its spatial distribution remain poorly understood. This study quantified the key factors influencing microplastic build-up and created a catchment-scale spatial predictive framework.
