title: Pedological and geochemical characteristics of highly weathered soils derived from ophiolitic rocks in Samar, Philippines
abstract: Limited information is available on the pedology of highly weathered soils derived from ophiolitic rocks in the Philippines. This study evaluated red, highly weathered soils across the ophiolitic landscape of Eastern Samar. Five soil profiles were described and sampled for laboratory analysis. abstract: Abattoir wastewater introduces organic matter, nutrients, suspended solids, microorganisms and potentially toxic metals into receiving rivers, producing complex water-quality responses that are difficult to interpret using single-parameter assessments. This study identified the critical variables and dominant pollution processes controlling water quality in the Effurun River, Delta State, Nigeria, using principal component analysis (PCA) and multivariate statistical analysis. title: Localization in the internet of things based on game theory with applications in the healthcare
abstract: Accurate indoor localization is critical for healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) applications such as patient tracking and asset management. However, maintaining localization accuracy under node mobility, signal attenuation, and faulty or adversarial behaviors remains challenging. Existing schemes either assume benign environments or employ rigid filters that permanently exclude noisy nodes, causing unacceptable losses in patient monitoring coverage. title: MycorrhizaTracer: A bioinformatic pipeline for fungi and plant classification of Sanger DNA sequences
abstract: Processing Sanger DNA sequences remains a routine, yet technically demanding step in many biodiversity and ecological studies, particularly when barcoding large numbers of environmental samples. Manual inspection and editing of trace files, DNA sequence alignment and classification using taxonomic reference databases are time-consuming, inconsistent and prone to error, compromising workflow standardisation, traceability and reproducibility. title: Computational intelligence approaches for seismic data analysis: a comprehensive analysis of detection and prediction methods
abstract: The global imperative for early earthquake prediction is indisputable. As computational capabilities continually evolve alongside technological advancements, a profound opportunity emerges for researchers to confront the intricate challenges inherent in detecting and predicting precursory signals associated with earthquakes by developing innovative models using integrating statistical methods with emerging technologies. title: Venice in the Jungle: An Archetype of the Urban Amazon
abstract: Résumé Partout en Amazonie, on trouve des villes et des zones urbaines comparées à Venise. title: Engineering PET surface colonization with a synthetic bacterial consortium
abstract: Introduction Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a widely used synthetic polymer that persists in the environment because of its resistance to biological degradation. Although engineered PET hydrolases have shown improved catalytic performance, translating these advances into effective whole-cell degradation remains challenging because cells and enzymes must interact with an insoluble polymer surface. title: A comparison of consumer preferences for cell-based seafood across European countries
abstract: Global seafood consumption has been increasing and is expected to continue rising, driven by population growth and evolving dietary patterns. Cell-based seafood has the potential to complement capture fisheries and aquaculture in meeting this growing demand. However, the long-term viability of this emerging sector will depend largely on consumer acceptance. This study examines consumer preferences and acceptance of cell-based seafood in four European countries—Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Hungary. title: Not So Stories
abstract: Three short autobiographical stories introduce a host of characters (human and beyond), places, and objects that bridge worlds – worlds of fact and fiction, past and present, Africa and Europe. The three autobiographical reflections, How the Outside Got In, Of Migrants and Music, and New Transvaal Stories, serve as points of departure for diffractive engagements with relational ontologies, histories, and cultures. title: Field-SCADA measurement analysis of power-curve deviation and sector-dependent underperformance in an operating utility-scale wind turbine
abstract: Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) data can support transparent power-curve screening, but residual calculation, sector aggregation and wind-speed-bin median fitting are established tools rather than algorithmic innovations. This study analyzes 50,530 ten-minute records from a public 2018 single-turbine dataset containing active power, wind speed, wind direction and a source-supplied theoretical reference. title: Technical–ethical–governance circuit–breaker framework for safe and sustainable AI governance
abstract: The growing use of large language models and autonomous AI systems in high-risk settings has created safety risks that cannot be addressed through technical safeguards alone. Existing approaches often treat technical failure control, ethical oversight, and institutional governance as separate domains, making coordinated intervention difficult when risks escalate across these boundaries. This study proposes the technical–ethical–governance (TEG) framework as an integrated circuit-breaker architecture for managing risks in high-risk AI systems. The framework combines technical, ethical, and gove

title: Evaluation of Water Quality from Atmospheric Water Generators Deployed Across Multiple Indian Cities: A Comparative Study
abstract: Atmospheric Water Generators (AWGs) represent an emerging decentralized water solution that extracts moisture from ambient air to produce potable water without reliance on conventional freshwater sources. This study evaluates AWG-produced water quality at three Indian deployment sites — Pune (October 2025), Sringeri (November 2025), and Chennai (October 2025) — against IS 14543:2024, the Indian Standard for packaged drinking water, and benchmarks results against the WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality. Organoleptic, physical, chemical, toxicological, and microbiological parameters were a
journal: Journal of Earth and Environmental Sciences Research

title: Sulfur Dioxide Point Sources Remain Important for Daytime Plume‐Scale New Particle Formation in the United States: Case Study for Gary, Indiana During the Summer 2023 AEROMMA Aircraft Campaign
abstract: Abstract Plumes from sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) point sources have been shown to be significant contributors to new particle formation (NPF), but SO 2 emissions in the United States (US) have decreased drastically by ∼10× since the early 2000s. We present observations of plume‐scale NPF from SO 2 point sources over the industrial hub in Gary, Indiana and assess the importance of SO 2 plumes to NPF using the P6 subgrid NPF parameterization and model the subsequent aerosol growth using the Statistical Oxidation Model‐TwO Moment Aerosol Sectional (SOM‐TOMAS) kinetic gas/aerosol model. title: SIRT2-mediated deacetylation of ANT3 at Lys96 promotes cell death
abstract: Abstract ANT3 is a key molecule that constitutes the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) and mediates cell death. Disruption or conformational changes in ANT3 protein homeostasis can trigger cell death. However, the molecular mechanism of ANT3 protein homeostasis regulation remains unclear. We found that prolonged starvation induces cell death by mediating ANT3 deacetylation-dependent pathways through the mitochondrial translocation of SIRT2, which in turn regulates ANT3 protein levels and conformational changes. title: Locking Down Science Gateways with Landlock and Seccomp
abstract: Abstract The most recent Linux kernels have a new feature for securing applications: Landlock. Like Seccomp before it, Landlock makes it possible for a running process to selectively relinquish access to certain system resources including network and filesystem access. Rather than being a proper successor to Seccomp, Landlock has different and somewhat complementary capabilities. In this paper, we will evaluate the applicability of using a combination of Landlock and Seccomp (Landlock/Seccomp) in the setting of securing science gateways—codes which need to parse and act upon user-supplied and

title: Beyond cichlid diversification: environmental drivers of biodiversity across the Nicaraguan lake system
abstract: Abstract The Nicaraguan lake system, comprising two Great Lakes and several isolated crater lakes, is a natural laboratory for investigating how environmental heterogeneity and isolation shape biodiversity and a classic model for Midas cichlid diversification. We asked whether lake characteristics associated with cichlid diversification are also linked to prokaryotic and eukaryotic diversity patterns. Using environmental DNA metabarcoding of water and sediments, we characterized communities in the large, shallow Great Lakes and smaller, deeper crater lakes. Lakes differed markedly in environme

title: Pathways to care in pinyon–juniper woodlands: Insights from Indigenous‐led monitoring and a public survey
abstract: Abstract Conservation decisions often require navigating tensions among ecological, cultural, economic and social priorities. While debates frequently centre on single‐species outcomes, less is known about how care for landscapes may contribute to co‐stewardship. Pinyon–juniper woodlands of California's Eastern Sierra Nevada provide a compelling case study. These culturally significant, climate‐stressed ecosystems are cared for by Tribes of the Eastern Sierra and Great Basin and managed by federal agencies, requiring coordination across knowledge systems and institutional mandates. title: Maintenance of bone health by osteoblasts in the absence of osteocytes: comparative analysis of gene expression in medaka and zebrafish vertebrae
abstract: Osteocytes are regarded as the strain-sensing bone cells; their capacity to sense and convert mechanical loads into biological signals underpins our current understanding of how bone is (re)modelled to normalise local strains. However, most extant fish are anosteocytic and lack osteocytes, yet their bone structure and (re)modelling abilities remain unimpeded, sitting uncomfortably with this paradigm. title: Local Wisdom-Based Marketing of Mahakam River Fish Commodities in West Kutai Regency, Indonesia
abstract: Mahakam River fisheries in West Kutai Regency play an important role in supporting food security and the local economy. However, fish marketing faces challenges, including long marketing chains, weak bargaining power among fishers, and increasing pressure on fisheries sustainability. This study analyzes the marketing structure of Mahakam River fish commodities and examines the role of local wisdom in supporting the sustainability of fisheries. Stakeholders interviewed included fishers, fish farmers, village collectors, market traders, and retailers. A descriptive approach was used to analyze m

title: Analysis of Vessel Clearance in and Clearance Out Procedures at PT Eleanor Pradana Shipping
abstract: This study aims to analyze the procedures for ship clearance in and clearance out services at PT Eleanor Pradana Shipping, identify operational bottlenecks, and evaluate strategic efforts to optimize service efficiency. A descriptive qualitative method was employed, utilizing primary data gathered through field observation, semi-structured in-depth interviews with key personnel on General Manager, Head of Operations, and Operational Staff, and administrative documentation. Data analysis followed the interactive model of Miles and Huberman on data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing

title: Marginalized Yet Enduring: Anglo-Indian Histories in Colonial and Post-Colonial Odisha
abstract: This article examines the overlooked history and present-day invisibility of the Anglo-Indian community in Odisha by spotlighting Dr. Josiah Dashwood Gillies and Captain Eric Tucker. Gillies, a colonial-era doctor, faced institutional prejudice that limited his professional recognition. Tucker, celebrated as a military hero after independence and Odisha’s first Ashok Chakra awardee, remains mostly unrecognized in regional history. title: Wudu in the Anthropocene: Reclaiming Ṭahārah–Najāsah as an Islamic Epistemology of Pollution in Indonesia's Environmental Fatwas, 2011–2023
abstract: This study asks whether an older, more granular epistemic resource within classical fiqh — the doctrine of ṭahārah–najāsah (ritual purity and impurity), with its finely graded taxonomy of contamination (najis mukhaffafah, mutawassiṭah, and mughallaẓah) — has likewise been mobilised. institutions: Universitas Islam Negeri Profesor Kiai Haji Saifuddin Zuhri Purwokerto

title: Recommendations for microbiological sampling in infected hard-to-heal wounds: an Italian association for cutaneous ulcers (AIUC) perspective
abstract: Chronic and hard-to-heal wounds represent a significant and growing healthcare burden, frequently complicated by infection and impaired healing. Despite the availability of international guidelines, microbiological assessment in clinical practice remains highly heterogeneous, with substantial variability in sampling techniques, timing, and interpretation of results. This variability occurs within a broader One Health context, where antimicrobial resistance and microbial ecology are shaped by interconnected human, environmental, and healthcare factors. title: A novel multivariate vine-copula–based drought index with application to high-elevation catchments
abstract: Abstract Drought is a complex, slowly evolving hazard governed by multiple interacting hydro-climatic factors, making it difficult to monitor, characterize, and predict. Conventional single-variable indices fail to capture the nonlinear, asymmetric dependence between precipitation and temperature—a limitation that is particularly critical in data-scarce, high-mountain catchments, where incomplete drought characterization undermines the reliability of early-warning systems. To address this, we propose a novel vine-copula-based Multivariate Drought Index (VMDI) that integrates the Standardized P

title: Innovation in health tourism: a service innovation perspective and research agenda
abstract: Health tourism (HT) is an umbrella domain encompassing medical tourism and wellness tourism. While these subdomains have developed substantial research, service models increasingly connect hospitals, clinics, hotels, resorts, and wellness providers, creating overlaps between healthcare, hospitality, and travel. This study uses innovation to connect these subdomains and explain the development of HT and identify future directions. We analysed 365 English-language Scopus and Web of Science documents published between 2003 and 2025. Bibliometric analysis mapped the keyword co-occurrence and thema

title: Source of giant Au-Sb mineralization in the Xiahe-Hezuo district, western Qinling: Constraints from Pb-S-Sb-Hg isotopes
abstract: The Xiahe-Hezuo district, located in the western Qinling orogenic belt, hosts several giant gold (Au) deposits, including the Ludousou, Zaozigou, and Jiagantan deposits arranged from north to south, which together contain > 300 t Au and significant Sb resources. However, the sources of metals and fluids, as well as the ore-forming processes responsible for the formation of these giant Au-Sb mineralizations, remain debated. institutions: State Key Laboratory of Geological Processes and Mineral Resources

title: Combination of instrumental and biomonitoring approaches elucidate the contributions of multiple and contrasted sources of atmospheric exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: A combined approach was implemented to investigate the origins of elevated PAH concentrations in a complex urban environment where numerous emission sources coexist. This approach integrated one year of atmospheric measurements PM10 filters and continuous atmospheric monitoring), alongside lichen biomonitoring and soil analyses. Results revealed diffuse multi-source contamination, characterized by high PAH levels in both soils and lichens, with a major contribution from the resuspension of soil particles from contaminated brownfields. title: Identification of rainfall-activated multi-indicator pollution pulses and lagged responses in Erhai Lake based on continuous water quality monitoring
abstract: Rainfall runoff can activate non-point source pollution and generate short-term water-quality anomalies in plateau lake basins, but event-scale multi-indicator responses remain difficult to identify using conventional mean-based assessments. Here, water-quality records available between June 2021 and December 2024 from the Lake Center, Jiangwei, Xiaoguanyi, and Jinhe monitoring sections of Erhai Lake were combined with daily precipitation data to identify 127 rainfall events. title: SYSTEM FOR LAND-BASED EMISSIONS ESTIMATION IN KENYA(SLEEK) AND LAND-SECTOR CARBON ACCOUNTING IN KENYA: EVIDENCE FROM EMISSIONS AND REMOVALS ACCOUNTING, 1990-2015
abstract: Developing countries face persistent constraints in producing transparent, consistent and nationally owned greenhouse-gas inventories for the land sector. Kenya responded through the System for Land-based Emissions Estimation in Kenya (SLEEK), a national programme designed to integrate activity data, country-specific parameters, spatial modelling, reporting tools and institutional capacity. journal: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
institutions: Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change

title: Flow Tree: a model for navigator dynamics and environmental complexity
abstract: Navigation is a dynamic process, involving learning new environments and manoeuvring through them. Individuals differ widely in their abilities and strategies. Prior research often uses static measures, such as total distance travelled or location tallies, which overlook the variability and asymmetry in how trajectories unfold. To address this, we introduce the Flow Tree, a novel data structure that encodes how trajectories evolve relative to each other through time and space. Branching points capture when groups split into subgroups, producing a compressed, dynamic trace of group decision-mak
journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface

title: A first, provisional, annotated checklist of the microlepidoptera of Albania (Insecta: Lepidoptera)
abstract: All available published data on the microlepidoptera fauna of Albania are collated and combined with the results of modern sampling to form the first known checklist of Albanian microlepidoptera. Published data are minimal as a consequence of the political history of the country; these historic reports are supplemented by active sampling during the present millennium. In total we record 1266 species across 46 families. Of these, a total of 932 species (72%) are recorded in the present millennium and are considered to be currently resident. title: Documented service-chain maturity and policy coordination capacity in climate services for tourism: A scoping review
abstract: Climate services for tourism (CST) face challenges in implementation and long-term continuity because policy coordination and governance mechanisms remain poorly documented. This study assessed whether the CST evidence base reflects a transition from climate-information products to mature service chains supported by policy coordination arrangements. We conducted a scoping review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). After screening 969 records against four CST core inclusion criteria, we retained 58 document
institutions: Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region Meteorological Bureau

title: Effects of compound microbial fertilizer combined with potassium fulvic acid on soil physicochemical properties, microbial community structure, and cotton productivity in saline-alkali soil
abstract: To explore the effects of compound microbial fertilizer (containing Lactobacillus acidophilus and Corynebacterium glutamicum ) combined with potassium fulvic acid on cotton growth and soil ecology in Xinjiang saline-alkali soil, a two-year field experiment with seven treatments was conducted in a randomized block design. We analyzed cotton emergence rate, yield components, rhizosphere soil physicochemical properties (pH, water-soluble salts, major ions), and soil microbial community structure using high-throughput sequencing. title: Transparent forecasting with XAI: Improving accuracy and trust in electricity demand prediction
abstract: This research is based on forecasting the net demand for electricity by considering the previous trends. Considering the overall increase in demand for electricity year by year, predicting such a trend plays a crucial role in a country’s development, as it helps make an accurate prediction of future energy consumption and prepare accordingly. The trends will be considered in light of various factors that affect the electricity usage rate. Different algorithms would be applied to a pipeline to predict appropriate results. title: Macroinvertebrate communities respond to spatial patterns of water quality and habitat within mining-influenced headwater streams of central Appalachia
abstract: Surface coal mining in central Appalachia (USA) often results in salinization of headwater streams, with documented loss of several macroinvertebrate taxa and changes in community metrics across streams that vary in specific conductance (SC). However, the extent to which this salinization alters within-stream patterns in water chemistry and macroinvertebrate communities in these headwater streams is largely unknown. title: IOT-driven multimodal deep visual analytics for air pollution forecasting in firework industrial regions
abstract: Abstract The increasing atmospheric burden associated with firework manufacturing requires intelligent environmental monitoring frameworks capable of integrating heterogeneous pollution indicators. This study presents an IoT-driven multimodal surveillance architecture designed for industrial air quality assessment in Sivakasi. The framework integrates environmental sensors with camera-based visual analytics to improve Air Quality Index forecasting under dynamic industrial conditions. title: Analysis of Barge Mounted Power Plant Production Process at PT PAL Indonesia
abstract: General Background Floating power station construction requires highly structured manufacturing workflows to deliver clean energy infrastructure reliably. Specific Background Barge Mounted Power Plant (BMPP) fabrication in shipyards operates under job shop environments with complex assembly sequences and extended production cycles. Knowledge Gap Although workflow mapping tools clarify manufacturing stages, operational bottlenecks and supply chain disruptions during initial production phases of specialized barges remain insufficiently detailed in empirical literature. title: Spatiotemporal wildfire occurrence, burn severity and early post-fire vegetation recovery in a tropical Andean landscape: Quilanga, southern Ecuador
abstract: Wildfires are recurrent environmental hazards in tropical Andean landscapes, where limited spatial records can constrain prevention, impact assessment, and post-fire management. This study presents an integrated assessment to characterize wildfire occurrence, burn severity, and early vegetation-greenness recovery in Quilanga, southern Ecuador. Official wildfire records from 2010-2025 were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Mann-Kendall tests, Sen’s slopes, and multiscale kernel density estimation. title: The Role of Simulation Technology in Enhancing Port Crane Operator Competence and Safety
abstract: Global maritime trade increasingly depends on efficient and safe port operations, where crane operators play a vital role in container handling. Although traditional training methods are effective, they require considerable time and may involve operational risks. Simulation-based training offers a risk-free, cost-effective, and performance-oriented alternative. This study evaluated the effectiveness of simulator training for ship-to-shore (STS) and rubber-tyred gantry (RTG) crane operators by examining error types, training periods, and changes in operator performance. journal: Turkish Journal of Science and Technology

title: Simplifying Macroinvertebrate Biodiversity Assessment: A Standardised Metabarcoding Method for Invertebrate Samples With High Volumes of Debris
abstract: DNA metabarcoding of freshwater macroinvertebrate samples can provide rapid and accurate identification of species diversity. Processing samples where macroinvertebrates are not separated from net contents can substantially reduce time and cost. We devised and tested a standardised method for processing combined kick/sweep samples using DNA metabarcoding to provide accurate estimates of macroinvertebrate species diversity. title: Development Strategy for Snakehead Fish (Channa striata) Albumin Agroindustry in South Kalimantan: SWOT Analysis and IE Matrix
abstract: Snakehead fish albumin is a product based on South Kalimantan fishery resources that has the potential to be developed as a value-added agro-industrial product, but its development still faces various strategic obstacles. This study aims to formulate a strategy for developing snakehead fish albumin through an analysis of internal and external factors using the SWOT approach combined with the IFAS, EFAS, and IE matrices. abstract: Küresel ticaretin omurgasını oluşturan denizyolu taşımacılığı, son yıllarda artan dışsal şoklara ve jeopolitik kırılmalara karşı oldukça hassas bir yapı sergilemektedir. journal: International Journal of Management Economics and Business

title: Unlocking microbial dark matter: A biotechnology framework for replenishing the antibiotic pipeline
abstract: The antibiotic pipeline is in crisis, even though microbial natural products account for most approved antibacterial drugs and retain vast, untapped biosynthetic potential. Genuinely new scaffolds are rare because discovery remains constrained to a narrow set of cultivable taxa and expressed biosynthetic gene clusters, while most microbial chemistry persists as "dark matter" in uncultured organisms and silent clusters. title: Insights of the Different Sectors on the Readiness for the Implementation of DOST Smart and Sustainable Communities Program (SSCP)
abstract: This research investigated the multi-sectoral readiness of Barcelona, Sorsogon, to implement the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) Smart and Sustainable Communities Program (SSCP). Utilizing a qualitative descriptive research design through the lens of the Quadruple Helix model, the study evaluated the insights and perceptions of twentyfive purposively sampled key informants from the Government, Academe, Industry (farmers and fisherfolks), and Civil Society Organization (CSO) sectors to transition into a "Smart Community". journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

title: Enabling Smart Home Sustainability with LoRaWAN: A Review of Energy and Water Sensing Technologies and Applications
abstract: LoRaWAN is cost-efficient, provides long-range communication, and has low power consumption, making it an appropriate communication technology for the IoT-based energy and water sensing system. This review presents recent developments in LoRaWAN for domestic energy monitoring, water sensing, and integrated smart-home resource management. Research was conducted through thematic analysis of studies retrieved from extensive searches of major scientific databases between 2020 and 2026. journal: International Journal of Computer Science and Engineering

title: Techno-economic optimization of low-CAPEX/OPEX seafood valorization in SMEs using the TIDE framework
abstract: The valorization of seafood by-products is often framed as a technical opportunity, yet adoption in practice depends on whether small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can embed new systems in their operational, economic, spatial, and regulatory realities. Drawing on survey-based evidence from Greek fisheries and seafood enterprises, the analysis identifies key operational and economic constraints and translates them into a configurational model of adoption credibility for blue SMEs. title: A Comparative Hedonic Analysis of Condominium Asking Rents in Bangkok, Phuket, and Pattaya
abstract: This study estimates condominium rental price differentials from online listings across Thailand’s three major tourist cities, using Bangkok as the benchmark for Phuket and Pattaya while controlling for observable unit characteristics. Intercity differentials are measured with a hedonic regression in which the dependent variable is the natural logarithm of monthly rent (in Thai baht). Model 1 controls for the number of bedrooms, while Model 2 adds unit size through log(size_sqm), allowing the effect of unit composition on estimated city effects to be assessed. journal: International Journal of Building Urban Interior and Landscape Technology (BUILT)

title: A convolution–attention network predicts boiler slagging and warns of waterwall overheating from the furnace temperature field
abstract: Abstract Slagging and wall-temperature overheating rank among the costliest threats to safe and economical coal-fired boiler operation, yet plants still diagnose them separately although both grow out of the same non-uniform furnace temperature field. This paper treats them jointly. institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

title: How reporting cadence shapes hourly precipitation extremes
abstract: Hourly precipitation products are often assembled from station records with heterogeneous sub-hourly reporting cadences, yet users rarely know how much of the resulting difference in extreme diagnostics reflects temporal support, clock-hour alignment, the aggregation implementation, or the temporal structure of the rainfall. We present a controlled coarsening framework that separates these four causes within a single experiment in which the meteorology is held fixed and precipitation mass is conserved. title: Changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026
abstract: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. institutions: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Bioash amendments from biomass energy systems reshape rhizosphere bacterial communities and reduce metal bioavailability in contaminated soils
abstract: Biomass-derived ashes (bioash) from energy production are increasingly promoted within circular bioeconomy frameworks as soil amendments that recycle nutrients and mitigate soil acidity. However, their impacts on rhizosphere bacterial communities in metal-contaminated soils (MCS) remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how four bioash types applied at three rates influence rhizosphere biogeochemistry and bacterial community dynamics of lettuce ( Lactuca sativa L.) grown in MCS. title: Mathematical Simulation‐Based Evaluation of Measurement Error Impacts on Topographic Change Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Topographic change detection is widely applied in fields such as geological hazard early warning, environmental monitoring, and geographic process analysis. However, measurement errors—such as random and systematic errors—are inevitable during the acquisition of topographic data, and their propagation and accumulation can significantly increase the uncertainty of change detection results. title: Enhanced supplier clustering using an improved arithmetic optimiser algorithm
abstract: Finding the appropriate supplier is becoming increasingly difficult because of the complexity in evaluation criteria. Clustering algorithms and metaheuristic algorithms continue to face challenges while dealing with large data because of their inconsistent convergence, inconsistent balance between exploration and exploitation, and scalability problem. In this paper, we propose an Improved Arithmetic Optimiser Algorithm (IAOA), which integrates population feedback control, directed L´evy search, and cluster-aware soft Lloyd update to improve convergence and avoid local optima trapping. title: Improving radar rainfall estimation accuracy in the composite area of Takhli and Sattahip radars using spatial and hourly time-varying bias adjustment
abstract: In estimating rainfall over the composite coverage area of the Takhli and Sattahip radars, the use of a composite Z–R relationship may still result in residual errors due to differences in the physical characteristics of rainfall. These differences can be attributed to the effects of the Earth’s curvature, variations in terrain characteristics, and event-to-event differences in rainfall, including variations in the spatial distribution of raindrops over time. title: Depth-stratified boreal peatland microbiomes reveal recurring community organization and methane-cycling potential
abstract: Microbial communities in peatlands vary with depth, but most studies have been limited in spatial extent or replication, constraining assessment of general community patterns. We characterized microbial community structure and metabolic potential across replicated depth profiles in seven boreal peatlands in Sweden. Combining 16S rRNA gene sequencing and shotgun metagenomics, we identified recurring vertical stratification across sites. title: Status and Challenges in the Implementation of LCP-Modular Distance Learning (MDL) of Lutucan Integrated National High School: A Proposed Comprehensive Action Plan Tool
abstract: This study assessed the status and challenges in the implementation of Modular Distance Learning (MDL) at Lutucan Integrated National High School during the School Year 2020–2021. Conducted from May to September 2020, the study utilized a Mixed-Method Research Design — descriptive survey to measure implementation status, supplemented by qualitative inquiry to identify challenges. title: Women in Portuguese industrial microbiology: a fifty-year perspective on progress and persistent barriers
abstract: Industrial microbiology sits at the heart of food safety, fermentation technology, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance, and sustainable biotechnology, yet leadership in the field remains disproportionately male. Only 26% of full professors in Europe are women, despite women making up the majority of life-science graduates. Portugal offers a particularly telling paradox. title: When Clades Collide: Genomic Admixture in Blacklegged Ticks ( Ixodes scapularis ) From the Great Plains
abstract: ABSTRACT Ixodes scapularis ticks transmit a number of pathogens important to human health, including Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto, the causative agent of Lyme disease. While I. scapularis is found across the Eastern United States, Lyme disease transmission is largely limited to the Northeast and Upper Midwest and is nearly absent in the South. This indicates that differences in northern versus southern clades of I. scapularis are associated with differences in Lyme disease transmission risk. title: Differential testicular toxicity of deoxynivalenol: insights from juvenile and adult mice
abstract: Deoxynivalenol (DON) is a mycotoxin that contaminates approximately 60% of food worldwide and can impair reproduction. Although puberty represents a critical window of susceptibility to toxic insults, the effects of DON exposure during this period remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of DON on testicular structure, oxidative status, inflammatory responses, and sperm parameters in prepubertal and adult mice. abstract: BACKGROUND: Most crop plants, including sugar beet (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris), suffer from domestication bottlenecks and low genetic diversity caused by extensive selection for few traits. abstract: This article examines the functioning of proper names from a sociolinguistic and political perspective, focusing on the name of the Republic of Belarus across languages. The aim of the study is to explain why the form Belarus (Byelarusʹ) is promoted by Belarusian authorities and communities, and why traditional exonyms continue to be used in other languages. abstract: Auxotrophy, the inability of bacteria to synthesize one or multiple essential metabolites, is thought to be common among bacteria. However, studies often rely on either bioinformatic genome-based prediction of auxotrophies or on experiments with low strain numbers. abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial cultivation remains essential for understanding the physiology, ecology, and biotechnological potential of environmental microbes, yet conventional plate-based methods (CPM) recover only a minute fraction of the environmental microbiome. title: Study on Development, Prospects, Challenge, and Applications of Solar Panel: Global and Local Perspective
abstract: Solar power is a rapidly growing renewable energy source that converts sunlight into electricity using photovoltaic (PV) cells. Global solar capacity has grown exponentially over the past decade, driven by plummeting technology costs and aggressive government climate targets. China, the United States, and the European Union lead in total installed capacity. Continued efficiency improvements in perovskite solar cells and bifacial panels promise even higher energy yields. abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐term laboratory propagation can be associated with phenotypic and transcriptional differences in model organisms, but comparisons with recently isolated strains and earlier laboratory lineages remain limited. title: Cross-organ multilayered biological perturbations driven by food chain-transferred microplastics: implications for mammalian health effects and risks
abstract: Microplastic pollution has emerged as a global environmental and health concern. To elucidate its realistic biological impact, this study established a food chain‑transferred exposure model using polystyrene microplastics, from mealworms to mice. abstract: Extreme rainfall modeling is crucial for flood-risk assessment, drainage design, and urban planning in tropical monsoon regions. This study analyzed annual maximum rainfall in Makassar, Indonesia, using stationary and non-stationary generalized extreme value (GEV) models. abstract: While machine learning has greatly advanced data-driven mineral exploration, its effectiveness is often limited by geological heterogeneity arising from the coexistence of multiple mineralization types within the same area. For example, in eastern Junggar, Xinjiang, China, copper deposits occur within a broadly shared regional metallogenic framework and exhibit similar surface expressions, yet different deposit types vary significantly in ore-controlling factors and geochemical signatures. title: The Mediating Role of Satisfaction on Perceived and Hedonic Values in Shaping Revisit Intention at Bali Beach Clubs
abstract: Tourism growth in emerging destinations has intensified competition among leisure venues, particularly in Bali’s beach clubs, which have become a distinctive attraction for domestic and international tourists. Sustaining revisit intention is critical for the long-term success of these establishments, yet little is known about the determinants of loyalty in this context. abstract: The spatiotemporal variability in annual rainfall and rainfall erosivity (R factor) is a crucial factor in assessing seasonal soil erosion dynamics and regional water resource management, since it has a substantial impact on complex interactions involving the water, soil, and surroundings under the variable climate regime of Eastern India. abstract: Purpose: Malang is an Indonesian District struggling with waste management: low collection rates, fly-tipping, and burning. This study conducts a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) on the end-of-life pathways of plastic waste (PW) in Malang. All the stages of the PW management system are covered, from PW generation and transportation to unregulated and regulated PW management strategies. abstract: This research article examines the notion of the green school through the lens of health and wellness; outdoors education; and stewardship of resources. abstract: Grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) generation is strongly affected by short- and long-term variations in solar irradiance, ambient and module temperature, humidity, wind, cloud cover, and associated balance-of-system losses. abstract: Microbial contamination of food-contact surfaces is an important food-safety concern. UV-C irradiation may provide a supplementary non-chemical approach for reducing bacterial contamination on tableware; however, the effect of different exposure durations under standardized conditions requires further evaluation. abstract: Abstract Mallards ( Anas platyrhynchos ) have been domesticated and released in Europe and North America for centuries to supplement hunter harvest and in attempts to increase populations. They have interbred with wild mallards, most notably in the Atlantic Flyway of North America. Published research indicates that >90% of mallards harvested in the Atlantic Flyway are hybrids, and the species has formed a hybrid swarm of wild‐strain and game‐farm (GF) birds. title: Photoaging-driven amplification of polystyrene microplastic toxicity in wheat: physiological and multi-omics insights
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in agroecosystems displayed phytotoxicity; however, the differential effects of pristine and photoaged MPs remain unclear. title: Evaluation of larvicidal efficacy of Clerodendrum infortunatum Linn extracts against Culex quinquefasciatus Say (Diptera, Culicidae)
abstract: Clerodendrum infortunatum Linn (Family, Lamiaceae), extracts of acetone, methanol and aqueous evaluated against larvae of Culex quinquefasciatus Say, showed promising results. Acetone leaf extract recorded an LC50 value of 345.41ppm, and was found effective for the management of Cu. quinquefasciatus. In vitro cytotoxic analysis of L929 mouse cell lines using the plant extract proved safe for non-target organisms, higher vertebrates. Phytochemical screening of the acetone extract revealed the presence of secondary metabolites that may have contributed to its insecticidal activity.

abstract: ABSTRACT The Astur [ gentilis ] superspecies comprising five species has a long record of taxonomic debate. abstract: ABSTRACT Floods remain among the most frequent and damaging natural hazards globally, with effective flood early warning messages (FEWMs) playing a critical role in reducing disaster risk and enhancing community preparedness. Despite advances in early warning systems, many rural communities in developing countries continue to experience challenges in accessing, understanding, and responding to warning information. abstract: The discrepancy between sustainability claims and actual practices in tourism and hospitality has brought forth the "greenwashing" phenomenon. This conceptual study analyzes the multi-dimensional effects of greenwashing perceptions on consumer trust through legitimacy theory, signaling theory, and attribution theory. abstract: Reliable sensor data is essential for understanding process dynamics and enabling data-driven monitoring in machining processes. abstract: The Grand Strategy aims to align a state’s means and resources with its strategic priorities in pursuit of national interests, while taking into account internal and external constraints. For Morocco, the Grand Strategy provides a key framework for achieving national interests and redefining the country’s position within the international community. abstract: The Free Nutritional Meals (MBG) program is one of the Indonesian government's largest post-2024 social interventions and positions schools as a crucial arena for fulfilling the right to food and developing human capital. This article evaluates the MBG program for students in its second year of implementation by developing an integrative framework linking state responsibility, the social investment paradigm, implementation theory, William Dunn's policy evaluation criteria, and the Context–Input–Process–Product (CIPP) model. abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) has emerged as one of the most pressing environmental health challenges in East Africa, where rapid urbanization, industrial expansion, and reliance on biomass fuels converge to elevate exposure levels. Understanding the historical dynamics and future trajectories of these populations is crucial for developing effective conservation strategies, yet they remain poorly understood. abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) represent one of the most common bacterial infections worldwide and are increasingly complicated by the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) uropathogens. abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial neurological disability, and effective strategies for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) are limited. abstract: Afghanistan became one of the principal arenas in which great power rivalry, regional intervention, and internal political fragmentation intersected during the Cold War. This study analyses the political transformation of Afghanistan from the Soviet invasion of December 1979 to the Taliban’s capture of Kabul in September 1996 within its historical context. abstract: This study examines how Early Republican Türkiye was perceived by Spanish academics and students who visited İzmir and İstanbul during the 1933 Mediterranean University Cruise, an educational initiative organized during the Second Spanish Republic. abstract: Deep image classification algorithms may suffer from redundant feature responses, unstable class boundaries, and weak robustness when sample differences are subtle and class distributions are complex. abstract: Value-chain emissions constitute the majority of environmental impacts across industrial systems, yet scalable, life-cycle-based strategies for reducing these impacts remain limited. Biochar has been widely studied as a functional material with climate benefits, but its contribution to supply-chain decarbonization is typically constrained by moderate inclusion rates and limited impact per unit mass. abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) bears a disproportionate burden of neurological and pain-related diseases while facing a severe shortage of trained specialists. This Perspective proposes a context-sensitive framework in which three interconnected domains—territory, culture, and capacity—shape the accessibility, acceptability, and sustainability of neurological care. abstract: Much of the existing scholarship on sport in Qatar has been shaped by the 2022 FIFA World Cup and the broader issues around it. title: A sensitivity analysis of data imputation in daily PM10 prediction
abstract: Reliable daily prediction of particulate matter (PM10) depends not only on model structure and predictor selection, but also on how missing data are treated during preprocessing. In air-quality applications, gaps are common in both ground-based monitoring records and satellite-derived predictors due to instrument downtime, quality screening, and cloud contamination. We developed a user-generated content (UGC)-based text-mining framework and applied it to eight cultural-creative industrial heritage sites in central Chongqing, China. abstract: Abstract In recent years, Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) have emerged as a pivotal domain within wireless technologies. Emergency Response MANETs (ER-MANETs) support communication among emergency responders during critical scenarios. Ensuring the real-time integrity and availability of these highly dynamic networks requires robust security measures beyond traditional approaches. abstract: Abstract Indirect competition is a fundamental mechanism shaping the structure of biological systems, from food webs to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) networks. title: Data-driven School Planning: The Role of Educational Report Cards in Strengthening Governance and Accountability in Indonesian Primary Schools
abstract: Educational governance increasingly prioritizes data-driven decision-making as a basis for accountability and quality enhancement. The implementation of the Rapor Pendidikan (Educational Report Card) in Indonesia represents a national initiative to incorporate evidence into school planning. title: Multifunctional wood composites: advancing sustainable solutions for smart and functional applications – a review
abstract: Wood, as an abundant and renewable natural resource, has long played a vital role in meeting both structural and non-structural needs. abstract: Despite the importance of groundwater as a source of drinking and domestic water, limited information is available on groundwater quality in the Chehelsoton area. The lack of localized data on key physicochemical parameters limits assessment of potential health risks and sustainable groundwater use. Therefore, systematic evaluation of groundwater quality is needed. abstract: The ever-increasing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions primarily Carbon Dioxide (CO 2 ), are adversely impacting the climate at an unprecedented rate, leading to more frequent extreme climate events. Reducing GHG and counteracting climate change can be achieved by decarbonizing energy systems and challenging the status quo of current industrial practices of producing and consuming energy. abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a significant opportunistic pathogen and the capacity to form biofilms and multidrug resistance restricts the usefulness of traditional antibiotic treatment in the case of HAIs. The extracellular metabolites of probiotics are called cell-free supernatants (CFSs) and may have antibacterial and antibiofilm activity. abstract: Abstract Rainfall-runoff (R-R) forecasting in data-scarce regions remains challenging due to limited hydrometeorological observations, uncertainties in satellite-based precipitation products (SPPs), and the inability of individual modeling approaches to fully represent complex watershed dynamics. abstract: Course syllabus review is an arduous and complex task that requires diverse methods, techniques, and tools to facilitate the active participation of the faculty members who teach the course. This document describes a course syllabus review exercise conducted by the faculty members who teach the course, with the aim of providing a systematic and feasible procedure that can be replicated in other revision processes. abstract: Passion fruit is susceptible to postharvest spoilage, requiring innovative preservation strategies. This study developed a novel Cu 2+ -chelated curcumin/chitosan composite coating (CuCur-CS) via self-assembly. Under ambient temperature, CuCur-CS treatment was the most effective, exhibiting the lowest weight loss rate (only 5.6% on day 18), along with superior fruit shape and surface color retention. abstract: This study aimed to assess the major sources of poultry feed and their nutritional composition in northern Ethiopia. The synthesis of nitroguanidine (NQ), an energetic material, was characterized and optimized as a model for hazardous reactions. abstract: Given the broad therapeutic benefits of molecular hydrogen, gastrointestinal delivery of this gasotransmitter is attractive for treating localized inflammatory diseases, yet conventional H2-releasing formulations suffer from limited solubility and poor tunability. Here, we develop gas-releasing frameworks (GRFs) for effective H2 delivery to the gastrointestinal tract. abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is an important foodborne pathogen that causes human gastroenteritis worldwide through the secretion of staphylococcal enterotoxins in food. Consumption of contaminated raw food or cooked food handled by S. aureus carriers is the primary cause of staphylococcal food poisoning. In this study, a one-year surveillance of S. aureus in Boiled Salted Goose was conducted in Yangzhou, eastern China. abstract: Abstract The rhizosphere microbiome is critical for forest ecological functions, yet the mechanisms through which tree species identity and neighbour tree interactions are associated with its assembly remain poorly understood. Using Illumina MiSeq and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS), we investigated how tree species (pine vs. liquidambar) and forest composition (pure vs. mixed) shape rhizosphere microbial communities and root metabolites in subtropical forests. abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the DRC and Uganda raises urgent questions about the efficacy of existing Ebola virus (EBOV) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). abstract: This study aims to assess the impact of the cement industry on surface and groundwater quality. The research focuses on a specific cement plant location Athwajan Srinagar J&K and evaluates the physico-chemical parameters of water samples collected from various points around the plant. Parameters such as pH, temperature, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, total dissolved solids, hardness, calcium, alkalinity, sulphate, nitrate, fluoride, chloride, and iron are analyzed to determine the extent of pollution. abstract: The sustainability of international shipping involves not only emissions reduction and energy efficiency, but also institutional quality, transparency, and policy enforcement. This study examines the relationship between corruption perceptions and environmental governance to highlight the institutional conditions required for sustainable development in shipping. abstract: The thermal emission spectra of terrestrial exoplanets provide a window into their surface compositions and corresponding geological processes. Close-in, rocky planets orbiting M dwarfs are ideal targets for these studies, as observations have shown that most have little to no atmosphere. LHS 3844 b is an ultra-short period super-Earth orbiting a nearby M dwarf, and is the most favorable target that does not have a dayside magma ocean. abstract: This paper presents a systematic approach to plan and execute a time-efficient sailboat trajectory under the challenging stochastic wind conditions for automated sailboat. Unlike deterministic scenarios, stochastic wind disturbances introduce challenges such as gust unpredictability, directional shifts, and fluctuating apparent wind speeds. title: What Do City Codes Say About Climate Risk?
abstract: Climate change is intensifying natural hazards, and preparing cities for them falls primarily to local governments. Yet what municipal codes say about hazards, and whether their requirements match each city's risk profile, has not been measured. I analyze 3.6 million sentences from 204 U.S. cities' municipal codes and compare each city's hazard text to its actual risk from FEMA's National Risk Index. I document four patterns. abstract: IoT terminals served by LEO satellite constellations transmit data to passing satellites in discrete uplink windows. abstract: The 1-ton prototype detector for Jinping neutrino experiment (JNE-1ton) has completed its hardware upgrade and has been successfully operated in both water and liquid-scintillator modes at CJPL-I, which is situated under a 2400-m rock overburden. During the upgrade, the detector's mechanical support structure and PMT layout were redesigned. abstract: Skills equip LLM agents with professional knowledge and guidance to complete long-horizon and complex tasks. Although skills have been widely adopted in recent agent paradigms and harnesses, how to synthesize reliable training data and how to train agents for skill use remain underexplored. In this work, we propose SkillGym, an automatic pipeline to build verifiable environments, collect trajectories, and train skill-use agents. abstract: A surgical robot policy needs to know where each instrument's working end sits relative to the camera and to the other instrument, yet a laparoscopic operation leaves only the endoscope video, and a draped instrument hides every optical path on itself. We estimate the tool tips from distances and an IMU alone. abstract: Long-running LLM agents compress past interactions into persistent memories that may be reused as premises for later tasks. abstract: The inclusion of isospin-breaking corrections arising from electromagnetic interactions and the up-down quark mass difference is becoming increasingly important in lattice QCD calculations, as the precision of observables is at or approaching the percent level. abstract: Reliable automated research requires agents to vet data, verify analyses, and generate hypotheses grounded in trustworthy evidence, potentially reducing routine scientific workload while allowing scientists to focus on interpretation and discovery. abstract: Quantum infrared (IR) spectroscopy is a novel technique based on nonlinear interferometry and quantum sensing with undetected photons. abstract: Multiple-choice benchmarks are cheap to grade and are running out of room, and the standard remedy, writing harder items, is slow and repeated for every benchmark. abstract: Abstract Accurate stellar ages are fundamental to interpreting the evolutionary histories of habitable zone (HZ) planets. Because stellar luminosity evolves over time, HZ boundaries migrate outward, meaning that present-day HZ planets may have experienced different irradiation environments earlier in their evolution. abstract: As LLM capabilities advance, agents are tackling increasingly complex tasks over longer horizons. abstract: Sundarban deltaic ecosystem is highly vulnerable to environmental degradation and livelihood insecurity related to weaknesses in ecological conditions and dependence on natural resources. The study examines the impact of the air, water, soil and acoustic quality variables in Gosaba block on livelihood dynamics and sustainable development of the region. title: U-Net-based time-series mapping of tidal flat areas and carbon sink variations under fluctuating tidal levels
abstract: Tidal flats are crucial for carbon storage but are threatened by human activities. Satellite remote sensing data and deep learning methods help extrapolate field-based carbon measurements to broader spatial and temporal scales. However, inconsistent tidal heights during satellite image acquisition can bias carbon sink estimates. This study employed a U-Net model to map tidal flat areas and estimate their organic carbon sequestration rates from 2016 to 2024 in Seocheon, South Korea. title: Determination of Heavy Metal Pollution in Agricultural Soils of Maden Complex (Elazığ), Türkiye
abstract: Increased concentrations of metals in the soil can be harmful to human health and ecosystems. This study evaluated the amounts of As, Ni, Co, Cu, Cr, Pb, Zn, and Mn in 20 soil samples to identify potential ecological concerns and sources of heavy metal contamination in the soils adjacent to the Maden Complex. abstract: China’s fisheries economy has long faced multiple external shocks, and enhancing its resilience is crucial to achieving sustainable development. title: Mapping and dynamic monitoring of desertification on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau using surface Albedo and Solar-Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence
abstract: Desertification poses a significant threat to humanity's long-term survival and sustainable development. In this study, four types of 2D desertification assessment models were created by integrating surface albedo with four vegetation-related indicators: NDVI, MSAVI, EVI, and solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF). abstract: ABSTRACT The widespread application of fiber‐reinforced polymers (FRP) in engineering is primarily attributed to their superior durability compared to traditional materials. However, under prolonged exposure to harsh service environments, the material inevitably undergoes progressive degradation. abstract: Abstract Combinations of seasonal Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) metrics that serve as proxies for aboveground biomass, primary productivity, and phenology can be used to define Ecosystem Functional Types (EFTs), discrete areas with similar carbon gain dynamics. abstract: Abstract Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) satellite platforms and quantum‐optical sensing technologies may provide new observation approaches for improving Earth's static gravity field models. abstract: Abstract At least eight species of pangolins, or “scaley anteaters,” are extant today. All are classified as vulnerable, endangered or critically endangered, with the most significant threat coming from the illegal trade in pangolin scales. Radiocarbon analysis is now frequently used help monitor and understand the illegal trade of ivory and rhino horn, and to understand the biology and ecology of certain species. title: Tree-ring-anchored analog reconstruction of daily climate distributions from instrumental data with Bayesian distributional regression: Application to the European Alps
abstract: Daily to seasonal weather information remains rare in Quaternary science, because proxy archives typically resolve only seasonal or annual means. Yet climate is felt at daily timescales, through frost, snowfall, wind and precipitation. Here a framework of Bayesian Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape is presented that anchors a modern day-of-year marginal climatology to a proxy-reconstructed seasonal mean, two millennia into the past. title: Relationship between land-use change and flow patterns: a duration curve analysis in the Babahoyo River basin, Ecuador
abstract: Anthropogenic land use and land cover changes alter watershed hydrological processes by modifying the partitioning of precipitation into evapotranspiration, infiltration, and surface runoff. title: Dynamic and reversible bonds in polymeric membrane fabrication: towards recyclability-by-design
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable separation technologies has intensified interest in polymeric membranes due to their energy efficiency and versatility. However, many conventional membranes are fabricated from permanently crosslinked or non-degradable polymers, limiting their recyclability and contributing to environmental waste. In this review, the integration of dynamic bonds into membrane materials is explored, focusing on their potential to enable reprocessability, repairability and recyclability. abstract: Abstract In complex industrial environments, single monitoring signals, limited labeled data, and varying operating conditions often lead to low accuracy and poor generalization in cross-domain fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. To address these issues, a multi-channel information fusion with adaptive weighting network (MIFAWN) is proposed in this paper. abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD), acid rock drainage (ARD), and related acidic or metalliferous mine waters remain among the most persistent liabilities of sulfide-bearing mining because oxidation, hydrologic transport, secondary-mineral reactions, and legacy infrastructure can sustain contaminant release for decades after extraction ceases. abstract: Abstract The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG) underscores the need for eliminating hunger, improving nutrition, and promoting sustainable agriculture. For achieving SDG2, it is critical to address several factors such as agricultural production, groundwater depletion, and glacier decline under climate change. title: Fabrication and characterisation of biomimetic porous materials using diffusion-generated images and additive manufacturing
abstract: Biological porous materials exhibit complex architectures that are challenging to design using conventional modelling approaches. This study presents a reproducible workflow that integrates prompt-driven diffusion image generation with additive manufacturing to fabricate biomimetic porous polymer structures. abstract: Surface texture is a key functional property of metallic substrates and surface treatments. In industrial metrology, surface roughness is traditionally characterized by contact methods, such as stylus profilometry, standardized by ISO 4287. However, in cultural heritage applications, direct contact measurements may be unsuitable for delicate and heterogeneous surfaces, while non-contact optical profilometry is often not readily available for routine investigations. abstract: Abstract. Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas, and emissions from wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) represent a significant and highly variable source. title: Uncovering rainfall dynamics in Pernambuco, Brazil, through innovative polygon trend analysis
abstract: Abstract This study applied the Innovative Polygon Trend Analysis (IPTA) and the Trend Polygon Star Concept (TPSC) to high-resolution precipitation records (1961–2022) across Pernambuco, Brazil, to assess the spatial variability of monthly rainfall trends and transitions. Monthly precipitation totals derived from 820 BR-DWGD grid cells were analyzed to characterize long-term changes in rainfall patterns across the semiarid Sertão, humid Zona da Mata, and transitional Agreste regions. abstract: Construction-noise propagation models are typically formulated and validated outdoors, under free-field (FF) conditions, and for a single temporal noise pattern (most often impulsive pile-driving noise). abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as ubiquitous contaminants in the environment. Herein, laser-assisted micropyrolysis flowing atmospheric pressure afterglow high-resolution mass spectrometry (LAMP FAPA MS) is developed toward direct imaging of single-particle MPs collected on filters. abstract: ABSTRACT This study reports the design and synthesis of a novel amide‐functionalized monofunctional benzoxazine (TaPBA) and its incorporation into epoxy resin to develop high‐performance thermosetting networks with significantly enhanced overall properties. abstract: Many important plant diseases are caused by airborne spores. abstract: Architecture has long been regarded as a powerful medium through which societies express their values, priorities, and historical narratives. This study examined the architectural design of the Rivers State Government House, exploring how socio-economic and demographic factors influence its structure and symbolism. abstract: Autonomous docking of miniature unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) requires compact, low-cost, and robust sensing for estimating angles within short ranges. abstract: Boat tractors are essential for wetland mechanization, but their high cost and the added investment for semi-autonomous navigation raise financial viability concerns for smallholders farming less than 2 ha/year. This study compares manual versus GPS-integrated semi-autonomous boat tractor operation in shallow wetland conditions. abstract: : Satellite thermal infrared (TIR) data are essential for remote sensing of energy exchange processes at the Earth-atmosphere interface. Current satellite sensors are subject to a trade-off between spatial resolution and temporal coverage. Daily TIR observations from MODIS and VIIRS are limited to coarse spatial resolutions of ∼400–1000 m, whereas higher-resolution Landsat TIRS observations (∼100 m) provide infrequent temporal coverage (∼8 days). Downscaling methods that correlate TIR imagery with higher-resolution multispectral data can improve the availability of fine-scale TIR observations.

abstract: Geblek is a traditional cassava-based snack from Kulon Progo, Yogyakarta, that generally has limited nutritional value because of its relatively simple ingredient composition. Ulva sp., a green seaweed, contains macro- and micronutrients, antioxidants, and other bioactive compounds, making it a potential functional food ingredient. abstract: Intact tropical forests store high amounts of carbon biomass, but this long-stored carbon has not been widely quantified at the regional scale. This study integrates multi-source remote sensing data and Random Forest (RF) to model above- and below-ground biomass carbon (AGBC and BGBC) in intact forests across Southeast Asia from 2000 to 2020. abstract: The burgeoning market for heavy-cargo transportation poses an increasing challenge to the normal use of highway bridges. This study investigates the vehicle-bridge coupled dynamic response of a twin-tower three-span cable-stayed bridge under the load of heavy-cargo transportation by employing the holistic solution method and the direct integration method. abstract: Drought is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon that includes meteorological, agricultural, hydrological, and socio-economic components. abstract: Abstract We examine the key challenges associated with insuring climate-related risks in the context of a changing climate. abstract: Calculating net solar radiation (Rn) is of great importance in various fields, including agriculture, the environment, and industry. title: Tracking hydrological drought propagation in river networks: an event-based framework
abstract: Hydrological droughts are dynamic phenomena that evolve across space and time, propagating through river networks under the influence of climatic forcing, catchment properties, and human regulation. Despite substantial progress in drought research, most existing approaches rely on aggregated indicators or statistical relationships, limiting their ability to explicitly characterise how individual drought events propagate within connected river systems. This study introduces a novel event-based framework to analyse the spatiotemporal propagation of hydrological droughts along river networks. The

title: Integrated analysis of nuclear safety, security and physical protection systems: A comparative evaluation of nuclear terrorism risks
abstract: This study examines nuclear safety and nuclear security within an integrated framework, systematically analysing the functional distinctions and common denominators of these fields. The design processes of physical protection systems (PPS), layered defence architecture, domestically developed analytical software tools and risk assessment models are evaluated through a literature synthesis methodology. title: Spectral sensitivity-adversarial MixUp approach for the remaining useful life prediction of bearings across operating conditions with limited data
abstract: Abstract An accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings is crucial in industrial systems. However, the scarcity of labeled degradation data and heterogeneity of data distributions are known to lower the prediction accuracy and generalization capability of model. To address these issues, a spectral sensitivity-adversarial MixUp method is proposed for predicting the RUL of rolling bearings under different operating conditions with limited data. title: Self‐Healing Pd(II) Cage Metallogels for Iodine Capture in Water and Heterogeneous Photocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Adaptive multifunctional systems that integrate responsiveness, environmental remediation, and catalysis within a single platform remain exceptionally rare. Herein, two carbazole‐derived metal‐organic cages (MOCs) were constructed through coordination‐driven self‐assembly and subsequently transformed into fibrous metallogels ( MOC1G and MOC2G ) in mixed DMSO/H 2 O media through cooperative π−π stacking and dynamic supramolecular interactions. The resulting metallogels display reversible gel−sol transitions, interconnected nanofibrous architectures, and pronounced viscoelastic behavior

title: Modeling the impact of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation on the dynamics of dengue outbreaks in Argentina between 2018 and 2024
abstract: Background Dengue fever has become an epidemiological concern worldwide, with 531,617 cases reported in Argentina during the 2023–2024 season. The El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon has been linked to changes in dengue dynamics. This study assessed the relationships among ENSO, local climatic variables, and dengue outbreaks in Argentina from 2018 to 2024. Methods A nationwide spatiotemporal analysis was conducted using dengue cases and monthly mean temperature, relative humidity, and rainfall. title: Analysis of Enrichment-Controlling Factors and Seismic Prediction of Gas-Rich Zones in Tight Sandstone Gas Reservoirs: A Case Study from the Second Member of the Qianfoya Formation in Bazhong Area, Sichuan Basin
abstract: Abstract The Qianfoya Formation in the Bazhong area of the Sichuan Basin comprises a typical tight sandstone formation characterized by low porosity, low permeability, and strong reservoir heterogeneity. Effective reservoirs in this region are relatively thin, and seismic responses between gas-bearing layers and dry layers differ only slightly. These geological complexities create substantial challenges for predicting tight sandstone reservoirs and gas-rich zones, which necessitate targeted and effective geological and geophysical prediction research. title: The past, present, future and applications of Canada’s analog seismic data
abstract: Canada has been seismologically instrumented for more than one hundred twenty-five years. Analog instruments were first deployed in Canada in 1897 and dominated seismic monitoring for almost a century until they were replaced by digital instruments, first deployed in the late 1970s in Canada. Although many analog seismograms have been lost, approximately one million remain. These records contain a wealth of data about earthquakes, explosions and many other phenomena. title: A unified pipeline for traffic sign detection using resolution aware dataset reduction
abstract: Abstract Robust traffic sign detection is an important factor of safe autonomous driving, allowing vehicles to accurately interpret and comply with dynamic road regulations. However, real world deployment remains heavily challenged by distant, extra-small signs, as well as partial occlusions from trees, structures, or other vehicles. While optimizing training datasets through size reduction can dramatically lower computational overhead and storage footprints, conventional pruning methods often discard critical spatial features, severely degrading model accuracy. title: Water Quality Improvements and Hydrogeomorphic Change Over 20 Years Contributed to Macrophyte Community Recovery in the Upper Mississippi River
abstract: Several large rivers across the globe have recently undergone noticeable improvements to water quality. Yet, the cascading ecological consequences for aquatic life, including macrophytes, are largely unknown, owing to the lack of suitable long-term data and the difficulty of modelling community-level responses. Our study leveraged multiple big datasets from 1998 to 2019 within a 400-km stretch of the Upper Mississippi River in the United States, which experienced major changes to hydrogeomorphology, water quality, and climate during the 22-year study. title: Soil Spatial Distribution Analysis as a Method for Optimal Land Management
abstract: To effectively manage agricultural fields and select suitable methods for field operations, it is essential to have a basic understanding or access to a database specific to that area. A field study was conducted in the Abu Ghraib area, west of Baghdad, Iraq, to ​​map the spatial distribution of soil properties. Forty-seven soil samples were randomly collected from the area based on land use diversity. title: Eccentric Compression Behavior of Geopolymer Concrete-Filled Stainless Steel and Carbon Steel Tube Stub Columns
abstract: This paper presents an experimental investigation of the structural performance of circular geopolymer concrete-filled stainless steel and carbon steel tube stub columns subjected to combined compression and bending. A total of eight stub columns were tested under eccentric compression, consisting of four geopolymer concrete-filled stainless steel (GCFSST) specimens and four geopolymer concrete-filled carbon steel tube (GCFST) specimens. title: Protecting Ports using Range-Free Triangulated Sensor Networks: A Case Study
abstract: Range-free wireless sensor networks rely on sensors that detect only the bearing of an incoming signal, so that localizing a transmitter requires simultaneous detection by at least three sensors, a condition known as triangulated coverage. This paper extends a previously developed geospatial computational framework with a formal treatment of sensor activation and applies it to the protection of the port of Thessaloniki, Greece. title: Ultraviolet Photocatalytic Treatment of Petroleum Refinery Wastewater: A Case Study of Azzawiya Refinery, Libya
abstract: Abstract Petroleum refinery wastewater contains complex mixtures of refractory organic and inorganic contaminants that are difficult to remove using conventional treatment technologies. This study investigated the feasibility of ultraviolet (UV)-assisted photocatalytic oxidation using zinc oxide (ZnO) as a photocatalyst for the treatment of wastewater collected from the Azzawiya Oil Refinery, Libya. title: Blue-Green-Grey Infrastructure for Urban Carbon Reduction and Heat Resilience: A Review of Mechanisms, Methods, and Assessment Challenges
abstract: Urban blue-green-grey infrastructure (BGGI) is increasingly discussed as a strategy for reducing carbon emissions and improving heat resilience, but evidence on its mechanisms and assessment methods remains fragmented. This review synthesizes BGGI studies retrieved from Web of Science and ScienceDirect, focusing on carbon reduction pathways, analytical approaches and unresolved assessment challenges. The review distinguishes direct carbon storage and sequestration in blue-green components from operational emission reduction linked to microclimate regulation and changes in building energy deman

title: Iran’s nuclear retrenchment, 1977–1980: the unravelling of US-Iran nuclear cooperation
abstract: In August 1978, as protests swept Iran, a quieter crisis unfolded within Prime Minister Jamshid Amuzegar’s government. A high-level commission recommended suspending Iran’s nuclear programme, then among the most ambitious in the developing world. This article argues that Iran’s nuclear retrenchment began not with the 1979 revolution but months earlier, driven by fiscal crisis, the erosion of institutional autonomy at the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, and the withdrawal of Western suppliers during the final years of the Pahlavi monarchy. title: Innovative performance indicators for effective Quality, Safety, and Environment management in oil drilling operations
abstract: Abstract Effective management of Quality, Safety, and Environment (QSE) performance is critical in high-risk oil drilling operations. Despite extensive research on generic Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) frameworks, there remains limited guidance on context-specific, operationally validated methodologies that integrate leading and lagging indicators within unified QSE systems for drilling operations.
