title: Rethinking transmission line health indices under rising lightning activity
abstract: Health and condition indices (HI and CI), based primarily on physical inspections, are fundamental in asset management but show severe limitations in regions with high lightning activity. In a 230 kV transmission line (TL) in Colombia, failure rates vastly exceeded design Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) despite assets being classified in "good condition", evidencing the inadequacy of static evaluations. title: Quantifying the Net Environmental Benefits of Food-Grade Recycled PET in Cameroon: Application of the Circular Footprint Formula to Mid-Scale Mechanical Recycling
abstract: Mechanical recycling is often assumed, rather than demonstrated, to deliver a net environmental benefit relative to virgin plastic production, particularly in Sub-Saharan African contexts where primary process data are scarce. This study quantifies that benefit for food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) produced at mid-scale in Cameroon, using the European Commission’s Circular Footprint Formula (CFF) applied to a gate-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA; ISO 14040/14044) of the Opur and Supermont mineral-water bottle streams recycled at Ecogreen Sarl, Douala. title: Multi-frequency acoustic metasurface carpet cloak based on groove structural unit
abstract: This paper presents a multi-frequency acoustic metasurface carpet cloak (AMCC) composed of groove-structured units. These structural units function as multi-frequency metasurfaces and operate effectively at both the fundamental and harmonic frequencies. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed AMCC can effectively cloak a triangular object, with a broad operational bandwidth ranging from 3110 to 3750 Hz near the fundamental frequency. title: Paying Attention to the Earth: The Development of Ecological Poetics in Jorie Graham's Materialism
abstract: The article examines Jorie Graham’s 1993 collection, Materialism, as a pivotal transitional moment in the development of her ecopoetics. It argues that the collection marks a discernible shift from the central experiences of virtuality and alienation characterised in Region of Unlikeness (1991) towards a decisive and sustained engagement with physical matter. title: Reusing Chemically Recycled Cross-Linked Matrix from Succinic Acid–Epoxidized Linseed Oil
abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of thermoset resin circularity, the solvolyzed products from biobased succinic acid/epoxidized linseed oil (ELO) cross-linked resin were valorized into new starting materials for the preparation of recycled cross-linked systems. First, the recycled product was characterized by using spectroscopy and chromatography techniques (FT-IR and LC-MS), providing insights into their molecular composition. title: Assessment of intraspecific skull variation in the Campanian baenid turtle Plesiobaena antiqua
abstract: Baenids are freshwater paracryptodiran turtles with a fossil record ranging from the Early Cretaceous to the Eocene. The baenid Plesiobaena antiqua is the most common turtle in the Campanian (Late Cretaceous) Dinosaur Park Formation in Canada, but the apparent intraspecific variation remains poorly understood. We apply micro-computed tomography scanning technology (μCT scanning) and bone-by-bone segmentation to a sample of four crania and three mandibles representing different size classes. title: Advances in Municipal Solid Waste Management in Nigeria: A Review
abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) are unwanted or undesirable products obtained from food-scraps, papers, plastics, electronic waste, metals, glass and other used materials from our day to day domestic, institutional and industrial activities which are discharged into the environment. However, as the global production of MSW increases due to increase in population, economic and industrial advancement and urbanization in Nigeria, MSW has become a global concern due to its persistence in the environment, causing various issues like climatic change, global warming and contamination of soil, air and wat

title: Assessing Climatic Vulnerability for Yellow-eyed Pigeon (Columba eversmanni) in India's Arid Region
abstract: Columba eversmanni, commonly known as the Yellow-eyed Pigeon, is a species with a limit-ed geographical distribution. It breeds in Central Asia and it moves toward South Asia during winters. The species faces significant threats from human activities and climate change. In this study, we used the MaxEnt model to assess the current and potential future distri-bution of the species based on climatic variables across its non-breeding range in the arid region of Rajasthan, India. title: Liberation-controlled beneficiation of Moroccan andalusite ore through particle size optimization and integrated gravity–magnetic separation
abstract: The beneficiation efficiency of andalusite ores is strongly governed by particle size because of its effect on mineral liberation and separation selectivity. In this study, the effect of particle size on the upgrading performance of an andalusite ore from the Moroccan Sidi Bou-Othmane deposit was investigated using shaking table gravity concentration followed by dry high-intensity magnetic separation. title: An open-access workflow combining climate model projections with epidemiological frameworks to assess air quality mortality
abstract: Surface-level air pollution is a major source of human mortality worldwide, and future climate change is expected to alter concentrations of pollutants such as ozone and particulate matter. Estimating the health burden of these changes requires combining climate model projections with epidemiological frameworks, such as those developed in the Global Burden of Disease (GBD). However, significant barriers hinder this integration. Climate model outputs differ from health metrics in spatial resolution, temporal aggregation, and pollutant metrics. title: Technoeconomic and Life Cycle Analyses of the Co-production of Olefins, Aromatics, and Alkanes Using Microwave-Assisted Conversion of Polypropylene Plastic Waste
abstract: Abstract There is a growing interest in utilizing plastic waste to produce olefins and aromatics, which serve as essential building blocks for polyolefin production. In this paper, a novel microwave-assisted catalytic process is developed for converting polypropylene plastic waste into propylene, with simultaneous co-production of ethylene, aromatics, and alkanes, thereby closing the material loop by returning end-of-life plastic waste back into the petrochemical value chain as a high-value chemical feedstock, a key principle of the circular economy. title: Comparing Remotely Sensed and Weather Station Measured Rainfall Data for Flood Prediction in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme rainfall events frequently trigger flash floods, which cause widespread damage to ecosystems, infrastructure, and livelihoods. Accurate rainfall estimation is therefore essential for flood modeling and early warning systems. This study assessed the performance of the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) and the Global Precipitation Measurement Integrated Multi‐Satellite Retrievals for GPM (GPM‐IMERG) against weather station rainfall observations collected across KwaZulu‐Natal, South Africa, between 2000 and 2022. title: Fish locomotor dynamics quantified using multiple inertial measurement units
abstract: Abstract Animals exhibit a diversity of locomotor behaviours that vary with body shape, ontogeny, motivation and environment. Documenting these behaviours often relies on recording videos of animals in controlled conditions displaying stereotyped behaviours. By contrast, animal-borne motion sensing data loggers can document diverse behaviours of animals in their natural environment. Traditionally, one data logger is used to infer body dynamics; however, a single location presents an incomplete picture of body movement. title: Geotechnical parameters estimation using electrical resistivity tomography data: Case study of Jorf Lasfar, western Morocco

title: Beyond resilience: engineering antifragility and hazard mitigation in safety–critical systems using a stress–strain model
abstract: Abstract Traditional resilience engineering struggles with modern safety–critical systems operating under extreme uncertainty. Antifragility, the ability to gain from systemic stressors and near-misses, remains a philosophical ideal, lacking a rigorous, quantitative framework for engineering. The Systemic Stress–Strain Model (SSM) is a quantitative framework that operationalizes antifragility by analogy to material science. title: Improving the Quality of Chest X-rays Through Adaptive Image Enhancement Filters (ACEF)
abstract: Respiratory diseases are difficult to identify due to picture distortion, hence chest X-rays are commonly used to diagnose lung ailments, particularly in low-light settings. Raw radiographs frequently exhibit issues such as insufficient contrast, picture distortion, and poor tissue border definition, all of which can have a negative impact on radiographic accuracy, especially in low light. This paper describes the Adaptive Chest Enhancement Filter (ACEF), a three-stage preprocessing filter that combines image decongestion, lung-specific contrast enhancement, and tissue boundary preservation. title: Bayesian Analysis of Seasonal and Periodic Time Series: Evidence from Nigerian Monthly Rainfall, 1981–2024
abstract: Monthly rainfall in Nigeria exhibits pronounced annual seasonality, season-dependent variability, and changes in temporal dependence that may not be adequately represented by a single fixed-parameter model. This study presents a Bayesian modelling framework for monthly rainfall records from 37 Nigerian Meteorological Agency stations spanning January 1981 to December 2024, a 44-year period comprising 528 monthly values per station. title: Reconstructing Ancient Copper Smelting Practices in the Eastern Part of the Srednogorie Metallogenic Zone (SE Bulgaria) Using Slag Mineralogy and Chemistry
abstract: This study reconstructs the smelting conditions of ancient copper production in the eastern Srednogorie metallogenic zone (SE Bulgaria) based on the mineralogical and chemical composition of archaeological slags. Slag samples from three ore fields were investigated: Rosen (Propadnala Voda, Korucheshme and Rosen deposits, and Atiya metallurgical centre), Zidarovo (Krushevets archaeological site) and St. Ilia (Boyadzhik archaeological site). title: Findings on the efficacy of sonic debridement in chronic wound management – a case series
abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate the physiological rationale, mechanism of action, and emerging clinical evidence supporting sonic debridement as an adjunctive approach for wound hygiene and maintenance debridement in chronic wound management. METHODS A structured review of wound healing principles, biofilm biology, and current debridement modalities was performed alongside analysis of clinical observations and case series data using a sonic debridement device. title: A review of research on programmable airburst less-lethal munitions
abstract: As the demand for less-lethal response operations and their application in complex scenarios increases, the limitations of conventional less-lethal munitions in terms of strike accuracy, effective coverage, safety and controllability have become increasingly apparent. Programmable airburst less-lethal munitions have garnered attention due to their ability to detonate in a preset airspace and provide a controllable dispersal footprint. title: Bauxite Residue (Red Mud) from the Bayer Process: A Critical Review of Management, Safe Storage, Valorization, Critical-Metal Recovery, and Industrial Integration
abstract: Bauxite residue (BR), commonly termed red mud, is the strongly alkaline, fine-grained solid generated during Bayer alumina refining. This critical review synthesizes a primary contemporary corpus of 145 publications from January 2020 to 23 September 2026, supplemented by a small set of pre-2020 foundational sources used only for historical and mechanistic context, and evaluates BR as an integrated management-and-resource system rather than an isolated waste stream. title: Soils sentinels: A step towards harmonisation of microbial parameters in European initiatives
abstract: Soil health is a critical component of agroecosystems, supporting plant growth, nutrient cycling, and ecosystem services. However, soil is a non-renewable resource on human timescales, and its degradation poses significant challenges for sustainable agriculture. Despite numerous European initiatives (e.g., LUCAS, EcoFINDERS, EXCALIBUR, SHARInG-MeD, among others), there remains a lack of consensus on standardized soil health indicators, particularly regarding microbiological parameters. title: Physics-informed cross-domain image synthesis for microalgae growth phase classification in turbid media
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based classification of microalgae growth phases in Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) requires representative training images. However, the available public data originate from a water medium with characteristics that differ from those of the POME. Existing methods apply uniform weighting to each channel and are inconsistent with light absorption in turbid media, leading to the collapse of the chromatic margin between the growth phases. Thus, these methods can only meet the global distribution (C1) but fail to simultaneously maintain inter-phase discriminability (C2).

title: Patterns, drivers, and consequences of narrow-ranged species loss for angiosperm functional diversity across East Eurasia
abstract: ABSTRACT Functional diversity links species traits to ecosystem functioning, yet its large-scale patterns and vulnerability to species loss remain poorly understood. Here, we assembled a comprehensive distribution and trait dataset of all angiosperms across East Eurasia and investigated geographic patterns of functional diversity represented by the richness (FR) and structure (standardized effect size of FR, sesFR) of functional traits, the environmental drivers underlying these patterns, and the potential consequences of losing narrow-ranged species. title: Simplified analysis of concentrically loaded reinforced concrete columns
abstract: Abstract Reinforced concrete columns subjected to concentric and eccentric compression loads are typically treated in an identical manner, taking into account both the imperfect shape, creep, and the second order effects, as described for example in fib Model Code 2020 and Eurocode 2. For concentrically loaded steel or timber columns and masonry walls simplified analyses are available, which are based on the cross‐sectional load bearing capacity reduced by a factor, which depends primarily on the slenderness. title: Exploring the gender wage gap in Indian agriculture—an interaction-based panel regression approach
abstract: This study investigates the gender wage disparities in Indian agriculture utilizing a pseudo-panel dataset and an interaction-based panel regression framework. The study seeks to examine the association of gender on agricultural wages over the years, especially in response to the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), which was enacted in 2005. title: Avaliação de modelos digitais de altura da vegetação derivados de dados LiDAR
abstract: Os Modelos Digitais de Altura (MDA) da vegetação são gerados pela subtração entre o Modelo Digital de Superfície (MDS) e o Modelo Digital de Terreno (MDT), que podem ser construídos pela interpolação das coordenadas tridimensionais obtidas por sistemas de perfilamento a laser (LiDAR). No entanto, os modelos interpolados podem apresentar erros provenientes tanto da topografia quanto do tipo de interpolador utilizado. title: Hybrid GA-DQN for opportunistic cluster head selection and routing in resource constraint Internet of Things networks
abstract: Abstract Energy efficiency and reliable data transmission are two important challenges in Internet of Things (IoT) networks because of the limited energy resources of sensor nodes and their dynamic nature. Accordingly, this research develops a Genetic Algorithm Deep Q-Network (GA-DQN) based hybrid framework for intelligent cluster head selection and adaptive IoT Network routing to counter these threats. title: Assessment of seismic velocity changes from ambient noise single-station cross-component analysis in Altamira, Brazil
abstract: Methods capable of monitoring groundwater systems are essential to support decisions and resource management. In recent years, techniques based on the analysis of ambient seismic noise have consolidated passive seismic methods as valuable monitoring tools. This work focuses on a single-station cross-component analysis based on Ambient Noise Seismic Interferometry and Coda Wave Interferometry to quantify seismic velocity variations ( δν/ν ) between 2014 and 2016 near the city of Altamira and the Belo Monte hydroelectric complex, located in the Xingu River Basin in Brazil. title: The Large Deviation Principle for the Stochastic 3D Primitive Equations with Transport Noise
abstract: Abstract We prove the small-noise large deviation principle for the three-dimensional primitive equations with transport noise and turbulent pressure. Transport noise is important for geophysical fluid dynamics applications, as it takes into account the effect of small scales on the large scale dynamics. The main mathematical challenge is that we allow for the transport noise to act on the full horizontal velocity, therefore leading to a non-trivial turbulent pressure, which requires an involved analysis to obtain the necessary energy bounds. Both Stratonovich and Itô noise are treated.

title: Groundwater Overdraft and Climate-Driven Land Subsidence in the Sulaimani-Sharazoor Basin, Iraq: Insights from InSAR Techniques

title: Timely composition monitoring in the distillation process of saline-organic ternary mixtures: A case study for water–NaCl–ethanol during spray flash vacuum distillation
abstract: Determination of the ternary composition in a multicomponent distillation is critical for process control and system operation. However, monitoring saline-organic solutions (Water-NaCl-Ethanol) remains a challenge due to the non-linear interference between ionic conductivity and organic solvent concentration. Specifically, there is a “conductivity suppression” phenomenon in which increasing ethanol concentration significantly reduces the solution's electrical conductivity, rendering standard salinity probes ineffective. title: Coordination ring-opening transamidation copolymerization of cyclic lactones and lactams towards circular and biodegradable poly(ester amide) adhesives
abstract: Abstract The efficient synthesis of poly(ester amide)s (PEAs), which combine polyamide-like mechanical strength with polyester-like biodegradability, has remained a longstanding challenge. Herein, we introduce a unique coordination ring-opening transamidation copolymerization (CROTCP) mediated by a tetranuclear titanium catalyst. This reaction allows for the copolymerization of ε-caprolactone and ε-caprolactam under mild conditions, thereby overcoming the high-temperature and side-reaction issues associated with conventional lactam polymerization. title: Projected climate extremes and demographic change provide a spatial context for linguistic vulnerability in Multilingual Yunnan
abstract: Abstract Climate change may reshape the demographic and socioeconomic conditions under which minority languages are maintained, although projected population change alone cannot demonstrate migration, language shift, or language loss. Focusing on multi-ethnic and multilingual Yunnan, China, this study integrates outputs from eight CMIP6 climate models with 1-km gridded demographic projection of resident population to examine changes in very-wet-day precipitation (R95p), warm-day frequency (TX90p), consecutive dry days (CDD), and resident population from 2020 to 2100 under the SSP5–8.5 scenario

abstract: Fine-grained air quality monitoring is critical for assessing personal exposure to air pollution in indoor micro-environments; however, dedicated air quality sensors are costly and offer limited spatial coverage. In this work, we present AirComm , a smartphone-based air quality sensing system that requires no additional hardware. abstract: Real-world situations require DSRC-based vehicular ad hoc networks that employ sensor fusion and perception systems. This paper presents a new approach to DOA estimation for autonomous vehicles, using a nested sensor array and the Cuckoo Search (CS) Algorithm. title: Hydrochemical Analysis and Associated Health Risk Assessment of Groundwater Quality of Hisar District of Haryana, India
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater is a major drinking water resource supporting nearly half of the world's population but its quality is being compromised by various anthropogenic factors. This study provides an in‐depth analysis of groundwater quality in Hisar district, Haryana, India by integrating hydrogeochemical parameters and advanced analytical techniques. It evaluates the groundwater quality using samples collected from 76 locations (wells, tube wells, and hand pumps) in the pre‐monsoon season. abstract: Mechanically scanned photoacoustic tomography (PAT) provides high detection sensitivity and flexible system configurations, but its application to dynamic quantitative imaging is limited by the trade-off between temporal resolution and spatial sampling density. title: Real-time heuristic evacuation pathfinding algorithm for flood avoidance
abstract: Floods rank among the world’s most devastating annual disasters in terms of casualties and economic losses, making evacuation route planning crucial for mitigating flood risks. This study proposes a Real-time Heuristic Flood Evacuation Path Planning Algorithm (RHEPFA) based on dynamic flood simulations using the ANUGA 2D model. abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of gross primary production (GPP), the mass of carbon fixed by plants through photosynthesis, and long‐term GPP trends is essential for monitoring ecosystems, analyzing the carbon cycle, and evaluating biosphere models. abstract: Abstract Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation is a core technology in array signal processing, which is widely applied in radar, communications and sonar systems. Traditional subspace methods suffer from poor performance under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and limited snapshots, while Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) methods have high computational complexity. title: The impact of compound soil conditioner on the physicochemical properties of acidic farmland soil in Sichuan Province, China

abstract: Abstract Valve leakage in offshore pipelines threatens operational safety, while acoustic-emission (AE)-based identification remains difficult because leakage signals are non-stationary and sensitive to environmental interference. This study proposes BACNet, a lightweight auditory-inspired network for the closed-set identification of ten leaking valves and one no-leak condition. title: Spatial zoning of rural marginalization under environmental stress using geographic information systems and system dynamics
abstract: Abstract The persistence of regional development inequalities has highlighted the necessity of using dynamic models that encompass the multidimensional nature of rural isolation. Traditional spatial planning frameworks often overlook the synergistic impacts of service deprivation and geological hazards on the phenomenon of marginalization. abstract: Abstract In 3D reverse time migration (RTM), high computational costs and massive storage requirements remain major challenges that are largely determined by the different imaging conditions. The cross-correlation imaging condition (CCIC) provides high imaging resolution but requires storing a large volume of source-wavefield data on the disk and subsequently reading these data back into the memory during imaging. abstract: Continuous eddy covariance measurements of carbon fluxes remain unknown for pine forests in the forest-steppe zone of European Russia, limiting our understanding of the seasonal dynamics of ecosystem carbon exchange. This study aimed to assess net ecosystem carbon exchange between the atmosphere and an old-growth pine forest in Usmansky Bor during the autumn–winter period of 2025–2026. abstract: Indonesia harbors extensive mangrove ecosystems with considerable untapped potential as sources of functional bioactive ingredients. Sonneratia caseolaris (L.) Engl., a mangrove species traditionally used in ethnomedicine, contains diverse polyphenolic compounds. abstract: This study aims to compare the performance of the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Adaptive Momentum Backpropagation (AMBP) models for predicting monthly rainfall in West Nusa Tenggara Province. The data used consists of monthly rainfall from the NASA POWER dataset for the period from January 1981 to December 2025. title: Assessing forest ecological sustainability through wavelet decomposition and stationarity tests: a comparative analysis of major forest product producers
abstract: Introduction Forest ecosystems are central to environmental sustainability, yet the persistence of forest-specific ecological conditions remains insufficiently explored, particularly across different time horizons. Existing research has predominantly examined CO₂ emissions and aggregate ecological footprint indicators, while relatively limited attention has been devoted to the stochastic properties and frequency-dependent persistence of forest ecological balance (FEB). title: Fish diversity reflects biological invasions and environmental change in highly urbanized Chinese river networks
abstract: Urban rivers, which provide essential ecosystem services and support significant biodiversity, are experiencing rapid species loss due to various anthropogenic stressors, yet they have received relatively limited research attention. In this study, we analyzed fish diversity and its relationship with environmental factors in northern Shenzhen, the third most populous city in China. title: Mechanisms of long-term degradation in plasticized PVDF pressure barriers under offshore service exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) is commonly used as a pressure sheath material in offshore flexible pipelines; however, there is limited experimental data from long-term service exposure. In this study, three PVDF layers recovered from a flexible riser after ten years of offshore operation were examined to understand the degradation mechanisms that occurred under field conditions. abstract: In recent decades, housing purchasing prices have outpaced incomes, increasing spatial inequalities and creating a growing challenge to homeownership. Despite housing markets being highly localised with most residential moves made at local scales, analyses of housing affordability have typically focused on national- and regional-level trends. abstract: ABSTRACT Frugivorous vertebrates, as seed dispersers and predators, play critical roles in forest ecosystem dynamics. abstract: Improving agricultural efficiency is central to the country's transition from output expansion toward higher-value, resource-efficient and climate-resilient production. This study develops an empirical framework for measuring provincial agricultural production efficiency using Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) and panel econometrics, while reporting the complete descriptive evidence that can be verified from the currently assembled National Statistics Office (NSO) dataset. abstract: Objectives The quality and safety of bottled drinking water are of growing concern in Yemen due to increasing dependence on groundwater resources and potential contamination by trace metals. This study presents an integrated secondary analysis of previously published inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) data to evaluate the concentrations of seven heavy metals (Hg, Cd, Cr, Ni, Al, Co, and Cu) in 27 bottled water brands marketed in Yemen, combining health risk assessment with multivariate statistical analysis. abstract: Accurate characterization of subsurface heterogeneity is essential for understanding groundwater flow and contaminant transport. However, the value of integrating multiple data and how it relates to heterogeneity requires further investigation. abstract: Red-Green-Blue (RGB) vision based supervised learning is demonstrated for the purpose of identifying subsurface groundwater seepage for low-cost and accurate inspection of dams and slope embankments using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). abstract: Pneumatic launch systems represent a critical technology for converting stored compressed gas energy into kinetic energy. While computationally efficient thermodynamic models are commonly used to analyze such systems, their simplified assumptions often obscure the complex flow dynamics that govern energy conversion and dissipation. title: Block-structured mesh generation for large rotations and translations
abstract: We present a novel approach for the block-structured meshing of moving domains with large translations and rotations, even supporting topology or connectivity changes during the simulation. The idea is based on different block-structures, each tailored to the geometry at different instances in time during the simulation. Each block-structure defines the topology with exact geometry definitions and grading information assigned; it serves as the basis for generating higher-order meshes. The key aspect is how changes in the block-structures are handled at selected instances during the simulation.

title: Embracing Zero Waste as a Critical Tool for Addressing Climate Change: A Cross‐National Analysis of Mitigation Evidence
abstract: Global waste generation has become an increasing environmental pressure of the twenty‐first century, with humanity now producing between 2.1 and 2.3 billion tons of municipal solid waste annually. Without intervention, this figure is projected to reach 3.8 billion tons by 2050. 1 The World Bank reports waste generation reached 2.56 billion tons in 2022—years ahead of projections—and could reach 3.86 billion tons by 2050 if trends continue. 2 The crisis is most severe in Sub‐Saharan Africa and South Asia, where waste is rising fastest and collection infrastructure is weakest.

abstract: Abstract RGB-Thermal (RGB-T) salient object detection localizes salient regions where appearance cues alone are insufficient, since thermal radiation stays informative under poor illumination. abstract: Passive buildings (PBs) offer substantial advantages in reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, making their promotion a strategic priority for China’s carbon goals. However, high upfront costs, unclear long-term benefits, and long payback periods hinder adoption. This study develops a Life-Cycle Incremental Cost-Benefit Model (LCICBM) covering design, construction, and operation. The model quantifies and monetizes economic, environmental, and social benefits. abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional villages are heritage settlements whose continuity depends on interactions among cultural practice, ecological condition and governance capacity. This study examined how cultural power and governance networks are associated with ecological resilience in nine traditional villages in Zhejiang Province, China. title: Thermal Shifts Dominate Single‐Gene Responses to Transcription‐Targeting Antibiotics
abstract: ABSTRACT Combined exposure to thermal and antibiotic stresses is ubiquitous. How cells adapt to these concurrent cues at the single‐gene level remains unresolved. Here, we show that in Escherichia coli , both cold and heat shock responses dominate antibiotic stress responses across multiple levels of physiology. title: Diversity and disparity in mammalian fossil assemblages of the John Day Formation, Oregon, USA
abstract: Abstract The John Day Formation offers a remarkably complete terrestrial record of Eocene-, Oligocene-, and Miocene-aged mammalian faunas in central Oregon. Sites in the John Day Formation have yielded numerous mammalian species spanning across many taxonomic orders, offering a unique opportunity to closely examine changes in mammalian diversity and disparity across a geographically constrained region. abstract: The Average Temperature Trends and rainfall patterns within Jere local government area of Kaduna State, Nigeria have been studied from 1989 to 2018. abstract: Heavy rainfall is a major driver of floods, flash floods, and landslides, significantly impacting lives, property, and infrastructure. These risks are intensifying under climate change, which increases both the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall events. This study analyzed the characteristics and assessed the risk of maximum daily cumulative rainfall in Thailand using the Generalized Extreme Value for the r-largest order statistics (GEVr) model. abstract: In humans, dietary intake is thought to be the main route of exposure to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Extreme climatic events (ECEs) are increasingly recognized as major drivers of insect declines, yet remain rarely incorporated into biodiversity projections. abstract: La regeneración natural es fundamental en la dinámica de los ecosistemas forestales y su comprensión contribuye al diseño de prácticas de conservación, restauración y silvicultura. title: A practical model and online tool to predict cover crop nitrogen content and carbon-to-nitrogen ratio via remote sensing
abstract: Abstract Purpose Estimations of cover crop (CC) nitrogen (N) content and carbon-to-nitrogen (C:N) ratio are crucial for guiding N fertilizer recommendations for subsequent cash crops, yet prediction tools that can be easily adopted by practitioners are lacking. This study aims to (1) develop models to predict CC N content and C:N ratio using Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalized Difference Red Edge Index (NDRE) from Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAV) and satellite imagery, combined with growing degree days (GDD, base 5 °C) and CC species; and (2) integrate the models develop

title: Insights into life cycle assessment and rapid removal of malachite green by biochar derived from shrimp shell and sheep manure
abstract: Malachite green (MG) contamination of water resources poses significant ecological and human-health risks, while the environmental sustainability of its treatment strategies has rarely been evaluated. This study addresses this critical gap by integrating the synthesis of hybrid biochar from sheep manure and shrimp shells at a 2:1 ratio for MG removal with a comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA). title: Economic Losses Associated With Tropical Cyclones in Mexico: A Two-stage Model
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) are among the primary drivers of disaster declarations in Mexico, causing substantial economic losses. This study assesses reported TC-related economic losses in Mexican states from (Funk 1980 ) to 2023 and identifies the hazard and socioeconomic determinants of both the probability of loss occurrence and loss magnitude. title: Assessment of compressive characteristics of coir fiber-reinforced concrete modified with wheat straw ash using predictive modeling
abstract: The growing demand for environmentally responsible construction materials requires reliable tools to predict the compressive strength of concrete incorporating agricultural waste and natural fibers. This study investigates the prediction of compressive strength of sustainable concrete incorporating wheat straw ash (WSA) and coir fiber (CF) using explainable ensemble machine learning. A database of 361 concrete mixtures was compiled from published experimental studies, considering cement, WSA, fine aggregate, coarse aggregate, water, superplasticizer, CF, and curing age as input variables. abstract: Abstract Multi-step deformable metamaterials usually exhibit a deficiency in auxetic behavior, which limits their potential for improving load-bearing capacity and energy absorption. In this study, a bi-material enhanced double-arrow honeycomb (EDAH) is proposed by integrating a multi-step deformation mechanism with a double-arrow honeycomb design. title: Unsupervised learning for detection of defects during machining of additively manufactured components
abstract: Detection of defects such as porosities is important in additive manufacturing to ensure the desired material properties. Most additively manufactured components require finish machining to achieve the desired surface finish and geometric tolerances. This paper presents an unsupervised machine learning approach using an autoencoder to detect defects during the machining of additively manufactured components. title: Study on Students' Exercise Load Monitoring in PE Classroom Based on the Fusion of FedAvg and Grey Relationship Analysis
abstract: Real time observation of students' exercise load is very important for scientific sports teaching and injury prevention. However, the traditional centralized monitoring paradigm faces significant privacy challenges when it processes highly sensitive physiological and biological characteristics. At the same time, existing federated learning algorithms often degrade global model performance due to "client drift" arising from Non-IID data caused by individual differences among students. title: Investigating the influence of brewery ingredient byproduct inclusion during the dry-aging process on beef strip steak attributes
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the influence of brewery ingredient inclusion during the dry-aging (DA) process on beef steak attributes. Loins ( N = 4; USDA Choice, 21d postmortem, previously frozen) were sectioned and equally, randomly assigned to treatments: conventional DA (CON), DA with Kviek yeast (BY1), DA with Saccharomyces yeast (BY2), DA with yellow koji (KM1), or DA with white koji (KM2). title: PhysioGraph transformer a multimodal physiological emotion recognition personality aware dynamic graph transformer
abstract: The key to affective computing is emotion recognition based on multimodal physiological and behavioral responses and aids in intelligent systems to monitor mental health, adapt human-computer interaction, and predict the intent of affectivity. Although the existing deep models show remarkable advances, most of them process modalities in isolation and do not consider causal, temporal, and individual specific mechanisms underlying the expression of emotions. title: Antibacterial and mechanical response of sustainable PLA/PHBH biodegradable bio-blends with optimized spherical nano-Cu content in MEX additive manufacturing
abstract: Greener yet multifunctional polymeric blends and their composites remain a strong industrial challenge regarding sustainability and ecological balance. Herein, Polylactic acid (PLA) and Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyhexanoate) (PHBH), two popular environmentally friendly biopolymers, are engaged to prepare an optimized blend. Spherical nano-Copper (Cu) was then introduced in various loads (1 wt. % - 5 wt. %.), to optimize the mechanical metrics and induce biocidal properties. title: The impact of logistics performance on economic growth: a comparative ARDL analysis for Turkiye and Poland
abstract: Transportation activities are among the most influential factors shaping economic growth and development. Since freight mobility and transport infrastructure play a strategic role in sustaining economic activity, understanding how different transport modes contribute to economic performance has become a critical research issue. title: Spacing Effects in Guided Vertical‐Axis Wind Turbine Arrays for Highway Energy Harvesting Under Multi‐Vehicle Wake Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Highway‐induced airflow generated by passing vehicles represents an underutilized source of localized renewable energy that can be harvested using vertical‐axis wind turbines (VAWTs). While prior studies have demonstrated the feasibility of single‐turbine configurations, the aerodynamic interaction between vehicle wakes and multi‐turbine arrays—particularly the role of inter‐turbine spacing—remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Concentrations of fine 2.5μm Aerosols particulate matter containing black carbon (soot) are considered to have significant harmful health effects, especially those resulting from the combustion of petroleum derivatives during crude oil extraction operations, whether for workers in the oil sector or citizens residing in nearby areas. The current study provides an assessment and calculation of particulate matter 2.5 concentrations in the Baba Industrial Area resulting from the emission of flares burning through extraction field operations. title: Endotoxins and Biological Implications—Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Endotoxins, also known as lipopolysaccharides (LPSs), are structural components of the outer membrane of Gram‐negative bacteria and some cyanobacteria. They are among the most potent pyrogens and remain a persistent challenge in environmental, occupational, and clinical settings. This review brings together current understanding of their structure, stability, and methods of detection, while also highlighting the main routes through which humans are exposed. title: Value of Innovation as a metric to drive technology development
abstract: Innovation characterizes industrial, economic, and societal development. Within the domain of the built environment, technological advancements are continuously pursued to enhance structural safety, functionality, and cost efficiency. At the same time, the challenges associated with ageing infrastructure and constrained resources necessitate the systematic development and effective diffusion of technologies, including those related to information systems, intervention strategies, and maintenance management. title: Municipal waste management, clean energy transition, and environmental performance: a CS-APQR analysis with governance moderation in OECD countries
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between environmental performance, municipal waste management and clean energy transition in OECD countries spanning period from 2000 to 2023, this relationship is moderated by green governance quality. The municipal waste management and clean energy transition indices are constructed using principal component analysis (PCA) based on multiple indicators. title: Uncertainty-aware reconstruction of full process maps in laser-directed energy deposition using scarce data
abstract: Abstract Accurate representation of bead geometry is essential for establishing reliable process-geometry relationships in laser-directed energy deposition (L-DED). In contrast to existing approaches that focus on constructing complete process maps within a single manufacturing process, this work leverages experimentally derived scalar bead descriptors (width, height, and area) from a source process to enable data-efficient reconstruction of process maps for a different target manufacturing process. title: Hydro-climatic extremes: trends, anomalies and implications for urban water management
abstract: ABSTRACT Assessing the trends and anomalies of hydro-climatic extremes for improving the urban water managment. Intensifying hydrological and climatic risks are threatening infrastructures and services; therefore, understanding anomalies in hydro-climatic extremes (HCE) is imperative for sustained infrastructure/services. This study investigates the dynamics of HCE and implications for urban water management, with a case of Pokhara Metropolis (Nepal). title: Mapeo del Índice de Aire y Salud por contaminación atmosférica de partículas finas PM2.5 en la Zona Metropolitana del Valle de Puebla
abstract: Se construyen mapas híbridos de índices de Aire y Salud (IAS) de partículas en suspensión menores a 2.5 micrómetros (PM2.5), de mediciones de la Red Estatal de Monitoreo Automática (REMA) y estimaciones basadas en datos satelitales del Servicio de Monitoreo Atmosférico de Copernicus (CAMS). Se estima el IAS para PM2.5 en zonas donde la REMA no tienen alcance empleando la información de CAMS, para describir la contaminación atmosférica en la zona de estudio. title: Directional policy alignment in water resources carrying capacity for sustainable city futures in drylands
abstract: Sustainable city futures in drylands are increasingly constrained by hard water resource limits under climate change, city expansion, and low-carbon transition. Water resources carrying capacity (WRCC) is not only an indicator of water security, but also a diagnostic tool for identifying development boundaries, policy-deviation risks, and adaptive governance priorities. title: How can prospective life cycle assessment support the eco-design of an innovative battery-grade lithium carbonate production process?
abstract: The transition to low-carbon energy systems drives increasing lithium demand, making alternative recovery technologies essential for long-term supply resilience. This study shows how eco-design principles guide the identification of the most environmentally-friendly configuration, supporting future mitigation-oriented design choices. institutions: Bureau de Recherches Géologiques et Minières

title: Tree-ring chronologies reveal unexpected geographic patterns of drought vulnerability in western Canadian forests
abstract: Adaptive reforestation under climate warming will increasingly involve northward or upslope movement of tree species and seed sources. However, in western Canadian boreal and sub-boreal forests, release from cold constraints may be offset by emerging drought limitations, where low evapotranspiration has historically supported tree growth despite modest precipitation. We used 392 tree-ring chronologies from western Canada to compare drought resistance, recovery, and resilience among seven common conifer tree species across regional climatic gradients. abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. In earlier work, we introduced CARDAMOM, an algorithm that uses temporal snapshots of scRNA-seq data to calibrate a GRN-driven mechanistic model of gene expression. title: A provincial environmental technology transition indicator for Vietnam: Green finance, spatial diffusion, and absorptive capacity
abstract: This paper develops and validates a provincial Environmental Technology Transition (ETT) indicator for Vietnam and uses it to assess whether green finance is associated with cleaner technology upgrading, eco-innovation, and energy-efficiency improvement. Using a balanced panel of 63 Vietnamese provinces over 2014-2024 (693 observations), the study combines indicator construction, principal-component validation, Spatial Durbin modelling, and an IV-spatial estimator to examine both within-province and cross-province technology-transition dynamics. title: THE TRANSCALAR POLITICS AND SPATIAL IMPLICATIONS OF INVESTMENTS IN SHOPPING MALLS IN AFRICAN CITIES : A Study of Accra's West Hills Mall, Ghana
abstract: Abstract A surge in the number of shopping malls across many African cities reflects capital's responses to the continent's growing middle class and deepening neoliberal globalization. This article develops an analysis of the transcalar nature of these urban investments using the case of the West Hills Mall (WHM) in the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area (GAMA). title: Between Custom and Sanction: Theft in the Vinodol Code and the Poljica Statute
abstract: This paper addresses the regulation of theft as an illicit act in two major medieval Croatian legal monuments: the Vinodol Code (1288) and the Statute of Poljica. Rather than offering a systematic comparison of legal systems, the study concentrates on the legal nature, normative structure, and penal treatment of theft within these statutory frameworks, situating the offence in its broader social and institutional context. title: Performance Optimization and Prospects of Double Network Hydrogels for Flexible Electronic Devices
abstract: Dual‐network (DN) hydrogels possess tunable polymer network architectures, exceptional mechanical robustness, and superior water retention capability. They demonstrate substantial potential in structural optimization and performance stabilization, thus garnering widespread attention from both the academic and industrial sectors in the field of flexible devices such as supercapacitors, temperature sensors, and zinc‐air batteries. title: From “curse” to “gospel”: how can industrial relocation lead cities to cross the resource dependence gap
abstract: Industrial relocation offers a novel solution to help mitigate the “resource curse” by reducing dependence on natural resources and fostering diversified economic systems, thereby optimizing the industrial structure. This paper explores the mechanism and economic consequences of industrial relocation’s dependence on the host country’s resources, focusing on the National Industrial Relocation Demonstration Zones (NIRDZ). title: Bird-plant frugivory networks in two secondary Araucaria forests in southern Brazil
abstract: The properties of mutualistic networks may vary depending on the habitat structure in which partners interact. In this research, we evaluated two plant-bird frugivorous networks from the South Brazilian Atlantic Forest (Araucaria Forest) and tested how different past disturbance history and present successional stage can influence the structure of these networks. abstract: The turbulent wake behind detached 60° divergent ribs mounted on one wall of a square duct was investigated with regard to turbulent motion, coherent structures, vortex dynamics and temporal organization, as well as the spatial and temporal characteristics of large-scale turbulent structures. title: Spatial coupling between historic buildings and tourism development in China’s historical and cultural cities
abstract: Historic buildings are an important category of built heritage, but evidence on their coordination with tourism is often based on local cases. Of 143 candidate city-level units, 127 were retained after screening. This study examines 1176 historic-building records and their relationships with domestic and international tourism. The analysis combines spatial analysis, a coupling coordination degree (CCD) model, repeated nested cross-validation, province-grouped validation, and SHAP interpretation of held-out Random Forest predictions. abstract: Abstract. Relativistic runaway electron avalanches (RREA) play a key role in producing high-energy radiation in thunderstorm environments, yet their quantitative description remains largely empirical, with limited validation across atmospheric conditions. In this work, we develop a unified framework that consistently describes both avalanche development within the electric field and particle propagation beyond it, using CORSIKA simulations at four high-altitude stations spanning a wide range of atmospheric densities. title: Darkness Warshed Over the Dude: Comic Resolution, Hamlet and War Anxiety in The Big Lebowski
abstract: The Coen brothers’ 1998 film, The Big Lebowski is a comic inversion of the thematic concerns, philosophical aspirations, character expectations and genre tropes common to film noir. It also engages the history of ideas in scattershot, ludicrous ways, underscoring a disregard for final meanings and a comic understanding of the instability of philosophical and political principles. title: H–D Exchange in Ultraviolet-irradiated Water: Methane Ice Mixtures
abstract: Abstract The deuterium-to-hydrogen (D/H) ratio in solar system volatiles is commonly used to diagnose volatile formation conditions. This ratio may be altered by a range of processes under solar nebula conditions, however, including energetic processing of icy grains. In this study, we investigate the effects of ultraviolet (UV) irradiation on the H/D exchange in mixed methane–water ices, a model system for water and organics ice mixtures. abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of increasingly frequent extreme heat events, mitigating land-surface heat exposure on urban streets is crucial for safeguarding public health. Existing studies have often overlooked the spatially differentiated effects of complex street environments on land-surface heat exposure and the associated cooling thresholds. abstract: The public long-term care insurance (LTCI) scheme has emerged as a key policy initiative to promote universal access to long-term care services in China. abstract: Based on the "dual carbon" strategic goals and the era background of developing new quality productivity, this article focuses on the important proposition that "new quality productivity itself is green productivity", and explores the internal impact mechanism of new quality productivity on the low-carbon economic development of cities at the prefecture level. abstract: This paper compares economic growth, carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions, and renewable energy use in the United States and China—the world's two largest economies and largest greenhouse gas emitters—over the period 1990 to 2024. Prepared as a capstone project for the final year of secondary school, the study draws on freely available data from the World Bank, Our World in Data, and the European Commission's EDGAR database. abstract: The evaluation of soil properties under a century-old traditional rice-fallow practice in highly fragile topography (i.e., hill slopes and lowlands) of North-east (NE) India in the Eastern Himalaya faces multiple challenges in conventional studies of soil properties. Alternatively, remote sensing offers a viable solution. abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing interest in recycled polymer composites and natural fiber reinforcement, relatively few studies have systematically examined low-density polyethylene (LDPE)/recycled polyethylene terephthalate (r-PET) blend systems reinforced with cellulose fibers recovered from used disposable paper cups, particularly through a direct comparison of untreated and methacrylic acid-grafted fibers. title: Electrification reshapes BRICS vehicle urban mining: Material flows and circularity by 2050
abstract: Vehicle electrification is increasing demand for critical battery materials and shifting end-of-life management from whole vehicle scrap toward component-level streams, especially retired vehicle batteries. The five BRICS founding countries—Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa—represent a critical and diverse testing ground for this transition because they combine large and growing vehicle markets, divergent electrification pathways, and uneven recycling capacities. title: Environmental courts, industrial pollution, and grain production: the reach of judicial environmental enforcement in Chinese cities
abstract: Judicial environmental enforcement operates through litigation, therefore the entitlements it protects are only binding when a discharge can be traced to an identified source within the jurisdiction that adjudicates it. This delineation logic implies that specialized environmental courts reduce pollution selectively, and that their reach stops short of sectors they do not adjudicate. title: From raw occurrence records to accessible knowledge: Transforming biodiversity infrastructure through evidence-manifesting design
abstract: Biodiversity informatics has made occurrence records widely accessible, yet many databases remain optimized for human browsing rather than structured machine consumption by large language models (LLMs) and AI agents. This creates a bottleneck: analytical capacity is accelerating while biodiversity evidence remains fragmented, weakly documented, and difficult to cite reproducibly. Here we introduce evidence manifestation, a design approach that transforms raw occurrence data into versioned, citable, machine-readable knowledge artefacts with explicit provenance. title: Frequency-aware Mamba and dynamic optimization DETR for real-time tiny-object detection in UAV aerial imagery

title: Approximating FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference evapotranspiration with a wind-augmented Hargreaves–Samani model across the Czech Republic
abstract: Study Region: The Czech Republic, represented by 1 301 722 daily observations from 171 meteorological stations during 2000–2025. Study Focus: FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference evapotranspiration (FAO-PM) requires inputs that are often unavailable. We developed a four-parameter wind-augmented Hargreaves–Samani model (HS-WA) combining a calibrated temperature–radiation baseline with an additive temperature-derived demand term and a bounded, concave wind response. title: A scalable latent-free Vecchia approximation for Bayesian spatially varying coefficient models with censored data
abstract: Abstract Soil contamination by heavy metals, such as lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd), poses a persistent threat to agricultural productivity and food safety, necessitating high-resolution spatial characterization for targeted remediation. Spatially varying coefficients (SVC) models offer a flexible framework for capturing non-stationary relationships between environmental predictors and contaminant concentrations across agricultural landscapes, overcoming the limitations of standard geostatistical models with external drift. abstract: The Stoniness of Molloy’s Anxiety: An Attempted Petrification in Samuel Beckett’s Molloy. As an ardent admirer of Jack Butler Yeats’s petrified aesthetics, Samuel Beckett redirects his attention to affective strategies that would ultimately block the possibility of conventional engagement with his post-war work. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the complexity of interactions in quantitative terrestrial food webs is a key challenge in ecology, particularly in tropical habitats where reports are scarce. Documenting tri‐trophic interactions in these ecosystems is essential to advance understanding of how community dynamics and specialisation shape network structure. abstract: Abstract Mefite d’Ansanto (Southern Apennines, Italy) is one of the largest known non‑volcanic CO 2 degassing sites worldwide. The degassing process observed here is widely recognized as the surface manifestation of the interaction between mantle-derived CO 2 and a complex shallow fracture network. abstract: A hierarchical nonlinear control benchmark is presented for gust load alleviation (GLA) and maneuver load alleviation (MLA) in a highly flexible winged UAV. abstract: Given the increasing frequency of extremely high temperature events due to global warming, life insurers need to incorporate temperature impacts in their mortality models and long-term liability valuations. Current actuarial literature, primarily using monthly or annual data, inadequately captures the non-linear and delayed effects of temperature on mortality. abstract: Deforestation remains one of the greatest obstacles to limiting global warming, yet the economic mechanisms linking global supply chains to final consumers are poorly understood. Fine-scale satellite monitoring tracks where forests are lost, but rarely reveals who ultimately drives this loss through consumption. abstract: Abstract Bedload transport widely occurs in natural environments and encompasses flow regimes from saltation to sheet‐flow, with markedly different fluid‐particle interaction characteristics. abstract: Mountain ecosystems are functionally diverse and have concentrated environmental gradients. Exploring the changing characteristics and trade-offs of ecosystem services (ESs) under different environmental gradients is beneficial to the conservation and sustainable use of mountain resources. This study evaluated the spatial-temporal changes of habitat quality (HQ), soil conservation (SC), water yield (WY), water purification (N output load) and net primary productivity (NPP) in the Qilian Mountains from 2000 to 2018, and analyzed their responses to environmental gradients. abstract: Capsicum, often known as sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum var. grossum L.), is becoming more and more popular in Bangladesh as a vegetable. However, a number of obstacles must be overcome for its production to occur, such as limited cation exchange capacity, poor soil fertility, fast mineralization of soil organic matter, and acidity of the soil. abstract: Plastics are widely used as food contact materials, which have the potential to release microplastics (MPs), nanoplastics (NPs), and plastic-associated organic and inorganic chemicals into foodstuffs, thereby posing a potential risk to human health. abstract: Satellite image classification plays an important role in various applications like monitoring, surveillance, land cover planning, etc. Deep learning models with many learnable parameters face overfitting as model depth increases and have struggled to extract both fine details and broader patterns simultaneously. abstract: Abstract In response to the insufficient conformability, limited grasping stability, and low force threshold of existing magnetically driven grippers for highly curved and fragile workpieces, this study proposes a magnetically actuated adaptive gripper that integrates spring-based energy storage and magnetorheological particle blocking. abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) systems are among the most promising renewable energy sources, yet their efficiency is critically compromised under partial shading conditions (PSC). It employed five CMIP5 climate models under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios along with a satisfactory SWAT model with acceptable predictive uncertainty. abstract: The transition of cultured meat and seafood technologies from laboratory research to commercial production depends on biological performance and the robustness, safety, and sustainability of the underlying manufacturing infrastructure. When scaling-up, choices regarding material selection, component compatibility, and interface design can significantly influence process reliability, contamination risk, and environmental impact. title: Policy coordination of public data openness and supercomputing center for agricultural chain resilience
abstract: Strengthening agricultural supply chain resilience is critical for safeguarding food security and promoting high-quality agricultural development in the face of escalating external shocks, including climate extremes, market volatility, and geopolitical uncertainties. Although public data openness and supercomputing infrastructure represent critical pillars of digital transformation, how their coordinated deployment enhances agricultural resilience remains both theoretically underdeveloped and empirically underexamined. title: From situational awareness to systemic stability: A phased institutional pathway for space traffic management
abstract: Rapid growth in satellite deployments has transformed Earth orbit from a sparse operational environment into a continuously negotiated shared domain. Modern tracking networks increasingly detect conjunction risks, yet collision avoidance remains dependent on bilateral coordination between operators rather than predictable procedural rules. Space situational awareness (SSA) is therefore indispensable but incomplete: it provides probabilistic knowledge of orbital conditions but does not yet constitute a traffic management regime capable of ensuring consistent, system-level predictability. abstract: Reducing CO 2 emissions from the cement industry is challenging because a large share of the emissions arises from core chemical processes, and the further handling of the CO 2 depends highly on regional CO 2 storage availability. We provide the first quantitative, system-wide comparison of oxygen-from-electrolysis, CO₂ grid, and flexible grinding for cement decarbonisation, based on an endogenous linear optimisation model quantifying the system-cost and technology-mix implications. title: Team cognition in remote maritime operations: a scoping review and cross-domain theoretical synthesis
abstract: Introduction Remote maritime operations increasingly depend on complex, distributed socio-technical systems in which safe and effective performance relies on team cognition rather than on individual decision-making alone. Despite its importance, the conceptualisation and measurement of team cognition in this domain remain fragmented and underdeveloped. title: Agrivoltaic systems can improve agricultural yield by mitigating extreme plant temperatures
abstract: Agriculture suffers from more intense, prolonged, and frequent extreme temperature events such as heat waves, droughts, and frosts. Agrivoltaic systems offer an opportunity to mitigate such events by deploying photovoltaic (PV) panels above crops. In this study, measurements of plant, air, and soil temperatures, along with solar and infrared radiation, wind speed, and soil moisture demonstrate that plants benefit from cooler microclimates beneath PV panels during extreme heat events, and conversely from warmer microclimates during cold nights. title: CAZyme-guided modification of cactus and regional polysaccharides for food hydrocolloid applications
abstract: Food-hydrocolloid performance depends on polymer architecture and processing history rather than ingredient name alone. This critical narrative review evaluates CAZyme-guided modification of cactus-derived pectic materials and related regional polysaccharides for food hydrocolloid applications. Opuntia mucilage and pectic fractions are the focal substrates; non-cactus pectins provide the closest mechanistic evidence, and arabinoxylan is retained only as a bounded comparison for substitution and oxidative crosslinking. title: Stepwise-clustered downscaling of spatiotemporal variations in compound drought-heatwave extremes over the Yangtze River Basin
abstract: Global warming is intensifying compound drought-heatwave events (CDHWs), yet coarse-resolution climate models cannot adequately resolve local variations across the complex terrain and monsoon climate of the Yangtze River Basin (YRB). This study developed a Stepwise Clustering Drought-Heatwave Downscaling (SCDHD) framework to downscale daily maximum temperature, precipitation, and potential evapotranspiration at the station scale and project CDHW variations across the YRB and its five climatic regions under SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5. title: Risk-aware hierarchical reinforcement learning for investment and operations in cross-border energy supply chains under the belt and road initiative
abstract: Abstract Cross-border energy supply chains under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) face unprecedented challenges, including geopolitical instability, macroeconomic volatility, and operational disruptions. Traditional optimization or flat reinforcement learning (RL) methods often struggle to address the scale, uncertainty, and multi-stakeholder complexity inherent in such environments. title: LDF-Net: a transformer-based lightweight detail fusion network for UAV engineering vehicle detection
abstract: UAV engineering vehicle detection is a fundamental task for intelligent construction monitoring, as engineering vehicles directly reflect construction progress, equipment deployment, and potential safety risks in dynamic construction scenes. However, reliable detection in UAV construction scenes remains difficult due to three major challenges: the lack of a dedicated benchmark dataset, severe scale variation and background interference, and the loss of discriminative details during cross-scale feature fusion. abstract: This paper proposes a path deviation control method that integrates laser vision guidance and trajectory prediction to address deviations caused by limited environmental perception in multi-drone cooperative tasks. title: GeoCaseRec: a knowledge graph semantics-driven framework for sustainable urban renewal recommendation
abstract: As urbanisation shifts from outward expansion to the regeneration of existing built environments, sustainable urban renewal increasingly depends on the effective reuse of historical cases. However, this remains constrained by fragmented multi-source geo-referenced data, semantic heterogeneity, and limited case evaluation. abstract: Additive manufacturing of superelastic Nitinol (NiTi) braided metamaterials is demonstrated in this study, enabling the creation of a wide variety of concepts for personalized vascular medical devices. title: Predicting cultivation probability to target monitoring in smallholder landscapes: Proof of concept from dispersed medicinal plant cultivation in Taihe County, China
abstract: Dispersed medicinal plant cultivation by smallholder farmers presents a monitoring challenge that differs fundamentally from conventional agricultural monitoring: fragmented fields, mixed spectra, and canopy occlusion make direct detection difficult, while exhaustive field surveys are prohibitively costly. Rather than detecting every plot, we combined Random Forest modeling with geographical detector analysis to predict cultivation probability from environmental covariates, transforming monitoring from an open-ended search into targeted, spatially guided effort. title: Staged digital transformation and firms’ total factor productivity: evidence from Chinese cultural firms
abstract: This study explores the effects of digital transformation (DT) on firms’ total factor productivity (TFP) across the digital technology application (DTA) stage and digital business model innovation (DBMI) stage. Using a sample of 245 Chinese listed cultural firms from 2011 to 2022, we examine how DT impacts TFP differently across these stages. title: Review on the applications of electromagnetic method in landslide geohazard investigation
abstract: Abstract Frequent large-scale geological disasters, triggered by both natural geological processes and intensive human activities, have resulted in significant casualties and property losses worldwide. Geophysical electromagnetic (EM) methods have emerged as important tools for investigating such hazards. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the application and development of ground-based, airborne, and semi-airborne (ground-to-air) EM methods in various geological disaster scenarios. title: Parametric analysis of greenhouse design for hydroponic barley cultivation: a case study in sustainable agriculture in arid regions
abstract: In greenhouse energy studies, particularly in hydroponic systems, many studies focus on a single aspect. However, a systemic approach and passive measures are often lacking, despite the need to consider the interactions between climate, energy, ventilation, solar gains, the building envelope, orientation, crops, and control strategies. abstract: Mediterranean rivers are exposed to climate-driven hydrological change, yet environmental-flow assessment relies on static habitat metrics that poorly represent fish habitat variability over time. We developed a time-explicit framework that converts monthly weighted usable area (WUA) series into indicators of the magnitude, variability, duration, frequency and persistence of limiting physical habitat conditions. abstract: Low nitrogen use efficiency of prilled urea contributes to substantial economic loss and environmental pollution through leaching, denitrification, and ammonia volatilization. title: Cloud computing and global satellite products for potential groundwater recharge estimation: application to the Basin of Mexico
abstract: Groundwater recharge (GWr) estimation is fundamental for assessing aquifer storage changes, ensuring groundwater sustainability, and supporting effective water management. However, regional groundwater recharge assessment remains challenging because it requires integrating large geospatial datasets, computational resources, and hydrogeological information that are often unavailable in data-limited regions. abstract: Background Prenatal cannabis exposure is associated with adverse offspring outcomes including altered neurodevelopment. However, there is insufficient evidence to establish a direct association. abstract: The transition of urban energy systems toward sustainability and smartness depends on effective policy design. Despite significant scholarly attention, research remains fragmented across policy instruments, system components, and analytical perspectives. To address these limitations, this study presents an integrated framework that combines a PRISMA-guided systematic review, artificial intelligence-assisted topic modeling (BERTopic), and Multi-Level Perspective (MLP) transition theory. abstract: DNA methylation at CpGs silences repetitive elements and transposable elements (TEs) within constitutive heterochromatin in the genome. abstract: Context Fertilization of tropical pastures in Latin America is limited and predominantly based on urea as the sole nitrogen (N) source. This contrasts with the widespread multi-nutrient limitations of highly weathered soils, which may restrict the effectiveness of N-only fertilization. abstract: Abstract. Ocean waves erode the waterline of Antarctic ice-shelf fronts and carve a thermo-erosional notch. title: Spall Failure of Coral Skeleton beneath Gas-Laden Canopies: An Idealized Blast-Fishing Model
abstract: Improvised explosives used for fishing on shallow Indonesian reefs shatter coral skeleton, yet the damage they cause has been described largely through empirical radii and ecological surveys. title: LoopLUT: 3D Lookup Tables with Progressive Region Refinement for Real-Time 4K Image Enhancement
abstract: Color enhancement of 4K images must meet a quality target under a tight compute budget. Three-dimensional lookup tables (3D LUTs) dominate real-time enhancement because they decide at low resolution and apply a per-pixel lookup at full resolution. A single global LUT, however, is spatially invariant, so an underexposed shadow and a well-exposed region that share a pixel value receive identical corrections. abstract: In atmospheric neutrino analyses, the usable zenith-angle range is generally restricted to upward-going events to suppress the cosmic-ray muon background. Motivated by the exceptionally low underground muon background at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL), we investigate whether extending the zenith-angle acceptance can improve the sensitivity of atmospheric neutrino oscillation measurements. abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Collaboration has reported a nuclear-recoil candidate at $248\pm23~({\rm stat})\pm23~({\rm sys})~{\rm keV}$ in an extended high energy search window. title: EP-Mem: Elastic Privacy Memory for Social Relationship-Aware LLM Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents face critical privacy risks when acting as delegates in human-agent-human communication. To prevent such breaches, agents must understand users' social relationships and adhere to context-dependent social information disclosure boundaries. Current studies on agent memory privacy focus on instantaneous interactions, leaving the long-term relational disclosure problem unexplored. title: The TIB Terminology Service and Its Terminology Collection for the Earth System Sciences
abstract: Advancing Earth System Sciences (ESS) depends on our ability to integrate highly diverse data from a range of disciplines, including geographical information sciences, palaeontology, marine science, biodiversity research, atmospheric sciences and biology. A major scientific obstacle to this integration is semantic heterogeneity: different disciplines use different methods and terms to describe data, resulting in fragmented vocabularies. title: Africa’s first permanent Ocean Observatory: powering science, defending nature, and shaping policy for ocean governance and the blue economy
abstract: Sustained, high-resolution ocean observation is essential for understanding how marine ecosystems respond to climate variability, human pressure, and conservation action. Yet long-term observing platforms remain scarce across the Global South, limiting the capacity to detect environmental change, evaluate management interventions, and support evidence-based ocean governance. abstract: Abstract The presence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants in the environment enables their dissemination and transfer from and into human microbiomes. Environmental surveillance is a recognized cornerstone for evaluating, understanding, and mitigating emergence and exposure to resistant pathogens. title: From emergence to exposure: one health attribution of azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus in Southeast Asia
abstract: Southeast Asia is a hotspot for azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus yet remains underrepresented in global surveillance. Disciplinary approaches, including genomics, environmental sampling, and social science, have progressed but remain poorly integrated. We outline a One Health attribution framework linking selection pressures, environmental reservoirs, exposure pathways, and clinical resistance signals to prioritise surveillance, target interventions, and allocate resources where they will have greatest impact.

title: From Local Evidence to Regional Leadership: Post-Preeclampsia Care in Thailand
abstract: Abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, particularly preeclampsia, identify women at increased risk of persistent hypertension and later cardiovascular disease, yet postpartum services often remain organized around short-term obstetric recovery. abstract: Crab fisheries are important components of coastal food systems, but their sustainable development depends on selective fishing gear, reliable field information, and reduced ecological disturbance. abstract: Gender equality and the empowerment of women are core priorities of the European Union. title: The role of intermediary actors in driving just adaptation
abstract: Abstract Just adaptation refers to the process of adapting to climate change in ways that are fair, equitable, and inclusive, especially for those most vulnerable to its impacts. However, there are significant challenges in realizing justice principles across different scales of adaptation. Drawing on consultations with 22 climate adaptation stakeholders in Kenya, we argue for the important role of intermediary actors in addressing these challenges.

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in urban infrastructures and governance, shaping how people, spaces, and futures are classified, prioritised, and managed. Yet, most AI systems are developed within a narrow set of linguistic and geopolitical contexts and exported globally, embedding particular epistemic assumptions into diverse urban environments. abstract: Generative AI is widely framed as a productivity tool. abstract: Global climate change is reshaping the schedules and routes of migratory birds, which can disrupt annual cycles, ecological interactions and the fitness trade‐offs of migrating or staying resident. abstract: Unoccupied critical habitat designation is often highlighted as a beneficial U.S. Endangered Species Act provision for conserving biodiversity in the face of climate change.
