abstract: AI platforms, while offering many positive applications, also present new risks to society, including the facilitation of trade in threatened and illegal wildlife. Although these platforms employ safeguards to block harmful or criminal requests, studies show such protections are imperfect and can be easily bypassed. abstract: As China’s economy grows, healthcare equity concerns intensify. This study examines healthcare disparities at a grid level using a two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) that accounts for distance decay. title: The promise and paradox of a just energy transition in Bangladesh: Governance deficits, justice gaps, and the architecture of an equitable transition
abstract: Bangladesh confronts an acute and multi-dimensional tension between formal commitments to clean energy transformation and the entrenched structural realities of a fossil-fuel-dependent economy. abstract: The Water-Energy-Food (WEF) nexus is a critical framework for addressing interconnected resource management challenges in Iran, particularly under increasing environmental constraints, groundwater depletion, and socio-economic pressures. abstract: Public avoidance behaviour following radiological events can persist even when authoritative assessments judge the associated exposure to be negligible, posing a persistent challenge for radiological protection communication. abstract: South Travancore's sociocultural history underwent a sea change in the nineteenth century, when caste prejudice, untouchability, gender inequity, illiteracy, and economic backwardness were prevalent. In this regard, the London Missionary Society (LMS) missionary Rev. Charles Mead became a trailblazing social reformer whose work went much beyond theological pursuits. After moving to South Travancore in 1817, he spent more than 50 years working to improve underprivileged areas via institutional development, education, healthcare, women's welfare, and vocational training. abstract: Abstract Detecting sand beds in laboratory sediment experiments is challenging, especially when artificial vegetation or other structures are present. RGB‐D cameras offer fast, high‐resolution, and low‐cost sand bed reconstruction. However, the commonly applied Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM)‐based approaches for RGB‐D data often fail on the flat and textureless sand surfaces with artificial structures, due to difficulties in RGB‐D‐based camera pose optimization. abstract: RATIONALE: Work participation is associated with improved health and wellbeing. Vocational rehabilitation (VR) programs support individuals, including those with mental health problems, in obtaining and maintaining employment. Integrating mental health and work support in VR is considered more effective but requires cross-sector collaboration. abstract: Introduction: This paper explores the intersection of ecopreneurship and sustainable business practices through the lens of Northeast Indian literature. title: To release or not to release? Understanding sawfish release behavior in a global south complex fishery
abstract: Abstract What socio‐economic, cultural, subjective, or institutional factors might motivate a socially marginalized, economically constrained fisher to voluntarily release a highly valuable catch such as a sawfish? This study looked at fishers' attitudes (ability, willingness, and challenges) toward the live release of Critically Endangered sawfish in Bangladesh. The study findings revealed that while goodwill and cultural beliefs were found to encourage live release, the most frequently mentioned challenges were financial loss, fear of injury, and unintentional gear entanglement among others.

abstract: Sustainable local economic development at the village level requires a balance between community welfare, environmental protection, and effective local governance. In Madura, the utilization of natural resources remains insufficiently aligned with environmental carrying capacity, creating challenges for achieving sustainable village development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). abstract: Sathurukondan wetland in the Batticaloa District contains valuable mangrove resources, yet baseline ecological information remains rather scarce. This study assessed mangrove vegetation from May to October 2023, focusing on species distribution, abundance, and diversity. A total of 59 line transects and 99 quadrats were established to compile a species checklist and evaluate community structure using diversity indices such as the Shannon–Wiener index, Pielou’s evenness, and Margalef richness. title: Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Development in the Niger Delta: Community Participation, Environmental Governance, and the Road to Achieving the SDGs 2030
abstract: The Niger Delta region of Nigeria represents one of the most ecologically significant yet environmentally vulnerable ecosystems globally. Since the onset of oil and gas exploration in the 1950s, the region has experienced severe environmental degradation manifested through oil spills, gas flaring, deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and declining fish populations. These anthropogenic activities have led to biodiversity loss, compromised ecosystem services, and heightened socio-economic vulnerabilities among local communities. abstract: Baleen whale strandings are rare in the southern Gulf of Mexico and can provide valuable molecular information where species are infrequently documented. We analyzed tissue from a highly decomposed whale stranded on the central coast of Veracruz, Mexico, by amplifying and bidirectionally sequencing the mitochondrial DNA control region. title: Place-based climate adaptation: How Atlantic Canadian communities translate local knowledge into action
abstract: This study examines how communities in Atlantic Canada recognize, value, and integrate local knowledge into climate change adaptation, focusing on the enabling and constraining roles of funding, governance, and institutional structures. Guided by the Socio-Ecological Systems (SES) framework, the research forms part of a larger transdisciplinary project on collaborative governance in financing climate adaptation and mitigation. title: From total volume control to governance logic: a legal review and institutional solution for the production cap rules in global plastics agreements
abstract: The issue of global plastic pollution has become a pressing environmental concern that requires a unified response from the international community. Ongoing negotiations for the “Global Plastics Convention” are positioning upstream production controls as the primary strategy for combating plastic pollution. Among these provisions, the debate over whether to impose an upper limit on the total volume of virgin plastic production stands out as the most contentious. title: The limits of Antarctic conservation governance
abstract: Abstract The Antarctic region exerts a profound influence on the Earth system, making its conservation fundamental to sustaining planetary health and human wellbeing. The Antarctic Treaty System (ATS) holds near-exclusive authority for environmental protection across the region, yet questions remain regarding its capacity to address a growing range of conservation threats. We investigate this by analysing over 90,000 scientific and policy documents (1961–2023) to examine how conservation threats are discussed across science and ATS policy deliberations. abstract: Frontiers journals encourage editors to publish perspectives pieces that overview the field and chart the journal's future direction. title: Integrated Regional Tourism Development Planning in Saudi Arabia: A Framework for Sustainable Infrastructure and Destination Growth under Vision 2030
abstract: Saudi Arabia is moving away from having tourism based on a number of individual flagship destinations towards establishing a development system that is linked across territories, in which issues relating to mobility, utilities, heritage, ecosystems, communities and investment have to be coordinated on a regional basis. This study presents an integrated framework for regional tourism development planning aimed at achieving sustainable infrastructure and destination growth in line with Vision 2030. abstract: An estimated one billion children live at extremely high risk of adverse effects from climate change. Even when children are not exposed to direct physical impacts, the existential threat of climate change can have a psychological impact by creating a stressor that exacerbates underlying mental health disorders or contributes to the development of new disorders. title: A global mitochondrial genomic atlas illuminates freshwater microeukaryote diversity
abstract: Abstract Environmental genomics has transformed our view of the microbial world, yet progress remains largely prokaryote-centric. Among microbial eukaryotes, inconsistent marker choice and limited species-level resolution blunt diversity estimates and hinder cross-study synthesis. Consequently, regional‑to‑global gradients in richness, turnover, and phylogenetic structure remain poorly resolved. Here we establish a global mitogenome-based framework that converts shotgun metagenomes into species‑resolved, phylogeny‑anchored inventories. abstract: La informalidad laboral en México representa un obstáculo estructural para el ejercicio pleno del derecho a la seguridad social y para la sostenibilidad del sistema de protección social. Actualmente, más del 54% de la población ocupada trabaja sin afiliación a la seguridad social, lo que implica exclusión de servicios médicos, pensiones y otras prestaciones, el problema se agrava para el caso de personas trabajadoras del hogar con un alarmante índice de informalidad laboral del 96,5%, a pesar de que la legislación mexicana contempla el registro obligatorio en el régimen del seguro social de la

abstract: Abstract Quick and cheap water quality monitoring is an increasingly important tool to make the best use of an increasingly valuable resource. Fluid conductivity is an important parameter and can be measured contactless using inductive or capacitive coupling while maintaining low cost. Only the inductively coupled sensors are completely free of electrode polarization effects due to the absence of electrodes. title: Toward a Resilient Geoscience Enterprise in Latin America and the Caribbean
abstract: Geoscience in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) operates amid persistent variability that challenges the continuity, credibil-ity, and public value of scientific work. This paper analyzes the resilience of the geoscience enterprise in the region—how science is designed, conducted, synthesized, and shared to serve public mandates—under shifting political, institutional, economic, environ-mental, and social conditions. title: Historical changes and role of river discharge in water quality: 30 years of environmental monitoring in Uruguay River
abstract: Abstract Background Land-use intensification has enhanced impacts on water quality of South American rivers. A long-term database was compiled from public monitoring data to evaluate the temporal variation in water quality in the mid-lower Uruguay River from 1987 to 2019. Forty-two parameters (physicochemical, nutrients, metals, microbiological, pesticides, persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic substances and hydrological) in three sites across 440 km of the river were selected. title: Strategic Pathways for Magnesium–Aluminum‐Layered Double Hydroxides: Multidimensional Footprints of Production Routes
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium–aluminum‐layered double hydroxides (MgAl‐LDHs) are used in flame retardants, remediation, and catalysis. Sustainability comparisons of industrial routes are insufficient. This study couples techno‐economic analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA) to evaluate two routes (hydrothermal synthesis and modification) at 1000 t/a using industrial data. abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater discharge plays a key role in maintaining habitat suitability for cold‐water fish by generating streamflow and modulating temperatures. In the unglaciated Kenai Peninsula Lowlands (KPL), Alaska, groundwater originates from shallow hillslope groundwater (HGW) or deeper aquifer‐outcrop groundwater (AOGW) sources. abstract: ABSTRACT Sorption‐based atmospheric water harvesting (SAWH) offers a promising route for decentralized freshwater production, but practical water output is often limited by slow sorption kinetics in salt‐loaded hydrogel sorbents. abstract: While kelps hold significant potential as sustainable food and feed ingredients, their high iodine content remains a key regulatory and processing challenge for widespread commercial utilization and product inclusion. abstract: ABSTRACT Rifts host a substantial proportion of the world's hydrocarbon resources because lithospheric extension commonly generates sustained subsidence, thick sedimentary fills and laterally connected migration systems that enhance petroleum‐system efficiency. abstract: Knowledge plays an important role in Disaster Risk Management (DRM). abstract: Somateria mollissima dresseri (American Common Eider) numbers are declining in parts of their historic breeding range in eastern North America. We conducted nesting surveys on 16 islands in 2013 to investigate eider breeding phenology and breeding effort, and whether predation pressure on eiders nesting in the Eastern Shore Islands Wildlife Management Area could be contributing to observed declines in eider numbers in Nova Scotia, Canada. abstract: Bangladesh possesses extensive surface and groundwater resources; however, integrated comparative assessments of their quality across all six Upazilas (sub districts) of Feni District remain limited. This study evaluated spatial and source-based water quality using 18 surface-water and 18 groundwater samples collected across six Upazilas. abstract: Abstract Urban flooding severely disrupts emergency services. Equitable mitigation requires identifying if socially vulnerable neighborhoods face disproportionate travel delays. Previous research overlooks estimation biases, where underestimating risks for vulnerable populations can skew assessments, ultimately hindering effective efforts to reduce risk inequities. abstract: The German sector of the North Alpine Foreland Basin contains more than 50 oil and gas fields. To determine the origin of the oils, Lower Oligocene source rocks—the only significant source rock for which no modern data is available—were examined and compared with recently published data from the Jurassic Posidonia Shale and from Permo-Carboniferous rocks. title: Between restrictions and rewards: Understanding community perceptions of protected area governance and outcomes
abstract: Protected areas (PAs) play a critical role in conserving biodiversity and maintaining ecosystem functions, yet their effectiveness is closely associated with how local communities perceive conservation outcomes and governance practices. This study examined community perceptions of ecological benefits, conservation costs and PA benefits, and governance practices associated with the Magamba Nature Forest Reserve (MNFR), Tanzania. title: Strategic ambitions and discursive divergences: China’s belt and road initiative in official and academic narratives
abstract: The present article seeks to analyse and interpret the discursive construction and strategic orientation of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). It aims to elucidate how the initiativeis framed within geopolitical, economic, sociocultural, technological, environmental, and institutional contexts, while critically assessing the coherence and divergences between China’s official narratives and academic discourses. title: Uncharted links from mining to fed animal systems: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract Animal-source foods are an increasingly large part of human diets worldwide, with feed production representing the primary driver of environmental impacts in farmed animal systems. While much attention has focused on agricultural and fisheries-based feed ingredients, the role of mineral supplements - a critical feed component - remains largely overlooked in sustainability assessments. title: Maximizing Tourism Potentials in Rivers State
abstract: Tourism is a pivotal driver of economic growth, cultural preservation, and social cohesion. However, in Nigeria, and particularly in Rivers State, the tourism sector remains largely underutilized despite the state's vast natural resources, vibrant cultural heritage, and strategic location in the Niger Delta region. This study explores the untapped potential of tourism in Rivers State; this paper explores the various tourism potentials of Rivers State, examining its cultural, ecological, recreational, educational, and industrial attractions. title: Quantifying ecosystem degradation via energetic deficits
abstract: Abstract Ecosystem degradation is accelerating, posing critical threats to both biodiversity and human economies. A central challenge is to quantify degradation relative to a reference baseline in a way that supports restoration planning and resource allocation. title: Reconstruction of an Ecosystem-Based Law Enforcement Model: Transformation of the Principle of Utility for the Restoration of Protected Forests
abstract: Indonesia, as a megabiodiverse country, faces serious challenges from the degradation of protected forests caused by land conversion into illegal agricultural areas. This study aims to analyze current law enforcement efforts against forest land conversion and formulate an environmental restoration-based law enforcement model grounded in the principle of legal utility. title: Environmental Jurisprudence in Anthropocene: Evaluation of Law in Addressing Impact of Environment Degradation on Economically Disadvantaged Communities
abstract: The Anthropocene represents a period in which human activities have become a major force influencing the Earth’s ecological systems. Environmental degradation arising from climate change, pollution, deforestation, biodiversity loss and resource depletion does not affect all sections of society equally. Economically disadvantaged communities, including rural, tribal, forest-dependent, agricultural and fishing communities, often experience greater environmental burdens because of their dependence on natural resources and their limited capacity to adapt or to obtain effective remedies. title: A privacy-preserving framework for compressed pattern matching over encrypted data using lightweight XOR-based encryption and bit-parallel processing
abstract: With the tremendous growth of cloud computing, cyber threat intelligence systems, and compressed big-data storage, efficient and secure compressed pattern-matching techniques are in high demand. Traditional compressed pattern-matching methods mainly focus on computational efficiency and do not consider privacy preservation or pattern search over encrypted patterns. abstract: The Act East Policy of India, launched in 2014 as the successor to the Look East Policy, has been envisioned to enhance India's economic, strategic, and diplomatic relations with ASEAN in the changing context of the Indo-Pacific region. The progress achieved in bilateral relations raises the question of whether the Act East Policy generated any real economic benefits and enhanced India's influence in the region compared to China that continues to build its economic position. title: How port governance shapes living labs for energy transitions
abstract: Ports are increasingly central to decarbonisation, energy-system integration, and resilience, yet less is known about how port governance shapes experimentation and whether learning becomes embedded in organisational practice. Living Labs (LLs)—organised forms of multi-actor experimentation in real-life settings—offer a promising approach, but are often treated as governance-neutral. title: Snake diversity based on rescue records in urban Jaipur, Rajasthan, India
abstract: We documented the snakes of Jaipur City, Rajasthan, India, using rescue records generated through a structured volunteer network, comprising primary data collected between January 2024 and October 2025, supplemented by historical records. A total of 787 primary rescue events along with past records (before January 2024), yielded records of 21 snake species across six families, including three venomous and 18 non-venomous taxa. Rescue records were dominated by Naja naja (65.4% of all rescues), while other frequently recorded species included Platyceps ventromaculatus and Spalerosophis atriceps.

title: Recognition, Coexistence, and Civic Trust in Gerbang Mas Perkasa Transmigration Area, Sambas Regency, West Kalimantan
abstract: This article examines how coexistence in the Gerbang Mas Perkasa transmigration area, Sambas Regency, West Kalimantan, can be understood through Charles Taylor's politics of recognition. The area is a border transmigration zone in which transmigrant and local communities live within a plural society marked by historical memory, economic vulnerability, ecological pressure, and uneven public services. title: Sacred forests in space and time: Intangible Cultural Heritage and naturebased solutions
abstract: Sacred forests have a long history of protection and many of them are old-growth forests with centuries old trees important for conservation. Some of these forests can be traced back to lands and territories inhabited for millennia by Indigenous peoples. These sites are considered important in the development of religion and spirituality in our distant ancestors and today their Intangible Cultural Heritage demonstrates a special relationship between people and nature. abstract: ABSTRACT Informed by scholarship on climate change and polar bears, this paper analyses alternatives to images of polar bears stranded on ice floes. The empirical frame of reference is recent prize‐winning images and photo essays in popular media, drawn from a selection of news reports on targeted websites. The aim is not to produce a comprehensive data set of polar bear images, but to ask what messages about climate change impacts these images can help to convey. abstract: China’s community and neighborhood governance has become increasingly multi-actor, yet the literature remains fragmented across residents’ committees, homeowner self-governance, social organizations, crisis response, and participatory regeneration. abstract: MAUSAM is officially published by India Meteorological Department. It has a huge scope in the field of meteorology, hydrology and geophysics. title: Beyond the Seat at the Table: Structural Justice, Academic Agency, and the Reality of "Africa Rising"
abstract: Africa is central to the world's future. The continent holds immense human potential, vast natural wealth, and a very young population. Yet, historical trauma from colonialism and ongoing neocolonial practices still hold African nations back. Unfair global financial rules, high borrowing costs, and severe climate impacts create deep systemic barriers. title: Sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices, skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among Malaysian national-level outdoor athletes
abstract: Outdoor athletes in equatorial regions are exposed to high levels of ultraviolet (UV) radiation year-round, increasing the risk of cumulative photodamage. However, evidence on sun protection behaviours and personal UVB exposure among athletes in tropical settings remains limited. This study assessed sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP), skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among national-level outdoor athletes in Malaysia. title: The Spatial Morphology of Future History
abstract: Big History characterizes cosmic evolution as a sequence of thresholds where ordered systems—from stars to civilizations—harvest energy to maintain rising complexity. However, standard historical narratives typically terminate at the present, treating the future as a domain of pure uncertainty. This study proposes that while specific events are unpredictable, the morphological structure of civilization follows a trajectory shaped by the time-invariant constraints of its generalized environment. title: Fostering Transnational Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics Education: An Exploration of Climate-Smart Practices
abstract: This paper discusses the pressing need for a transboundary approach to tackle climate change through STEM education, which is currently limited by traditional education methods. It introduces the Climate-Smart Transnational STEM Framework, encompassing seven dimensions: Cross-border Collaboration, Localised Climate Context, Innovation for Mitigation and Adaptation, Measurement and Data, Awareness and Action, Teacher Capacity, and Equity and Access. abstract: Introduction The present study is part of the PRIMA Fish-PhotoCAT project, which aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a smart purification system for improving water quality, fish production, and environmental sustainability in aquaculture. abstract: Watermelon seeds are nutrient-dense, phytochemical-rich by-products often discarded by the food industry. The present study aimed to develop effervescent granules from defatted watermelon seed flour and to evaluate their physicochemical characteristics. Watermelon seeds were processed and defatted using n-hexane solvent extraction. Ten distinct formulations (WSFG01–WSFG10) were prepared by wet granulation using precise stoichiometric ratios of citric acid, tartaric acid, and sodium bicarbonate. title: Direct 3D extreme rainfall risk mapping from urban aerial LiDAR point clouds
abstract: Flooding is one of the most frequent and damaging natural hazards, increasingly intensified by rapid urbanization and extreme precipitation events. Accurate modelling of water accumulation and runoff in dense urban environments remains challenging due to complex geometries and the limitations of conventional surface-based representations. Most approaches require extensive LiDAR preprocessing before hydrological analysis. title: From Reactive Remediation to Predictive Prevention: A Systems Synthesis of Global Soil Salinization and Sodicity
abstract: Soil salinization and sodicity are accelerating worldwide, reducing crop productivity across more than 160 million hectares of farmland and causing production losses approaching USD 27 billion annually. Despite decades of research documenting these impacts, the extent of salt-affected soils continues to expand. Salt-affected soil degradation emerges from feedbacks among physical, biological, and socioeconomic processes that operate across scales and resist intervention when addressed in isolation. abstract: Abstract This article examines how investor–state dispute settlement (ISDS) tribunals engage with the precautionary principle (PP) when environmental measures are challenged in the face of scientific uncertainty over ecological harm. An analysis of awards identifies three recurrent treatments: (i) strong risk prevention, (ii) flexible risk management, and (iii) nominal acknowledgement. Across these approaches, the PP fails to supply reviewable criteria for adjudication, resulting in inconsistent outcomes and limited doctrinal coherence. abstract: Abstract Microbial ammonia oxidation, the first and rate-limiting step of nitrification, plays a central role in soil nitrogen cycling. It is most relevant in agricultural soils as nitrifiers compete with crops for ammonia-based fertilizers. Therefore, synthetic nitrification inhibitors are widely used alongside fertilizers to reduce the activities of dominant drivers of this process, i.e., ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) and bacteria (AOB). abstract: This paper analyses the European Commission’s first informal opinion on a sustainability agreement between competing port terminal operators, representing a landmark case aimed at reconciling decarbonisation objectives with European competition law. Our study focuses on a specific project involving APM Terminals and its competitors in jointly purchasing and standardising electrical container handling equipment. This study investigated the effectiveness of integrating visible and multispectral imagery with staged feature selection for fine-scale grassland land-cover classification. abstract: This study aims to map the intellectual structure and development of research on the implementation of the rule of law through order and security, with particular attention to its relevance to the Philippine governance context. A qualitative descriptive bibliometric approach was employed to examine scholarly publications retrieved from Dimensions AI, Google Scholar, and selected secondary sources. abstract: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology enables efficient thermal management through high solar reflectance and thermal emission within the atmospheric infrared window. However, conventional radiative coolers predominantly exhibit white or silver appearances due to stringent solar reflectance requirements, thereby limiting their aesthetic appeal. abstract: Abstract This article investigates the world of the late Seleucid Empire on the eve of Roman control of the Eastern Mediterranean. abstract: Purpose This study examines how toilet graffiti can be documented and organised as a researchable form of vernacular material for qualitative research. Rather than analysing the content of graffiti, the study focuses on the methodological and ethical conditions under which ephemeral and anonymous expressions found in public toilets can be rendered researchable. title: Digital Colonialism and the Reproduction of Hegemony in Africa: A Postcolonial Approach
abstract: This article presents a critical analysis of contemporary manifestations of digital colonialism in Africa, focusing on how global technology powers reproduce traditional patterns of domination through modern digital infrastructures and platforms. Drawing on a postcolonial analytical framework, the authors examine how data extraction, technological dependency, and regulatory asymmetries reinforce new forms of digital hegemony across the continent. abstract: The Niger Delta presents a uniquely challenging emergency logistics environment characterized by extensive creek systems, seasonal inundation of road networks, and dispersed communities accessible only by water or air, yet emergency response operations in the region rely predominantly on road transport, with minimal integration of inland waterway and aviation modalities. title: Challenges and Opportunities for Sustainable Water Resources Management in Nigeria: A Review
abstract: Water resource management in Nigeria is a complex issue shaped by its diverse geography, climate variability, and rapid population growth. Despite substantial water resources, the country faces significant challenges in ensuring reliable access to clean and safe water. This paper examines the current status of water resources in Nigeria, highlighting issues such as uneven distribution, infrastructure deficiencies, pollution, and the impacts of climate change. title: A generalized lineage nomenclature for viral genomic epidemiology
abstract: Pathogen genomics has become increasingly integrated into outbreak response, with recent virus epidemics better characterized by large numbers of viral genetic sequences. Effective international communication of viral diversity requires a scalable, adaptable nomenclature, and existing systems may not accommodate rapid sequence generation. The Pango lineage nomenclature system was designed to address these problems and has been applied to SARS-CoV-2 since early 2020. abstract: This paper undertakes a comparative examination of two geographically distant but conceptually convergent traditions of vernacular building: the timber architecture of the Dong ethnic minority in Guizhou, China — epitomised by the drum tower (gulou) and wind-and-rain bridge — and the earthen and painted vernacular forms of sub-Saharan Africa, exemplified by Dogon settlement architecture in Mali and Ndebele mural-house traditions in southern Africa. abstract: Amplicon sequencing typically results in a wide distribution in the number of sequences obtained from each sample. How best to account for this variation has been a persistent problem in the microbial ecology literature. Historically, rarefaction has been used in ecology and this practice was adopted by microbial ecologists. abstract: ABSTRACT Evidence on climate adaptation innovations remains fragmented, limiting evidence‐informed policy. This meta‐analysis of 418 studies (2010–2023), stratified by outcome and design with publication‐bias adjustment, synthesizes effectiveness, equity, and scalability. title: Contract enforcement and foreign direct investment in Nigeria: A critical review of legal predictability and investor confidence
abstract: This paper critically examines the relationship between contract enforcement and foreign direct investment (FDI) in Nigeria, highlighting the legal, institutional, and economic factors that shape investor behaviour. Employing a structured review methodology, the study synthesises evidence from peer-reviewed literature, policy analyses, and legal scholarship to identify trends, challenges, and gaps in Nigeria’s commercial legal environment. abstract: The development of efficient and durable non‐noble metal electrocatalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a critical challenge due to the sluggish four‐electron kinetics and the reliance on scarce iridium/ruthenium‐based materials. title: Global patterns of genetic diversity and evolution in chikungunya virus E2 glycoprotein
abstract: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. abstract: Abstract This study asks why certain Western materials and practices came to be understood as modern science in China. By examining a corpus of Chinese local gazetteers ( difangzhi 地方志) representing roughly 52% of all collated titles within this genre, it argues that the gazetteer actively mediated an emerging technological reality between 1840 and 1949, thereby shaping a Chinese scientific modernity through material, geospatial and epistemic paths. abstract: ABSTRACT Rates of evolutionary change vary by gene. While some broad gene categories are highly conserved with little divergence over time, others undergo continuous selection pressure and are highly divergent among populations or species. But such comparative evolutionary studies rely on gene ontology categories that are rarely validated in the study's focal species. abstract: The hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) is widespread throughout Europe, except in the northeastern parts. Due to its exceptional nutritional profile and associated health benefits, it’s recognised as a premier nut crop, ranking fifth among nut crops, based on total harvested area. abstract: Research into seaport–dry port corridors has tended to focus on the design of the physical network on the one hand and the coordination of governance on the other. It is hard to maintain this separation in well-established Maritime Silk Road corridors. A corridor might have routes, inland nodes and digital platforms, and still not function smoothly at the rail/dry-port interface. abstract: Conservation outreach programs (COPs) aim to reduce illegal bushmeat hunting by providing communities with tangible benefits and fostering positive attitudes toward wildlife, but their influence is difficult to separate from law enforcement and wider social change. We compared how COPs beneficiary and non-beneficiary communities perceived and explained illegal bushmeat hunting dynamics in the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem across 2018-2024. abstract: Abstract John Broome and Duncan Foley argue that future generations should shoulder the full burden of climate mitigation. abstract: ABSTRACT Due to the low damping characteristics of thin plate structures, harmful vibrations can easily occur under external excitation, potentially leading to fatigue failure and a reduced service life. A single dynamic vibration absorber (DVA) is often insufficient to effectively suppress the multimodal vibrations of the plate. Moreover, over time, factors such as fastener loosening and rubber aging can cause shifts in the resonant frequency of a single absorber, significantly affecting its vibration suppression performance. title: Wastewater irrigation effects on contaminant fate soil quality nutritional traits and human health risks in rice agroecosystems with emphasis on microplastics
abstract: Freshwater scarcity, rapid urbanization, and rising agricultural demand have increased interest in wastewater irrigation, especially in water-intensive rice systems. Wastewater reuse can support crop production through nutrient recycling and reduced fertilizer dependence, yet it also introduces a persistent mixture of contaminants into soil–plant systems. abstract: This article examines the manuscript collection of the Holy Monastery of Leimonos on Lesbos as a complex body of material evidence preserving aspects of Byzantine and post-Byzantine literature, Orthodox worship, education and local history. abstract: Until recent decades, the monastery of Lios Mòr (Lismore) in Argyll, Scotland, established by Saint Mo Luóc in the sixth century, was attested only via historical references and local traditions. abstract: Abstract Elephants use low-frequency rumbles to communicate among individuals. Rumbles occur in several patterns: as discrete, non-overlapping calls, in antiphonal sequences where individuals alternate vocalizations, and in choruses where multiple individuals produce overlapping calls. Despite the wide availability of bioacoustics tools, most studies focus on non-overlapping signals rather than on choruses. title: Between Revelation and Digitality: A Gadamerian Qur’anic Hermeneutics of Prophet Jonah and the #KaburAjaDulu Phenomenon
abstract: The emergence of the hashtag #KaburAjaDulu on various social media platforms represents a manifestation of psychosocial distress, structural criticism and the younger generation’s urge to escape the economic pressures and public policies perceived as failing to prioritise their interests. This qualitative, literature-based study aims to contextualise the Qur’anic narrative of the story of Prophet Jonah in Surah al-Anbiya’, verse 37, using Hans-Georg Gadamer’s hermeneutic framework. abstract: The Maximum Entropy Theory of Ecology (METE) derives probability distributions for micro-scale variables, such as species abundances and metabolic rates, solely from macro-scale observables like total abundance and species richness. abstract: Protein phosphorylation orchestrates cellular signaling and controls most biological processes, with its dysregulation driving diseases, notably cancer. Comprehensive, high-throughput phosphoproteomics remains limited by detection sensitivity, data completeness and computational bottlenecks, especially in low-input settings. Here we present a comprehensive empirical human phosphoproteome resource, regrouping over 200,000 class I phosphosites across 33 diverse human cell lines. We demonstrate that this spectral library dramatically improves single-shot phosphoproteomics with 30-fold faster data

title: Sustainability and Willingness to Pay: A Review of Approaches in Urban Mobility and Climate Change Resilience
abstract: Willingness to pay (WTP) is widely used to inform sustainability-related policy and investment decisions, yet its application remains fragmented across research domains. In urban mobility, WTP is typically employed to value service quality improvements, technological adoption, and efficiency gains, while climate change resilience research primarily frames WTP around risk reduction, loss avoidance, and adaptation measures. title: Lightweight visual detection approach for apple ripeness perception in intelligent orchard harvesting scenarios
abstract: Apple ripeness detection in complex orchard scenarios is plagued by fruit occlusion, overlapping, intense illumination interference, and subtle maturity feature differences among similar fruits. Conventional lightweight detection models also suffer from low accuracy and severe feature loss in field environments. To address these problems, this paper proposes a real-time lightweight method for apple ripeness detection with optimized multi-dimensional network structures, which balances lightweight deployment and feature perception capability for complex orchard backgrounds. title: Spatiotemporal modelling of post-COVID recreation reveals persistent and emerging pressures on freshwater ecosystems
abstract: Restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic pushed large numbers of recreationists towards freshwater ecosystems, but whether this shift was temporary or lasting has remained unclear. Using 129045 freshwater-related Wikiloc records (2016–2024), we modelled how recreation changed in time and space along the entire river network of the Catalan River Basin District (NE Spain), separating the pandemic effect from the platform's own growth. journal: Journal of Outdoor Recreation and Tourism

title: The evolution of Pakistan and China’s engagement with Afghanistan since 9/1
abstract: This study examines how Pakistan’s and China’s interests toward Afghanistan have evolved since 9/11 in pursuit of their security and political and economic objectives. Existing scholarship tends to treat Pakistan–Afghanistan and China–Afghanistan relations separately and rarely trace continuity and change across the whole post-9/11 period. title: Infrastructure and Inclusiveness in Election Administration: Insights from India’s General Elections
abstract: The Lok Sabha (Lower House of Parliament) elections of India, represent the world’s largest democratic exercise, requiring an extraordinary scale of logistics, manpower and infrastructural readiness. This paper analyses the operational magnitude of Lok Sabha elections by assessing candidates, electors, polling stations, mobility assets, observers, surveillance teams, home-voting facilities, etc. The findings suggest that India's electoral process is characterised by a strong emphasis on inclusiveness and involves substantial human and material resources and elector-friendly polling stations. title: Curating the Polycrisis: Affective Assemblages, the Interactive Synopticon, and Trans-Corporeal Narratives in the Anthropocene
abstract: Humanity currently navigates an era defined by the Anthropocene and the “polycrisis”—a complex, destabilizing web of interconnected ecological, social, and political emergencies. Concurrently, our primary mode of processing, debating, and governing these existential threats is mediated through the algorithmic infrastructure of digital platforms. title: Governing urban floods in an emerging capital region: a social-ecological-technological systems policy analysis of Samarinda City, Indonesia
abstract: Urban flood governance in Samarinda is entering a new regional context. The establishment of Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) and the emerging IKN–Samarinda–Balikpapan urban ecosystem are accelerating spatial, infrastructural, and institutional interdependence across East Kalimantan. This transition increases the importance of ensuring that Samarinda's flood policies are not only technically effective but also socially inclusive and ecologically grounded. title: Household and community drivers of Aedes aegypti infestation in tropical cities: Guiding community-led interventions
abstract: Disadvantaged communities characterised by poor sanitation conditions, overcrowding, and limited vector control are highly susceptible to Aedes aegypti proliferation and arboviral disease transmission. Effective mosquito vector control requires a detailed understanding of Ae. aegypti oviposition preferences and spatial distribution within such urban environments. title: Governance, dependency, and performance in nuclear megaprojects: A strategic analysis of the Akkuyu NPP
abstract: This study examines the Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) as a strategic governance system within Türkiye’s long-term energy transition. While existing research has primarily focused on the technical, environmental, and economic aspects of nuclear energy, limited attention has been given to the governance mechanisms that shape high-risk megaprojects. title: Global Harmonization of Life Cycle Assessments for Small- and Medium-Scale Wastewater Treatment
abstract: Abstract Wastewater management (WWM) is vital for protecting human health and the environment, yet conventional centralized systems are resource-intensive and unsuited to growing urban pressure. Small and medium WWMs offer a potentially more sustainable alternative, but the lack of standardized life cycle assessment (LCA) approaches limits robust comparison and informed decision-making. In this study, we conduct a global harmonization of life cycle assessments of small- and medium-scale systems across 96 LCAs and 9 treatment technologies. title: An Ecocritical Perspective on the Poems “Darg‘a” and “Tabiat Xato Ketdi” by the Uzbek Poet Tursunoy Sodiqova
abstract: The relationship between human beings and nature has been interpreted in various ways throughout history, and the meanings attributed to the natural environment have evolved in response to social, cultural, and economic transformations. Literature, as a reflection of human experiences and perceptions, has consistently incorporated natural elements and, particularly in the modern era, has developed new perspectives in response to growing environmental concerns. title: Nature-based solutions in built environment education for developing sustainability competencies through bibliometric and systematic analysis
abstract: Abstract Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly recognized for their potential to address complex urban sustainability challenges; however, their integration into higher education curricula within built environment disciplines remains fragmented. This study examines how NbS contribute to the development of professional sustainability competencies and identifies pedagogical strategies most effective for embedding NbS in built environment education. title: Access and Benefit Sharing in India: Reconciling Biodiversity Conservation, Sustainable Development and Community Rights
abstract: International environmental law has historically centered on the control and ownership of natural and biogenetic resources. Numerous environmental conventions have addressed this question, prioritizing benefit-sharing mechanisms. Among these, Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) emerged as a key solution, aiming to balance the interests of developed and developing nations while conserving biodiversity. title: Integrating Local Wisdom into Business Strategy: Chinese Ethnic Entrepreneurs in Madura and the Relevance of Islamic Economic Values
abstract: Purpose – The integration of local wisdom by the Chinese ethnic group in Madura serves as an effective business strategy. It determines a venture’s success, particularly within a complex cultural context like Madura. An effective business strategy is a key determinant of enterprise success, particularly within complex cultural contexts such as Madura. abstract: Tahyna virus (TAHV) is a neglected mosquito-borne Orthobunyavirus pathogenic to humans. In Italy, TAHV was first recorded in Friuli Venezia-Giulia and then repeatedly in Emilia Romagna Region (Northern Italy). This study was set up to verify the presence of TAHV in Central Italy and to identify its potential vectors. Mosquito surveillance was conducted from April to November 2025, using 78 CDC-CO₂ traps across Latium and Tuscany Regions. title: Nature and interbeing: an ecocritical-postcolonial reading of Thich Nhat Hanh's poetry
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this research article is to explore nature and interbeing in the poetic works of Thich Nhat Hanh within the context of ecocritical-postcolonial theories. Design/methodology/approach This research article is designed to discuss two key dimensions: nature as a witness to war and colonization, and interbeing as ecology's resistance to colonial violence. title: A lightweight model for steel surface defect detection based on EDGI-YOLO
abstract: To address the limitations of YOLOv8n in steel surface defect detection–namely, its large parameter count and computational cost, insufficient multi-scale feature modeling capability, and poor scale adaptability of the detection head– we propose a lightweight improved model named EDGI-YOLO. The model is restructured along four dimensions. title: Public perspectives on water quality communication and interest in participatory monitoring approaches in Jalisco, Mexico
abstract: Surface water governance depends not only on monitoring capacity but also on whether residents can access relevant information, navigate institutional responsibilities, and recognize opportunities to participate. This study examined these dimensions in Jalisco, Mexico, through a statewide, face-to-face household survey assessing exposure to and perceptions of surface water quality communication, information-seeking practices, awareness of inquiry and feedback mechanisms, and interest in public hearings and participatory monitoring, including perceived motivations and barriers. title: Dual‐Timescale–Based Cache and Bandwidth Control Scheme in Integrated Satellite‐Terrestrial Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Recently, the integrated satellite‐terrestrial network (ISTN) system offers a promising solution for extending wireless communication services to remote and underserved areas. To effectively provide a variety of services, it is essential to cache the corresponding services on satellites while dynamically allocating the satellite bandwidth. abstract: Ancient Indian philosophical literature, including the Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Mahabharata, Ramayana, and classical scientific treatises such as the Vaisheshika Sutra, Sushruta Samhita, Charaka Samhita, and Aryabhatiya, contains numerous discussions concerning cosmology, mathematics, medicine, astronomy, causality, and the nature of matter. title: Sustainable Risk Management of the Porang Supply Chain as an Agro-Industrial Commodity in Madiun Regency
abstract: Porang is a key agro-industrial commodity in Madiun Regency, Indonesia. Its supply chain currently faces numerous challenges, particularly in terms of risk management and sustainability issues. Various risks continue to affect the stability and performance of supply chains, posing a threat to their long-term viability. Additionally, stakeholder involvement remains fragmented, with limited collaboration across supply chain networks in the industry. This study aimed to identify and analyze supply chain risks and develop relevant risk mitigation strategies from the perspective of sustainability.

title: Remote estimation of plastic distribution in California agriculture using Sentinel-2 imagery: a case study
abstract: Global application of agricultural plastic mulch is increasing. While these films offer benefits for crop production, they also are a large source of plastic waste and pollution in both terrestrial and aquatic systems. The current scale of global mulch application and its deleterious impacts are unclear. Current estimates of agricultural plastic use remain limited by field-specific growing patterns and data limitations. abstract: Efficient data dissemination in large-scale internet of things (IoT) networks remain challenging due to energy constraints, congestion, and delay under dynamic network traffic. This paper introduces a joint routing and medium access control (MAC)-layer scheduling framework (JRSM), incorporating priority-aware clustering to enhance energy efficiency and reduce latency in the IoT data acquisition layer. title: Still seeking permission to narrate: On international law and the question of Palestine
abstract: Abstract At the foundation of knowledge production is the question of who exactly is doing the producing, on what basis, when, where and for whom? Are all views equal? Whose views are or ought to be included? And with what implications? In this 2025 LJIL Lecture, Professor Ardi Imseis meditates on these and other related questions through the prism of one of the most pressing international legal and moral issues of our time: Palestine.

abstract: Abstract This study quantifies the lagged association between grass pollen exposure and the onset of allergic rhinitis (AR) symptoms, including differences between asthmatic and non‐asthmatic subgroups. Data included 114,834 self‐reported AR symptoms collected from 25,194 uniquely identified users of a smartphone application. title: On Prizes
abstract: ABSTRACT This article discusses prize‐creation and prize‐allocation. Such activities may seem morally neutral, or perhaps even beneficial. A central thesis of this article is that such practices have significant moral implications and should be brought under the remit of moral reasoning. I suggest that in many cases, the harmful effects of prizes are overlooked, and that they stand in need of scrutiny, revision, and possibly abolition. title: Global Research Trends and Empirical Evidence on Physician Response Time and Family Psychological Outcomes in Emergency Departments: A Bibliometric Study
abstract: Physician response time is a key performance indicator in Emergency Departments (ED), influencing service efficiency and quality of care. Although research has expanded, the literature remains fragmented, limiting a comprehensive understanding of global research trends and thematic development. This study aims to analyse global research trends, scientific contributions, collaboration patterns, and thematic evolution related to physician response time in ED using a bibliometric approach. abstract: Abstract This article analyzes the Inter-American Court of Human Rights’ 2025 advisory opinion on the climate emergency from the perspective of its implications for Canada. The authors identify key legal developments: “climate emergency” as a decisive interpretive element; the peremptory ( jus cogens ) obligation not to generate irreversible harm to the common planetary ecosystem; a new right to a healthy climate; and states’ “enhanced” due diligence obligation. title: An AI-Powered, Multilingual Pedagogical Support Framework for Integrated Science Teacher Education in Resource-Constrained Nigerian Contexts
abstract: Integrated Science teacher education is central to developing scientifically literate learners capable of understanding and applying concepts across biology, chemistry, physics, and environmental science. However, teacher education programmes in many Nigerian contexts face persistent challenges, including limited instructional resources, inadequate pedagogical support, linguistic diversity, and uneven access to digital technologies. title: Prospects and complexities in sustainability impacts of global residue-based bioenergy deployment
abstract: Amid rising global demand for sustainable energy, agricultural and forestry residues (AFRs) emerge as a key yet underutilized resource in energy transition. Mechanisms of how optimizing multipath AFR utilization advances sustainability contributions in varied socioeconomic contexts remain underexplored. abstract: This article presents the evolution of financial reporting regulations and practices regarding decommissioning liabilities with a focus on the managerial approach to value creation processes in mining companies. Firstly, the author demonstrates the importance of provisions for the above-mentioned obligations for their overall financial standings. abstract: BusyBox is widely reused in Linux-based Internet-of-Things (IoT) firmware, but stripped symbols, heterogeneous instruction sets, uncertain component versions, and selective patch backports make N-day vulnerability localization difficult. We propose EvoPatch-IoT, an evolution-aware retrieval framework whose novelty lies not in another standalone encoder, but in coupling target-local geometric localization, architecture-normalized anonymous multi-view evidence, and a version-causal historical prototype memory for reference-guided retrieval. title: Multi-facility GNSS antenna calibration
abstract: Abstract Accurate antenna calibrations are a cornerstone of high-quality global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) positioning, time and frequency transfer, precise orbits, and troposphere estimates. The international GNSS service (IGS) antenna committee maintains antenna phase center corrections in the ANTEX file relying on five calibration facilities. title: Reframing antimicrobial resistance as a land-system challenge through environmental pathways and climate interactions
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a planetary health challenge, yet land-system change remains overlooked. This review examines how agriculture, urbanisation, waste management, deforestation, aquaculture and climate-driven transitions shape resistance through altered input intensity, habitat reorganisation and enhanced connectivity. It identifies evidence gaps across vulnerable settings and proposes pathway-based surveillance, integrated datasets, longitudinal studies and coordinated interventions to reduce resistance selection, persistence and transmission across connected landscapes

title: Namibia’s Perspectives on Green Economy Management, Sustainable Development and Technological Transformation.
abstract: Namibia is emerging as a pioneer in Africa's green transition, leveraging its abundant renewable resources to pursue a development pathway that integrates green economy management, sustainable development, and technological transformation. This abstract examines Namibia's strategic approach, which is anchored in the Long-Term Low-Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS) and the sixth National Development Plan (NDP6). We surveyed 219 households living near the Kafue National Park in the Central province of Zambia, and applied a discrete choice experiment (DCE) with a split-sample design: half the respondents answered direct questions; the remainder used an indirect questioning format that masks individual answers. abstract: Variational mode decomposition has been widely used for vibration signal analysis due to its clear variational formulation and non-recursive decomposition mechanism. abstract: Photoaging is a major contributor to premature skin aging and results from the cumulative effects of ultraviolet (UV) radiation on cutaneous structures. abstract: The Gadaa system of the Oromo people represents one of the world's most enduring and sophisticated indigenous democratic governance systems. This article examines the recent peaceful transfer of the Alangee (ceremonial baton of authority) from the 70th Gadaa leader, Abbaa Gadaa Goobana Hoolaa (Gadaa Meelbaa cycle), to the 71st Abbaa Gadaa of the Tulama Oromo, Geetuu Taliilaa (Gadaa Muudanaa cycle), which occurred at the sacred site of Ardaa Jilaa Dhaka Koraatti in June 2026. title: Distinct prosocial behaviors associated with persistent symptom trajectories in psychiatric disorders
abstract: Prosocial behavior, the tendency to act for others' benefit, is essential for mental health. Although social contexts strongly shape prosocial behavior in healthy individuals, its relevance across psychiatric disorders remains unclear. We examined whether context-dependent prosocial behaviors were associated with baseline psychiatric symptoms and longitudinal symptom trajectories. title: A Human Rights Analysis of the Legal Framework Governing Communication Surveillance and the Right to Privacy in Tanzania
abstract: The increasing adoption of digital communication technologies has enhanced States' ability to monitor communications for national security, crime prevention, and law enforcement. While such surveillance may serve legitimate public interests, it poses significant privacy risks if surveillance powers are broadly defined or poorly regulated. This article critically analyses Tanzania's legal framework for communication surveillance, evaluating whether it adequately protects the right to privacy. abstract: Introduction: It is important to utilize a microfluidic imaging platform to dynamically monitor the life cycle stages of an example, Brevibacillus bacteria, as this contributes in regulating human nutrition, cardiovascular health, and metabolism. abstract: Why do governments using broadly comparable digital governance technologies during the COVID-19 pandemic exhibit markedly different levels of observable digital compliance? Institutional capacity, technological capability, and regime characteristics help account for this variation, but they do not fully explain why similar interventions generated different trajectories as implementation unfolded. title: Significance of Environmental Justice for Human Dignity: A Nexus between Right to life and Right to Environment
abstract: The impact of environmental pollution, climate change, and loss of biodiversity poses a direct threat to the existence of human beings. This article examines the development and interaction of these two fields through references to legal instruments, constitutional provisions, and cases that support a sustainable environment for human rights. abstract: Individualized therapeutic prompts such as physical, gestural, or verbal cues are necessary to enable children diagnosed with autism to become independent in daily activities. However, the automated detection of the prompts in naturalistic conditions is difficult. title: Value chain dynamics, opportunities, and constraints shaping Baru (Dipteryx alata Vog.) commercialisation in the Brazilian Cerrado
abstract: Abstract The nut of the Baru tree ( Dipteryx alata Vogel), native to Brazil’s Cerrado, has gained attention for its strong nutritional profile and growing market potential. At the same time, the Cerrado faces increasing deforestation driven by agricultural expansion. In this context, Baru is considered a promising sustainable land-use option within forest-based bioeconomy strategies. title: MilsPD: a lightweight multiphysics-integrated peridynamics solver
abstract: Abstract This paper presents MilsPD, a highly efficient multiphysics-integrated peridynamics (PD) solver designed for fracture mechanics applications. It addresses a key computational challenge in the field: the expensive simulation of large-scale multiphysics problems involving evolving fractures and fluid–solid interactions. title: Decontamination Risk Management in Radioisotope Facilities: A Bibliometric Review
abstract: Background: Risk management in the decontamination process of radioisotope and radiopharmaceutical production facilities has garnered significant research attention due to its vital contribution to environmental safety and occupational health. While the volume of literary evidence regarding radiation safety continues to expand, study focuses and methodological approaches remains diverse. abstract: Indigenous storytelling is both cultural heritage and a powerful mode of science communication. This article examines how Storywork rooted in relationships, Country, and community authority can convey scientific knowledge alongside Western approaches. abstract: Our time is one in which headlines regularly feature news about this or that death-world. title: A Qualitative Case Study of Overtourism vs. Regenerative Tourism in Bali, Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: The booming tourism in Bali has further fuelled the debate on overtourism, destruction of the environment, commercialisation of cultures, and the rising pressure on available resources that require destination management strategies beyond traditional sustainability planning. This study seeks to critically address governance, community engagement, and environmental management practices as a way of transitioning overtourism into regenerative tourism in Bali. title: Engineered Artificial Minerals (EnAM) Approach for Chromium Recovery and Stabilization in Steelmaking Slag
abstract: Steelmaking slag represents one of the largest industrial by-products, with estimated annual generation exceeding 500 million tons worldwide. These slag materials contain valuable alloying elements such as chromium, nickel, and vanadium that remain in the slag. Chromium, in particular, has a dual role: it is essential for corrosion resistance of steels but creates environmental and resource recovery challenges when transferred into the slag. title: Slavery and slave-raiding in Africa in the nineteenth century
abstract: Aim: The General Assembly of the United Nations on 25 March 2026 adopted a resolution declaring “the transatlantic slave trade the gravest crime against humanity”. Leaving the political rhetoric of “the gravest crime” to one side, I note that the history of slaving and slave-hunting in Africa was completely neglected, as was the Islamic involvement in the African slave trade and slave employment (and the role of Western traders in the Islamic slave trade as well.). title: NetSyn: prokaryotic genomic context exploration of protein families
abstract: Abstract Background The growing availability of large prokaryotic genomic datasets presents an opportunity to discover new metabolic pathways and enzymatic reactions useful for industrial or synthetic biological applications. Efforts to identify new enzyme functions in this vast number of sequences cannot be achieved without bioinformatics tools and the development of new strategies. Standard methods for assigning a biological function to a gene are based on sequence similarity. title: HyBEAR: a hyperspectral benchmark for bare soil detection
abstract: Abstract. Detecting bare soil areas is an important step in the analysis of Earth observation data in a variety of Precision Agriculture (PA) applications focused on quantifying soil properties and assessing soil quality. In this paper, we introduce the HyBEAR benchmark – a novel large-scale collection of high-resolution hyperspectral aerial images (with 2 m ground sampling distance) accompanied with manual bare soil annotations verified with domain experts. title: Outcome-as-a-service for multi-objective Dask-based Earth Observation processing
abstract: Distributed Earth Observation (EO) workflows require cluster configurations that balance competing objectives (execution time, computational cost, energy consumption, and resource-use efficiency), yet practitioners typically provision resources using fixed heuristics that ignore most of these dimensions. This paper presents an outcome-as-a-service framework for Dask-based EO processing that jointly optimises all four objectives. title: Fine Brown Carbon Aerosol Emitted by Wood Pyrolysis - New Harmful Tracers and Cytotoxicity in Human Lung Cells
abstract: Abstract Biomass burning (BB) is a major global source of light-absorbing organic aerosols, the so-called atmospheric brown carbon (BrC), which negatively affects human health. However, the interplay between the molecular composition and toxicity of BB emissions remains ambiguous. In this study, cytotoxicity analyses and molecular-level characterization of fine BrC generated by wood pyrolysis at 350 °C, representative of smoldering combustion during vegetation fires, were performed. title: The model alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii forms mutualistic interactions with Verticillium fungi
abstract: Abstract Algal–fungal interactions are widespread in natural environments and contribute to key ecological processes such as primary production, nutrient cycling, and soil formation. Yet, molecular mechanisms underlying these associations remain poorly understood due to the complexity of natural systems and the lack of experimentally tractable models. Here, we describe a genetically tractable interaction between the model alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and the soil-borne fungus Verticillium dahliae. title: A framework for unit-level biodiversity credit integrity and market-level governance
abstract: Biodiversity credits (BCs) are one innovative financing scheme that the Global Biodiversity Framework proposes to mobilise private capital and narrow the biodiversity financing gap. BCs and the voluntary biodiversity markets (VBMs) around them are nascent, offering an opportunity to learn from shortcomings of the adjacent voluntary carbon markets and design them for both ecological and social integrity from the outset. title: Weight gain during successful tuberculosis treatment increases the risk of post-tuberculosis metabolic syndrome
abstract: Abstract Background Little is known about the relationship between weight gain during treatment and the subsequent risk of cardiovascular and metabolic (cardiometabolic) diseases. We assessed the relationship between changes in body mass index (BMI) during TB treatment with prevalence of post-TB metabolic syndrome, a strong predictor of cardiometabolic diseases. Methods We enrolled a prospective cohort of individuals successfully treated for TB disease in Tbilisi, Georgia, from 2019–2022. title: That’s not what a uterus looks like: representations of female reproductive anatomy produced by Adobe Stock creators and the generative AI tools they use
abstract: The production of medical illustrations has traditionally required professional skills in illustration, knowledge of human anatomy, and access to reference material such as cadavers, specimens, or surgical photos. The ability of generative AI tools to rapidly produce visually compelling illustrations introduces new issues in trustworthiness of medical illustrations. We collected representations of the female reproductive system on the Adobe Stock platform that had been created with generative AI. title: An interdisciplinary perspective on the interpretation of legal‐scientific concepts in rights‐of‐nature initiatives
abstract: Abstract Despite an ever‐growing body of environmental laws, biodiversity loss and climate breakdown persist globally. This has prompted debate over whether existing legal regimes can be strengthened sufficiently to address these crises, or whether more transformative legal approaches are needed The concept of rights of nature , which is gaining traction worldwide, represents one such transformative approach by recognising ecosystems as rights‐bearing entities. title: Tribal Culture, Lifestyle, and Sustainable Development: A Path of Harmony with Nature
abstract: Introduction: This paper explores the sustainable lifestyle practices of tribal communities in Andhra Pradesh, focusing on their deep-rooted connection with nature. The history of human evolution is a story of adaptation, survival and transformation, and while some early groups chose permanent settlements, tribes continued a mobile existence deeply connected to the natural world. title: Dilemmas of engagement: local government officials’ perspectives on roles and responsibilities in climate change adaptation in rural and remote Nordic municipalities
abstract: As climate change impacts intensify across the Nordic countries, calls for deeper and more sustained citizen engagement in adaptation efforts have become increasingly prominent in both national and local policy agendas. This shift has spurred growing scholarly interest in how citizen responsibilisation is reshaping the roles and responsibilities of local government officials. While existing research has predominantly focused on urban contexts, this article examines local government officials in remote rural municipalities in Denmark and Norway. title: The Body as a Bridge Between Earth and Mars: Tai Chi Culture and the Human Art of Space Adaptation
abstract: Long-duration spaceflight raises a human question as well as an engineering one: how can crews maintain physical coordination, emotional steadiness, and supportive relationships when familiar conditions change? This conceptual article introduces the Cosmo-Embodied Adaptation Framework, a research map for connecting Tai Chi (Taijiquan, 太极拳) cultural practices with specific questions about space adaptation. title: Mito-nuclear discordance in a genus of darkling beetles (Coleoptera: Tenebrionidae: Dailognatha ) reveals both incomplete lineage sorting and introgression driven by complex island paleogeography
abstract: Abstract Phylogenetic studies of insular radiations have traditionally relied on mitochondrial DNA, yet the increasing availability of genomic datasets has revealed numerous cases of phylogenetic discordance between mitochondrial and nuclear markers across animal taxa. The present study focuses on the Aegean Dailognatha, a group of six predominantly insular darkling beetle species. title: Traditional versus Next-Generation Probiotics for the Control of Multidrug-Resistant Enterococci: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract: Multidrug-resistant enterococci, particularly vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE), represent an important clinical challenge because of their antimicrobial resistance, intestinal persistence, and potential for transmission and infection. The limited effectiveness of conventional antimicrobial approaches in preventing intestinal colonization has increased interest in microbiome-based strategies, including traditional probiotics and next-generation probiotics (NGPs). title: Carbon credits as market-based mechanisms for climate mitigation: Opportunities, challenges and future perspectives
abstract: Carbon credits are a promising market-based tool for combating climate change, biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation, three of the most pressing environmental problems currently facing the global environment. Carbon credit schemes have stimulated investments in renewable energy, forestry, sustainable agriculture, soil carbon management and decreased emissions by putting a monetary value on greater carbon sequestration and reduced emissions. title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza as a systemic risk - implications for control and preparedness
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has evolved from episodic outbreaks into a globally entrenched, multi-host panzootic, with recurrent spillover into mammals. The expanding host range and increasing wildlife–livestock interfaces challenge traditional control strategies, increase opportunities for viral adaptation, and thereby elevate zoonotic risk. We therefore propose that HPAI should be reframed as a long-term systemic risk requiring resilience-based governance, and strengthened One Health control and preparedness.

title: Mapping In Silico Strategies for Natural Product-Derived Candidates in Atopic Dermatitis: A Bibliometric Analysis and Methodological Review
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease with a complex pathogenesis involving multiple molecular targets and biological pathways. The multicomponent nature of natural products broadens the range of potential compound-target interactions, supporting the use of in silico approaches to identify and prioritize therapeutic candidates. This review aimed to map the development of in silico strategies used to prioritize natural product-derived candidates for AD and to evaluate how these strategies have been applied across the literature. title: Digital traceability for end-of-life battery recovery in green ports: government cost sharing and supply-chain decisions
abstract: As batteries are widely used in port operation vehicles, cargo handling equipment, and fixed energy storage systems, ports need to establish reliable mechanisms for battery recycling and disposal. This study develops a Stackelberg model led by a battery system integrator, with an authorized recovery service provider and a representative green-port operator. title: Climate Change Evidence: Driving Value-Added Use for Better Decisions
abstract: This article examines the evolving ecosystem of climate solution evidence tools and distinguishes the different functions they serve, including evidence aggregation, assessment of evidence strength, comparison of solution options, spatial targeting, policy benchmarking, and adaptive management. Drawing from research on evidence-informed policymaking and climate decision science, the authors identify persistent barriers to evidence use, including misalignment with decision needs, deep uncertainty, institutional incentives, and limited capacity for collective sensemaking. abstract: ABSTRACT Sand mining is widely recognized as one of the most significant threats to river health in the Lower Mekong Basin, where intensive extraction interacts with sediment starvation, hydropower development, climate variability, and delta subsidence to produce complex, transboundary environmental impacts. Yet despite expanding scientific evidence on channel incision, bank instability, salinity intrusion, and socio‐ecological risk, governance interventions remain largely reactive and unevenly effective. title: Human vs. AI: A Comparative Analysis of Translating Near-Synonymy in the Quran
abstract: Near-synonymy in the Qur’an challenges translators because related lexical items can differ in intensity, scope, expressive force, and contextual function. This exploratory qualitative study compares selected English expressions by Arberry and Irving with excerpts reported as GPT-4 outputs. Eleven lexical items in ten verse contexts are examined through a translation-oriented adaptation of Murphy’s Relation by Contrast approach. title: Urban Accessibility, Housing Prices and Socio-Economic Status: A Spatial Analysis of Istanbul Neighbourhoods
abstract: Multidimensional accessibility shapes both housing markets and the socio-economic composition of neighbourhoods, yet fine-grained evidence from rapidly urbanising contexts remains limited. This study examines how pedestrian accessibility to 88 urban services relates to listed housing prices and socio-economic status across 816 Istanbul neighbourhoods with at least 1,000 residents. title: Mapping the exposome of Zimbabwean preschool-aged children using a novel peptide microarray approach
abstract: Immune responses vary substantially between individuals and populations, reflecting differences in genetics, environment, and cumulative antigenic exposures. Characterizing these exposures, or the immunological exposome, is essential for understanding population-specific immune development, susceptibility to infection, and responses to interventions. title: Localizing water and climate SDGs: comparative insights from Ecuador and Switzerland’s governance contexts
abstract: Abstract Localizing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is critical for achieving global sustainability, yet translating international commitments into actionable local policies remains challenging, not least because interdependent goals require coherent implementation. This article examines how external pressure, local capacity, and local demand condition coherent SDG localization at the level of discourse, norms, and institutions.
