abstract: Planetary Health Knowledge (PHK) refers to knowledge about global conditions and interrelations between the health of the planet, human health, and human civilization. In times of various humanitarian and environmental crises, knowledge about and awareness of these problems become increasingly important. This is reflected in the Sustainable Development Goals and various Global Citizenship Education programs that emphasize the importance of knowledge about global challenges as a key characteristic in promoting sustainability. title: Uncontested Transnational Identity: The Activation, Strengthening and Superiority of Nordic Identity in Finland’s EU Debate of the 1990s
abstract: This article investigates the activation and transformation of Nordic identity during a critical political juncture in the early 1990s with respect to EU membership discussions in the Finnish Parliament. Triggered by Sweden’s pursuit of EC membership in 1990 and the post-Cold War context, the discourse surrounding Nordicness gained significance as Finland, Sweden, and Norway prepared for the 1994 membership referenda. title: From Reactivity to Proactivity: The Use of Behavioural Data in Life and Health Insurance
abstract: Abstract Traditional life and health insurance compensates after the fact, acting reactively in response to adverse events. Today, the rise of digital technologies enables insurers to intervene proactively, monitoring policyholders’ behaviour and incentivizing lifestyle changes intended to reduce risks before they materialize. This article argues that the shift from reactivity to proactivity marks a profound transformation in the temporal logic and social role of insurance. title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of urbanisation induced environmental quality in arid city using a grid-based analysis in Jodhpur India from 2001 to 2021
abstract: Rapid urbanisation in arid regions intensifies heat exposure, vegetation loss, and particulate pollution, yet medium-sized desert cities remain underrepresented in integrated environmental assessments. We quantified spatiotemporal changes in environmental quality in Jodhpur, India, from 2001 to 2021 using a novel grid-based Environmental Quality Index (EQI). abstract: The increasing number of Indonesian citizens (WNI) departing the country by providing false information (misrepresentation) has become a challenge in the implementation of immigration supervision, particularly in preventing trafficking in persons (TIP) and the non-procedural placement of Indonesian migrant workers (PMI). title: Commercial Floriculture in Kerala, India: Major Cut Flowers, Production, Marketing and Business Prospects
abstract: Commercial floriculture in Kerala must reconcile the biological suitability of tropical ornamentals with the exacting requirements of a perishable, quality-differentiated market. This critical narrative review examines the principal cut-flower groups relevant to the state, their production systems, postharvest constraints, marketing arrangements and business prospects. abstract: The democratic health and pupils' involvement are positively related. This study attempts to do so by studying the associations among internal psychological resources (psychological well-being), institutional trust, and civic involvement, an empirical gap. abstract: This study aims to describe: (1) the planning and integration of the Pancasila and Rahmatan Lil Alamin Student Profiles (P5RA) to enhance meaningful learning; (2) teacher strategies, challenges, and solutions; and (3) the impact on students' learning at MI Al Hikmah Kajen and MI Al Fattah Juwana. abstract: BACKGROUND: Medication adherence is a persistent challenge in the treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and HIV. Routine counseling notes are an underutilized source of information on patient adherence context. METHODS: We applied natural language processing (NLP) to routine counseling notes from a randomized controlled trial of MDR-TB/HIV treatment in South Africa. title: Permutations of settler colonial rule in Gaza: A generational approach
abstract: This article mobilises generation as a lens for theorising and examining the contingent and permuting character of settler colonial formations, with a specific focus on Gaza. Generation, we argue, calls attention to settler colonial rule as situated and embodied, and temporalities of survival and resistance as layered and heterogenous. abstract: Abstract Visual environmental perception is the safety cornerstone of autonomous driving, yet robust vehicle detection remains challenging under intense glare, occlusion, and adverse weather. Although YOLOv11 provides an efficient baseline, it suffers from coupled frequency-spatial extraction and inadequate long-range dependency modeling, leading to misdetections of occluded or distant targets. abstract: Objectives This study investigated the effects of a nanocomposite comprising N-acyl -homoserine lactonase Est816 and silver nanoparticles (Ag-Est816) on the microbial community of an enriched in vitro biofilm model derived from supragingival plaque of children with early childhood caries (ECC). title: Reinforcement Learning‐Based Sliding Variable Optimal Control for Canonical Nonlinear Systems With Unknown Control Direction
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a sliding variable‐based optimal control (SVBOC) framework for canonical nonlinear systems with unknown control direction. The approach integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with neural network (NN) approximation to address the challenge of solving the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation in systems with unknown dynamics. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive national-scale assessment of biomethane potential from organic waste streams in Qatar, evaluating its impact on two strategic climate mitigation pathways: (1) sustainable energy in water supply and agriculture, and (2) potential natural-gas substitution in Qatar’s gas-to-liquids (GTL) industry. abstract: Abstract Ice crystal microphysical properties govern cirrus cloud radiative effects, yet their representation in climate models remains inadequate due to insufficient understanding of how thermodynamic histories control crystal morphology. Observational platforms provide only instantaneous snapshots of cloud properties, precluding direct measurement of the growth environments that determine final crystal structure. abstract: Introduction The World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement, adopted in May 2025, represents a major step toward strengthening global pandemic governance after COVID-19. abstract: This study examines the role of school leadership in promoting child safety and well-being in a public basic education school in Dumaguete City, Philippines. Anchored in an integrated leadership–school climate–child safety and well-being framework, it adopts a quantitative, descriptive-correlational, cross-sectional design. abstract: This study examines Piil Pesenggiri as the basic framework of education based on local wisdom and its role in promoting cultural identity and social cohesion among the people of Lampung Pepadun. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach, with a case study in Baradatu District, Way Kanan Regency. title: Big Fish Sinks Tourist Season: An Introductory Cost Accounting Case
abstract: ABSTRACT This teaching case study is designed for students in introductory managerial accounting classes and integrates the fictional events of the movie Jaws with real‐world financial data from Martha's Vineyard Island and the fishing industry. The case study reinforces key concepts of cost–volume–profit analysis, special‐order decisions, and managerial decision‐making in conditions of uncertainty. abstract: Programs that compute with physical quantities often need to convert between units of measurement, and as the Mars Climate Orbiter showed, these conversions can be a rich source of errors. title: Properties of biodiversity indices that incorporate future extinction risk
abstract: The loss of biodiversity due to the likely widespread extinction of species in the near future is a focus of current concern in conservation biology. One approach to measure the impact of this extinction is based on the predicted loss of phylogenetic diversity. These predictions have become a focus of the Zoological Society of London's 'EDGE2' program for quantifying biodiversity loss and involves considering the HED (heightened evolutionary distinctiveness) and HEDGE (heightened evolutionary distinctiveness and globally endangered) indices which are based on phylogenetic diversity on a tree.

abstract: The article examines the design and operating principle Launch and Recovery Systems (LARS) for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) based on unmanned boats (UBs) of various purposes. abstract: Diving accidents remain frequently fatal, and most stem from preventable human factors: panic, failed buoyancy control, and disorientation. title: Platformisation, Political Change and Democracy in Southeast Asia – for a Labour Turn in Digital Media Studies
abstract: Abstract In this paper, I examine the relationship between increasing digitalisation and platformisation on one side, and political mobilisation and political change in Southeast Asia on the other. Southeast Asia presents a particularly instructive case, as the penetration of social media and digital platforms is highly advanced — among the highest in the world — while political systems are undergoing dynamic transformations. title: Heterogeneous multi-AUV cooperative area search with an LLM-assisted hierarchical planning framework
abstract: In heterogeneous multi-AUV cooperative area search, existing methods often decompose the task region before assigning sub-regions to individual AUVs. However, coverage costs associated with platform capability differences, time-energy coupling, and temporal coordination constraints are often insufficiently considered during region decomposition, which may lead to suboptimal partitions and capability-task mismatches. title: Low-cost single-beam SONAR localization in AUVs: Systematic experiments with acoustic and optical perception
abstract: This work presents a low-cost acoustic sensing framework for underwater robot (UWR) localization and perception, using single-beam sonars (SBS) and an external forward-looking sonar (FLS) for confined environments in place of costlier Doppler velocity logs (DVL) and onboard imaging suites. Instead of utilizing an SBS for depth estimation alone, an SBS unit each is also used in surge and sway directions for localization. abstract: The destruction of the Kakhovka Hydroelectric Power Plant in 2023 resulted in a dramatic alteration of the hydrological regime of the Lower Dnieper and, consequently, in two overlapping processes. On the one hand, extensive areas previously submerged were exposed through large-scale drainage; on the other, intensified erosion of the shoreline within the former riverbed occurred as a result of uncontrolled water discharge. title: Evidence of an acetone carboxylation pathway in photoheterotrophic bacteria from the Arctic Ocean
abstract: Carboxylases are among the most important enzymes in nature as they catalyze the fixation of inorganic carbon (CO2), a central step in the global carbon cycle. In addition to their well-known function in autotrophic CO2 fixation, many carboxylases play a role in the heterotrophic assimilation of organic compounds. In this study, we provide genomic evidence for an assimilatory carboxylation pathway involved in acetone degradation in photoheterotrophic bacteria from metagenomes collected along a latitudinal transect of the Arctic Ocean. title: Length-weight relationships of 27 coastal fish species caught during exploratory fishery survey cruises in the Western Bay of Bengal, India
abstract: Fishery-independent exploratory survey cruises were conducted to sample coastal fish communities in the Western Bay of Bengal during the 2019-2020 period. Fishing operations were carried out using a bottom trawl net at depths ranging from 30-200 m, with a total of 169 hauls, and an actual fishing effort of 230.5 hrs. In this study, the length-weight relationships (LWR) of 27 coastal fish species belonging to 18 families were modelled using the power function, and the model parameters (a and b) were estimated for each species. abstract: Deep-sea unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) depend on reliable propulsion systems during cruising, docking, and observation missions. However, online propulsion health monitoring remains challenging because high-frequency reference states are difficult to obtain in real time, while the nonlinear dynamics of UUVs make the relationship between thruster inputs and state responses difficult to characterize accurately. title: Seasonal environmental assessment of PEMFC/BOP components in a ship hybrid propulsion system under Baltic Sea and North Sea conditions
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the impact of the marine environment on selected components of a ship hybrid propulsion system, including the PEMFC/BOP section (auxiliary equipment), structural elements and mountings. The analysis was carried out for Baltic Sea conditions, with four seasons, two exposure levels and North Sea reference scenarios with high chloride deposition. title: Development of the Range of Value (ROV) Method Based on Dynamic Weighting for Decision Support Systems
abstract: Decision-making in complex environments requires an evaluation framework capable of integrating multiple criteria with different levels of importance and performance. This study proposes Dynamic-ROV, a modified Rank Order Value approach designed to evaluate alternatives through data-driven criterion weighting and utility-based assessment. The proposed procedure consists of decision matrix normalization, standard deviation-based criterion weighting, best and worst utility evaluation, final utility calculation, and ranking. abstract: An underwater flexible joint-flexible link robotic manipulator (UFJFLRM) mounted on the autonomous underwater vehicles (AUV) can significantly enhance operating ranges, facilitating precise underwater grasping and inspection operations. However, in flowing water environments, the UFJFLRM is subject to hydrodynamic disturbances, dynamic parameters variation caused by the changes in grasping different object, and inherent joint/link flexibility, resulting in rotational angle fluctuations that degrade control performance. title: From surface to deep sea: A depth-resolved vertical profile of microplastics in the Canary Basin
abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination of the open ocean is well documented, yet the vertical structuring of MPs and the role of water masses in shaping deep-water inventories remain poorly resolved along the eastern boundary of the North Atlantic Subtropical Gyre. Here we present a high-resolution vertical profile of MPs in the Canary Basin, based on discrete water samples collected during the MSM/127 cruise (R/V Maria S. abstract: The cruise industry plays a pivotal role in the development of the tourism sector of nations. Yet, policies to attract cruise liners to call at a cruise terminal are still questionable. To fill literature gaps, the purpose of the study is to discuss the selection of cruise carriers (CCs) at ports of call. abstract: Slope failures and submarine landslides formation in the northern Emperor Seamounts Chain, the northern section of the Hawaiian-Emperor Ridge, were studied using bathymetric and seismic data. These data were obtained during cruise SO201-1a on the research vessel Sonne, carried out in frames of the Russian- German KALMAR project. title: Quantitative Study of Methane Sequestration by Hydrate-Encapsulated Bubbles at Cold Seeps: Kinetic Characteristics and Environmental Implications
abstract: Abstract Cold seeps are a major source of natural methane emissions from the seafloor and regulate the global ocean carbon cycle. Hydrate formation serves as a key natural barrier restricting methane escape, but its kinetic mechanisms remain poorly quantified due to limited in situ monitoring capabilities. Here, we employ time-series Raman spectroscopy to conduct quantitative monitoring of methane hydrate growth kinetics and coupled methane sequestration behavior across various fluid-bubble flows. title: Differentiated Design Strategies for Cruise Interior Styles Across Different Itineraries
abstract: With the global cruise market expanding, China’s cruise industry is transitioning from scale growth to high-quality, differentiated development. Cruise ship interiors, as specialized consumption spaces, must move beyond homogeneous designs copying international standards to meet diverse passenger needs and build competitive advantages. This study constructs a systematic framework for differentiated interior design based on regional culture, passenger demands, and engineering constraints. title: In-water ship hull cleaning: an unregulated source of hazardous organic contaminants to marine environments
abstract: In-water hull cleaning (IWC) is a recognized source of paint-derived contaminant release to marine environments, yet the dissolved organic chemical fraction of IWC effluents remains poorly characterized. Here, we investigated IWC effluents from four vessels, two container vessels (Ship A and B), a research vessel (Ship C), and a RO-RO ship (Ship D), at three major South Korean ports (Busan, Gwangyang, and Jangmok) to characterize hull-cleaning-associated dissolved organic contaminants. title: Riserless Drilling: The Technique to Contain Shallow Hazards in Deepwater Exploration Wells
abstract: Deepwater exploration often faces tight drilling margins from the mudline, with pelagic rocks and an overburden-parallel pore-pressure profile. Because seismic imaging cannot effectively resolve shallow-water overpressured sands, a precisely planned well is essential to reach the planned total depth. abstract: Standardizing underwater workforce competency represents a vital strategic imperative to guarantee structural integrity and execution safety for national strategic infrastructure projects. This research analyzes the strategic role of the Naval Diving and Underwater Salvage Command (Koppeba Koarmada RI) in establishing competency certification for subaquatic technical personnel supporting the Giant Sea Wall megaproject. abstract: To address spatiotemporal response mismatch and cross layer parameter coupling in USV-UAV cooperative control under complex sea states, this paper proposes a three layer architecture optimized by stage wise sequential hierarchical Bayesian optimization (HBO). abstract: The aim of this study is to examine how residents’ perceptions of cruise tourism in a spatially constrained heritage city are structured across multiple domains and which perceptual dimensions most strongly affect support for further cruise tourism growth. Using a resident survey in Kotor, Montenegro (N = 214), this study develops seven standardised composite indices and combines cluster analysis, MANOVA and hierarchical regression to reveal how perceptions cohere and what drives support for cruise tourism growth. title: Data, Movement and Capital on the Bay of Bengal: ‘View in the Island of Narkondam’ by Robert Hyde Colebrooke (1787)
abstract: This article discusses how seascapes became an issue of datafication in the British East India Company’s campaign toward global economic hegemony in the later 18th century. It focuses on a series of expeditions launched by the Company to explore the Bay of Bengal in the 1780s and discusses the work of surveyors, hydrographers, draughtsmen and other kinds of (both human and machine) ‘sensors’ employed to investigate logistically important locations and passages. abstract: A new aetideid species, Pseudotharybis janetgrievei sp. nov., is described from female specimens collected near the seafloor in the abyss of the Guinea Basin of the equatorial Atlantic Ocean. abstract: The escalating geopolitical volatility in the South China Sea and the widening military asymmetry in the Indo-Pacific have compelled Indonesia to reassess its national security posture fundamentally. abstract: Currently, total contribution of blue economy to Pakistan’s economy is 95% which is mainly based on maritime trade. There is currently negligible amount of contribution of maritime/ Coastal Tourism to the total revenue of the country. The motive of the study is to highlight the prospect of maritime tourism in growth and development of blue economy of Pakistan. abstract: Nitrogen isotope (δ 15 N) records preserved in mollusc shells have strong potential to reconstruct changes in nitrogen sources, transformations and transport in the ocean beyond instrumental observations. abstract: Kellia porculus Pilsbry, 1904, is recorded for the first time in the Russian waters of the Sea of Japan along the coast of Primorye (Valentin, Olga, Rynda bays and Tatarsky Strait). abstract: Bivalve aquaculture and land-based pollution increasingly affect benthic ecosystems in Jiaozhou Bay along the southern Yellow Sea coast of China. Meiofauna and macrofauna are key components of benthic communities and are widely used as indicators of ecosystem health, yet their responses to aquaculture impacts and environmental gradients remain poorly understood. title: Colonial Environmental Governance in Maluku (1652–1799): Historical Insights from Hongi Tochten
abstract: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) maintained its clove monopoly in the Maluku Islands through Hongi Tochten, a series of naval expeditions traditionally interpreted as instruments of military coercion and commercial control. However, their role as mechanisms of environmental governance has received limited scholarly attention. This study examines how Hongi Tochten unctioned as a system of colonial environmental governance and analyses its implications for indigenous social–ecological systems in Maluku between 1652 and 1799. title: Tropical Bastions: It’s Time for a Pacific Bastion Strategy in the First Island Chain
abstract: This article proposes an operational approach to the use of naval forces in the first island chain of the Pacific vis-à-vis the threat of the People’s Liberation Army Navy of China and its attempts to enforce the nine-dash line. It argues that geography, deception, and mobility, particularly in the Philippine Archipelago, offer policy makers and military planners opportunity for the employment of naval forces in natural inland sea bastions. title: Pharmakos and Sacrificial Womanhood: The Politics of Social Order in Euripides’ Iphigenia at Aulis and Idegu’s the Legendary Inikpi
abstract: Communal survival, gender, tragedy and sacrifice are recurring subject matter in Greek and Igala cultural and literary traditions. This study compares Euripides’ Iphigenia at Aulis and Idegu's The Legendary Inikpi to examine how sacrificial womanhood is constructed and used to sustain social order within two distinct cultural logics. abstract: Background: The global and Indonesian maritime sector requires accounting systems capable of addressing distinctive transaction characteristics, operational risks, and sustainability demands. abstract: This paper examines the pivotal role of cultural tourism in safeguarding regional history and ethnic identity, focusing on the I.V. Savitsky State Museum of Arts in Nukus, Uzbekistan. Known globally as the "Louvre of the Desert," the museum holds a unique dual repository consisting of the world's second-largest collection of Soviet avant-garde art and an extensive archive of traditional Karakalpak applied arts alongside ancient Khorezm archaeological antiquities. abstract: The objective of this research was to examine the morphological and descriptive morphometric characteristics of two sand crab species of the genus Macrophthalmus found in the rocky intertidal zone in Manado Bay, North Sulawesi. Three individuals of Macrophthalmus (Mareotis) purpureocheir were collected during the new moon phase, while one individual of Macrophthalmus (Mareotis) crinitus was collected during the first quarter moon phase. title: Methane oxidation in African lakes increases with phytoplankton and outweighs photosynthesis-driven oxic methane production
abstract: Lakes are large natural sources of methane (CH4), a potent greenhouse gas, resulting from the net balance of inputs from anaerobic and oxic methane production (OMP) and removal by methane oxidation (MOX). Here we investigate spatial patterns and causes of MOX variability in 79 African lakes. MOX is highest in the most productive lakes presumably due to methanotrophs attached to phytoplankton, as well as in lakes draining the wetlands of the Congo basin presumably due to inputs of methanotrophs from flooded forest soils. title: High-Altitude Exposure: Effects on Cognitive Performance, Neurovascular Mechanisms, and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Abstract Travel to and work at high altitudes expose individuals to hypobaric hypoxia; however, its effects on neural activity and function remain insufficiently understood. Here, we present findings from a longitudinal panel study incorporating oxygen supplementation tests in individuals who traveled from low altitude (Beijing, ∼50 meters above sea level (m.a.s.l.)) to high altitude (Xizang, 3600–5000 m.a.s.l.) and subsequently returned to low altitude. title: The Intertidal Hydroids of Mount Desert Rock, Maine
abstract: We examined the intertidal hydroids of Mount Desert Rock, ME, a remote island in the Gulf of Maine. Our study was conducted concurrently with a long-term ecological survey. We collected 20 specimens of hydroids in June through August 2023 and identified these specimens using a combination of morphological keys and DNA barcoding with the 16S rRNA gene. We recorded 13 species representing 6 families and 12 genera. Our investigation reveals a diverse group of species not reflected in modern ecological surveys and represents the first inventory of hydroid species for this island.

title: Conservation Messages as Catalysts of Post-Visit Action: Insights from Zoo and Aquarium Visitors
abstract: Zoos and aquariums face an urgent challenge to convey conservation messages that motivate visitors to change their environmental behavior. This study explores the reflections of 768 visitors to one of twelve zoos and aquariums in Australia, USA, and Canada regarding the features of conservation messaging that prompted their post-visit involvement in specific environmental behaviors. Thematic analysis uncovered eight features of conservation messaging that visitors felt prompted them to adopt new behaviors or increase their engagement in existing environmental actions. title: Estimating biomass density in land-based cultivation of Ulva spp. using a low cost RGB imaging system
abstract: Abstract Seaweed cultivation faces scalability challenges due to labor-intensive biomass monitoring. Here, we demonstrate a low cost RGB imaging system for Ulva spp. biomass estimation (0.5–5.0 g L − 1 ) in land-based raceways. title: Acoustic emission monitoring of infrastructure using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) techniques - possibilities, limitations, and optimization
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) testing is an established method for structural health monitoring and damage detection in engineering structures. Conventional AE systems are based on piezoelectric sensors that are applied at discrete locations, requiring extensive cabling and offering limited spatial coverage. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) provides an alternative approach as a fiber-optic measurement technique, in which a single optical fiber cable serves as a continuous, spatially distributed sensor. In this work, both methods are systematically compared with respect to their detection capability

title: An annotated district-wise account of Odonata (Dragonflies and Damselflies) from Uttarakhand, India
abstract: This study presents a list of 135 odonate species recorded from Uttarakhand, based on an extensive and critical review of published literature. Notes on the present status of some recorded taxa are included. The documented diversity includes 15 families and 73 genera, comprising 84 species of Anisoptera and 51 species of Zygoptera. Among the districts, Dehradun has the highest recorded species richness, followed by Nainital and Pauri Garhwal. Five species recorded are endemic to India. abstract: Mangroves are ecologically vital ecosystems that present unique logistical challenges for field-based environmental education and research due to seasonal tidal fluctuations, difficult muddy terrain, and visitor safety considerations. Balancing sustainable conservation with accessible site exploration requires innovative approaches. abstract: The siphonostomatoid copepod Dirivultus spinigulatus Humes, 1999 (Dirivultidae) was originally described as an associate of the siboglinid tubeworm Paraescarpia echinospica Southward, Schulze, and Tunnicliffe, 2002 from the Edison Seamount hydrothermal vent in Papua New Guinea. title: Carbon intensity compliance of a crude oil tanker: A five-year voyage-level analysis
abstract: The Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) of ships is evaluated annually; however, this aggregated calculation may conceal substantial variation in carbon intensity across different voyage types. To investigate how voyage parameters affect CII outcomes, this study presents a five-year (2020–2024) voyage-level empirical analysis of a Suezmax crude oil tanker. abstract: This paper examines the civilizational role of the Arabian Gulf islands as depicted in classical sources from the 4th century BCE to the 4th century CE. Classical Greek and Roman historians and geographers produced a wealth of significant scholarly works that serve as authoritative references for the history of regions within their sphere of interest and influence, most notably the Ancient Near East, the Arabian Peninsula, and the Arabian Gulf region in particular. abstract: Recently the phylogeny of the order Neogastropoda based on exon-capture [Fedosov et al., 2026], has confirmed the monophyly of the group and achieved high resolution for many deep nodes. Thorough examination of the sequenced species frequently revealed novel and distinctive morphological characters, and in several cases highlighted unresolved taxonomic issues. abstract: We integrate demography, morphology and genetics to assess the biology and population structure of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat (Zyzomys woodwardi), a habitat specialist of the monsoonal tropics. The species is confined to the extreme north-west of the continent and 16 adjacent islands that were part of the mainland during the last Pleistocene glaciation. abstract: The increasing development of Wing-in-Ground (WIG) craft as an energy-efficient maritime transportation system has highlighted the importance of integrating environmental protection into the early stages of vessel design. title: Sustainability comparison of petrol and electric small boats on Lake Balaton: A life cycle and total cost analysis
abstract: Because Lake Balaton is shallow and ecologically fragile, the regulation of small-boat traffic on the lake currently rests mainly on propulsion type: recreational use of internal-combustion-powered small boats is effectively prohibited. In contrast, purely electric-powered boats may operate freely. This study examines the environmental and economic differences between petrol and electric-powered small boats over their full life cycle, and considers what these differences imply for further developing the regulatory framework. title: Challenges of the assessment of nature conservation value of aquatic habitats using microalgae
abstract: Abstract The increasing focus on ecosystem restoration in European environmental policy highlights the need for reliable methods to quantify the nature conservation value (NCV) of aquatic habitats. Current Water Framework Directive (WFD) metrics assess ecological quality mainly through the phytoplankton community composition and abundance. title: Science as added value? Tourists’ perceptions of science-tourism practices in Antarctic deep-field tourism and implications for ambassadorship
abstract: This paper investigates the role of science-tourism practices in shaping tourists’ perceptions and ethical positioning within Antarctic deep-field tourism. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in East Antarctica and semi-structured interviews, the study examines how operators’ support for science influences tourists’ pre-trip decision-making, perceptions of legitimacy, and environmental responsibility. abstract: ABSTRACT Relocating large hollows to minimise the potential impacts of development on threatened species is generally considered too difficult and/or too costly. title: Formation of the sclerites in Solenogastres and Caudofoveata (Mollusca, Aplacophora)
abstract: Solenogastres and Caudofoveata are vermiform, shell-less molluscs, with the mantle covered by calcareous scales or spines (sclerites) embedded in a cuticle secreted by the mantle epithelium. Molecular studies recover them as a single clade (Aplacophora), sister of Polyplacophora, and together, they form the sister group to all other molluscs. abstract: Food safety remains an absolute cornerstone of global public health and socioeconomic stability. Unsafe food causes an estimated 866 million illnesses and 1.52 million deaths globally each year, resulting in an annual economic loss of US$ 310 billion across the globe. The main objective of this mini-review is to synthesize current knowledge on foodborne pathogens, food additives, heavy metals, microplastics, emerging anthropogenic hazards, and advances in diagnostic methods. abstract: Multiagent settings are naturally characterized by coevolutionary dynamics, where agents must adapt and learn in the context of their teammates. A key challenge in such domains is determining how to credit an agent for its individual contribution to team performance. Fitness shaping approaches partially address this by identifying and isolating an agent's direct contribution to team success. title: Taxonomic and ecological assessment of an Antarctic Eocene Folivora (Mammalia) metacarpal using three‐dimensional geometric morphometrics
abstract: Here, we reassess the taxonomic affinities and functional morphology of TMM 44190-1, an isolated metacarpal II from the Eocene La Meseta Formation, Marambio (Seymour) Island, Antarctic Peninsula, previously referred to an indeterminate xenarthran. We evaluated its morphological similarities using three-dimensional geometric morphometrics. title: A high-throughput method for quantifying degradation in maritime PEM fuel cells using a multichannel potentiostat
abstract: The durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells under maritime conditions is influenced by the vessel's operational profile, for example idling and intermittent shutdowns. To investigate this, we introduce a high-throughput accelerated stress test (AST) methodology using a multichannel potentiostat to simultaneously analyze up to eight membrane electrode assemblies. Voltage hold ASTs identified 0.825 V as a practical upper limit for idling voltage, above which Pt oxidation and dissolution significantly accelerate electrochemical surface area (ECSA) loss. institutions: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
Centre for Research and Technology Hellas

title: “They can smell the ‘short-termness’ on you”. Student learning and sense of belonging in the Arctic
abstract: BACKGROUND: Student well-being is recognized as central to academic success, yet little is known about how extreme, isolated learning environments may shape this relationship. PURPOSE: To explore student's and staff's perception of student well-being and learning at the University Centre in Svalbard (UNIS), focusing on the Arctic context. METHODS: We used a qualitative, exploratory design, conducting semi structured interviews and focus groups with students and staff at UNIS. journal: International Journal of Qualitative Studies on Health and Well-Being
institutions: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

title: Regulatory Intermediation and Energy Transition Readiness at the Port of Keelung, Taiwan
abstract: International maritime environmental regulation is changing port sustainability from a predominantly local environmental-management task into a cross-organisational challenge involving vessels, energy systems, terminal operations, logistics customers, public authorities, and port-city communities. This article examines how the International Maritime Organization’s greenhouse-gas framework and the European Union’s FuelEU Maritime regime transmit strategic pressure to the non-EU Port of Keelung in Taiwan. The study develops a qualitative, embedded single-port research design that combines regula
journal: International Journal of Innovative Research in Engineering & Management

title: A Love Made of Stones: Contemporary Anishinaabe Lyric and Asiniig Sovereignty
abstract: This article delves into the literary motif of the stone (asiniig) in contemporary Anishinaabe poetry as an ontological assertion of Indigenous sovereignty. By synthesising Michelle Raheja’s “visual sovereignty” (2007) and Kenneth White’s “geopoetics” (1979; 2004), I trace how poets Kimberly Blaeser, Louise Erdrich, and Denise Sweet deploy an Indigenous geopoetics that challenges settler-colonial cartographies. I argue that these poets reconfigure the lyric mode from a passive backdrop of Western Romantic contemplation into an active, decolonial practice of relationality. In addition, this stu

title: A tengeralattjárók fejlődésének története
abstract: A tengeralattjárók fejlődése a haditechnika egyik legizgalmasabb és legdinamikusabb területe, amely a kezdeti, egyszerű víz alatti járművektől a modern, nukleáris meghajtású, nagy hatótávolságú tengeralattjárókig terjed. A cikk – nagy vonalakban - áttekinti a technológiai innovációk és a stratégiai alkalmazások fejlődését, valamint a tengeralattjárók szerepét a hadviselés és a tengerészeti biztonság területén.

title: Pérez de Ribas’ Historia (1645) and the Protohistoric Period in Sonora and Southern Arizona
abstract: The protohistoric period along the Arizona-Sonora borderlands is an important yet poorly understood period. Historical sources, particularly Perez de Ribas’ Historia (1645), are discussed along with archaeological data that point to a late prehistoric expansion of the Opata into O'odham lands. Evidence of warfare and invasion is presented that may help explain the appearance of forts and defensive retreats, Sobaipuri origins, and Eudeve/Teguima linguistics.

title: Water Bodies and Colonization of the Niger Delta, 1800 to 1900
abstract: It is a truism that water bodies provided the gateway for the colonization of the Niger Delta. The work argues that the explorers, missionaries and traders promoted European political and economic interests in the Niger Delta hence, the Lander Brothers through their exploration opened up the Delta for commerce and used the waterway to explore the interior while providing information of their findings to Britain. journal: American journal of social and humanitarian research.

title: Full‐Waveform Seismic Tomography of the Upper Mantle Beneath the Arabia‐Eurasia Collision Zone
abstract: Abstract Despite being one of the most recent major orogenic events, the timing of the Arabia‐Eurasia collision is still debated. Much of the discrepancy arises due to uncertainties over the amount of continental subduction of the Arabian passive margin and the timing of a hard collision of cratonic Arabian lithosphere with Eurasia. Subducted continental lithosphere and underthrusted cratons can be imaged using high resolution seismic tomography, which can be used to improve understanding of the tectonic history of the region. In this study, we perform a full waveform inversion of seismic wave
institutions: University of Texas Institute for Geophysics
The University of Texas at Austin
University at Buffalo, State University of New York

title: Outpacing: A Grand Strategy for Avoiding the Carthaginian Error
abstract: This article warns Western democracies against committing the Carthaginian error, that is, not taking a strategic rival seriously. It argues strategic rivals should be dealt with through a grand strategy of Outpacing, the aim of which is to establish a lead over them severe enough to cause their political and economic collapse, or their forfeiture of the competition.

title: The Fortified Disposition, Part I: Strategic Complexes, Historical Attenuation, and the Return of the Guarded City
abstract: Fortification is better understood as a movement-slowing strategic complex than as a wall that either holds or fails. This paper traces the long attenuation of that disposition in the West, then shows how scarce manpower, costly platforms and persistent surveillance are bringing it back—first of all in the guarded, closable city assembled through dual-use fabric, regulation and urban air defence.

title: Strategy and Contradiction: Towards a Theory of Strategic Judgement
abstract: Strategy is commonly concerned with relating political purposes to the means available for their achievement. This article asks a prior question: what conditions make strategic judgement necessary in the first place? It argues that strategic problems arise from the contradictory character of political life, in which competing purposes cannot be permanently reconciled, and every decision alters the circumstances confronting those that follow. Strategy therefore requires practical judgement rather than the application of predetermined solutions. Drawing upon Clausewitz and examining deterrence,

title: The Golden Dome, Missile Defenses and Deterrence
abstract: This article examines the Trump administration proposal for a Golden Dome missile defense system in terms of its implications for technology, strategy and U.S. national security policy. It also considers whether the proposed missile defense system, once having been deployed, will support deterrence as we now understand it, or require a rethinking of past assumptions about nuclear-strategic stability.

title: Research on Tourism Environmental Economy of Hainan Free Trade Port: Evolution Context, Hotspot Review and Frontier Prospect
abstract: As the highest form of opening-up in the global contemporary economy, the free trade port undertakes the strategic function of promoting institutional reform and high-quality regional development through opening-up. As the core experimental field of China’s open economic system with Chinese characteristics, Hainan Free Trade Port (Hainan FTP) deeply integrates tourism, ecological environment and economic development in its construction process, forming a unique research field of tourism environmental economy. Taking the tourism environmental economy of Hainan FTP as the research object, this p

title: FEATURES OF THE USE OF FIBER-OPTICAL TECHNOLOGIES FORINFORMATION SUPPORT OF DRONES USED IN MILITARY OPPOSITION TO THE AGGRESSOR
abstract: The article analyzes the current state and prospects of implementing fiber-optic technologies in unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) as an effective response to the challenges of modern electronic warfare. Their potential applications are considered both in the field of intelligence gathering and for the delivery of explosives to designated targets.The classification features of drones are systematized, their main functional purposes are defined, and the advantages and limitations of traditional radio-controlled systems are examined. Particular attention is paid to their vulnerability to electro
publisher: Open International University of Human Development Ukraine

title: Oligocene radiolarian fossil assemblage preserved within goethite concretions from the Nishinoomote Formation, Kumage Group distributed in Tanegashima Island, Kagoshima, SW Japan
abstract: 種子島中部の西海岸に分布する熊毛層群西之表層から産出した，コンクリーションの鉱物組成と内部に保存される放散虫化石群集を検討した．コンクリーションは，ゲーサイト及び石英で構成される緻密な外殻と，石英や斜長石といった母岩と同様の鉱物で構成される内部から構成される．本コンクリーション（ゲーサイトコンクリーション）の内部から放散虫化石が産出し，前期漸新世後期（放散虫化石帯RP20c帯下部〜RP21a帯中部）の年代を示した．本コンクリーションを含む層準付近の岩相も考慮すると，種子島北部に分布する西之表層とほぼ同時期の地層が種子島中部にも分布していることが判明した．本研究で検討したコンクリーションに類似した鉄酸化物の殻で覆われているコンクリーションは世界中で産出が報告されている．今後，より多くの微化石情報を得るための手段として，特に海成層に産出するこれらのコンクリーションの活用が期待される．
journal: The Journal of the Geological Society of Japan

title: Heteroptera (Insecta, Hemiptera) fauna of Eritrea
abstract: The suborder Heteroptera, commonly known as “true bugs,” represents the largest group within hemi-metabolous insects, comprising over 45,000 species. Eritrea, characterised by a Hot Semi-Arid to Hot Desert Climate, is notable for its four regional centres of vegetation endemism and approximately 430 woody plant species. This study aims to review and update the list of Heteroptera fauna recorded in Eritrea, based on existing historical literature. A total of 136 published works, spanning from 1870 to 2025, were reviewed. In total, 384 species across 236 genera and 40 families have been document

title: Trigonometrical Juridism in British India: Unificatory Images and Jurisdictional Rationality
abstract: Abstract This article engages with two aspects of how cartography enabled law and jurisdictional ordering in a specific historical context. First, by interrogating the ways in which the great trigonometrical surveys of the British colonial enterprise and the Atlas of India entrenched “India” as a distinct, coherent, and contiguous geographical entity, this article will demonstrate how an epistemology rooted in a civilising impulse produced the perception of India as a thoroughly refined British legal territory. Second, by engaging with the maps and records of colonial cadastral and revenue sur
journal: Asian Journal of Law and Society

title: Opegaster plateen n. sp. (Digenea: Opecoelidae) from the giant mudskipper Periophthalmus schlosseri (Pallas, 1770) (Perciformes: Gobiidae) from Thailand
abstract: Abstract Mudskippers (Oxudercinae) are amphibious gobioid fishes inhabiting intertidal and mangrove ecosystems throughout the Indo–West Pacific region. Despite their ecological importance, information on their helminth fauna remains scarce. During a survey of parasites infecting the giant mudskipper, Periophthalmodon schlosseri (Pallas, 1770), in Chumphon Province, Thailand, specimens of an undescribed species of Opegaster Ozaki, 1925 (Opecoelidae) were recovered from the intestine. The species is described herein as Opegaster plateen n. sp. on the basis of morphological and molecular evidence
institutions: King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang

title: Systemic risks for Greece’s economy and the need for its national strategy of new industrialization. Lessons for Ukraine
abstract: The research paper focuses on the structural imbalances in the Greek economy, which pose systemic risks to its development amid geopolitical turbulence, global trade wars and a slowdown in economic growth in EU countries – its main trading partners. The structural imbalances in the Greek economy are categorised into four interrelated groups, and the paper examines their causes and consequences. We analysed the core factors of the protracted and deep Greek financial and economic crisis, which entered its active phase in 2010 and lasted for almost ten years. institutions: Institute for Forecasting of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

title: Analysing user-generated overtourism posts on social media: a content analysis
abstract: Overtourism is an increasing concern for destinations seeking to accommodate visitor growth while protecting residents’ quality of life and long-term sustainability. Yet, how overtourism is represented through user-generated social media content remains underexplored. Drawing on destination image theory, this study analyses 600 Instagram posts tagged #overtourism to examine the visual themes, attraction types, sentiment, and thematic framing associated with overtourism. title: Archipelagic memories at Lau King Howe Hospital Memorial Museum
abstract: Colonial pasts, geopolitical differences, and plural social constructions of Malaya/post-independence Malaysia contributed to and were reflected in hospital design. Sarawak in East Malaysia, on Borneo Island, saw developments that paralleled those in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur. How did the multi-ethnic complexity of the patient demographic impact post-independence medical institutions? Situating this research in the region’s medical developments, this article explores hospital museums as repositories for institutional memories. Examples discussed include the urban Sarawak General Hospital in K
journal: Interstices Journal of Architecture and Related Arts

title: Influence Without Alliances: China, Pakistan, and Indirect Military Engagement in the Persian Gulf
abstract: This article examines how China expands security influence in the Persian Gulf without alliances, bases, or direct intervention. It introduces indirect military engagement to explain influence through technology diffusion, defence-industrial cooperation, intermediary partnerships, and partner adaptation. Focusing on Pakistan, it argues that Chinese systems gain regional relevance through Pakistani absorption, localisation, training, maintenance, and demonstration. journal: Asian Journal of Middle Eastern and Islamic Studies

title: Kåre Bremer: Synantherologist, Pioneer of Cladistics and Co-Architect of APG
abstract: Swedish botanist Kåre Bremer (b.1948) reshaped modern botany across three interconnected domains: the systematics of Compositae, the theory and practice of cladistics, and the phylogenetic classification of flowering plants. As a synantherologist, he produced foundational revisions of South African Gnaphalieae and Anthemideae, conducted the first comprehensive cladistic analysis of the entire Compositae family, and edited Asteraceae: Cladistics and Classification (1994), the first encyclopedic global treatment of the family in nearly a century, which remains a cornerstone of Compositae researc

title: Violating the Sacred Order: Sin, Punishment, and Ecological Consciousness in Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
abstract: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner by Samuel Taylor Coleridge explores themes of sin, guilt, retribution, and salvation. According to the research, the Mariner’s killing of the Albatross violates the sacred bond among humans, nature, and the divine and is a moral transgression. The study examines how Coleridge portrays punishment as a psychological and spiritual process rather than a consequence, drawing on the poem’s symbolism, supernatural imagery, and religious themes. The Mariner's pain, loneliness, incapacity to pray, and recounting of his tale serve as phases of moral development and repent

title: Modern Air Operations and Wylie’s Cumulative and Sequential Operational Patterns
abstract: Strategist Joseph Caldwell Wylie argued that strategies were implemented through two general types of operational patterns: sequential and cumulative. This article discusses the conceptualisations of these two patterns and then applies them to three modern air war cases to bring out their subtleties and nuances. Wylie’s simple typology has a surprising depth that makes it useful to air strategists when considering future air operations whether in peace of war.
journal: Contemporary Issues in Air and Space Power

title: Churns and Churning as a Solution for Preserving Excess Milk Yields and Surplus as Dairy Products: A Case Study from the Late Chalcolithic of the Southern Levant
abstract: Abstract The first clear evidence of advanced dairy production in the Southern Levant emerges during the Late Chalcolithic period. This shift is marked by the widespread discovery of clay churns across diverse geographic regions, alongside herd management practices and organic residue analyses that point to a dairy-oriented economy. A comprehensive study of Late Chalcolithic churns suggests that, alongside increased reliance on herds for milk production, churning became significant. title: First records of the millipede genus Hedinomorpha Verhoeff, 1934 (Diplopoda, Polydesmida, Paradoxosomatidae) from Vietnam, with descriptions of two new species
abstract: The millipede genus Hedinomorpha Verhoeff, 1934 is recorded in Vietnam for the first time with two new species, Hedinomorpha caobang sp. nov . and Hedinomorpha vast sp. nov . Both species are described and illustrated. The COI and 16S rRNA fragments are also provided for the two new species.
institutions: Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology

title: Life cycle assessment of diesel, e-diesel, and hydrotreated vegetable oil for passenger cars
abstract: Biofuels and electrofuels (e-fuels) are among the proposed options allowing the continued sale of new internal combustion engine light-duty vehicles beyond 2035. However, their environmental performance is still predominantly assessed through climate change indicators, overlooking potential burden shifting towards other impact categories. title: Supersonic sustainability transitions: an integrated life cycle and triple bottom line assessment with socio-technical transition lenses for next-generation passenger aircraft
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the environmental, economic and social sustainability of next-generation commercial supersonic transport and develops the Supersonic Sustainability Transition Assessment Model (SSTAM) to distinguish near-term actionable pathways from options dependent on wider socio-technical readiness. Design/methodology/approach SSTAM integrates ISO 14040/44-aligned life-cycle assessment, triple bottom line indicators, multi-criteria decision analysis, scenario and Monte Carlo uncertainty testing and socio-technical systems/multi-level perspective interpretation. title: The impact of behavioural activity on the EEG power spectrum, its source localisation, and global functional connectivity in rats
abstract: The behavioural activity of freely moving animals is a confounding factor that affects the recording, analysis, and final results of animal EEG experiments. Along with the lack of standardisation in animal in vivo electrophysiology experiments, this could lead to huge inconsistencies, especially in the analysis of centrally acting drugs. Therefore, the main aim of this paper is to investigate the effects of behavioural activity versus inactivity on the multichannel EEG in freely moving rats. title: Cosmo-currere: Conventional to circumspective
abstract: Through autobiographical study, I explore the relations of my lived experiences with my academic interests. Conversations are complicated not only by the singularity of the individual, but also by the world, conceived here as historical and biospheric. Engagements with the worlds of within and without and study through and on the method of currere (Pinar, 1975) structure the research. title: The Impact of the Stress Management in Improving the Instructor's Professional Efficacy in Mariners Polytechnic Colleges Foundation (MPCF) in Canaman, Province of Camarines Sur
abstract: Background: Teaching in maritime higher education places simultaneous demands on instruction, assessment, student support, and administrative work. Objective: The study described stress management and perceived professional efficacy among instructors at a Philippine maritime college, and compared rank patterns across program-size groups. Methods: A cross-sectional questionnaire was administered to 39 instructors during the second semester of academic year 2025–2026. abstract: Purpose. title: Sacred waters, gendered labour and survival: Ngamee women in the floating village of Loktak Lake
abstract: Loktak Lake in Manipur is more than an ecological resource — it is a deeply storied landscape embedded with material, cultural, and spiritual significance. Central to its ecological uniqueness is the phumdi , a floating biomass that supports both human habitation and rich biodiversity. However, state-led interventions like the construction of the Ithai Barrage in 1983 and the implementation of the Loktak Lake (Protection) Act, 2006, have disrupted the ecological balance and delegitimised indigenous lifeways by labelling native fisherfolk as ‘occupiers’. title: The Nucleus of the Brachium of the Inferior Colliculus Contains Thalamic‐Like and Midbrain‐Like Subregions
abstract: The ventral division of the medial geniculate body (MGV) is the core auditory thalamic nucleus and is bordered dorsally, medially, and ventrally by shell nuclei; a caudal shell counterpart has not been identified. The nucleus of the brachium of the inferior colliculus (nBIC), long viewed as a rostral extension of the midbrain IC, contains neurons that project to auditory and adjacent cortex, blurring the thalamus-midbrain boundary. abstract: Purpose. The aim of the work is to present aspects of semantics associated with sacrifices, identified in the materials of mound 7 of the Sargat culture of the Tartas-2 burial ground (Baraba forest-steppe). The authors’ attention is focused on the design of the ditches, the particularities of the placement of the lintels and the methods of their “closure”, and the localization of sacrifice in the grave structure. title: CHANGES IN WATER POLLUTION IN THE KARATAL RIVER DURING GLACIER SHRINKAGE IN THE SHYZHY AND KORA RIVER BASINS
abstract: This study examines the spatial and seasonal variability of water quality in glacier-fed river systems within the Karatal River basin, located in the north-western sector of the Zhetysu Alatau (Kazakhstan). The investigation focused on the Kora and Shyzhy rivers, which play a key role in forming the hydrological regime of the Karatal River. Fieldwork was carried out in 2025 and included two sampling campaigns (July and September), during which a total of 30 water samples were collected from the upper, middle, and lower river reaches. title: Mission Energy-Based Modelling to Assess the Performance and Feasibility of Battery-Powered Aircraft Retrofit: A Case Study of the BN-2B-26 Islander in Scotland
abstract: This study develops a mission energy-based framework to assess the performance and technical feasibility of retrofitting an existing commuter aircraft with battery-electric propulsion. The Britten-Norman BN-2B-26 Islander is selected as the case study aircraft for selected domestic routes in Scotland. A MATLAB-based parametric assessment framework was developed to evaluate aircraft and the feasibility of selected routes, and it integrates key design parameters including power, energy, battery system, operations and payload. title: Shaped by humans but increasingly threatened: pathways for the conservation of Palaearctic grasslands
abstract: Palaearctic grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems of the Northern Hemisphere, but their conservation depends on continued management that must be reconciled with agricultural production, rural livelihoods and other socio-economic demands. Introducing a special issue that brings together 18 contributions from across Eurasia, we synthesize the interacting pressures shaping these grasslands and identify pathways towards their effective conservation. title: An end-to-end conversational AI coach for heavy-duty eco-driving: An industrial case study
abstract: Heavy-duty trucks account for a disproportionate share of road-transport emissions, yet the eco-driving coaches deployed in commercial fleets typically deliver generic and opaque feedback. This paper reports an industrial case study, conducted with Volvo Group, of an end-to-end conversational AI coach for heavy-duty eco-driving. Per-segment LightGBM models predict fuel efficiency from vehicle-level telemetry aggregated over weekly to monthly windows for two operational segments, 5XT (50–59 t Gross Combined Weight) and 7XT (70–79 t). title: Historical Turning Point: the Battle of Zigetvar a Turning Point in Ottoman Military and Political History: The Siege of Szigetvar (1566)
abstract: The Siege of Szigetvar in 1566 was the closing move of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent's 46-year reign and one of the peak points of the Ottoman Empire's military strategies towards Western Europe in the 16th century. Historians examine the military, logistical, socio-economic, and political dimensions of the campaign with an interdisciplinary approach. This study provides a multifaceted investigation of the Siege of Szigetvár, comparing the defensive strategy of the fortress commander Nikola Šubić Zrinski with the siege, fortification, and artillery techniques of the Ottoman army. title: Chinese Expansionist Philosophy’s Historical Bacground
abstract: This article examines the historical foundations and contemporary manifestations of ideas commonly associated with Chinese expansionism. It asks how classical concepts such as Tianxia, Confucian moral authority, Legalist state capacity, and tributary relations are reinterpreted in present-day foreign policy. The study applies qualitative historical analysis, comparative political thought, discourse analysis, and a focused case study of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). title: The Mosses of Mount Muruk Mio and Bukit Rimau in Sipitang District of Sabah, Malaysian Borneo
abstract: This study presents the results of bryological surveys conducted in 2003 and 2012 on Mount Muruk Mio and Bukit Rimau in Sipitang, Sabah, Malaysian Borneo, with a focus on assessing species richness and composition of mosses. This trade, however, used, developed and altered independent forms of knowledge that relied heavily on skills and competencies formed through experience and familiarization. title: Work Stress, Coping Strategies, and Job Satisfaction Among Food Service Workers in Bohol: A Descriptive-Correlational Study
abstract: Work stress is a significant occupational concern in the food service industry, with documented links to burnout, emotional labor, reduced service quality, and turnover intentions. This study examined the relationships among perceived work stress, coping strategies, and job satisfaction among food service workers in Bohol, Philippines, and explored which stressor domains – particularly social support – are more salient in this context. title: ‘John Herschel's Preliminary Discourse (1830) and Manual of Scientific Enquiry (1849): the question of amateur contributions to elite science’
abstract: In his Preliminary Discourse (1830), John Herschel (1792-1871) set the scene for discussions of induction as the method of scientific inquiry, such as those carried on by William Whewell (1794-1866) and J. S Mill (1806-1873). Another less-noticed theme of his book is the focus on accumulation of empirical information in repositories as a necessary condition of major scientific discoveries. This preoccupation influenced Herschel's call for preliminary observations from untrained individuals - even though he emphasized that all observation required skill, experience and judgment. title: Apatite Geochemistry as a Key to Typification and Petrogenesis of Pegmatites from Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica
abstract: Apatite is a sensitive indicator of magmatic and post-magmatic processes in granitic and pegmatitic systems. This study investigates accessory apatite from different types of pegmatites and granites of Larsemann Hills (East Antarctica) in order to classify the pegmatites and reconstruct their formation conditions. The results show the Types I and III pegmatites crystallized at higher temperatures than Type IV pegmatites with miarolitic cavities and the Progress granites. abstract: Handling wild reptiles is common among amateur herpetology enthusiasts, professional researchers, social media influencers, and photographers. However, the potential for these interactions to spread diseases that threaten wild reptiles remains underappreciated. With the rise in such interactions due to today's socially connected landscape and the offering of an increased number of wildlife-focused ecotourism trips, the possibility of increased spread of human-vector-mediated reptile diseases is substantial. This article examines how these technologies are changing migrant smuggling connected to Brazil and the challenges they pose to intelligence and security in the Global South. abstract: The Neoperla (Formosita) lushana-group is revised using an integrative taxonomic approach combining morphological and molecular evidence. abstract: Travel serves as a doorway to other worlds and a tool for self-discovery, allowing travellers to transcend preconceptions and gain a more profound comprehension of individuals and locations. This paper explores how firsthand interactions with foreign cultures, environments, and social realities alter perception. Travellers frequently form opinions about a place before visiting it based on media, anecdotes, and other people's experiences. title: Multilevel risks and war related crisis severity shape tourist psychological distress and responses to crisis management
abstract: War-related crises exacerbate fear, insecurity, risk, and emotional tension. In light of these conditions, we propose and test a novel framework applying stress mindset theory to a war-crisis setting. Specifically, we investigate the effects of multilevel risks (personal, travel, and destination) on tourists’ psychological distress and subsequent emotional exhaustion. title: Active layer microbial inocula restore missing functions across thawed permafrost soils
abstract: Abstract Microbial dynamics in thawing permafrost induce a climate feedback of uncertain magnitude. Upon thaw, active layer microorganisms may establish in formerly frozen layers and introduce missing functions. Here we test the prevalence of functional limitations and how active layer microorganisms can mitigate these across four widespread permafrost types over 389 days. By restoring functions with a multifunctional microbial community, we demonstrate widespread functional limitations, as increased CO 2 emissions across four permafrost types, and onset N 2 O emissions in two of those. abstract: ABSTRACT Parallel evolution of similar phenotypes under similar selective pressures is often viewed as evidence for natural selection. abstract: This two-part essay addressed a two-part question: “If extraterrestrial life exists, then where are they?” and “Is interdimensional travel possible and, if so, how?” Drawing upon the insights of Jane Roberts’s philosophical psychology, the following thesis is advanced and defended: Alternate life planes and reality systems exist and make contact with the spacetime structure of our own physical universe at coordinate points through which non-human intelligent beings may travel that can be scientifically investigated utilizing both objective instrumentation and subjective tools. title: Book Forum | Land of famished beings: West Papuan theories of hunger
abstract: Sophie Chao's 2025 monograph, Land of Famished Beings, which received the 2026 Mid-Career Book Prize from the Asian Studies Association of Australia, examines how Indigenous Marind communities understand and theorise hunger in lowland West Papua, a place where industrial plantation expansion and settler-colonial violence are radically reconfiguring ecologies, socialities, and identities (Figure 1).By centering Indigenous feminist theories of hunger, Chao offers new ways of thinking about the relationship between the environment, food, and nourishment in an age of self-consuming capitalist grow

title: Predicting severe high-altitude de-acclimatization syndrome from pre-return exposure dose and laboratory indicators: a prospective cohort study of 475 males
abstract: Abstract High-altitude de-acclimatization syndrome (HADAs) poses significant health challenges to individuals returning from high-altitude residence, yet its de-acclimatization process of laboratory indicators and the extent to which it can be predicted before descent remain poorly characterized. We conducted a longitudinal cohort study involving 475 participants with repeated assessments at high-altitude residence (T0), 1 month after return to plain area (T1), and 3 months after return to plain area (T2). title: Guadua londonoae (Poaceae, Bambusoideae), a new bamboo species from the Amazon Basin with remarkably large foliage leaf auricles
abstract: Summary A new species of Guadua (Poaceae, Bambusoideae) from the Amazon Basin is described and illustrated. Guadua londonoae is easily distinguished from other species in the genus by a unique combination of primarily vegetative morphological characters. The most prominent diagnostic feature is the size of the auricles on the foliage leaves, which are on average four times longer than the maximum length previously recorded for any Guadua species. institutions: Instituto de Pesquisas Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro

title: Battlefield Nuclear Thresholds and the 2025 India–Pakistan War
abstract: Is limited or battlefield nuclear employment re-emerging as a usable instrument of statecraft? This article takes the four-day India–Pakistan confrontation of May 2025 as its empirical anchor for that question. The study is a theory-guided interpretive single-case analysis that draws on official statements and briefings issued by both governments, post-crisis reconstructions by research institutions, and contemporaneous reporting, read against the established scholarly literature on deterrence thresholds. title: Beyond McManus’s “Hollow Space”: Reframing Historical Erasure in Atwood, Ballard, and Gibson
abstract: Dystopian fiction usually warns us about the future, but its most critical force often lies in what it erases from the past. Patricia McManus identifies a “hollow space” in dystopian narrative where history is suppressed, yet critical scholarship frequently treats this absence as a mere structural device. Re-examining Margaret Atwood’s The Handmaid’s Tale, J. G. Ballard’s Hello America, and William Gibson’s Neuromancer, this paper argues that erasing history functions as an active weapon of political power designed to strip individuals of their agency and capacity to resist. title: ULUS OF JOCHI AND THE GRAND DUCHY OF LITHUANIA, 1380–1395 FROM VASSALAGE TO ALLIANCE
abstract: Introduction This article examines relations between the Ulus of Jochi and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in 1380–1395 in their military-political, diplomatic, and legal-fiscal dimensions. Aim and objectives. The study aims to identify the mechanisms through which Jochid legitimacy shaped the Grand Duchy’s rights over the Ruthenian lands while simultaneously preserving the khan’s sovereign prerogatives. title: Economic Development and the Revitalization of Small Town America: A Comparative Analysis of Four Michigan Communities
abstract: This research article presents a comparative analysis of economic development efforts in four West Michigan communities: Grand Haven, Holland, Hudsonville, and Zeeland. These cities have developed economic development plans specifically targeting the revitalization of their downtowns and commercial districts. This paper discusses the history of each community, assesses their current economic development efforts, and frames them within a greater discussion of scholarship on economic development strategies in small and rural U.S. communities. title: Unshackled?: China, the ‘unequal treaties’, and the limits of international law, 1919–1929
abstract: Abstract The post-1919 international order extended to China formal sovereign equality while offering few legal means to exercise it. The Sino-Belgian treaty dispute of 1926–29 reveals this: when China abrogated its 1865 treaty with Belgium and Brussels sued at the Permanent Court of International Justice, the institutions that promised peaceful revision could not deliver it without the consent of the powers whose privileges were at stake. title: From collective action to collective rescue: rethinking distribution and cooperation in climate governance under common peril
abstract: Distributive conflict is central to climate governance but is often treated as an external obstacle to cooperation. This conceptual paper argues that such conflict is partly generated by the dominance of a Collective Action Problem (CAP) cooperation grammar, which frames climate mitigation as managing a shared resource and makes agreement over individual contributions a precondition for action. Once institutionalized, CAP embeds distributive questions into the authorization of action itself, contributing to delay and deadlock. title: Metodologías activas e Inteligencia Artificial para fortalecer el pensamiento matemático y la inclusión de estudiantes con necesidades educativas especiales en Educación Básica y Bachillerato: una revisión sistemática de la literatura
abstract: La integración de metodologías activas e Inteligencia Artificial (IA) ofrece nuevas posibilidades para fortalecer el aprendizaje matemático y responder a la diversidad presente en Educación Básica y Bachillerato. El objetivo de esta investigación fue analizar sistemáticamente la evidencia científica publicada entre 2021 y 2025 sobre la aplicación de metodologías activas y herramientas de IA para fortalecer el pensamiento matemático y favorecer la inclusión de estudiantes con necesidades educativas especiales (NEE). title: REDEFINING LIMINALITY IN THE READING OF ICELANDIC SAGAS
abstract: Redefining Liminality in the Reading of Icelandic Sagas. This article introduces a revised and expanded definition of the concept of liminality, with the purpose of utilising it as a methodological tool in the study of the corpus of medieval Icelandic sagas. The paper proposes an alternative interpretation of liminality, distinct from that established in foundational works such as those of Arnold van Gennep and Victor Turner. title: Veins of Influence: Photographic Albums, Curatorial Authority, and Colonial Self-fashioning in Charles Hose’s Sarawak
abstract: Charles Hose (1863–1929) is widely recognised for his contributions to ethnography, natural history and colonial administration in Sarawak during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. While scholarship has focused on his fieldwork and extensive collections, his photographs have largely been treated as individual ethnographic images embedded in texts or dispersed across museum archives, rather than as parts of structured visual artefacts. title: THE CYPRUS ISSUE IN THE EUROPEAN UNION’S REPORTS ON TURKEY: APPROACH, DISCOURSE, AND POLICY
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze how the Cyprus issue was addressed in the European Commission’s Regular Reports on Turkey published between 1998 and 2025, the thematic shifts it underwent, and its impact on Turkey-EU relations. The scope of the study includes the decisions of the 1999 Helsinki Summit, the 2004 Annan Plan referendum process, the commitments under the 2005 Additional Protocol, the suspension of eight negotiation chapters in 2006, and the disputes over maritime jurisdiction areas in the Eastern Mediterranean highlighted in recent reports. title: THE BALKANS AS A HETEROTOPIC SPACE IN HARRY DE WINDT’S THROUGH SAVAGE EUROPE
abstract: In this paper, the depictions of the Balkan Peninsula in Harry de Windt’s 1907 travelogue Through Savage Europe are explored in relation to Michel Foucault’s notion of heterotopia. This concept is brought into connection with Maria Todorova’s notion of Balkanism, as the two can function in complementary ways and elucidate our understanding of the Balkans as imagined by travel writers. We explore how the Balkans are constructed as a special place, a counter-site to Europe. Particular emphasis is placed on the Otherness of the Balkans, as well as their mixed, hybrid nature. title: The Pillars of Faith: A Guide to the 28 Fundamental Seventh-day Adventist Beliefs
abstract: The Seventh-day Adventist Church, a Christian denomination with a global presence, articulates its theology through a formal statement of 28 Fundamental Beliefs. This article, titled "The Pillars of Faith: A Look at the 28 Fundamental Beliefs of Adventists," seeks to demystify these doctrines by presenting them not as a rigid checklist, but as a cohesive and interconnected story. Drawing on the historical metaphor of "pillars" used by early Adventist pioneers, the article organizes the beliefs into thematic categories to enhance understanding. journal: Journal of Education and Development Lab

title: Royal Idealism in the Achaemenid Persian Empire and Its Iconographic Reflections in Anatolia
abstract: The Persians, who established an empire in the mid-sixth century BCE, came to control a vast portion of the ancient world. Centered in Iran, this imperial formation was governed by the Achaemenid dynasty. Although the Achaemenids adhered to Zoroastrian religious traditions, they also incorporated earlier Mesopotamian ideological and political models—particularly those of the Assyrian Empire—into their imperial discourse and legitimizing strategies. title: BEYOND MADNESS: A RE-EVALUATION OF THE STRATEGIC RATIONALE BEHIND THE BYZANTINE–SASANIAN WAR OF 572
abstract: The reign of Emperor Justin II (565–578) is commonly overshadowed by that of Justinian I and is frequently portrayed in traditional historiography as an irrational and hubristic interlude, largely because of the war launched against the Sasanian Empire in 572. This article reconsiders that judgement by reassessing the strategic rationale behind Justin II’s decision and the factors that shaped the war’s trajectory. title: CENTRAL ASIA THROUGH THE LENS OF AN INDIAN TRAVELER: PEOPLE, CUSTOMS, AND TOPONYMY
abstract: Introduction. The article examines the work of the Indian traveler Mir Izzatullah “Masir-i Bukhara” based on the original source. The Indian traveler’s travelogue to Central Asia was written in Persian. Mir Izzatullah was a representative of the local people who worked for the British East India Company. He went on a trip to Central Asia at the request of William Moorcroft (1767-1825) a representative of the British East India Trading Company. title: Receptor‐Targeted Niosomal Nanocarriers: Advances, Challenges, and Opportunities in Natural Compound Delivery for Cancer Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Receptor‐induced targeting of a niosomal delivery system may be a good tool for targeted and safe delivery of bioactive natural compounds to the tumor site with reduced systemic toxicity. Natural phytochemicals have strong therapeutic effects; however, their clinical applications are greatly hampered due to poor solubility, rapid metabolism, and low bioavailability. This review systematically reviews the state‐of‐the‐art surface‐engineered niosomes for phytochemical oncology, with a particular focus on ligand‐mediated delivery to overexpressed tumor receptors. title: Reimagining Desire Beyond Gender: Body Politics and Ambiguous Identity in Jeanette Winterson’s Written on the Body
abstract: The paper attempts to examine ambiguity, and bodily existence in Jeanette Winterson’s Written on the Body. At the central core of the narrative exists an unnamed narrator, whose identity is deliberately rendered ambiguous. Due to the ambiguity the gender remains unrevealed. In the novel, Jeanette Winterson has adopted this innovative narrative strategy to challenge conformist expectations about gender identity, sexuality and desire.
