title: Learning across Borders: Pre-Service Teacher Development through Overseas Classroom Observation across Diverse Asian Contexts
abstract: This study examines the impact of short-term overseas classroom observation experiences on pre-service teachers' professional development in different Asian contexts, using a convergent mixed-methods design. The sample consisted of reflective narratives from 20 pre-service teachers studying at the Faculty of Education, Prince of Songkla University in Thailand. Descriptive statistics, correspondence analysis, and reflexive thematic analysis were applied to identify interconnections among reflection patterns and the underlying themes across destination contexts. title: UPRISINGS OF THE KAZAKHS OF THE JUNIOR ZHUZ AGAINST THE ABOLITION OF THE AUTHORITY OF SULTAN-RULERS
abstract: Introduction. The administrative and territorial reforms introduced by the Russian Empire in the late 1860s marked a critical turning point in the colonization of the Kazakh Steppe. The rapid dismantling of traditional local governance, combined with social restructuring, caused deep discontent among the nomadic population, leading to powerful anti-colonial uprisings. Goals and objectives. title: A digital specimen of the extinct Imperial Woodpecker: integrating museum scans, historical film and animated feather articulation
abstract: The Imperial Woodpecker ( Campephilus imperialis ), the world’s largest woodpecker species, is presumed extinct following the collapse of old-growth pine forest in its endemic range in the Sierra Madre Occidental, Mexico. Here, we present a detailed, animated 3D reconstruction of an adult female C. imperialis , built from photogrammetric scans of a physical museum study skin and parameterised against historical footage of the species in the wild. title: Phase composition and microstructural heterogeneity of ancient ceramics from east Kazakhstan: raman spectroscopy, x-ray microtomography and scanning electron microscopy
abstract: This study presents the results of a comprehensive investigation of ceramic fragments from the Shagantogay archaeological site (Makanchi District, Abay region, Republic of Kazakhstan) using modern non-destructive analytical techniques: Raman spectroscopy, X-ray microtomography, and scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS). The present research aims to analyze his life and activities within their historical context and highlight his role in the political, military, and diplomatic dynamics of the era. title: Adaptive variable-exponent sliding mode control for energy management of battery-supported hybrid electric vehicle
abstract: This study presents a robust converter-level control framework for a fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) equipped with a multi-source hybrid power system (HPS) comprising a fuel cell (FC), an ultracapacitor (UC), and a lithium-ion battery. The considered powertrain employs a boost converter for the FC and bidirectional converters for the energy storage units and is represented by a fourth-order nonlinear model. title: Trascendencia en ciencia ficción: análisis comparativo de la Saga Ringworld y Childhood’s End
abstract: This paper examines the connections between science fiction and religion through the lens of transcendence in two iconic works: Ringworld by Larry Niven and Childhood’s End by Arthur C. Clarke. Using the concept of the novum as a starting point, it explores how both authors interpret transcendence from a secular perspective that nonetheless carries strong religious associations. While they share certain thematic elements, the two works differ significantly in how transcendence functions within the narrative, its relevance, nature, scope, and underlying causes. title: Accounting and Taxation in the Hotel Industry of the Autonomous Region of Madeira: Challenges, Strategies and Perspectives
abstract: This study examines accounting and taxation in the hotel sector of the Autonomous Region of Madeira, with a focus on the interaction between specific tax regulations and financial management practices that impact companies' economic sustainability. The study discusses the diversity of applicable tax regimes, including rates on revenue and taxable profit, and the importance of adapting to legislative reforms to optimize the tax burden and liquidity. title: What Kind of Universe do You Want?: Physical Laws, Life, and Humans
abstract: This paper examines how complexity in the universe emerges from the interconnected roles of fundamental particles, forces, physical laws, and governing parameters. Particles provide the basic constituents of matter, while forces mediate their interactions under the constraints of physical laws such as quantum mechanics, relativity, and thermodynamics. The specific values of fundamental parameters—such as coupling strengths and particle masses—set the conditions under which stable structures can form. title: Altitudinal gradient patterns and community assembly mechanisms of birds in the eastern Kunlun Mountains, Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, China
abstract: Avian altitudinal distribution on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau is shaped by contemporary environmental heterogeneity, history lineage diversification, and high-altitude adaptation. Understanding this pattern is crucial for explaining biodiversity maintenance in the “Third Pole”. However, in extreme arid boundaries with minimal human impact, how the interplay of historical evolutionary constraints and contemporary ecological filters shapes avian communities remains largely unquantified. title: The Volga Bulgars’ Ambush on the Mongols and the Death of Jebe Noyan
abstract: Research objectives: This study seeks to reassess the events that occurred during the return phase of the Dasht-i Kıpchak campaign, led by Jebe Noyan and Subutai Ba’atur, with a particular focus on determining the circumstances of Jebe Noyan’s death. By critically analyzing historical sources, the research aims to reconstruct the sequence of events and evaluate competing hypotheses regarding his fate. title: Transcendental Structures in Critical Phenomenology: The Example of Resonance in Hartmut Rosa
abstract: As different as Lisa Guenther (2019, 2021) and Johanna Oksala (2022) may be, they agree that the positing of transcendental structures of meaningful experience leads to oppressive normativity. Their contestation of transcendental structures reflects a trend in recent critical phenomenology that resists phenomenological appeals to transcendental structures in favor of quasi-transcendental ones. title: Beyond Turkish representation: The evolution of the function of Janissary music in Europe from military bands to concert halls
abstract: The adoption of Janissary music and instruments into European military bands represents one of the earliest examples of direct musical exchange between the Ottoman Empire and Europe. While previous scholarship has primarily examined the appearance of Turkish elements as markers of exoticism, less attention has been given to their long-term functional transformation within the Western musical tradition. title: Work recovery through virtual and real nature experiences: Employee perspectives
abstract: While nature is known to support employee wellbeing, virtual leisure activities can also be utilised for work recovery. The study examines the role of virtual and real nature in employee recovery by using the experience economy framework. In this randomised crossover trial, with a qualitative approach, 57 employees visited real and virtual nature. The virtual visits in different types of nature environments were described as providing escapism, while in real nature, it was more difficult to detach from duties. title: Master of Light Arkhip Kuindzhi’s Contributions to Luminism, Philosophical Aesthetics, Art Pedagogy, and Regional Cultural Identity
abstract: This study provides a systematic examination of the multifaceted legacy of Russian landscape painter Arkhip Ivanovich Kuindzhi (1842–1910), extending beyond his established contributions to luminist technique to investigate lesser-explored dimensions of his pedagogical practice, interdisciplinary links to music, and long-term cultural influence. abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric new particle formation is driven by condensable vapors such as sulfuric acid and highly oxygenated organic molecules (HOMs). Measuring these gases is challenging because they are present at trace concentrations, they are easily lost through condensation onto surfaces, and they include a wide range of chemically diverse species. title: Academic discussions on hostel: limits, challenges, and perspectives
abstract: O fenômeno conhecido como hostels é um tipo de acomodação que, essencialmente, facilita a sociabilidade entre os hóspedes. Desde estruturas físicas específicas, como cozinhas e quartos compartilhados, para estimular a interação humana, até um contato ainda mais próximo com os anfitriões, essas são, em geral, as características básicas desse tipo de hospedagem. O objetivo deste artigo é discutir a produção de conhecimento sobre o hostel, identificando os focos, os temas mais abordados e também as lacunas percebidas nessa produção acadêmica. title: Britain’s reaction to the 1857–61 Mexican Civil War
abstract: By focusing on the British response to the 1857–61 Mexican Civil War, this article provides, for the first time, a study of the calls for military action that were made by the diplomats on the ground, Charles Loftus Otway and George Benvenuto Mathew. It highlights how their conflicting views of the liberal and conservative governments evolved as the war unfolded, and it assesses the Foreign Office’s response to their dispatches. title: Humans are Made of Mud: the Genealogy of Farmland Legal Protection in Religious Traditions
abstract: Abstract: This article delves into the sacred origins of farmland legal protection, aiming to illuminate the profound rituals and beliefs that historically shaped human relationships with land and, more specifically, farmland. This analysis requires a deeper reflection on the interplay between land, religion, agriculture, and societal structures, ultimately contributing to the intricate process through which communities imbue land with meaning and, in so doing, give a value to it. title: Inventing the ninja ancestor: Prince Shōtoku and the media circuits of martial tradition
abstract: This article traces the modern invention, transnational circulation, and persistence of the claim that Prince Shōtoku (574–622), the ancient Japanese regent, founded or patronized ninjutsu. While early chronicles portray Shōtoku as a statesman, Buddhist patron, and military leader, little to no premodern evidence connects him to such espionage traditions. Drawing on archival research, textual analysis, and media history, the article shows how this genealogy emerged in postwar Japan through Fujita Seiko (1899–1966), a self-styled ninja, and was expanded by the local historian Okuse Heishichirō

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based 3D Beam Adaptation for Underwater Wireless Optical Communication with AUVs
abstract: Underwater Wireless Optical Communications (UWOC) provide essential high data rates for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), but reliable connectivity is critically affected by transmitter-receiver misalignment. This work addresses the beam pointing problem for a moving AUV subject to unknown ocean currents through a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework. title: A Unified Dynamics Framework for Reinforcement Learning and Classical Control of a Six-DOF Pipeline-Tracking ROV in NVIDIA Isaac Sim
abstract: Reinforcement learning controllers for underwater vehicles are usually trained against one physics representation and deployed against another, so reported performance does not always describe behavior outside training. title: Physics-Guided Spectral Distillation for Underwater Image Enhancement on Resource-Constrained Devices
abstract: Underwater image enhancement is crucial for improving visual perception in marine applications. Existing underwater image enhancement studies mainly focus on enhancement quality and visual fidelity, while rarely considering real-time deployment capability, which is essential for resource-constrained underwater robots. title: Onboard Vision and MPC Navigation for Underwater Robots: An Open BlueROV2 Platform for Multi-Robot Experiments & Docking
abstract: Autonomous underwater robots require robust perception, estimation and control to operate in confined environments. This paper presents an open-source BlueROV2 platform combining onboard vision with nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) for autonomous navigation and docking. The platform integrates an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX and an Intel RealSense D435i stereo camera in a modular pressure housing. title: Benchmarking EMlog Calibration for Autonomous Surface Vehicles
abstract: Accurate velocity measurement is a fundamental requirement for autonomous surface and underwater vehicles. Commonly, velocity is provided by a Doppler velocity log (DVL) sensor, yet it becomes unavailable due to operational altitude constraints. In such situations, electromagnetic logs (EMLogs) provide a critically robust alternative for continuous velocity estimation. title: Project CERES: Nuclear Thermal Transportation and In-Situ Propellant Production A Foundational Architecture for Solar System Logistics
abstract: Project CERES proposes a reusable deep-space transportation architecture centered on the dwarf planet Ceres, combining nuclear thermal propulsion (NTP) with in-situ production of water, hydrogen, oxygen and ammonia. Its first flight, a Pathfinder that surveys Ceres and returns samples, also bears on the question of life: Dawn found the ingredients of prebiotic chemistry there, and returned material would show just how far that chemistry went. title: Comparative Analysis of Green Building Rating Systems for Performance-Based Contracting in Southeast Asian Data Centres
abstract: Green Building Rating Systems (GBRSs) are widely used to promote and guide sustainable development across the built environment. However, a significant gap remains between certification achievement and actual operational performance, limiting the ability of existing GBRSs to support Performance-Based Contracts (PBCs), particularly in the rapidly growing and energy-intensive data centre sector. This gap underscores the need for PBCs, which rely on measurable and verifiable performance outcomes. abstract: Abstract Earth’s atmosphere and oceans experienced two major episodes of ocean-atmosphere oxygenation that transformed the planet and shaped the evolution of the oxygen-rich biosphere between 2.45 and 0.541 billion years ago (Ga). Three new compounds, including two rare cyclopropane-containing compounds, verrucacrylic acids A and B (1 and 2), and a new amino acid derivative, methyl N-[(2S)-2-methylbutanoyl]-D-tyrosinate (3), were isolated from Verrucosispora sp. FIM06025. Compounds 1-3 were structurally elucidated on the basis of extensive spectroscopic data analysis using 1D- and 2D-NMR, ECD, and HRESIMS. title: From Ocean Symbionts to Crop Allies: A Critical Appraisal of Seaweed-associated Microbiomes as Resources for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Seaweeds sustain dense and metabolically distinctive microbial communities whose members produce morphogens, phytohormone analogues, siderophores, vitamins, polysaccharide-degrading enzymes and antimicrobial metabolites. These properties have prompted the proposition that the seaweed-associated microbiome constitutes an underexploited reservoir of biostimulant and biocontrol agents for terrestrial crop production. title: Alleviating over-tourism and advancing sustainable tourism on coral island through virtual reality (VR)
abstract: The main objective of this study is to examine how virtual reality (VR) might help reduce overtourism in places with coral islands. A purposive sampling approach was used to reach people who had previously engaged in or were interested in VR tourism because there was no easily accessible database of VR users. A structured questionnaire was designed to collect data. Data were collected from 300 respondents, as 370 questionnaires were distributed among the respondents. title: Evidence of Seagrass-Saltmarsh Connectivity, and their Role in Coastal Seascapes – a Review
abstract: Abstract Seagrass beds and saltmarshes are two of the most ecologically valuable coastal habitats globally, providing a wide range of ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, coastal flood defence, and habitat provision for fauna. While both systems can co-occur within the same intertidal zone, they have often been studied in isolation, with less consideration given to how their functional connectivity may influence the continued ecological and geomorphological development of either system. title: Quantifying aggregation bias in marsh carbon flux estimates caused by rhizosphere oxygen heterogeneity
abstract: Abstract. Estuarine marshes are crucial components of coastal environments around the world and provide numerous ecosystem services, such as carbon sequestration. Plant-microbe interactions are potential key drivers of organic carbon cycling in these ecosystems, but their contribution to the ecosystem-level carbon balance has been rarely quantified so far. This is partly due to the substantial intra- and interspecific variation of plant traits that are affecting microbial functions. title: Lascars at war: Maritime labour and the logistics of empire in Amitav Ghosh’s Ibis trilogy
abstract: This article foregrounds lascars, an indispensable yet overlooked category of imperial labour, in its analysis of Amitav Ghosh’s Ibis trilogy: Sea of Poppies, River of Smoke, and Flood of Fire. Rather than being identifiable as subaltern heroes or figures of cultural hybridity, lascars are understood as agents who navigate the material conditions of empire and negotiate their status as shipboard, commercial, or martial units of labour discipline. title: Management and sustainable harvesting of marine macroalgae species: A North Atlantic perspective
abstract: Marine macroalgae are increasingly valued as a sustainable resource for food, feed, and high-value bioproducts, yet the regulatory frameworks governing their wild harvest and cultivation remain fragmented across the North Atlantic. This study reviews the management and harvesting of marine macroalgae species in Atlantic Canada, Iceland, the Republic of Ireland, France, the United Kingdom, and Norway (45° N–66° 34′ N), drawing on 148 sources, including 34 statutory documents, from a systematic search of peer-reviewed and grey literature. title: Suicide, Suicidal Behavior, and Prevention at a Coastal Site in the United Kingdom
abstract: Abstract: Background: Beachy Head is a high-frequency public coastal location associated with suicidal crisis, suicide attempts, and deaths by suicide in England. Although evidence from frequently used jumping locations supports access restriction and multicomponent prevention, the evidence specific to this site has not been systematically mapped. Aims: To identify and summarize academic, policy, and gray literature addressing suicidal crisis, suicidal behavior, deaths by suicide, and suicide prevention at Beachy Head. title: Community Structure of Echinoderms on Bunaken Island, North Sulawesi
abstract: Echinodermata are marine invertebrates characterized by their spiny skin, free-living and solitary nature, inhabiting zones ranging from the intertidal to the deep sea. This study aims to examine the community structure of Echinodermata in the waters of Bunaken Island. Data collection was focused on a single observation station and conducted over two days with an effective sampling duration of one hour per day (11:00–12:00 WITA). title: Enhanced pedogenic weathering of hard clay in the Changjiang (Yangtze River) Delta during the last-glacial sea-level lowstand
abstract: Deciphering lowland silicate weathering during glacial sea-level lowstands remains challenging because the exposure-related signal is superimposed on an inherited weathering background. The widespread hard clay in the Changjiang (Yangtze River) Delta provides a valuable archive of last-glacial lowstand exposure, recording parent-material accumulation, subaerial exposure and pedogenic weathering. title: Ecological-Geochemical Characteristics and Evolution of the Chemical Composition of Lake Karymsky after the Underwater Eruption in the Academii Nauk Caldera in January 1996 (Kamchatka Peninsula)
abstract: Abstract Based on the data acquired during the 2024 hydrochemical survey, taking into account previously published and archival material, the evolution of the chemical composition of Lake Karymsky was studied. The underwater eruption that occurred in the Academii Nauk caldera in 1996 had a significant impact on the hydrochemistry of the lake. It was seen as an increase in the concentration of all macrocomponents and a decrease in pH. Since 2015, there has been a stabilization of the chemical composition of the lake water. title: Resident damselfish influence the coral holobiont: species-specific responses in Acropora millepora and Acropora digitifera
abstract: Abstract Symbiotic interactions are central to coral ecology, spanning the coral holobiont’s internal microbial partnerships to broader associations with reef fishes and other motile species. Coral-dwelling damselfish live in close association with coral colonies, using their branches as shelter. These associations can influence the coral’s immediate environment through various mechanisms including nutrient inputs, oxygen dynamics, and sediment removal, while fish may also serve as vectors for microorganisms. title: Fatal coinfection by Mycobacterium fortuitum and Epicoccum sp. with concurrent severe coccidial enteritis in an olive ridley sea turtle (Lepidochelys olivacea)
abstract: Sea turtles are susceptible to opportunistic infections, particularly when debilitated, injured, or exposed to environmental stressors. Although nontuberculous mycobacteria are increasingly recognized as emerging pathogens in marine wildlife, documented cases in sea turtles remain limited, and coinfections involving mycobacteria and uncommon environmental fungi are rarely reported. title: Optimization of Biogenic Silver Nanoparticle Synthesis Using UV–Visible Spectroscopy from a Bacterial Strain Isolated from Coastal River Sediments
abstract: Abstract Microorganisms living in river sediments can reduce metal ions and produce nanoparticles through environmentally friendly processes. We aseptically collected sediment samples, serially diluted them, and cultured them to obtain morphologically diverse bacterial strains. title: Did the latitudinal diversity gradient and temperature-size rule hold during the Late Palaeozoic Ice Age?
abstract: The Late Palaeozoic Ice Age (LPIA) represents one of the most significant climatic transitions in Earth's history, characterised by dramatic fluctuations in atmospheric CO 2 , O 2 , and global temperatures. This study investigates the influence of these global climatic shifts and latitudinal gradients on the diversity, complexity, and size of trace fossils during the Carboniferous and Permian periods in continental deposits. title: Conicamides A−D: Linear Peptides with Protease Inhibitory Activity Isolated from the Red Sea Sponge Theonella conica
abstract: Abstract Guided by the serine protease inhibition assay, four novel linear peptides, conicamides A−D (1−4), were isolated from the marine sponge Theonella conica collected in two different locations in the Red Sea. Conicamides C (3) and D (4) consist of the unique α-keto-β-amino acid, keto-homo-tyrosine, and were found to inhibit the serine proteases chymotrypsin and elastase. Conicamides C (3) and D (4) are the first characterized linear peptides containing a C-terminal α-keto-amino acid. title: Evaluasi Implementasi Program Bulan Cinta Laut (BCL) dalam Mendukung Kebijakan Ekonomi Biru Di Indonesia
abstract: Program BCL merupakan inisiatif Kementerian Kelautan dan Perikanan (KKP) untuk mengurangi sampah plastik di laut dan mendorong implementasi ekonomi biru melalui partisipasi nelayan serta masyarakat pesisir. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi efektivitas pelaksanaan program menggunakan model CIPP (Context, Input, Process, Product) dengan pendekatan mixed-methods melalui survei, wawancara, dan observasi di 22 lokasi pelaksanaan tahun 2024. title: Rare Earth Elements in Chile: A Critical Review of Primary, Secondary and Marine Resources, Metallurgical Recoverability and Future Supply Chain Opportunities
abstract: The economic value of rare earth elements (REE) is concentrated in Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb. The supply chain for these elements is dominated by a single country, China, which accounts for about 60% of mined production, over 90% of refinement, and nearly 95% of permanent magnet manufacturing. This shifts the critical question from geological availability to the capacity to convert resources into products. title: The timescale of forming Earth’s earliest water ocean in the Hadean Eon
abstract: Abstract The timing of the first water ocean formation on Earth is critical for understanding the onset of habitability, but the duration of this process remains poorly constrained. Using a heat-budget model for the early atmosphere-ocean system, this study quantifies the transition from the final solidification of the magma ocean to the establishment of a stable hydrosphere. The results demonstrate that once the mantle transitioned to solid-state convection, a thick primordial steam atmosphere can radiatively cool and condense into a global water ocean within 10,000 years. title: Nursery use and construction-associated receiver detection patterns of the sicklefin lemon shark (Negaprion acutidens) at Dongsha (Pratas) Island
abstract: Shallow nearshore habitats can serve as nursery areas for coastal elasmobranchs but are increasingly exposed to coastal development. We used standardized population surveys, mark–recapture, acoustic telemetry, and passive acoustic monitoring to evaluate use of monitored shallow nearshore habitats by the sicklefin lemon shark ( Negaprion acutidens ) at Dongsha (Pratas) Island and to explore whether construction-associated underwater sound coincided with changes in receiver detections. title: Tectonic and environmental controls on Upper Triassic–Jurassic carbonate successions of the eastern Northern Calcareous Alps (Stumpfmauer, Austria)
abstract: The western Neo-Tethys Austroalpine and Southern Alps sedimentary successions are proven archives of environmental and climatic changes and tectonic activity across the Triassic to Jurassic times. These Upper Triassic–Jurassic, dominantly carbonate, shelf deposits witnessed the extensional tectonics related to the opening of the Penninic Ocean to the north-west and the partial closure of the Neo-Tethys Ocean to the south-east and contribute to the reconstruction of the evolution of a rifted passive margin. title: From victim to villain: Enemization, justice, and the democratic debate in the framing of Marine Le Pen’s condemnation
abstract: This article examines how the March 2025 conviction of Marine Le Pen for the misuse of European Parliament funds was framed in the French press and how the event became a discursive site for negotiating democratic legitimacy and political enmity. The ruling generated extensive media coverage that combined legal reporting with political interpretation. Drawing on a corpus of 45 articles from eight national and regional French newspapers collected through the Europresse database, the study combines textual data analysis with concordance analysis using Hyperbase. title: Going against the grain: return mobilities and rural transformation in coastal Bangladesh
abstract: Return mobilities are often conceptualised as an economic necessity or a failed migration outcome. However, in climate-vulnerable regions such as coastal Bangladesh, return mobilities emerge as an active process of adaptation shaped by intersecting socio-economic, political and environmental dynamics. This study explores return mobilities in two coastal villages in Bangladesh, examining how water politics, translocal ties and livelihood opportunities shape reintegration. title: Seasonal and Spatial Variability of Silicon Cycle in Godavari Tidal River Zone
abstract: Abstract Dam regulation of tropical monsoonal rivers enhances seasonal contrasts in the tidal river zone (TRZ) hydrology, altering the delivery of dissolved silicon (DSi) to the coastal ocean. Here, we identify the drivers of Si cycling in the Godavari TRZ and quantify their implications for Si delivery to the Bay of Bengal (BoB). We analyzed elemental concentrations and isotopic tracers (δ 30 Si, δ 18 O, δ 2 H, 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) of the water column and adjacent groundwater during dry (pre‐monsoon) and wet (monsoon) seasons to delineate mixing and biogeochemical processes in the Godavari TRZ. title: Southern Portugal hydroclimate of the last millennium from near‐annually resolved speleothem records
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydroclimate in Portugal is influenced by the North Atlantic subtropical high‐pressure system (the Azores High) and by internal climate modes, most prominently the North Atlantic Oscillation, which may shift in position and/or intensity due to anthropogenic climate change. title: Assessment of Beach Plastic Waste Pollution Using the Clean Coast Index: Evidence from Thanh Hoa Province, Viet Nam
abstract: Marine plastic pollution is an increasingly important environmental and socio-economic challenge for coastal provinces of Viet Nam, where tourism, fisheries, river discharge and coastal urbanization interact to shape the accumulation of beach litter. This study assesses the status, composition and seasonal variation of beach plastic waste in Thanh Hoa Province using a field-survey approach adapted from UNEP and NOAA guidance and the Clean Coast Index (CCI). Two survey campaigns were conducted during the Southwest and Northeast monsoon seasons along 22 transects in Sam Son, Hau Loc and Nghi Son

title: Study of a copper-lignin with laccase-mediated polymerization treatment for wood preservation: determination of durability in marine environment using novel technologies
abstract: Abstract In the marine environment, the durability of wood is heavily compromised by harsh conditions and the presence of marine xylophages. Biocide treatments are often employed to prolong the lifetime of wood, however, its leaching into the environment motivates the development of alternative treatments due to environmental concerns. In this study, Scots pine samples were treated with a solution based on copper and polymerized Kraft lignin via laccase enzyme was tested. title: The gross ecosystem product of oyster reefs
abstract: Oyster reefs are critical interfacial habitats that underpin coastal and marine bio-diversity, and enhance multiple ecosystem services of blue carbon habitats, including water filtration and shoreline stabilization. However, despite this ecological value, oyster reefs have suffered dramatic global declines. The absence of a systemic economic valuation of oyster reef ecosystem services introduces deep uncertainty in the prioritization of restoration areas, thereby constraining coordinated large-scale transboundary conservation, restoration, eco-engineering efforts, and policy. abstract: Для метацеркарий трематод, обнаруженных в пищеварительной железе черноморского моллюска Hydrobia acuta, получены первые морфологические и молекулярные данные. abstract: Context Geochemical proxies in bivalve shells can reconstruct past environmental conditions in dynamic estuaries, yet field-based validation of how quickly these proxies respond to ambient water fluctuations remains limited. title: Alteromonas macleodii breaches the diatom frustule triggering protoplast emergence and programmed necrosis-like death in Thalassiosira rotula
abstract: Abstract Diatom-bacteria interactions drive biogeochemical fluxes at the base of the marine food-web. Although bacteria are increasingly recognised as important drivers of algal mortality, the diversity of algicidal strategies remains understudied. Here we show that Alteromonas macleodii , a recurrent member of Thalassiosira rotula ’s microbiome, breaches the diatom’s silica frustule, inducing >95% of cells to emerge from their shells within 72 h, exposing protoplasts to lysis and exploitation. title: Cigarette Butt Pollution in Aquatic Ecosystems: Sources, Environmental Fate, Ecotoxicological Impacts and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Cigarette butts (CBs) are one of the most abundant forms of anthropogenic litter worldwide and represent an important source of chemical and microplastic pollution in aquatic ecosystems. An estimated 4.5 trillion CBs are discarded annually, with a substantial proportion entering freshwater, estuarine and marine environments. Cigarette litter contains a complex mixture of hazardous substances, including nicotine, cotinine, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), heavy metals, aromatic amines, BTEX compounds, tobacco-specific nitrosamines and cellulose acetate microfibres. title: Community-Based Mangrove Planting to Support Coastal Conservation in Tanjung Pasir Village, Tangerang Regency
abstract: The coastal area of Tanjung Pasir Village, Teluknaga Subdistrict, Tangerang Regency, faces various environmental challenges, including coastal erosion, land-use change, and pressures on the sustainability of mangrove ecosystems. These conditions highlight the need for conservation activities involving the participation of multiple stakeholders. This community service activity aimed to implement a community-based mangrove planting activity to support coastal conservation in Tanjung Pasir Village. abstract: Latvian urban space has been formed over many centuries due to human activity. Natural elements provide optimal living conditions for inhabitants, regardless of the size of continuously inhabited settlements. title: Setting the course for American manatee conservation in Brazil: Quantifying and mapping vulnerability to anthropogenic threats
abstract: Manatees are charismatic, wide-ranging megaherbivores increasingly threatened with extinction across much of their distribution. Although many studies have documented threats to manatee populations, no standardized framework has been applied to quantify their vulnerability, leaving available knowledge scattered and lacking a comprehensive assessment of impact magnitude and spatial scale. Here we aimed to quantify and map vulnerability of the American manatee to anthropogenic threats in Brazil. title: Defense Logistics and Rice Security in Indonesia: An Integrated Strategy Amid Geopolitical Turbulence
abstract: Rice security is at the center of national defense because of the growing geopolitical unrest in the Asia-Pacific region, especially in the South China Sea, which puts Indonesia’s food supply at risk through marine channels. Using a Systematic Literature Review in accordance with PRISMA 2020, this study synthesizes 63 peer-reviewed articles, official documents, and institutional reports from Scopus, Web of Science, ProQuest, and regional databases to develop an integrated defense logistics strategy for Indonesian rice security. abstract: Ascidian Lissoclinum patella is known to harbor a diverse community of symbiotic microorganisms, however, information on symbiotic microbes capable of growing outside their host originated from the waters of Talise is still limited. This study aimed to molecularly identify microorganisms capable of growing outside the host L. patella collected from Talise waters, North Minahasa, Indonesia. abstract: Adolescent girls are a vulnerable group to anemia because they experience menstruation, rapid growth, and often inadequate iron intake. Coastal areas have characteristics of food consumption patterns dominated by marine products and limited access to other sources of animal iron, so there is a risk of increasing the prevalence of anemia. abstract: Abstract Ecosystem service assessment is crucial for maintaining regional ecological balance and promoting sustainable development. Using the InVEST model and Geodetector, this study quantified four ecosystem services, including habitat quality, water yield, soil retention, and carbon storage, and identified their driving mechanisms in Quanzhou from 2013 to 2023. abstract: Background: Laryngeal cancer (LC) represents the most common head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Tanzania. Although global trends demonstrate declining incidence and improving outcomes, survival disparities remain substantial, largely driven by inequities in access to definitive surgical care and the increasing adoption of organ preservation strategies. abstract: Over the past few decades, microplastics have been globally recognized as a prevailing contaminant in marine, freshwater, as well as terrestrial ecosystems. title: Environmental Challenges and Opportunities for Sustainable Utilization of Phosphogypsum in Iran: A Review
abstract: Phosphogypsum (PG), a by-product of phosphoric acid production, represents one of the largest-volume industrial wastes globally and poses significant environmental management challenges. abstract: Harmful algal blooms represent one of the few climate-sensitive hazards capable of destroying an entire marine farm's standing biomass within days, yet the scientific literature that underpins farm protection remains fragmented across oceanography, fish pathology, sensor engineering and resource economics. title: Water–Energy Nexus: The Case of a Desalination Plant in the Semi-Arid Region of Brazil
abstract: Water and energy are interdependent resources essential for economic development and societal well-being. Consequently, increasing water demand has intensified water scarcity in many regions, a problem exacerbated by climate change. In such contexts, seawater desalination can provide a reliable and climate-independent source of freshwater, reducing pressure on conventional water resources through reverse osmosis. This paper provides an assessment of the integrated water–energy benefits of producing 1.0 m3/s drinking water through seawater desalination within a large-scale water-transfer system

abstract: Background/Objective: Sea buckthorn contains an exceptionally rich profile of bioactive nutrients and metabolites, with established systemic therapeutic benefits across diverse pathological models. This descriptive transcriptomic study establishes a predictive framework to guide the future application of sea buckthorn and its isolated derivatives in targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies. abstract: Abstract Drawing on archival materials from the Republic of China (Taiwan), the People’s Republic of China (PRC), the United States, and the former Soviet Union, this article discusses why the PRC’s 1949–50 strike plans for Taiwan went unfulfilled. What prevented the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) from “liberating” Taiwan was the fact that it lacked sufficient naval and air power to overwhelm the comparatively better equipped Kuomintang (KMT). title: Enrichissement des collections des Archives et Musées de la Ville de Bruxelles en 2025
abstract: Cet article analyse l’évolution du champ militant socialiste naissant en Turquie à travers une étude textuelle chronologique du Parti ouvrier de Turquie (TİP) et de la revue Yön (à partir des éditoriaux rédigés par Doğan Avcıoğlu), deux agents fondateurs du champ des années 1960. title: First Documented Macroscopic Regression of Fibropapillomatosis in a Recaptured Green Sea Turtle (Chelonia mydas): A Case Study from Curaçao
abstract: Fibropapillomatosis (FP) is a neoplastic disease affecting sea turtles worldwide and is particularly prevalent in green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas). Although spontaneous regression of FP has been documented in some populations, observations remain uncommon, and the mechanisms underlying regression are poorly understood. This study documents the first known case of macroscopic FP regression in a free-ranging green sea turtle from Curaçao. abstract: Abstract. Rhizosphere-associated bacteria play a key role in improving plant performance in saline and nutrient-poor soils. abstract: Risk management is key for companies, and the combination of finance and logistics is essential to support risk-related decisions made by supply chain managers. abstract: Abstract This article explores moral order through two cultural beliefs of usinga and limbwata as they operated in the coastal Tanga’s sisal plantations in north-eastern Tanzania, between the 1920s and the 1960s. title: Lake eutrophication increases unprotected organic carbon pools in sediments
abstract: Abstract Reactive iron oxide-bound organic carbon (Fe–OC) is a key pathway for long-term carbon burial, but its effectiveness under increasingly widespread eutrophication remains uncertain. Here we show that Fe–OC accounts for 16% of total organic carbon and buries at ~14 Mt C yr −1 in lakes globally, equivalent to ~27% of the marine Fe–OC sink despite lakes covering only ~1.25% of marine area. title: First record of Aximopsis s.l. (Hymenoptera, Eurytomidae) from China, with description of a new species parasitising the larvae of the coastal pollinator Ceratina smaragdula (Hymenoptera, Apidae)
abstract: The genus Aximopsis sensu lato (Hymenoptera, Eurytomidae) is a cosmopolitan group of parasitoid wasps, currently comprising 43 described species. The genus is defined by a suite of homoplastic morphological characters and its taxonomic boundaries remain unstable, with recent molecular phylogenies indicating paraphyly. title: Palestine in Foreign Travelogues: A Spatial and Social Reading from Sacred Geography to Everyday Life (1839–1864)
abstract: Seven foreign travel accounts published between 1839 and 1864 are examined comparatively to reveal how Ottoman Palestine was represented through sacred geography, mobility, and everyday life. While Jerusalem remains the principal focus, the study also considers Jaffa, Ramle, Bethlehem, Hebron, the Jordan River, the Dead Sea, Nablus, and Mount Gerizim within the same spatial framework. abstract: This study provides a detailed stratigraphic characterization of the successive stages within the erosion–accretion cycle of a beach–foredune system. title: Patterns of Indian Migration and Early Settlement in Kakamega Municipality, Kenya, 1901-1920
abstract: While existing scholarship extensively documents the dominance of Indian migrants in coastal and urban hubs of Kenya, the localised rural role of the diaspora in Western Kenya remains critically underexplored. Consequently, this study addresses the unresolved historical paradox in Kakamega. The study traces the history of migration and early settlement of Indians in Kakamega Municipality, Kenya, between 1901 and 1920. abstract: Ballast water can transport microorganisms, including potentially pathogenic bacteria (PPB), between aquatic environments. abstract: Market access is an important determinant influencing farmers’ adoption decisions by affecting prospective profitability, access to modern inputs, availability of information and extension services, and exposure to production and price risks. This systematic review is a synthesis of the evidence on the relationship between market access and CSA adoption in various agroecological settings. abstract: Floating solar photovoltaic (FSPV) systems have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional land-based photovoltaic (LSPV) systems by reducing land-use constraints and improving electrical performance through the natural cooling effect of water bodies. abstract: Synchronization between larval development and peak resource quality drives life-history evolution in forest defoliators from cold-temperate regions but is less considered in other ecosystems, such as those in the Mediterranean region. abstract: Natural compounds of animal and plant origin play a key role in maintaining human health and preventing diseases. abstract: Abstract In North Africa, the Middle Stone Age (MSA) has been associated with the emergence and evolution of Homo sapiens and is considered a pivotal period in the development of behavioral complexity. abstract: Abstract Fossil fuels continue to dominate the global energy supply. abstract: Abstract This paper investigates changing housing provision in rural Nottinghamshire during the 19 th and early 20th centuries using archival material and historical census data. abstract: This study examines whether Indonesian regional contingency budgets adapt to realised climate-related disaster experience, treating budget responsiveness as one dimension of fiscal resilience. abstract: Abstract. The Arctic is at the forefront of global warming. abstract: Saltwater and industrial contamination is gradually rendering groundwater in coastal India undrinkable, and the impact is most severely felt by the populations who lack access to centralised water treatment facilities. abstract: Abstract From the 1840s, Tyneside emerged as a key center for iron shipbuilding, rivaling Britain’s established hubs. This industrial shift was driven initially not by legacy firms but by migrant entrepreneurs from Aberdeen—John Coutts, Charles Mitchell, and Andrew Leslie. This article investigates the divergent trajectories of these entrepreneurs, asking why two succeeded in establishing sustainable enterprises while the other failed. abstract: This article examines how Palestinian wedding musicians in the Galilee region sustained engagement with regional Arab urban music traditions during the decades following the 1948 Nakba. While the events of 1948 shattered the musical infrastructure that had connected Palestinian cities including Haifa to the broader Arab world, cosmopolitan Arab art music continues until today to form part of the everyday sonic lives of Palestinian communities in northern Israel. title: Petrophysical Dataset of Representative Volcanic Rocks from Dokdo, South Korea
abstract: Dokdo, a volcanic island in the East Sea, comprises alkaline volcanic and pyroclastic rocks formed during multiple stages of Cenozoic volcanism. This study presents a petrophysical dataset for 61 rock specimens collected from Dongdo and Seodo, Dokdo, to support the interpretation of geological and geophysical data. The specimens comprise trachyte, trachyandesite I, II, and III, lapilli tuff, and ash tuff. title: The Lake Urmia Disaster – Manmade or Natural
abstract: Was the desiccation of Lake Urmia a natural disaster or a manmade collapse? This paper reverts climatic factors from foregrounds to background but brings forth a range of hidden drivers and diagnostic techniques to unravel the decisive role of the trigger cause: infrastructural encroachments, planning omissions, and governance failures. Applying the SPRC (Source, Pathways, Receptors, Consequences) framework, the analysis reveals how human decisions transformed a vulnerable lake into a wicked problem. journal: International Journal of Sustainability and Risk Control

title: GOVERNING INFORMALITY : Eviction, Recognition, and Legal Ambiguity in Kampung Akuarium, Jakarta
abstract: Abstract Informal settlements in Jakarta have long been governed through cycles of tolerance, eviction, and selective recognition. Rather than resulting from the absence of planning, informality is often produced through spatial regulations, legal ambiguity, and political intervention. This article examines Kampung Akuarium, a settlement in North Jakarta, to explore how informality is governed through planning instruments and political change. title: The Effect of Omega-3 Fatty Acids Supplement on Autism Spectrum Disorder
abstract: Autism is characterized by impairments in social interaction and communication skills, as well as repetitive behaviors and restricted interests. This review examined the potential effects of omega-3 fatty acid consumption on individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Articles included in the study were searched comprehensively in electronic databases such as PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar. abstract: Abstract Using archival and unofficial sources, this article examines how political calculations, economic considerations, local consumption patterns and international dynamics shaped the colonial administration’s water governance strategies in Hong Kong. It focuses on how the 1967 water emergency prompted the colonial government to recalibrate its approach, from a policy of manageable dependency to one of risk aversion. abstract: This article examines the aesthetic and political significance of the street writings of Hong Kong’s King of Kowloon (Tsang Tsou-choi) and Plumber King (Yim Chiu-tong) beyond celebratory framings of collective memory. title: Crop Husbandry After the Assyrian Conquest: The Case Study of Tel Kinrot (Kinneret, Tell el ʿ Orēme )
abstract: In 733/732 BCE, the Neo-Assyrian Empire conquered the Kingdom of Israel in the southern Levant, transforming settlement patterns and local economies. Scholars continue to debate the Assyrian economic agenda: some emphasise neglect, agricultural decline, and tribute extraction, while others argue that the Assyrian administration strategically reorganised agricultural production to meet local administrative and military needs. abstract: San Joaquin River-origin Central Valley Chinook Salmon are a species of conservation concern because they play an essential role in the health and function of California’s aquatic ecosystems yet experience low survival as juveniles pass through the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta (Delta) on their way to the Pacific Ocean. title: The Use of Suspended Substrate to Facilitate Juvenile Mussel Recruitment in Restored Mussel Reefs
abstract: Mussel reefs have been depleted globally by overfishing and habitat degradation, but the advent of reef restoration has produced promising results in terms of adult mussel survival and biodiversity enhancement. However, an absence of juvenile recruitment into restored mussel reefs is regularly cited as jeopardising their persistence and expansion. title: Settler colonial biopolitics at the border: a transnational entanglement of law, medical sciences, and migration control at Ellis Island
abstract: Migration from Europe to the United States in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries is known for its confrontation with racialized and gendered migration control. In line with this, this paper aims to analytically extend the migration control of that period to the biopolitics of settler colonialism. By patchworking transnational archives (in the United States and the Netherlands), it investigates how medical and immigration control infrastructures were established at Ellis Island (US) and how they operated to identify ‘undesirable immigrants’. title: It’s about time: On the uneven temporalities of Turkey’s first mega-dam
abstract: This article examines the Keban Dam (1966–1974), Turkey’s first mega-dam on the Upper Euphrates, as a case study of the uneven temporalities embedded in energy infrastructures. Conceptualising the dam as an infrastructural chronotope, it shows how mega-dams mediate conflicting temporalities linked to Cold War geopolitics, state-led modernisation and global capital. title: Scholars and Literati at the Académie Philomathique of Paris (1788–1800)
abstract: This document offers a concise portrait of the scholars who belonged to the Académie Philomathique of Paris from its founding in 1788 to the turn of the nineteenth century, in 1800. abstract: Preserving Indigenous Peoples’ values, rights, and sovereignty within food composition programmes is both an ethical obligation and a scientific necessity. The study investigates the ecclesiastical and political significance of these relations and their relevance to the strategic objectives pursued by European states in the region. abstract: This article uncovers an overlooked archive of religious poetry embedded in five Kyiv-Mohylian poetics manuals from 1685 to 1736, demonstrating how these poems served as a crucial mechanism by which Orthodox Kyiv participated in the learned culture of early modern Europe. abstract: Abstract Archaeological studies of the transatlantic slave trade in West Africa have traditionally focused on coastal and discrete sites of slavery, leaving interior communities comparatively underexplored. This paper advances methodological frameworks for the archaeology of transatlantic trade that move beyond the search for direct material signatures of enslavement to examine the circulation, appropriation, social valuation, and consumption of imported trade goods, and how they shaped political and economic landscapes in Peki, an Ewe-speaking polity in southeastern Ghana. abstract: Tropical montane forests provide essential ecosystem services that sustain human well-being and socioeconomic development, including provisioning, regulating, supporting, and cultural services. However, the absence of systematic economic valuation limits the incorporation of these services into public policy, territorial planning, and conservation investment decisions. abstract: Myths are recognized as cultural signifiers that encapsulate shared identity while simultaneously shaping societal norms. This dual function thus implies the interactions between individual agency and the construction of national consciousness. This study introduces the 2IN framework (phonetically ‘twin’) as an innovative model for myth and literary analysis. abstract: ABSTRACT Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) is the dominant non‐native fish species in Kenya's inland waters, but its spread reflects a coupled socioecological process rather than a simple biological invasion. This review examines the socio‐economic, governance and ecological drivers of its expansion within a socioecological systems and invasion biology framework, with evidence published between 2000 and 2025. abstract: Abstract Acoustic backscatter from gas bubbles is key to detecting and quantifying marine seeps and related processes, yet practical tools for target strength (TS) prediction remain limited. title: Personalized drug discovery from rare diseases to cancer
abstract: Precision medicine selects individual treatments from a small toolbox of therapies already available. Personalized drug discovery (PDD) brings this concept one step ahead, developing drugs for individual patient's diseases. Currently, PDD is being developed for rare disorders, where conventional drug discovery paradigms are non-applicable due to small patient sizes, but also for cancer. As a new frontier in precision medicine, PDD should be upscaled in rare and non-rare diseases.

abstract: Soil salinization is a widespread form of land degradation, yet how saline-alkaline stress is linked to belowground micro-food webs and shapes nitrogen transformations remains poorly understood. abstract: Abstract The integration of control augmentation techniques into helicopter systems aims to assist pilots during the critical phases of shipboard operations to mitigate the effects of ship motion, wind and other environmental factors that can compromise safety. abstract: Abstract The aviation industry is innovating to decrease its environmental impacts while maintaining high standards of safety. For example, new thermoplastic composite materials are being investigated to reduce weight and allow for material recycling (currently impossible with incumbent thermoset composites). abstract: Abstract Migratory bats remain poorly understood despite their ecological importance and increasing exposure to anthropogenic threats. abstract: ABSTRACT In aquaculture, omega‐3 fatty acids (FAs) are essential for fish health and growth during early development, making them important indicators of egg quality. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how far solid surfaces influence the structure of adjacent water remains a central challenge in interfacial science. Here, we demonstrate that nanoscale surface roughness can induce long‐range ordering of interfacial water extending over tens of molecular layers under ambient conditions. abstract: PREMISE: Understanding the process of species divergence and the mechanisms that drive genetic differentiation among closely related species is essential for explaining the origins of plant biodiversity. Geographic isolation and niche differentiation are key drivers of species divergence. Cycas chenii and C. guizhouensis are morphologically similar sister species from different river basins in Southwest China. abstract: Abstract. Space and time play a crucial role in multi-hazard impact assessment. When two or more natural hazards occur at the same location simultaneously or within a short time frame, the physical integrity of assets and infrastructures can be compromised and the resulting damage can be greater than the one generated by individual hazards occurring in isolation. abstract: Delivering exogenous compounds into fish eggs is a powerful tool for early stage manipulation. Here, we demonstrate that bath immersion enables efficient delivery of fluorescently labeled morpholino oligomers (MOs) into Atlantic salmon eggs when conjugated to the guanidinium rich cell-penetrating peptide nona-arginine. abstract: Anurans (frogs, toads, escuerzos) have been an important part of terrestrial ecosystems since the Mesozoic era. abstract: This study characterizes seismicity and stress regime in the westernmost part of the North Anatolian Fault Zone (NAFZ), focusing on the Saros segment, where dextral strike-slip deformation transitions into the transtensional northern Aegean domain. Unlike previous regional studies that combine Marmara and broader Aegean datasets or focus on individual rupture sequences, this study isolates a coordinate-bounded transition window to quantify the intrinsic seismic behavior of the terminal NAFZ–North Aegean Trough (NAT) linkage zone within a completeness-controlled framework. abstract: In invasive species, reproductive success may determine invasion outcomes and influence the choice of appropriate control and eradication. Trachemys scripta (Schoepff, 1792) is one of the world's most widespread invasive turtle species. Although some previous studies have focused on T. scripta reproduction, both in native and in non-native ranges, only one study has been carried out in Portugal, which reported clutch sizes. abstract: ABSTRACT Artemisia arborescens is a Mediterranean shrub widely used for essential oil production, generating significant amounts of spent biomass after extraction. abstract: Abstract Strong sky background radiation and motion-induced signal smearing are the key factors limiting the effective detection of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites during daytime. title: Characterisation of brown-rot decay in the historic Lejonström bridge using X-ray tomography and molecular identification of associated fungi
abstract: Abstract The gradual deterioration of historical structures is an urgent problem that requires regular monitoring, particularly when the main building material is pressure-impregnated Scots pine wood exposed to moisture and biological degradation. This study assessed the fungal degradation of the structural elements of the Lejonström bridge in Skellefteå, Sweden's oldest wooden bridge and a historically important and culturally significant monument. title: A comprehensive study on ferredoxin isoforms in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
abstract: Ferredoxins are central to cellular metabolism by mediating electron flow in energy conversion reactions. abstract: This research evaluated the occupational safety, health (OSH) conditions, operational performance, and workplace hurdles experienced by field engineers across the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Bohol First, Second, and Third District Engineering Offices (DEO). Anchored upon the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Theory, Institutional Theory, and the Swiss Cheese Model, the research used a total population census design (N=75, n=25 per district) involving Project Engineers, Project Inspectors, and Material Testing Engineers. abstract: Indonesia is a maritime country with a large potential in fisheries, however it has a big challenge to fulfill the market needs, especially for the commodities of freshwater fish like tilapia, catfish, and carp. Capital constraints, technology and small-tomedium scale producers mean that capacity aquaculture production cannot reliably fulfill the demands of industry. title: Further records of Lycodon irwini Naveen, Mirza, Choure & Chandramouli, 2025 (Squamata, Colubridae) from Great Nicobar, India
abstract: We report additional records of the recently described, supposedly rare species of wolf snake, Lycodon irwini Naveen et al., 2025, known only from Great Nicobar Island, India. We report 14 sightings of this species from opportunistic encounters recorded during sporadic surveys over seven months. This highlights the limited extent of previous surveys in this region and suggests that this species is not as rare as previously assumed. abstract: Abstract Underground gas storage (UGS) operations can perturb reservoir conditions and modulate local seismicity, but the temporal evolution of this response under cyclic injection–withdrawal remains poorly constrained. abstract: The use of lignocellulosic biomass as a renewable raw material for the production of cellulosic ethanol requires pretreatment. Unfortunately, this process can generate numerous by-products that have a toxic effect on yeasts. Understanding the response of yeast is crucial if measures are to be developed that allow adaptation under multifactorial stress conditions. abstract: Wetland plants must supply oxygen to their rhizomes and roots to maintain aerobic respiration despite soil anoxia. Excess oxygen can diffuse into the environment, strongly affecting rhizosphere biogeochemistry. This radial oxygen loss (ROL) has often been observed to increase in the daytime, perhaps supported by photosynthetic oxygen production and stomatal opening. title: Exploring male and female mate preferences using genetic algorithms and digital phenotypes
abstract: Abstract During mate choice, both males and females can exhibit choosiness when selecting a partner. The expression and measurement of preferences is typically constrained by the traits presented during mate-choice trials, which generally represent a subset of the phenotypic trait space and thus may not capture the full range of potential preferences. abstract: Defects are increasingly recognized as powerful modulators of the chemistry and photophysics of fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), enabling tunable optical responses toward exogenously introduced analytes. abstract: ABSTRACT Biocatalytic regioselective acylation is a powerful strategy for diversifying natural products and optimizing their pharmacological properties. title: Effects of Aeration on Growth and Production of Carps in Chitwan, Nepal
abstract: An experiment was conducted to assess effects of aeration on water quality and yield of carps at farmer‘s pond of Kathar, Chitwan, Nepal for 225 days from 25 May 2018 to 10 January 2019. abstract: The cooling efficiency of green spaces exhibits intra-urban spatial heterogeneity, yet systematic assessments of how greenness, benefiting population size, and other environmental factors affect this efficiency remain scarce. Taking Wuhan as a case study, this research proposes an integrated framework to elucidate how green space cooling benefits align with population needs and to explain the underlying environmental drivers of spatial variations in cooling efficiency. abstract: The El Gigante Metamorphic Complex, in the homonymous range (Sierras Pampeanas, Argentina), consists of three lithostratigraphic units that, from bottom to top, are: Quebrada Grande (Mesoproterozoic protoliths), Loma Cortada (Ediacaran-early Cambrian sedimentary protoliths), and Los Morteritos (middle to late Cambrian protoliths), all reworked by the Famatinian orogeny. title: Cold atmospheric plasma decontamination of indoor mold
abstract: Abstract Indoor molds damage building materials and can compromise occupant health. Correction of the moisture source and physical removal of contaminated material remain central to remediation, but inactivation of residual viable growth may be useful as an adjunct where heat or liquid biocides are unsuitable. title: Prevalence and associated factors of traditional eyelash epilation among patients with trachomatous trichiasis in South Ethiopia
abstract: Trachoma remains the leading infectious cause of blindness globally, with Ethiopia bearing the highest disease burden. Trachomatous trichiasis (TT), the advanced stage of trachoma, requires surgical correction to prevent irreversible blindness. However, many affected patients rely on traditional eyelash epilation as an alternative to surgery. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of traditional eyelash epilation and identify factors associated with its practice among TT patients in South Ethiopia. abstract: Ecosystem services (ES) are fundamental to achieving human well-being. To systematically evaluate ES and their interrelationships in forest-enriched regions, this study takes Guilin, a representative forest-rich area in China, as the study area and develops an integrated coupling model for the comprehensive measurement and interaction analysis of provisioning, regulating, and cultural ES. abstract: Purpose This study aims to assess flood-prone areas in Auckland, New Zealand, using stream order analysis as a geospatial tool to delineate flood risk zones. The research addresses the growing need for efficient flood risk mapping in urban settings by providing a simplified, yet effective, method for identifying high-risk zones. abstract: Abstract The extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix serves as a structural scaffold for biofilm organization, contributing to structural integrity and antimicrobial tolerance by modulating the penetration and distribution of antimicrobial agents. abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into software development workflows, their trustworthiness has become a critical concern. title: Simulated visual attention modelling in digital tourism interfaces: an integrative approach to destination communication
abstract: This paper introduces a simulation-based methodological and conceptual study addressing a critical gap in tourism research: the fragmented treatment of spatial, sequential and temporal dimensions of visual attention. abstract: Carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) are independent domains generally appended in carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) with carbohydrate-binding functions. abstract: Vegetation monitoring in areas affected by plant pathogens is essential for assessing the vulnerability of plant communities and supporting the management of infected territories. A total of 120 traditional cashew trees were sampled from the two districts, with 60 samples from each study site. Morphological descriptors for cashew developed by the International Board for Plant and Genetic Resources (IBPGR) in 1986 were used for the phenotypic characterization of traditional cashew populations. abstract: Introducción: La contratación pública puede ampliar el acceso de las micro, pequeñas y medianas empresas (MIPYMES) a mercados institucionales, aunque su aprovechamiento depende de capacidades administrativas, liquidez y condiciones de competencia. abstract: Logic-Based Therapy (LBT) is a method of philosophical counseling and psychotherapy based on Rational-Emotive Behavior Therapy (REBT) that uses logic, philosophy, and a network of “guiding virtues” to treat behavioral and emotional dysfunctions. abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread use of zebrafish as a biological model, comprehensive baseline elemental data across its developmental stages remain limited. In this work, ion beam analytical techniques were employed to establish the elemental composition of zebrafish larvae and adults under controlled vivarium conditions. abstract: The Cunqian Cu-Pb-Zn deposit is a significant skarn-porphyry deposit located at the junction of the eastern and central segments of the Qin-Hang metallogenic belt (QHMB) in China. However, ore prospecting in this area has been hindered by insufficient research on ore-related intrusions relative to adjacent areas. abstract: A high-level assessment of the production potential and costs of three synthetic e-fuels, methane, methanol and Fischer–Tropsch diesel, derived from renewable hydrogen and biogenic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) was conducted for maritime transport in the EU and Ireland for 2050. Biogenic CO 2 sources included by-products from biomethane production and ethanol fermentation (priced at €30/tonne), and emissions from biomass combustion (€80/tonne). abstract: ABSTRACT Hospitals generate wastewater enriched with human-derived microbes, making them strong sites for focused, near-source surveillance of pathogens. We compared in-sewer 24-h composite and passive sampling at two hospital discharge locations and influent sampling at a municipal wastewater treatment plant (WWTP). title: Repurposing the Insecticide Flufenerim, the Only Anti- Cryptococcus Compound Identified in the MMV Global Health Priority Box, as a Candidate for the Environmental Control of the Cryptococcosis Agents
abstract: Abstract Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are environmental fungi that cause cryptococcosis, a severe, life-threatening infection, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Current treatments are limited by toxicity, restricted availability, and the emergence of resistance, highlighting the need for novel antifungal agents. title: Automated fledgling call detection links adult songbird abundance to reproductive success in restored habitat
abstract: Many wildlife monitoring programs assume that adult abundance reflects habitat quality and, by extension, reproductive success, despite the possibility of these parameters decoupling. Abundance may be more likely to decouple with reproduction in human-modified landscapes such as those created through habitat restoration. However, the extent to which this occurs remains unclear due to extensive manual effort required for monitoring reproduction, especially at scale. Passive-acoustic monitoring (PAM) has recently shown promise for detecting fledgling begging calls to infer reproductive success.

title: Sex-specific intestinal transcriptional responses to oral polyvinyl chloride microplastic exposure in Wistar rats, with an in-vitro validation in a human gut model
abstract: The widespread presence of microplastics in the environment has raised concerns about potential health effects following oral exposure in humans, particularly in individuals with impaired intestinal barrier function. This study investigated the effects of dietary polyvinyl chloride (PVC) microplastics fragments (<25 μm) in healthy and dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis Wistar rats, with a complementary assessment in a human 3D intestinal microtissue model. title: N-LAS-IAM: Climate change in a balance-of-payments framework
abstract: Climate change is becoming a macro-financial development problem for peripheral economies, yet integrated assessment models remain poorly equipped to analyse climate vulnerability in externally constrained developing countries. Existing heterodox models are mostly closed or global, while balance-of-payments-constrained growth models treat climate in reduced form and incompletely formalise the financial channel. title: Genetic diversity and conservation of a rare Miconia species (Melastomataceae) from the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
abstract: Biodiversity is undergoing an unprecedented global decline, and genetic diversity plays a fundamental role in ensuring species persistence. Miconia ulei, an endemic species from the eastern Atlantic Forest in Santa Catarina, southern Brazil, is rare and has few known populations. We investigated genetic diversity and population structure using microsatellite markers and assessed its conservation status following IUCN guidelines and by incorporating genetic parameters in the evaluation. title: The cool façade paradox: Balancing urban climate regulation and outdoor thermal stress – A systematized review
abstract: Cool façades — building walls with high solar reflectance and high thermal emittance — are promoted as a passive urban cooling strategy. However, their effects on outdoor thermal strain remain insufficiently understood. This systematized review synthesizes evidence from 77 studies to quantify the effects of increased façade solar reflectance on air temperature and outdoor thermal stress in urban environments. title: When psychedelic discourse meets local narrative: Selective uptake of psychedelic meanings surrounding mad honey in Nepal
abstract: AIMS: 'Mad honey' is produced when bees collect nectar from Rhododendron species containing grayanotoxins, naturally occurring diterpenoid toxins that can produce dose-dependent intoxication. It has long been embedded in Nepalese medicinal and ritual practices but has recently become part of global psychedelic discourse. This study examined how globally circulating discourse and local narrative practices interact in shaping meanings of intoxication, using mad honey as a case. abstract: The untapped metabolome of filamentous fungi represents a profound reservoir for therapeutic lead discovery. Although genomic mining confirms an abundance of cryptic biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), axenic laboratory culture frequently lacks the ecological stimuli required to trigger their expression, inevitably leading to the redundant isolation of known metabolites. title: The Evolution and Assessment of Intelligence Architectures in Nigerian Security: A Historical Analysis
abstract: This paper has discussed the development and evaluation of intelligence structures in Nigeria, and how these structures are effective in dealing with the modern internal security issues. The study follows the historical evolution of intelligence systems in Nigeria, which started with indigenous security establishments in the pre-colonial period and colonial surveillance systems, through the centralization of the systems in the post-independent era, expansions of the systems in the military era, and the reform in the democratic era. abstract: Assessing magma storage conditions relies critically on crystal-melt equilibrium models. However, natural rocks are replete with disequilibrium features that testify to open-system processes and episodic crystal growth. Interface kinetics at the crystal-melt boundary lag behind changes of physicochemical conditions determined by magma dynamics. Since wide adoption of the One Health framework, wildlife species have been identified as important potential reservoirs and vectors of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria. abstract: Leafhoppers damage plants by piercing and sucking leaf tissues. Among the leafhopper species occurring in Central Anatolia, Zyginidia sohrab (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) is the most widespread and abundant species. This study was conducted under natural field conditions during the 2021 and 2022 growing seasons to investigate the bioecology of Z. sohrab in maize production areas. abstract: Biological invasions and range expansions act as natural experiments for understanding evolutionary processes at and beyond a species' range margin. However, unlike manipulative experiments, invasions and range expansions are less genetically tractable and often involve genotypes of uncertain origin that are subject to complex evolutionary pressures. abstract: BACKGROUND: Food systems are a key contributor to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Given the multi-sectoral nature of AMR, a One Health perspective has been advocated. Recent research situates AMR as an emerging property of a complex system, a perspective which can help identify root drivers of AMR and theorise the impacts of proposed solutions. This study aims to combine systems modelling and a One Health perspective to identify system-level dynamics and priority actions for addressing AMR in food systems. title: Development of a browser–based computational tool for preliminary estimation of vertical-axis wind turbine power output
abstract: Rapid estimation of vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) power output is essential for preliminary assessment. However, existing approaches using spreadsheets, software, or simulations are resource-intensive and require a tedious process. This study presents a lightweight browser-based computational framework developed using JavaScript for rapid preliminary estimation of VAWT power output. title: Shadow Pricing Ecosystem Services in Boreal Forests
abstract: Abstract Boreal forests jointly produce marketed goods and non-market ecosystem services, generating unavoidable trade-offs. We estimate shadow prices with the directional distance function (R. G. Chambers et al. 1996), endogenizing the directional vector and correcting for sampling variation via bootstrap methods. abstract: In the arid regions of Kazakhstan, agricultural crops are grown on low-productivity saline-alkali soils with varying properties across different horizons. Soil tillage is performed using non-plow implements that generate high traction resistance and turn over large clods of soil with a low degree of fragmentation. abstract: The implementation of digital systems in public administration has become increasingly important in improving the effectiveness, transparency, and accountability of public service delivery. abstract: This study investigates how shipping containers are repurposed as architecture in Accra, Ghana. The study reveals the spatial factors shaping the emergence of these adaptive structures. Rather than being randomly situated, containers cluster in strategic locations enabling access to livelihoods while also avoiding eviction threats. title: Differentiated mosquito adaptive strategies underlie regional dominance of three ECSA sub-lineages in chikungunya virus
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has emerged as a rapidly expanding global health threat and has been reported in 119 countries and territories, with recent outbreaks across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype has increasingly predominated in multiple regions, yet the molecular basis of its competitive advantage remains unresolved. abstract: Abstract The presence of a nebula around massive hot stars often works as an indicator that the object is either in an advanced evolutionary stage or a rare product of close binary interaction. abstract: Soil is an essential and strategic resource for the sustainability of agricultural production on the planet; however, it faces progressive degradation derived from unsustainable management practices and the effects of climate change. NASA’s Phenolic Impregnated Carbon Ablator, and its carbon preform, FiberForm, were subjected to aerothermal environments relevant to Earth and Titan atmospheric entry in the Plasmatron X inductively coupled plasma wind tunnel.
