title: How Socio-Cultural Structures Shape Strategies of Climate-Resilient Social Protection Pathways in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
abstract: Low-income households in Sub-Saharan Africa have limited resilience to climate change shocks despite the region's unique socio-cultural support structures. This article explores how socio-cultural structures such as gender norms, social networks, social cohesion, trust, indigenous knowledge, customs and traditions, and cultural values of reciprocity shape climate-resilient social protection pathways among low-income households. title: Aridity-driven shifts in plant–microbial diversity relationships across the arid and semi-arid grasslands of northern China
abstract: Abstract Climate change-driven aridification threatens above- and belowground biodiversity, yet how the relationships between plant diversity and soil microbial diversity change along aridity gradients remains unclear. Here, we conducted a 4,000-km field survey across arid and semi-arid grasslands in northern China. abstract: Engineered probiotic biointerfaces are the dynamic boundaries through which modified bacteria interact with their biological surroundings. They can improve bacterial survival, mucosal retention and therapeutic delivery, but the structural basis of these effects is often unclear. This review groups biointerfaces by their dominant role: barrier protection, recognition, responsiveness, interaction and renewal by living cells. abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) communication system between a Texas Instruments TMS320F28335 Microcontroller Unit (MCU) and an Intel Altera Cyclone V 5CSEMA5F31C6N Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). abstract: Community-level average genome size (AGS) is a key trait linking microbial diversity, functional potential, and eco-evolutionary strategy, yet estimates of AGS diverge markedly among common methods. title: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial
abstract: Abstract Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 has been proposed as a biological driver of Long COVID, a disabling chronic illness with no proven treatments. abstract: Purpose: This study examines the relationships between professionalism, mindfulness, and job satisfaction among airline pilots and explores the mediating role of mindfulness in the relationship between professionalism and job satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach: The study employs a quantitative survey design. The sample consists of 171 airline pilots. abstract: Mechanistic frameworks linking climate to zoonotic disease risk through host ecology remain rare, limiting transferable insights across systems. We develop a Bayesian framework combining an integral projection model of rodent demography with a compartmental disease model. title: Genetic diversity in soybean [ Glycine max ( L .) Merr.] genotypes based on agro‐morphological traits using univariate and multivariate statistical techniques
abstract: Abstract Soybean [ Glycine max (L.) Merr.] is a versatile leguminous crop that plays a vital role in biodiesel production, livestock feed, and enhancing global food security. Soybean production and productivity in Ethiopia are low compared to the national potential, mainly due to the lack of high‐yielding genotypes. Substantial genetic variability is essential for developing high‐yielding, climate‐resilient soybean varieties. title: Infant-caregiver vocal contingency changes across varying interpersonal space
abstract: Vocal contingency between caregivers and infants is a fundamental building block for socio-communicative development. This paper investigates vocal contingency in home settings and how it varies as a function of the physical distance between infants and their caregivers. We recorded 61 mother-infant dyads when infants were 5-14 months old during long-form home recording sessions (M = 7.2 h; SD = 2.3; Range = 1-13), using wearable audio and proximity sensors. title: Behaviour of the Eurasian otter at latrines along a gradient of anthropogenic landscape context
abstract: Abstract Increasing human pressure on fluvial ecosystems can alter wildlife behaviour, particularly where human activities modify habitat structure and the conditions under which behaviours are expressed at key communication sites. In this study, we examined how environmental and proxies of anthropogenic variables influence behavioural expression of the Eurasian otter Lutra lutra at latrine sites, which function as key locations for chemical communication. abstract: Mega-projects are large-scale developments that profoundly transform landscapes while delivering infrastructure and socio-economic benefits. However, they are also major drivers of biodiversity loss through multiple direct and indirect impacts. abstract: ABSTRACT Background The ability to learn is central to innovation and performance across industries, and it is the hallmark feature of the rapidly growing movement toward Learning Health Systems. While learning drivers—such as experimentation, risk‐taking, participative decision‐making, dialogue, and interaction with the external environment—are well defined, they have received little attention in healthcare contexts. abstract: A partir de los hallazgos de la investigación doctoral del autor, el texto plantea que las herramientas de la democracia participativa pueden ayudar a que el actuar del Estado se dirija hacia el desarrollo de ciertos derechos o principios constitucionales. abstract: ABSTRACT Visible/near‐infrared (Vis/NIR) spectroscopy offers a promising non‐destructive technique for assessing round eggplant ( Solanum melongena var. esculentum ) quality. title: Occupational branches of Japan’s ruling party: building linkages while hedging clientelist exposure
abstract: Abstract Reassessing the underappreciated grassroots of Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), I argue that the party’s localized institutions not only mobilize votes but also mitigate the risks of clientelism. Informed by field research and relying on documentary evidence, descriptive statistics, and financial records, I identify mechanisms that link the party to citizens, even in the periphery. abstract: Serratia proteamaculans is an environmentally widespread member of the genus Serratia isolated from aquatic animals, food products, plants, insects, environmental habitats and clinical sources. Ecologically broadly distributed, little is known about its genomic diversity and factors associated with antimicrobial resistance and virulence. In this study, we used five years (2020–2024) of passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) data from southern Vietnam to analyze the monthly and daily rhythms of vocal activity in a nocturnal tropical bird, the great eared nightjar (Lyncornis macrotis). The study draws on quantitative data collected by Statistics South Africa. The General Household Survey (GHS) for 2019 was manipulated to meet study objectives. abstract: Electromagnetically driven tools offer a promising way to accelerate conventional tools to high speeds in order to take advantage of the beneficial effects of high strain rates in material processing. abstract: Microplastic accumulation is an increasingly widespread anthropogenic disturbance in agricultural soils, yet ecological risk assessments remain dominated by simplified laboratory assays that may not capture context-dependent responses under field conditions. Here, we combined a five-year experiment across four semi-arid cropland sites with a global synthesis restricted exclusively to outdoor field observations to quantify microplastic effects on crop yield, soil quality, and ecosystem multifunctionality. title: Overwintering Strategies Drive Climate Change Impacts on Body Mass in Northern Mammals
abstract: Climate change drives variable shifts in mammalian body sizes, yet the mechanisms underlying this variation remain unclear. Two explanations prevail: (1) higher temperatures reduce thermal constraints, favouring smaller bodies; or (2) warming enhances primary productivity, supporting larger bodies. abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a leading cause of dementia, and neighborhood greenness may represent a protective environmental exposure. title: Comparing wolf feeding ecology between historical ranges and recently colonized human-dominated lowlands
abstract: The recent spread of wolves into highly human-modified landscapes in Europe is an important example of large carnivore recovery and illustrates their ability to live in environments very different from those usually considered suitable for the species. This study aimed to evaluate how wolf feeding habits vary over time and across space by comparing diet composition, trophic niche breadth, and key prey consumption between the historical Apennine range and the recently colonized Po Plain in north-western Italy, based on scat samples collected between 2021 and 2025. abstract: Lumpy skin disease (LSD) is a vector-borne transboundary disease that causes substantial productivity losses in cattle. abstract: Water resources management in semi-arid regions requires adaptive irrigation strategies that simultaneously consider climate variability, crop water demand, and water productivity. title: Integrative analyses revealed the domestication history, genomic targets of breeding and the spatiotemporal expression patterns of fruit traits in Chinese bayberry ( Myrica rubra )
abstract: Abstract he Chinese bayberry (Myrica rubra) is an important fruit crop in southern China with a domestication history longer than 3000 years. It is the only domesticated fruit crop in the family Myricaceae. In this study, we sequenced genomes of more than 200 wild and cultivated individuals and proposed that M. rubra diverged firstly in Northeast Asia before spreading from southwest to southeast China where the primary domestication occurred. title: Statistical confidence interval inference for subsurface electrical resistivity structure from magnetotelluric impedances and geomagnetic transfer functions, assisted by forward modeling
abstract: This paper proposes a scheme for the statistical confidence interval inference of a subsurface electrical resistivity model in magnetotellurics and geomagnetic depth soundings. The method assesses the confidence interval of resistivity for a target block in optimal model obtained through inversion. The target block consists of a number of model elements and is confined by an operator. title: A self-assembled Dendrobium polysaccharide hydrogel with anti-aging activity via the FOXO signaling pathway
abstract: Faced with the complexity and diversity of skin aging, it is critical to investigate multi-target synergistic anti-aging products. Herein, a novel composite hydrogel with anti-aging activity was developed based on Dendrobium polysaccharide, hyaluronic acid (HA), and nicotinamide (NMN). The hydrogen bond and van der Waals force were the main driving forces in the self-assembly interaction between Dendrobium polysaccharides (DDAM-1 and DOMOS), HA, and NMN. title: Determination of Certain Physicochemical Properties of Olive Oils Under Different Storage Conditions
abstract: Olive oil is a widely consumed vegetable oil known for its health-promoting properties. Unlike most other vegetable oils, it is obtained directly from the fruit and produced entirely through physical processes without chemical treatment, allowing it to be consumed in its natural form while preserving its vitamins, essential fatty acids, and other bioactive compounds. Due to its high nutritional value and antioxidant content, olive oil is suitable for direct consumption; however, maintaining these properties depends largely on appropriate storage conditions and packaging. title: Comparative Google Earth Engine Workflows for Flood and Landslide Diagnostics in Lower Silesia, Poland, and Batang Kali, Malaysia
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates Google Earth Engine (GEE) as the central computational environment for a unified, repeatable workflow for post-event geospatial diagnostics of two contrasting natural hazards: the September 2024 flood in Lower Silesia, Poland, and the December 2022 Batang Kali landslide in Selangor, Malaysia. Both cases followed the same analytical sequence: pre-event and post-event image selection, generation of a continuous change layer, threshold-based binary mask extraction, z-score standardization of change magnitude, point-based validation, and cartographic export. title: CHALLENGES OF ADEQUATELY RENDERING ENGLISH-LANGUAGE MILITARY REALITIES IN THE CONTEXT OF INTEROPERABILITY IN ACCORDANCE WITH NATO STANDARDS
abstract: This article examines the complex issue of the adequate translation of English-language military realia into Ukrainian, a critically important aspect of ensuring the linguistic and cultural interoperability of Ukraine's security and defense institutions with the armed forces of NATO member states.The relevance of the study stems from Ukraine's intensive integration into the Euro-Atlantic security environment, which requires impeccable communicative and terminological accuracy during multinational operations, military exercises, and the exchange of strategic information.The aim of the research

title: Asymmetric Dependence Structure Between Climate Risk Volatility and Chinese Crude Oil Futures Commodity Price Using Copulas
abstract: Outlining the volatility of climate risk has become increasingly important in the financial sector. This study examines the correlation between climate change risk, economic policy, and Chinese crude oil futures. The dynamic copulas approach is used to assess both overall and tail dependence. A significant relationship exists between Chinese crude oil futures and climate uncertainty (CU) as well as climate policy uncertainty (CPU). title: Effect of Nutrition Education Intervention Based on Health Belief Model on Dietary Diversity Practices of Pregnant Women in Rural Western Ethiopia: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial, 2026
abstract: Inadequate dietary diversity during pregnancy is a major public health concern in Ethiopia, contributing to maternal undernutrition and adverse pregnancy outcomes.Theory-based nutrition education interventions have shown promise but have not been rigorously evaluated in remote, low-resource settings using cluster-randomized designs.This study aimed to assess the effect of a nutrition education intervention based on the Health Belief Model (HBM) on dietary diversity practices of pregnant women in rural western Ethiopia.A community-based pretestposttest cluster-randomized controlled trial was co

title: The Role of Ultra‐Thin Passive Films and Organic Adsorbates on Aluminum Chips for a Friction‐Induced Solid‐State Recycling Process
abstract: Friction‐induced recycling is a method to recycle aluminum with a lower energy footprint than conventional methods. However, the quality of a metal–metal joint is strongly influenced by surface contamination, in particular by naturally formed oxide layers. Octadecyl phosphonic acid and methyl diphosphonic acid self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are deposited on aluminum chips bound for recycling in order to improve their storage stability. title: “External Debt and Development Resilience During Global Crises: Evidence from Developing Countries”
abstract: The accumulation of external debt has renewed concerns about the capacity of developing economies to withstand increasingly frequent global shocks. Yet the conventional debt literature remains largely centered on economic growth, offering limited insight into whether indebted economies can preserve broader development stability during crises. This study examines the relationship between external debt and development resilience across 40 developing countries over 2010–2024. journal: International Journal of Human Research and Social Development

title: Climate-driven shifts in the distribution of the rare earth element hyperaccumulator fern Blechnopsis orientalis: Implications for phytomining and conservation strategies in China
abstract: Rising global temperatures are altering species distributions, yet the long-term dynamics of pteridophytes remain poorly documented. Here, we project the potential habitat dynamics of Blechnopsis orientalis , a fern with exceptional rare earth element (REE) accumulation capacity and promising applications in green phytomining, across China under both contemporary and future climate scenarios. title: Expanding Solar-Powered Irrigation for Smallholder Farmers in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Web-Based Suitability Assessment Tool
abstract: Agricultural production in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is predominantly rainfed, making smallholder farming highly vulnerable to rainfall variability and climate change. Limited access to reliable and affordable energy further constrains irrigation expansion. Solar photovoltaic (PV)-powered irrigation offers a promising pathway to expand irrigation while reducing dependence on conventional energy sources. title: Secondary neurulation mechanisms likely arose in vertebrates during mesenchymal tailbud extension
abstract: Introduction The central nervous system (CNS) is an essential organ system common to all vertebrates and is one of the defining features of the Chordata phylum. In Chordates, neural tubes may form via either primary neurulation, secondary neurulation, or a mixture of the two. During primary neurulation, there is folding of an already-polarized epithelium. In contrast, secondary neurulation involves mesenchymal to epithelial transition, cell interdigitation and sometimes de novo cavitation from an initially solid rod of mesenchymal cells. title: Habitat Loss Through Renewable Energy Infrastructure: Budgeting the Energetic Consequences for Wintering Geese
abstract: The global expansion of renewable energy is a key societal objective but may conflict with nature conservation interests by causing habitat loss. Hence, planning energy infrastructure requires a thorough understanding of the behavior and habitat requirements of affected species during critical phases of the annual cycle. We assessed the energetic consequences of losing agricultural foraging habitat for a wintering goose species with a high degree of site-fidelity. title: Deployment-oriented benchmark for automated UAV-based facade defect detection
abstract: Integrating computer vision with UAVs can automate parts of building facade inspection while reducing labor and access risks. Applying UAV-based defect detection to regional multi-building screening, however, requires planning of coverage-derived data construction, task definition and labeling effort, detector selection, and recurring-error mitigation. This paper presents BFD-UAV2K, a benchmark comprising 2000 full-frame images collected from 42 reinforced-concrete buildings, with three-class defect annotations and building-disjoint data partitions. title: Processes of multi-system co-evolution: Insights from carbon capture and storage in Norway
abstract: Net-zero solutions such as carbon capture and storage (CCS) require the creation of whole new clusters of innovations rather than “merely” a transition in existing systems or the diffusion of single technologies. While prior work highlights negative cross-system interdependencies (e.g., chicken and egg problems), this paper presents a theorization and an empirical study of the processes of multi-system co-evolution that contribute to the formation and development of multi-system complexes. title: Circularity measures enhance resilience of net zero pathways for agriculture
abstract: Abstract Reducing environmental impact of agriculture is paramount for sustainable food production. Development of a circular bioeconomy can contribute to environmental objectives, yet the interaction of circularity measures with net zero strategies is poorly understood. Using integrated modelling and 12 key performance indicators, we assess the sustainability and resilience of two simulated circular strategies implemented within a business as usual and three net zero greenhouse gas emission pathways for Ireland’s land sector. title: Stable isotope signatures of pelotons and rhizomorphs reveal nutritional plasticity in Cremastra appendiculata (Orchidaceae)
abstract: Abstract Many photosynthetic orchids combine photosynthesis with fungal carbon acquisition, yet the isotopic relationships between orchids and their fungal partners remain poorly resolved. Direct stable isotope analysis of pelotons and extraradical fungal tissues can refine fungal baselines and clarify nutritional dynamics in orchid mycorrhizas. title: Cronología y estrategias de subsistencia durante el Gravetiense en la cueva de Altamira (Santillana del Mar, Cantabria)
abstract: La cueva de Altamira es mundialmente conocida como la Capilla Sixtina del Paleolítico. Sin embargo, el conocimiento sobre los modos de vida de los grupos humanos que la ocuparon durante el Paleolítico Superior es limitado. El presente estudio expone nuevos datos sobre la cronología y las estrategias de subsistencia de la ocupación gravetiense a partir del estudio de los restos bioarqueológicos, combinando un análisis arqueozoológico y tafonómico con paleoproteómica a través de ZooMS (Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry). title: Saponins induce lipid-dependent structural heterogeneity and modulate membrane organization in phospholipid bilayers
abstract: Abstract Saponins are amphiphilic natural compounds whose membrane activity is commonly attributed to sterol complexation, whereas their effects on sterol-free membranes remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how lipid packing governs the interaction of a Saponaria officinalis saponin extract with cholesterol-free phosphatidylcholine (PC) and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) membranes using differential scanning calorimetry, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, small-angle X-ray scattering, dynamic light scattering, atomic force microscopy, and calcein-release assays. title: New perspectives for high pressure X-ray emission spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction at ID27, ESRF: investigating spin transition in magnesiosiderite
abstract: The high pressure beamline ID27 at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility has been upgraded to include a von Hámos X-ray emission spectrometer, expanding the beamline's capabilities for investigating structural and electronic properties under extreme conditions. To test the setup, a natural magnesiosiderite (Mg0.42Fe0.56Mn0.02CO3) was studied in a diamond anvil cell up to 50 GPa. The experiments were carried out using incident beam energies of 23.5 and 15.6 keV. title: Atmospheric-pressure cold plasma assisted enhancement of germination and nutritional trait of peanut seeds
abstract: Introduction Improving seed germination and early seedling growth using environmentally friendly, chemical-free technologies is essential for enhancing crop productivity and agricultural sustainability. This study investigated the effects of low-power dielectric barrier discharge (DBD)-based ACP treatment on the physicochemical characteristics, germination, antioxidant activity, and early seedling growth of peanut seeds. title: Communication Technology and Globalization: Bridging Worlds or widening Divides
abstract: This study examines how communication technology shapes contemporary globalization and why the same technologies can simultaneously integrate and divide the world. Earlier scholarship has documented either the integrative or the exclusionary effects of digital media, but few studies explain the conditions under which each outcome prevails. Using an integrative narrative literature review, the study synthesized 35 scholarly and institutional sources retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the statistical repositories of the ITU and UNCTAD. title: Why Some Gestures Work Better than Others: Toward a Model of Gesture-Supported Vocabulary Learning
abstract: Abstract Gesture has emerged as a powerful multimodal tool in vocabulary acquisition, with converging behavioral and neuroscientific evidence for its facilitative role in second language (L2) vocabulary learning. Yet in both instructional practice and experimental research, gestures are often treated as relatively homogeneous, despite systematic variation in their characteristics and implementation that may contribute to heterogeneous learning outcomes. title: Sustainable colloidal nanostructures for advanced PEMFC coolants: stability, environmental implications, and lifecycle challenges
abstract: The development of advanced coolant media is increasingly important for improving thermal regulation in proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks while addressing concerns related to material use, operational durability, and environmental sustainability. Colloidal nanostructures dispersed in conventional and alternative base fluids have attracted considerable attention because their composition, concentration, interfacial behaviour, and dispersion characteristics can be tailored to modify coolant thermophysical properties. title: How to assess trade-offs in sustainability certification of low-ILUC-risk biomass – current status and proposals for best practices
abstract: Abstract Background Indirect land use change (ILUC) is a major challenge for sustainable biomass and bioenergy production. Although the use of low-ILUC-risk practices in sustainability certification could effectively manage ILUC risks, several potential trade-offs can arise from the use of such practices (e.g. biodiversity loss). However, it is not yet clear whether the certification criteria and indicators (C&I) proposed in certification schemes and in the literature to assess these trade-offs are appropriate to certify sustainable low-ILUC-risk biomass. title: Probabilistic validation of community-scale tornado damage models for historic unreinforced masonry buildings
abstract: Communities with rich cultural heritage are increasingly vulnerable to tornado hazards, yet the structural resilience of older unreinforced masonry (URM) buildings remains understudied. State-of-the-art platforms for predicting damage at a community scale, such as IN-CORE (Interdependent Networked Community Resilience Modeling Environment), use a single random wind speed on the Enhanced Fujita (EF) scale rather than a continuous spectrum, thereby introducing inherent stochasticity into model predictions. title: Progressive effects of upstream flow aeration on two-phase hydraulic jump dynamics in rectangular channels: a CFD investigation
abstract: A hydraulic jump is a rapid transition from supercritical to subcritical flow, associated with intense turbulence and air entrainment. Upstream aeration differentially influences key hydraulic jump components, including free-surface profile, roller length, turbulence characteristics and energy dissipation. This numerical study utilizes OpenFOAM with the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method and the Standard k–ε turbulence model to investigate hydraulic jumps at a Froude number (Fr) of 7.5, under controlled upstream aeration levels ranging from 0% to 50%. title: DS-PRNet: lightweight camouflaged object detection with dynamic sparse attention and feature-, attention-, and output-level distillation
abstract: Existing camouflaged object detection (COD) models are computationally demanding, which limits their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this challenge, we propose DS-PRNet, a lightweight COD framework that integrates a Dynamic Sparse Attention (DSA) module with a feature-, attention-, and output-level distillation strategy. title: VESTA: In-Vehicle Sensing with GNSS Satellite Signals
abstract: Vehicles have become an indispensable part of modern life. Over the past decade, perception systems such as radar and LiDAR have become increasingly popular for out-vehicle sensing. In contrast, comparatively little attention has been paid to in-vehicle sensing. While camera-based solutions raise privacy concerns, wireless sensing-based approaches typically require dedicated transmitters, increasing deployment costs and potentially interfering with existing wireless communications. title: An improved approach for rainfall-runoff simulation under anthropogenic influence
abstract: Human activities significantly influence the rainfall-runoff process, leading to pronounced fluctuations in runoff data and presenting substantial challenges for accurate simulation. In this study, the Water Allocation and Simulation (WAS) model was adopted and enhanced to simulate rainfall-runoff under the impact of human activities. The virtual reservoirs were established within the WAS model to effectively represent water consumption associated with human activities, including agricultural irrigation and pond storage. title: Seriation and Joint Probability: Unifying Archaeological Dates in the Central Mediterranean, ca. 4th-1st c. BCE
abstract: Probability theory has been applied to archaeological chronology since the advent of radiocarbon dating, but key chronological indicators, such as artifact typologies, continue to be dated in descriptive terms (e.g., “in the later 3rd c. BCE”). Moreover, the informational inter-dependency for how contexts and assemblages affect others’ dating can become opaque. title: Synthetic Approaches to Selenophosphates and Tellurophosphates
abstract: ABSTRACT Organoselenophosphates and tellurophosphates represent important structural motifs in organochalcogenophosphorus chemistry and exhibit unique electronic properties, distinctive biological activities, and versatile synthetic utility. This review provides a systematic overview of recent methodological advances in the synthesis of these two classes of compounds, with particular emphasis on the mechanistic features of key transformations. title: Influence of black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens L.) larval frass manure on plant growth, soil health and economics of sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.)
abstract: Black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens L.; BSF) larval frass has recently been considered a superior organic nutrient source for sustainable crop production because of its balanced nutrient content, which facilitates the conversion of organic waste into effective fertiliser that enhances residue recycling. The present study aimed to compare the effects of BSF larval frass, vermicompost, farmyard manure (FYM) and chemical fertilisers on the growth, yield, soil health and economics of sunflower (Helianthus annus L.) during the rabi season of 2024–25 at the College Farm, Agricultural College, Jagti

title: ACCURACY ANALYSIS OF VEHICLE POSITIONING USING GPS AND GLONASS DATA
abstract: The article presents a new computational strategy for determining the positioning accuracy parameter in car navigation, based on a multi-receiver solution of the SPP code method. The experiment was conducted in kinematic mode using five GNSS receivers mounted on the roof of the vehicle. These receivers recorded code observations from the GPS and GLONASS systems at a frequency of 1 Hz. title: Lithospheric delamination beneath the northern Eastern Cordillera plateau, Colombian Andes
abstract: The northern Eastern Cordillera (EC) in the Colombian Andes is a high-elevation subduction-related orogenic plateau above a flattened subduction zone. Previous constraints on crustal thickness have shown a shift from a thickened central region (~50–65 km) to a thinner northern part (~40–55 km). As no latitudinal dissimilarity in average elevation is observed, up to 1500 m of dynamic topography has been previously stated. title: Automated cloud-edge cyber-physical IoT infrastructure for optimizing the agricultural water-energy nexus and yield
abstract: Abstract Global agriculture faces increasing challenges associated with water scarcity and the growing demand for energy-efficient irrigation management. This study developed and evaluated an integrated three-layer cloud-edge cyber-physical Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure based on an ESP32 microcontroller and ThingSpeak–MATLAB cloud analytics to support automated irrigation management and real-time agricultural monitoring. title: A bacterial pangenome association study identifies a role for polyamine metabolism and alkaline tolerance in middle ear infections
abstract: Infection of the middle ear, or otitis media (OM), is a disease that commonly afflicts children, and Haemophilus influenzae is the most prevalent OM-associated bacterium. We sought new insights into mechanisms of pathogenesis by identifying bacterial genes associated with OM disease. We whole-genome sequenced >200 clinical isolates collected over time from 9 healthy and 12 OM-prone children. title: A (p,q,r)-spherical fuzzy CODAS framework for sustainable crop selection in agriculture
abstract: Crop selection is an important decision problem in precision agriculture and sustainable farm management, particularly in environmentally diverse and climate-sensitive regions. This paper proposes a (p,q,r)-spherical fuzzy ((p,q,r)-SF) extension of the combinative distance-based assessment (CODAS) method for evaluating crop alternatives under uncertain expert judgments. title: Towards Vision‐Language Geo‐Foundation Models: A Survey
abstract: ABSTRACT Vision‐Language Foundation Models (VLFMs) have made remarkable progress on various multimodal tasks, such as image captioning, image–text retrieval, visual question answering, and visual grounding. However, most methods rely on training with general image datasets, and the lack of geospatial data leads to poor performance on earth observation. Numerous geospatial image–text pair datasets and VLFMs fine‐tuned on them have been proposed recently. title: Using interactive immersive simulations and digital analytical records to improve cadets' decision-making and situational awareness
abstract: The rapid adaptation of future specialists to extreme conditions of professional activity highlights the relevance of introducing interactive simulations for realistic modeling of scenario-oriented didactic situations. The study assesses the pedagogical effectiveness of interactive simulation training in developing decision-making, situational awareness, and team interaction skills among cadets. title: Genomics Reveal Population Crash and Range Contraction in Elusive Fijian Hylaeus Bees
abstract: ABSTRACT The conservation of pollinators is of particular interest due to their keystone role in ecosystem function, but is hindered by systematic geographic and methodological biases such that baseline data are not often readily available. Islands are useful as simplified systems to understand evolutionary processes, are known to host higher bee species richness per unit area than mainland regions, and have disproportionate representation of threatened species. title: Multiphase transport interactions across multilayer proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers
abstract: The performance of Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers (PEMWE) at high current densities is governed by a complex interplay between mechanical assembly, electrochemical kinetics, and hydraulic transport. To quantify the impact of mechanical compression on Ohmic resistance and species transport, this study employs a thermodynamically consistent framework based on the Theory of Porous Media (TPM), implemented in FEniCSx (open-access finite element package) via a calibrated conductivity scaling approach. title: Defect-engineered semiconductor nanomaterials for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution: mechanistic insights, design strategies, and future perspectives
abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen production is an insistent route to solar fuel generation, yet its practical efficiency remains limited by charge recombination, photocorrosion, sluggish interfacial kinetics, and inadequate visible-light harvesting. Defect engineering offers a powerful solution by precisely reshaping semiconductor electronic structures, carrier dynamics, surface reactivity, and reaction pathways. title: The quantum Black-Scholes Hamiltonian and tunneling risk: An application to option contract valuation in an emerging market
abstract: Este artículo presenta un marco pedagógico que transforma el modelo clásico de Black-Scholes en un paradigma de Black-Scholes cuántico (QBS) mediante la schrödingerización. title: Engineering properties of green chickpea plants and pods for machine design of a green pod stripper
abstract: Sustainable product development in agricultural mechanization increasingly relies on data-driven knowledge to design efficient technologies and improve the utilization of energy inputs. Physical and engineering properties of the green chickpea crop plants and pods are necessary for designing efficient stripping, handling, and storage equipment. Two varieties (PBG7 and PBG10) and two planting methods (Bed and Flat) were taken as independent parameters. title: Hybrid Renewable Energy Supply System for Remote Villages of Grid in Madagascar Using Linear Programming by Simplex Method and Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper details the development of a linear model to optimize the sizing of a hybrid renewable energy supply system (HRESS) for remote rural villages in developing countries. The model studied is defined by its energy supply versatility to rural household consumers. It includes electrical energy, thermal energy for cooking, and also muscular energy used for transport and manual work related to the HRESS and agriculture. For HRESS design, the approach optimizes the objective function related to total annual cost. Our optimization methodology is organized around simplex and genetic algorithms
journal: International Journal of Energy and Power Engineering

title: A Snapshot of Pesticide Residues in Human, Animal, and Environmental Samples Across 10 European Countries
abstract: Intensive pesticide use raises concerns for environmental, human, and animal health, yet Europe-wide data on exposure remain fragmented. In this study, 224 pesticide residues were analysed in environmental and biological samples collected during the 2021 growing season across 10 European sites, covering conventional and organic farms. Samples included human (farmers, neighbours, consumers) and animal (cattle, goats, pigs, sheep, chickens, cats) matrices—urine, plasma, faeces, and silicone wristbands—as well as farm feed and environmental matrices including soil, earthworms, crops, water, sedim

title: Raman Analysis of RNA Nucleotide Strands From SARS‐CoV‐2 Variants and Subvariants: A Step Forward in the Definition of “Raman Genome”
abstract: Raman spectra of RNA nucleotide strands extracted from 20 SARS-CoV-2 strains, including the original Japanese isolate, Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Lambda, Theta, Mu, and 12 Omicron subvariants, were systematically collected, deconvoluted, and converted into Raman barcodes. title: Military Discourse during the Gaza War via Digital Platforms: A Comparative Analytical Study of Palestinian Resistance and Israeli Military Discourse
abstract: This study aims to identify the nature of military-media discourse circulated on digital platforms during the Gaza war and its impact on international relations, through a comparative analytical study of the speeches of the Palestinian resistance spokesperson (Abu Ubeida) and the Israeli army spokesperson (Daniel Hagari). The study belongs to descriptive research and employs the survey method based on content analysis of a sample of 40 military speeches: 17 by the resistance spokesperson and 23 by the Israeli army spokesperson, from Oct. 7, 2023, to early January 2024. title: Comparative niche modelling identifies conservation and cultivation opportunities for two Harpagophytum species in southern Africa
abstract: Overharvesting of wild medicinal plants is a major driver of biodiversity loss, particularly in semi-arid regions of southern Africa where commercially valuable species such as Harpagophytum procumbens (Burch.) DC. ex Meisn. and Harpagophytum zeyheri Decne. are extensively harvested. title: Multi‐Omics and Computational Pharmacology Approach With Experimental Validation Reveals the Antiproliferative Activity of Sophoricoside Against Pancreatic Cancer
abstract: Pancreatic cancer has a dismal prognosis and limited therapeutic options, highlighting an urgent need for effective treatments. Sophoricoside (SOP), a natural isoflavone glycoside, has exhibited anticancer activities in multiple malignancies, including lung cancer, glioblastoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma. We combined cellular assays, network pharmacology, machine learning, and multi-omics to investigate SOP's effects. title: Canopy functional composition as an indicator of bird traits, taxonomy, and vulnerability in tropical Peruvian forests
abstract: Tropical forests harbour exceptional biodiversity, yet anthropogenic change is rapidly altering forest composition and structure in ways that shape species' ecological strategies and persistence. While advances in remote sensing now allow detailed characterisation of canopy function, links between forest functional diversity and animal traits remain poorly understood. title: Illegal Hunting and Chimpanzee Distribution in the Seringbara Region of the Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve: A Multi‐Scale Modelling Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Guinea is home to approximately two‐thirds of the remaining Critically Endangered western chimpanzee population, and the Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve has been identified as one of eight West African regions with exceptionally high chimpanzee densities. Despite its protected status, the reserve faces three major threats: subsistence agriculture, poaching, and industrial mining. This study focuses on understanding chimpanzee habitat use in relation to human hunting activities within the Seringbara region of the reserve. title: An enhanced quantum reservoir computing framework for hydrological time series modeling
abstract: Abstract Accurate streamflow forecasting is essential for water resource management, yet it remains challenging due to the highly non-stationary and volatile nature of hydrological time series. This study examines an enhanced Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) framework for one-step-ahead monthly dischage forecasting of the Buzău River across three periods. title: African Community Media, AI, and the Question of Community Participation in the Disruptive Era
abstract: In this article, we examine the nexus of Southern African community newspapers’ sceptical AI integration and grassroots democracy. The sceptical approach to AI integration in marginalised media markets of Southern African community newspapers’ news ecosystems is interrogated. title: Environmental Drivers of Metabolic Plasticity in Rubia cordifolia From the Western Himalaya: Implications for Phytochemical Diversity and Antioxidant Potential
abstract: Rubia cordifolia L. is an important Himalayan medicinal plant valued for its diverse therapeutic properties. The present study investigated the influence of altitude, habitat conditions, and edaphic factors on nutritional composition, phytochemicals, and antioxidant activity of R. cordifolia populations collected from different habitats (open grassy, shady, and moist shady) in the western Himalaya. title: A comparative multi-criteria decision analysis framework for strategic energy storage investments: From data to decisions
abstract: Energy storage is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of Europe’s clean energy transition, yet Member States display heterogeneous levels of readiness to integrate and scale storage solutions. This study introduces the Investment Planning Tool, a multi-criteria, interactive decision-support framework designed to evaluate alternatives under diverse uncertainty levels, weighting schemes, and behavioural profiles. title: SW1D: A Python package for seismic surface wave solutions in 1-D elastic media
abstract: We present SW1D, a Python version of a legacy code for the forward computation of Rayleigh and Love wave dispersion curves as well as synthetic seismograms, in elastic, isotropic, laterally homogeneous media. This code solves the surface wave eigenvalue problem for 1-D media using a propagator-matrix technique and subsequently obtains surface wave excitations, in the frequency domain, for a point source described by its moment tensor. title: SeA-RVINS: Semantic-Aware Tightly Coupled RTK-Visual-Inertial System with Correlation-Preserving Robust Estimation for Urban Navigation
abstract: Reliable absolute pose estimation in urban environments is undermined by outlier measurements and incorrect temporal associations that can persist in tightly coupled estimators. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations provide globally referenced measurements but are prone to multipath effects. Visual-inertial sensing supplies local motion constraints, but false visual associations can corrupt the estimator. title: Resummation-scale uncertainties in PDF determinations
abstract: We investigate the impact of resummation-scale variations on parton distribution function (PDF) determinations. These variations introduce an additional source of theoretical uncertainty related to the evolution of PDFs and strong coupling $α_s$ that has never previously been accounted for in PDF fits. Using the open-source xFitter framework, we quantify this uncertainty in fits to HERA deep-inelastic scattering data and examine its implications for predictions of top-quark pair production at the LHC. title: Phoenix: A Modular and Versatile Framework for C/C++ Pointer Analysis
abstract: We present Phoenix, a modular pointer analysis framework for C/C++ that unifies multiple alias analysis algorithms behind a single, stable interface. Phoenix addresses the fragmentation of today’s C/C++ pointer analysis ecosystem by cleanly separating IR construction, constraint generation, solver backends, and client-facing queries—making analyses easy to compare, swap, and compose while exposing explicit precision–performance trade-offs. title: Estimating High-Energy Neutrino Effective Areas from Muon Propagation
abstract: Neutrino telescopes observe neutrinos through the muons produced by charged-current interactions. Most of those muons are born kilometers outside the detector, and how much energy they lose on the way is stochastic. We show that we can compute analytically the distance a muon travels before it falls below the detection threshold, while describing the statistical properties of its losses. title: Design and Validation of an Antagonistic Tendon-Driven Dexterous Robotic Hand with Bidirectional Operation
abstract: Dexterous robotic hands typically reproduce human hand morphology but inherit its one-sided grasping workspace, requiring wrist or arm reorientation to grasp from the opposite side. Existing reversible hands generally rely on non-anthropomorphic, soft, or task-specific finger arrangements, whereas conventional five-digit anthropomorphic hands remain designed primarily for palmar-side grasping. title: The LZ event with a two-state dark matter halo
abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a single nuclear-recoil candidate at $E_R \simeq 248$keV. LZ interprets it in terms of inelastic dark matter that scatters endothermically from its ground state, $χ_1 N \to χ_2 N$. title: Life-time patterns of reinfections: epidemic cohorts as traveling waves
abstract: Infectious disease models that allow for reinfection, such as the SIS or SIRS frameworks, typically treat all infections as exchangeable and independent, erasing the temporal structure of individual reinfection histories.
